```
    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_reject_root_frames_outside_the_configured_width() {
        let high_address = 1u64 << 40;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
            base: high_address,
            length: PAGE_SIZE,
            kind: 0,
        }])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&map).unwrap();
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let failure =
            match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config()) {
                Err(error) => error,
                Ok(_) => panic!("candidate creation accepted an out-of-range root frame"),
            };
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateCreateErrorKind::RootFrameOutOfRange);
        let frame = failure
            .frame
            .expect("root token is returned on validation failure");
        assert_eq!(frame.address(), high_address);
        allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_mapping_rejects_out_of_width_table_frames_transactionally() {
        let high_address = 1u64 << 40;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_1000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: high_address,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&map).unwrap();
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(frame.address(), 0x10_1000);
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            0xffff_9000_0000_1000,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::TableFrameOutOfRange);
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_walk_rejects_intermediate_tables_without_owned_tokens() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(2);
        let foreign_frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let root_index = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4)[0];
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        memory.foreign_child = Some((root_index, foreign_frame.address()));
        let candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address),
            Err(PageWalkError::Reader(
                CandidatePageTableReadError::UnownedTable
            ))
        );
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        allocator.deallocate(foreign_frame).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_release_failure_retains_owned_frames_for_retry() {
        const TOTAL_FRAMES: usize = 513;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(TOTAL_FRAMES);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let mut remaining_frames: [Option<Frame>; TOTAL_FRAMES - 1] =
            core::array::from_fn(|_| Some(allocator.allocate().unwrap()));
        for index in (1..remaining_frames.len()).step_by(2) {
            allocator
                .deallocate(remaining_frames[index].take().unwrap())
                .unwrap();
        }

        let failure = match candidate.release(&mut allocator) {
            Err(failure) => failure,
            Ok(()) => panic!("release unexpectedly fit a full range table"),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            failure.error,
            CandidateReleaseError::Frame(FrameError::RangeTableFull)
        );
        assert_eq!(failure.candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(failure.candidate.mapping_count(), 0);

        allocator
            .deallocate(remaining_frames[0].take().unwrap())
            .unwrap();
        failure.candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        for frame in remaining_frames.into_iter().flatten() {
            allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), TOTAL_FRAMES as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn active_candidate_rejects_mutation_and_release_until_deactivated() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(4);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
        // SAFETY: This is a synthetic test of the active-state guard; no CPU
        // actually uses the test candidate's root.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        assert!(candidate.is_active());
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.unmap_owned_page(0xffff_9000_0000_1000),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::Active)
        ));

        let failure = candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.error, CandidateReleaseError::ActiveRoot);
        let mut candidate = failure.candidate;
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), root);
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test never installed this root in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn active_owned_mapping_invalidates_before_returning_frame_ownership() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(8);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let physical_address = frame.address();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            virtual_address,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: true,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        candidate.memory.record_events = true;
        // SAFETY: The host backend records invalidations and no hardware CR3 is
        // changed; this tests active API state and ownership ordering only.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        // SAFETY: Synthetic active-root ownership is established above, and the
        // backend's invalidation operation records this leaf address.
        unsafe {
            candidate
                .map_owned_page_active(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
                .unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidation_count, 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidated_pages[0], virtual_address);
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[3],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::PageWrite { value, .. }) if value & 1 != 0
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[4],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::Invalidate { virtual_address })
        );
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address),
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
                if translation.physical_address == physical_address
        ));

        // SAFETY: The synthetic root remains the candidate's current test root;
        // unmap invalidates the address before the frame token is returned.
        let frame = unsafe { candidate.unmap_owned_page_active(virtual_address) }.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidation_count, 2);
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidated_pages[1], virtual_address);
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[5],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::PageWrite { value: 0, .. })
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[6],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::Invalidate { virtual_address })
        );
        allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        // SAFETY: No real CPU installed this host-test candidate in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_clone_preserves_inherited_entries_and_shared_tables() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let indexes = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4);
        let source_root = 0x8000;
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0], 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0] + 1, 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0x9000, indexes[1], 0xa000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xa000, indexes[2], 0xb000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xb000, indexes[3], 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 63));

        let root = parse_cr3_root(source_root, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        candidate
            .clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut allocator, &reader, root)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 4);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: 0x20_0000,
                leaf_physical_base: 0x20_0000,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions: PagePermissions {
                    writable: true,
                    executable: false,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 63),
            })
        );

        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn inherited_large_page_permission_change_splits_and_preserves_cache_type() {
        let total_frames = 16;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let indexes = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4);
        let source_root = 0x8000;
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0], 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0x9000, indexes[1], 0xa000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xa000, indexes[2], 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 7) | (1 << 12));
        let root = parse_cr3_root(source_root, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        candidate
            .clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut allocator, &reader, root)
            .unwrap();

        candidate
            .set_inherited_page_permissions(
                &mut allocator,
                virtual_address,
                0x20_1000,
                PagePermissions {
                    writable: false,
                    executable: false,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
            )
            .unwrap();
        let protected = match candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("split mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(protected.physical_address, 0x20_1000);
        assert_eq!(protected.page_size, PAGE_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(
            protected.permissions,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(protected.pat_index, 4);

        let neighbor = match candidate.walk(virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("neighbor mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(neighbor.physical_address, 0x20_2000);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.page_size, PAGE_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.permissions.writable, true);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.permissions.executable, true);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.pat_index, 4);

        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_borrowed_acpi_without_owning_its_frame() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let acpi_physical = 0x20_0000;
        let acpi_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE * total_frames as u64,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: acpi_physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let span = acpi_map
            .validate_acpi_span(acpi_physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            acpi_physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x0606_0606_0606_0606).unwrap();
        let mtrrs = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64)
            .validated_layout(40)
            .unwrap();
        let attributes = mapping
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map - 3);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: acpi_physical,
                leaf_physical_base: acpi_physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions: KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: acpi_physical | 1 | (1 << 63),
            })
        );
        let duplicate_virtual = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            duplicate_virtual.cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::MappingAlreadyPresent
        );
        let other_virtual = virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE;
        let other_mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            other_virtual,
            acpi_physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let duplicate_physical = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, other_mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            duplicate_physical.cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::PhysicalPageAlreadyMapped
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::OwnershipMismatch)
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        // SAFETY: This synthetic test checks the inactive-only guard; the CPU
        // never installs the candidate's root.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_acpi_page(virtual_address),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::Active)
        );
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test never installed this root in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.unmap_acpi_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_explicit_uncacheable_mmio_without_frame_ownership() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let mmio_physical = 0xfee0_0000;
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_d000_0000_0000;
        let mmio_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
            base: 0x10_0000,
            length: PAGE_SIZE * total_frames as u64,
            kind: 0,
        }])
        .unwrap();
        let mmio_span = mmio_map
            .validate_mmio_page(mmio_physical, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            mmio_physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            permissions,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let attributes = super::SelectedCacheAttributes {
            physical_start: mmio_physical,
            physical_end: mmio_physical + PAGE_SIZE,
            pat_index: 3,
            effective_type: EffectiveMemoryType::Uncacheable,
        };
        let before = allocator.free_frames();
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test treats this as a device page and never
        // dereferences it; the API's map authorization, range, permissions, and
        // UC requirements apply.
        unsafe {
            candidate
                .map_mmio_page(&mut allocator, mmio_span, mapping, attributes)
                .unwrap()
        };
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), before - 3);
        let translation = match candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("MMIO mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(translation.physical_address, mmio_physical);
        assert_eq!(translation.permissions, permissions);
        assert_eq!(translation.pat_index, 3);
        assert_eq!(translation.raw_leaf_entry & (1 << 63), 1 << 63);

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_mmio_page(virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::NotMapped)
        );
        candidate.unmap_mmio_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_reject_invalid_borrowed_acpi_mappings() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(8);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let physical = 0x20_0000;
        let other_physical = 0x30_0000;
        let memory_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE * 8,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: other_physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let span = memory_map
            .validate_acpi_span(physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let writable = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: true,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x0606_0606_0606_0606).unwrap();
        let mtrrs = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64)
            .validated_layout(40)
            .unwrap();
        let attributes = writable
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        let failure = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, writable, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping);
        let executable = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            PagePermissions {
                executable: true,
                ..KERNEL_READ_ONLY
            },
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let executable_attributes = executable
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate
                .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, executable, executable_attributes)
                .unwrap_err()
                .cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping
        );
        let user = validate_mapping_range(
            0x4000,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            PagePermissions {
                user_accessible: true,
                ..KERNEL_READ_ONLY
            },
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let user_attributes = user
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate
                .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, user, user_attributes)
                .unwrap_err()
                .cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping
        );
        let wrong_span = memory_map
            .validate_acpi_span(other_physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let read_only = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let read_only_attributes = read_only
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate
                .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, wrong_span, read_only, read_only_attributes)
                .unwrap_err()
                .cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn borrowed_acpi_mapping_rolls_back_new_tables_on_frame_exhaustion() {
        let total_frames = 3;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let physical = 0x20_0000;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE * total_frames as u64,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let span = map
            .validate_acpi_span(physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0xffff_9000_0000_1000,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x0606_0606_0606_0606).unwrap();
        let mtrrs = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64)
            .validated_layout(40)
            .unwrap();
        let attributes = mapping
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::OutOfFrames);
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_unmap_and_release_owned_frames() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), Some(root));
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let physical = frame.address();
        let virtual_address = 0x0000_4000_0000_1000;
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        };
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(&frame, virtual_address, permissions);

        candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 4);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: physical,
                leaf_physical_base: physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: physical | 0x3 | (1 << 2) | (1 << 63),
            })
        );

        let duplicate_frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let (duplicate_mapping, duplicate_attributes) =
            candidate_mapping(&duplicate_frame, virtual_address, permissions);
        let free_before_duplicate = allocator.free_frames();
        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(
                &mut allocator,
                duplicate_frame,
                duplicate_mapping,
                duplicate_attributes,
            )
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::MappingAlreadyPresent);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_duplicate);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();

        let returned = candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(returned.address(), physical);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent {
                level: PageLevel::Pt,
            }
        );
        allocator.deallocate(returned).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_arithmetic_overflow_and_writable_executable_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                0,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );

        let writable_executable = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: true,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x2000, PAGE_SIZE, writable_executable, Some(52), 48),
            Err(MappingError::WritableExecutable)
```
```
        );
```
```
    }
```

```rustix/docs/architecture/syscall-abi.md
     1	# Unix-like process and syscall direction
     2	
     3	**Status: partial address-space construction, host-tested syscall ABI decoding, and bounded static ELF64 metadata parsing/page initialization. No syscall entry/dispatch, executable process, or userland support is implemented.**
     4	
     5	Rustix aims to expose a small, versioned syscall surface that can support Unix-like processes and tools. The kernel must own this interface rather than inherit an ABI accidentally from a bootloader or emulator.
     6	
     7	## Proposed compatibility principles
     8	
     9	- Processes have independent virtual address spaces and explicit lifecycle states.
    10	- File descriptors are per-process integer handles to kernel-managed objects; descriptor inheritance, close-on-exec, duplication, and sharing semantics must be specified together.
    11	- Syscalls use one documented error convention and stable numeric identifiers. New operations must not silently repurpose old numbers.
    12	- Arguments crossing privilege boundaries are copied or validated using narrowly scoped helpers. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::copy_from_user` and `copy_to_user` preflight the complete lower-half mapped range, check writable metadata for kernel-to-user copies, and operate only on owned frame tokens through `UserFrameMemory`; they never form a Rust reference from a user virtual address. Backend copy faults report the completed prefix; hardware fault recovery is not yet implemented.
    13	- Blocking, interruption, cancellation, and restart behavior are explicit for each syscall class.
    14	- A compatibility layer (for example, POSIX-shaped libc behavior) remains separate from internal kernel APIs.
    15	
    16	## Initial syscall ABI v1 contract (specified; register decoding implemented)
    17	
    18	ABI version `1.0` is identified by `abi_version()`, syscall number `0`, returning `0x0001_0000` in `RAX`. The first entry path uses the register convention below. In v1, `RAX` returns a signed 64-bit result: nonnegative values are success (including byte counts and PIDs); errors are negative stable error numbers. ABI versioning is append-only: existing syscall numbers, argument meanings, layouts, and error values never change or get reused. There is no POSIX compatibility claim. `src/syscall.rs` currently implements the stable number/error constants and host-tested decoding of these register-level requests; it does not perform them or install an entry path.
    19	
    20	| Number | Call | Register arguments | Result / behavior |
    21	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
    22	| 0 | `abi_version` | none | `0x0001_0000` (major 1, minor 0). |
    23	| 1 | `exit` | `RDI`: signed 32-bit status in the low 32 bits (upper bits ignored) | Does not return; status is retained exactly by the parent wait record. |
    24	| 2 | `write` | `RDI`: fd, `RSI`: user buffer, `RDX`: byte length | Returns bytes accepted; a short positive result is valid. Initial descriptors 1 and 2 are stdout/stderr console streams; other descriptors return `-EBADF`. Maximum request is 4096 bytes; zero length returns 0 without validating the pointer. |
    25	| 3 | `wait` | `RDI`: child PID (0 means any child), `RSI`: optional user pointer to signed 32-bit exit status | Blocks until a matching child exits and returns its PID. A non-null status output must be writable before the child is reaped; no matching child returns `-ECHILD`. |
    26	
    27	All other numbers are unassigned and return `-ENOSYS`; assigning a number later is an additive extension, never a reinterpretation. Descriptor 0 is reserved for input but v1 has no `read`, `open`, `close`, or `dup` call. Standard descriptors exist for the process lifetime; inheritance and general file-object semantics are not yet exposed. The initial process is created by the kernel loader, not a syscall.
    28	
    29	Stable v1 error numbers (returned negated in `RAX`) are: `1 EINVAL`, `2 EBADF`, `3 EFAULT`, `4 ENOMEM`, `5 ECHILD`, `6 EINTR`, `7 EIO`, `8 ENOSYS`, `9 E2BIG`, `10 EOVERFLOW`, and `11 ENOTSUP`. Unknown syscall numbers return `-ENOSYS`. Pointer-plus-length ranges use checked arithmetic and must lie wholly in a mapped lower-half user range. `write` preflights the whole input range before output; a later endpoint failure may return a short count, and an error before progress returns `-EIO`. A copy fault after progress returns the completed prefix; unrecoverable hardware faults remain process-fatal until user-mode exception handling is implemented. `wait` validates its optional output range before blocking and keeps the child waitable if copying the exit status fails. V1 has no signals, asynchronous interruption, or automatic syscall restart; wait is uninterruptible.
    30	
    31	All ABI integers are fixed-width little-endian x86_64 values. The wait status is one signed 32-bit integer with no implicit padding or extra fields. No other user-visible structs exist in v1.
    32	
    33	## Initial x86_64 entry design (Milestone 4; not implemented)
    34	
    35	The first single-vCPU user-mode slice will enter the kernel with `int $0x80` through a dedicated IDT interrupt gate at DPL 3 and return with `IRETQ`. This intentionally avoids `SYSCALL`/`SYSRET`, `STAR`/`LSTAR`/`FMASK`, and `SWAPGS` state transitions in the first userspace path. It is a provisional architecture decision, not a published or implemented syscall ABI.
    36	
    37	- **Vector ownership:** `0x80` lies inside the device-vector range (`0x20..=0xef`) and is now reserved by `InterruptVectorAllocator`; generic IRQ allocation/release cannot claim it. The dedicated syscall stub and gate are not installed yet. Install a dedicated syscall stub rather than the generic device-IRQ stub. The gate must be an interrupt gate, so maskable interrupts are disabled on entry before Rust dispatch.
    38	- **Selectors:** the current GDT uses `0x08` for kernel code, `0x10` for kernel data, and `0x18` for the two-slot TSS descriptor. Ring-3 data and 64-bit code descriptors are appended at GDT indexes 5 and 6, with compile-time selector assertions for user data `0x2b` and user code `0x33` (RPL 3); the data selector is loaded into user `SS` on return. They are installed at bootstrap but remain unused until a validated return path exists.
    39	- **Privilege stack:** a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt uses `TSS.RSP0`; it must point to the top of the current process's mapped, writable kernel-entry stack before user execution is resumed. The bootstrap TSS initially points to one static ring-0 stack. `interrupts::set_kernel_entry_stack` validates canonical upper-half address shape and alignment before updating `RSP0`, but no per-process stack is allocated and no scheduler path calls it yet. Callers must disable local interrupts and guarantee the stack is mapped writable in every address space that can run until the next update. A future SMP design needs per-CPU TSS and entry-stack state.
    40	- **Entry frame and state:** the assembly stub must preserve the complete user register state and construct a separately specified syscall frame; it must not assume the existing fatal-exception frame is interchangeable. Kernel code must run with the direction flag clear. Preserve user x87/SSE state across kernel handling; AVX remains disabled under the current CPU-state policy. Do not form Rust references from user pointers.
    41	- **Initial register convention:** `RAX` carries the syscall number; arguments use `RDI`, `RSI`, `RDX`, `R10`, `R8`, and `R9`; `RAX` carries the result. This is only a proposed register convention. It becomes stable only together with ABI version discovery, syscall numbers, errors, and transfer semantics below.
    42	- **Return validation:** use `IRETQ`, not `SYSRET`. Before returning, validate that the saved `CS` and `SS` are exactly the ring-3 selectors, `RIP` and `RSP` are canonical and within the process's executable/code and stack regions respectively, and `RFLAGS` contains no privileged or unsupported bits. Construct a safe flags value rather than echoing user-controlled flags. A malformed frame terminates the process with a reported status; never attempt the return and rely on a ring-0 `#GP` to catch it.
    43	- **NMI and interrupt policy:** no GS-base swap is needed on this entry path. An NMI can still arrive during entry; the current NMI/exception path is fatal-only, and this design does not claim to recover from it. Keep that behavior explicit until user-origin exception/NMI policy is implemented and tested. Ordinary maskable IRQs may resume only after the entry state and scheduler ownership are consistent.
    44	
    45	This design depends on a process-owned address space that maps the syscall entry/return code, IDT, GDT, TSS, and the active kernel stack safely. No Ring 3 execution should be enabled until the address-space implementation is reviewed and validated.
    46	
    47	### Process address spaces (design; root construction partially implemented)
    48	
    49	Use a separate four- or five-level root per process. The initial source is the retained active clone of Limine's hierarchy, not a curated clean-room root. Each process root owns its root page, all lower-half intermediate tables, and every user leaf frame. Keep the kernel-root owner alive for the lifetime of every process root. Copy only upper-half top-level entries from that owner into each process root; these entries are non-owning references to shared kernel subtrees, not deep copies, and must never be released by a process teardown. Do not copy lower-half entries from the kernel root.
    50	
    51	Before publishing a shared kernel subtree, validate its page-table structure and physical bounds and reject any effectively user-accessible leaf. U/S permission is the conjunction of every entry on a path, so a U/S bit on one non-leaf alone does not grant user access. When copying upper-half root entries, clear their U/S bit as defense in depth; a user leaf then cannot become accessible if a lower entry changes. `paging::validate_supervisor_kernel_half` implements the bounded, read-only structural/effective-permission preflight, but it does not install roots or prove physical backing is readable; the supplied reader must provide that access guarantee. Sharing the active clone means every accepted upper-half supervisor mapping and alias is present in every process CR3. This is not a curated kernel map or kernel-page-table isolation, and it provides no transient-execution protection. User mappings remain private to one process, are confined to the lower canonical half, preserve W^X, and are non-global in the first implementation.
    52	
    53	The kernel address-space owner is the only authority allowed to modify shared upper-half tables. Mutations must be serialized with local interrupts disabled on the current single-vCPU system and invalidate the affected local translation before the mapping change is relied on. A process root may not edit or reclaim shared tables. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::destroy` releases only private user leaves, intermediate tables, and the root; the caller must first switch CR3 to a different live root and invalidate this root's local non-global translations. Keep the shared kernel owner alive. PCID-aware invalidation and SMP shootdown remain unsupported and need a separate design.

    55	The current `CandidatePageTables` deep-clones the inherited hierarchy, tracks all cloned tables as owned, and holds an exclusive mutable borrow of one memory backend; it is not itself the process-address-space abstraction. `SharedKernelHalf` validates and snapshots the sanitized upper root entries while borrowing the kernel owner. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` uses one exclusive backend borrow for multiple private roots, maps allocator-owned user 4 KiB leaves only in inactive lower halves, retains writable/executable permission metadata, validates that an initial instruction pointer is executable and its stack pointer resolves to a writable NX page, offers one-page-bounded range-preflighted copy-in/copy-out through a separate `UserFrameMemory` backend, and destroys private leaf/table/root frames without freeing shared subtrees.     pub fn allocate(&mut self) -> Option<Frame> {
```
```
        if self.free_count == 0 {
            return None;
        }

        let address = self.free[0].start;
        self.free[0].start += FRAME_SIZE;
        debug_assert!(self.free_frames > 0);
        self.free_frames = self.free_frames.saturating_sub(1);
        if self.free[0].start == self.free[0].end {

        }
        Some(Frame(address))
```

**Testing image segments**

I’m thinking about testing our multi-segment image using code, bss, and data. Currently, I have a single parsed integration with 16 bytes. It seems like I can make an update to use a full valid ELF with two segments. In the paging tests, right now I’m working with custom ELF bytes in a single segment. Maybe I can change the fixture to two segments, but the test still only validates the code. Adding a failure test in the ELF unit tests might be beneficial!
</thinking>

I’ve settled on a bounded loader API that uses the existing allocator-owned frame and user-frame contracts, and delegates per-page cache selection to a typed callback so callers must bind cache attributes to the exact physical range. On failure it will return any unconsumed frame and the number of pages already installed; this makes cleanup obligations explicit without hiding partial ownership or attempting a fragile rollback.

```
//!
//! This validates image metadata only. It does not allocate frames, apply
//! relocations, or install mappings into a process address space.

use core::convert::TryFrom;

    UnsupportedTlsSegment,
    ExecutableStackUnsupported,
    UnsupportedSegmentFlags,
    SegmentNotReadable,
    TooManyLoadSegments,
    InvalidSegmentSize,
    InvalidFileRange,
    InvalidVirtualRange,
    InvalidAlignment,
    WritableExecutableSegment,
    OverlappingLoadSegments,
    ImageTooLarge,
    NoLoadSegments,
    EntryNotExecutable,
}

#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ElfPagePopulationError<E> {
    InvalidSegment,
    InvalidPage,
    FrameMemory(E),
}

#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ElfLoadError<CacheError, TableError, FrameMemoryError> {
    OutOfFrames,
    Mapping(crate::paging::MappingError),
    CachePolicy(CacheError),
    Populate(ElfPagePopulationError<FrameMemoryError>),
    Map(crate::paging::ProcessPageMapError<TableError>),
}

/// A loader failure may leave earlier pages mapped in the inactive process root.
/// The caller owns `frame`, if present, and must reclaim it. Destroy the newly
/// created process root to reclaim `mapped_pages` and any retained page tables.
#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct ElfLoadFailure<CacheError, TableError, FrameMemoryError> {
    pub cause: ElfLoadError<CacheError, TableError, FrameMemoryError>,
    pub frame: Option<crate::frame::Frame>,
    pub mapped_pages: usize,
    pub rollback_retained_table_frames: usize,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct LoadedElf {
    pub entry_point: u64,
    pub mapped_pages: usize,
}

/// One validated, page-aligned PT_LOAD segment in a static executable.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct Elf64LoadSegment {
    virtual_start: u64,
    virtual_end: u64,
    file_offset: usize,
    file_size: usize,
    memory_size: usize,
    page_end: u64,
    flags: u32,
}

impl Elf64LoadSegment {
    pub const fn virtual_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.virtual_start
    }

    pub const fn virtual_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.virtual_end
    }

    pub const fn file_offset(self) -> usize {
        self.file_offset
    }

    pub const fn file_size(self) -> usize {
        self.file_size
    }

    pub const fn memory_size(self) -> usize {
        self.memory_size
    }

    pub const fn page_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.page_end
    }

    pub const fn page_count(self) -> usize {
        ((self.page_end - self.virtual_start) / PAGE_SIZE) as usize
    }

    pub const fn writable(self) -> bool {
        self.flags & PF_WRITE != 0
    }

    pub const fn executable(self) -> bool {
        self.flags & PF_EXECUTE != 0
    }
}

/// A validated view into a static ELF64 image with fixed-capacity PT_LOAD metadata.
#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct Elf64Image<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    entry_point: u64,
    segments: [Option<Elf64LoadSegment>; MAX_ELF_LOAD_SEGMENTS],
    segment_count: usize,
    load_page_count: usize,
}

impl<'a> Elf64Image<'a> {
    pub fn parse(bytes: &'a [u8], virtual_address_bits: u8) -> Result<Self, ElfError> {
        if bytes.len() < ELF64_HEADER_SIZE {
            return Err(ElfError::TruncatedHeader);
        }
        if bytes.get(0..4) != Some(&b"\x7fELF"[..]) {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidMagic);
        }
        if bytes[4] != 2 {
            return Err(ElfError::UnsupportedClass);
        }
        if bytes[5] != 1 {
            return Err(ElfError::UnsupportedByteOrder);
        }
        if bytes[6] != 1 || read_u32(bytes, 20) != Some(1) {
            return Err(ElfError::UnsupportedVersion);
        }
        if read_u16(bytes, 16) != Some(ET_EXEC) {
            return Err(ElfError::UnsupportedObjectType);
        }
        if read_u16(bytes, 18) != Some(EM_X86_64) {
            return Err(ElfError::UnsupportedMachine);
        }
        if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidAddressWidth);
        }
        if read_u16(bytes, 52) != Some(ELF64_HEADER_SIZE as u16) {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidHeaderSize);
        }
        if read_u16(bytes, 54) != Some(ELF64_PROGRAM_HEADER_SIZE as u16) {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderSize);
        }

        let entry_point = read_u64(bytes, 24).ok_or(ElfError::TruncatedHeader)?;
        let program_header_offset = read_u64(bytes, 32).ok_or(ElfError::TruncatedHeader)?;
        let program_header_count =
            usize::from(read_u16(bytes, 56).ok_or(ElfError::TruncatedHeader)?);
        if program_header_count > MAX_ELF_PROGRAM_HEADERS {
            return Err(ElfError::TooManyProgramHeaders);
        }
        let program_header_offset = usize::try_from(program_header_offset)
            .map_err(|_| ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
        let program_header_bytes = program_header_count
            .checked_mul(ELF64_PROGRAM_HEADER_SIZE)
            .ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
        let program_header_end = program_header_offset
            .checked_add(program_header_bytes)
            .filter(|end| *end <= bytes.len())
            .ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;

        let lower_half_end = 1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1);
        let mut image = Self {
            bytes,
            entry_point,
            segments: [None; MAX_ELF_LOAD_SEGMENTS],
            segment_count: 0,
            load_page_count: 0,
        };

        for header_offset in
            (program_header_offset..program_header_end).step_by(ELF64_PROGRAM_HEADER_SIZE)
        {
            let kind = read_u32(bytes, header_offset).ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
            match kind {
                PT_DYNAMIC | PT_INTERP => return Err(ElfError::UnsupportedDynamicSegment),
                PT_TLS => return Err(ElfError::UnsupportedTlsSegment),
                PT_GNU_STACK => {
                    let flags = read_u32(bytes, header_offset + 4)
                        .ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
                    if flags & PF_EXECUTE != 0 {
                        return Err(ElfError::ExecutableStackUnsupported);
                    }
                }
                PT_LOAD => {
                    image.add_load_segment(header_offset, virtual_address_bits, lower_half_end)?
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }

        if image.segment_count == 0 {
            return Err(ElfError::NoLoadSegments);
        }
        if !image.segments().any(|segment| {
            segment.executable()
                && !segment.writable()
                && entry_point >= segment.virtual_start
                && entry_point < segment.virtual_end
        }) {
            return Err(ElfError::EntryNotExecutable);
        }
        Ok(image)
    }

    fn add_load_segment(
        &mut self,
        header_offset: usize,
        virtual_address_bits: u8,
        lower_half_end: u64,
    ) -> Result<(), ElfError> {
        if self.segment_count == MAX_ELF_LOAD_SEGMENTS {
            return Err(ElfError::TooManyLoadSegments);
        }
        let flags =
            read_u32(self.bytes, header_offset + 4).ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
        if flags & !PF_MASK != 0 {
            return Err(ElfError::UnsupportedSegmentFlags);
        }
        if flags & PF_READ == 0 {
            return Err(ElfError::SegmentNotReadable);
        }
        if flags & (PF_WRITE | PF_EXECUTE) == (PF_WRITE | PF_EXECUTE) {
            return Err(ElfError::WritableExecutableSegment);
        }

        let file_offset =
            read_u64(self.bytes, header_offset + 8).ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
        let virtual_start =
            read_u64(self.bytes, header_offset + 16).ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
        let file_size =
            read_u64(self.bytes, header_offset + 32).ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
        let memory_size =
            read_u64(self.bytes, header_offset + 40).ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
        let alignment =
            read_u64(self.bytes, header_offset + 48).ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;

        if file_size > memory_size {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidSegmentSize);
        }
        if memory_size == 0 {
            if file_size == 0 {
                return Ok(());
            }
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidSegmentSize);
        }
        if (file_offset | virtual_start) & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidAlignment);
        }
        if alignment > 1
            && (!alignment.is_power_of_two()
                || file_offset % alignment != virtual_start % alignment)
        {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidAlignment);
        }

        let file_offset = usize::try_from(file_offset).map_err(|_| ElfError::InvalidFileRange)?;
        let file_size = usize::try_from(file_size).map_err(|_| ElfError::InvalidFileRange)?;
        if file_offset
            .checked_add(file_size)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > self.bytes.len())
        {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidFileRange);
        }

        let virtual_end = virtual_start
            .checked_add(memory_size)
            .ok_or(ElfError::InvalidVirtualRange)?;
        let last_virtual = virtual_end - 1;
        if virtual_start < PAGE_SIZE
            || virtual_start >= lower_half_end
            || last_virtual >= lower_half_end
            || !is_canonical(virtual_start, virtual_address_bits)
            || !is_canonical(last_virtual, virtual_address_bits)
        {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidVirtualRange);
        }
        let page_end = virtual_end
            .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE - 1)
            .map(|end| end & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1))
            .filter(|end| *end <= lower_half_end)
            .ok_or(ElfError::InvalidVirtualRange)?;
        let page_count_u64 = (page_end - virtual_start) / PAGE_SIZE;
        let page_count = usize::try_from(page_count_u64).map_err(|_| ElfError::ImageTooLarge)?;
        self.load_page_count = self
            .load_page_count
            .checked_add(page_count)
            .filter(|count| *count <= MAX_ELF_LOAD_PAGES)
            .ok_or(ElfError::ImageTooLarge)?;
        if self
            .segments()
            .any(|segment| virtual_start < segment.page_end && segment.virtual_start < page_end)
        {
            return Err(ElfError::OverlappingLoadSegments);
        }

        let memory_size = usize::try_from(memory_size).map_err(|_| ElfError::ImageTooLarge)?;
        self.segments[self.segment_count] = Some(Elf64LoadSegment {
            virtual_start,
            virtual_end,
            file_offset,
            file_size,
            memory_size,
            page_end,
            flags,
        });
        self.segment_count += 1;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub const fn entry_point(&self) -> u64 {
        self.entry_point
    }

    pub const fn segment_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.segment_count
    }

    pub const fn load_page_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.load_page_count
    }

    pub fn segments(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = Elf64LoadSegment> + '_ {
        self.segments[..self.segment_count]
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .copied()
    }

    pub fn segment_file_bytes(&self, index: usize) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
        let segment = self.segments.get(index)?.as_ref()?;
        let end = segment.file_offset.checked_add(segment.file_size)?;
        self.bytes.get(segment.file_offset..end)
    }

    /// Populate one page of a validated load segment, zero-filling bytes not
    /// covered by the segment's file payload (including BSS).
    pub fn populate_segment_page<U: crate::paging::UserFrameMemory>(
        &self,
        segment_index: usize,
        page_index: usize,
        frame: &crate::frame::Frame,
        user_memory: &mut U,
    ) -> Result<(), ElfPagePopulationError<U::Error>> {
        let segment = self
            .segments
            .get(segment_index)
            .and_then(Option::as_ref)
            .copied()
            .ok_or(ElfPagePopulationError::InvalidSegment)?;
        if page_index >= segment.page_count() {
            return Err(ElfPagePopulationError::InvalidPage);
        }

        let page_offset = page_index
            .checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE as usize)
            .ok_or(ElfPagePopulationError::InvalidPage)?;
        let file_end = page_offset
            .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE as usize)
            .ok_or(ElfPagePopulationError::InvalidPage)?
            .min(segment.file_size);
        let file_start = page_offset.min(file_end);
        let mut page = [0; PAGE_SIZE as usize];
        if file_start < file_end {
            let bytes = self
                .segment_file_bytes(segment_index)
                .ok_or(ElfPagePopulationError::InvalidSegment)?;
            let source = bytes
                .get(file_start..file_end)
                .ok_or(ElfPagePopulationError::InvalidSegment)?;
            page[..source.len()].copy_from_slice(source);
        }
        user_memory
            .copy_to_frame(frame, 0, &page)
            .map_err(ElfPagePopulationError::FrameMemory)
    }

    /// Allocate, populate, and map every validated PT_LOAD page into an inactive
    /// process root. Cache attributes are selected separately for each exact
    /// physical page by `select_cache_attributes`.
    ///
    /// On failure, pages already installed remain owned by the process root and
    /// are reported in `mapped_pages`; any returned frame remains caller-owned.
    /// Destroy a newly created root to reclaim partial mappings and retained page
    /// tables before abandoning a failed load.
    pub fn load_into_process_root<M, U, F, CacheError>(
        &self,
        roots: &mut crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
        allocator: &mut crate::frame::FrameAllocator,
        handle: crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
        user_memory: &mut U,
        physical_address_bits: u8,
        virtual_address_bits: u8,
        mut select_cache_attributes: F,
    ) -> Result<LoadedElf, ElfLoadFailure<CacheError, M::Error, U::Error>>
    where
        M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory,
        U: crate::paging::UserFrameMemory,
        F: FnMut(
            crate::paging::ValidatedMappingRange,
        ) -> Result<crate::paging::SelectedCacheAttributes, CacheError>,
    {
        use crate::paging::{validate_mapping_range, PagePermissions, PAGE_SIZE};

        let mut mapped_pages = 0;
        for (segment_index, segment) in self.segments().enumerate() {
            let permissions = PagePermissions {
                writable: segment.writable(),
                executable: segment.executable(),
                user_accessible: true,
            };
            for page_index in 0..segment.page_count() {
                let virtual_address = u64::try_from(page_index)
                    .ok()
                    .and_then(|index| index.checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE))
                    .and_then(|offset| segment.virtual_start().checked_add(offset));
                let Some(virtual_address) = virtual_address else {
                    return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                        cause: ElfLoadError::Mapping(crate::paging::MappingError::AddressOverflow),
                        frame: None,
                        mapped_pages,
                        rollback_retained_table_frames: 0,
                    });
                };
                let Some(frame) = allocator.allocate() else {
                    return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                        cause: ElfLoadError::OutOfFrames,
                        frame: None,
                        mapped_pages,
                        rollback_retained_table_frames: 0,
                    });
                };
                let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
                    virtual_address,
                    frame.address(),
                    PAGE_SIZE,
                    permissions,
                    Some(physical_address_bits),
                    virtual_address_bits,
                ) {
                    Ok(mapping) => mapping,
                    Err(error) => {
                        return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                            cause: ElfLoadError::Mapping(error),
                            frame: Some(frame),
                            mapped_pages,
                            rollback_retained_table_frames: 0,
                        });
                    }
                };
                let cache_attributes = match select_cache_attributes(mapping) {
                    Ok(attributes) => attributes,
                    Err(error) => {
                        return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                            cause: ElfLoadError::CachePolicy(error),
                            frame: Some(frame),
                            mapped_pages,
                            rollback_retained_table_frames: 0,
                        });
                    }
                };
                if let Err(error) =
                    self.populate_segment_page(segment_index, page_index, &frame, user_memory)
                {
                    return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                        cause: ElfLoadError::Populate(error),
                        frame: Some(frame),
                        mapped_pages,
                        rollback_retained_table_frames: 0,
                    });
                }
                if let Err(failure) =
                    roots.map_user_page(allocator, handle, frame, mapping, cache_attributes)
                {
                    return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                        cause: ElfLoadError::Map(failure.cause),
                        frame: Some(failure.frame),
                        mapped_pages,
                        rollback_retained_table_frames: failure.rollback_retained_table_frames,
                    });
                }
                mapped_pages += 1;
            }
        }
        Ok(LoadedElf {
            entry_point: self.entry_point(),
            mapped_pages,
        })
    }
}

fn is_canonical(address: u64, address_bits: u8) -> bool {
    let sign_bit = (address >> (address_bits - 1)) & 1;
    let upper_bits = address >> address_bits;
    let expected_upper_bits = if sign_bit == 0 {
        0
    } else {
        u64::MAX >> address_bits
    };
    upper_bits == expected_upper_bits
}

fn read_u16(bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Option<u16> {
    let end = offset.checked_add(2)?;
    let bytes = bytes.get(offset..end)?;
    Some(u16::from_le_bytes([bytes[0], bytes[1]]))
}

fn read_u32(bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    let end = offset.checked_add(4)?;
    let bytes = bytes.get(offset..end)?;
    Some(u32::from_le_bytes([bytes[0], bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3]]))
}

fn read_u64(bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Option<u64> {
    let end = offset.checked_add(8)?;
    let bytes = bytes.get(offset..end)?;
    Some(u64::from_le_bytes([
        bytes[0], bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3], bytes[4], bytes[5], bytes[6], bytes[7],
    ]))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{Elf64Image, ElfError, ElfPagePopulationError, MAX_ELF_LOAD_PAGES, PAGE_SIZE};
    use crate::frame::{Frame, FrameAllocator};
    use crate::memory::{MemoryMap, RawMemoryRegion};

    const FILE_SIZE: usize = 0x3000;
    const CODE_PH: usize = 64;
    const DATA_PH: usize = CODE_PH + 56;

    fn valid_elf() -> [u8; FILE_SIZE] {
        let mut bytes = [0; FILE_SIZE];
        bytes[..4].copy_from_slice(b"\x7fELF");
        bytes[4] = 2;
        bytes[5] = 1;
        bytes[6] = 1;
        put_u16(&mut bytes, 16, 2);
        put_u16(&mut bytes, 18, 62);
        put_u32(&mut bytes, 20, 1);
        put_u64(&mut bytes, 24, 0x4000_0000);
        put_u64(&mut bytes, 32, CODE_PH as u64);
        put_u16(&mut bytes, 52, 64);
        put_u16(&mut bytes, 54, 56);
        put_u16(&mut bytes, 56, 2);
        set_load_segment(&mut bytes, CODE_PH, 5, 0x1000, 0x4000_0000, 64, 128, 0x1000);
        set_load_segment(
            &mut bytes,
            DATA_PH,
            6,
            0x2000,
            0x4000_1000,
            128,
            0x1800,
            0x1000,
        );
        bytes[0x1000..0x1040].fill(0x90);
        bytes[0x2000..0x2080].fill(0x5a);
        bytes
    }

    fn set_load_segment(
        bytes: &mut [u8],
        header: usize,
        flags: u32,
        file_offset: u64,
        virtual_address: u64,
        file_size: u64,
        memory_size: u64,
        alignment: u64,
    ) {
        put_u32(bytes, header, 1);
        put_u32(bytes, header + 4, flags);
        put_u64(bytes, header + 8, file_offset);
        put_u64(bytes, header + 16, virtual_address);
        put_u64(bytes, header + 32, file_size);
        put_u64(bytes, header + 40, memory_size);
        put_u64(bytes, header + 48, alignment);
    }

    fn put_u16(bytes: &mut [u8], offset: usize, value: u16) {
        bytes[offset..offset + 2].copy_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
    }

    fn put_u32(bytes: &mut [u8], offset: usize, value: u32) {
        bytes[offset..offset + 4].copy_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
    }

    fn put_u64(bytes: &mut [u8], offset: usize, value: u64) {
        bytes[offset..offset + 8].copy_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
    }

    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
    enum SyntheticFrameError {
        WrongFrame,
        OutOfBounds,
    }

    struct SyntheticFrameMemory {
        frame_address: u64,
        bytes: [u8; PAGE_SIZE as usize],
    }

    // SAFETY: This test backend accesses only its matching synthetic frame token
    // and enforces page bounds for every operation.
    unsafe impl crate::paging::UserFrameMemory for SyntheticFrameMemory {
        type Error = SyntheticFrameError;

        fn copy_from_frame(
            &mut self,
            frame: &Frame,
            offset: usize,
            destination: &mut [u8],
        ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
            let end = offset
                .checked_add(destination.len())
                .filter(|end| *end <= self.bytes.len())
                .ok_or(SyntheticFrameError::OutOfBounds)?;
            if frame.address() != self.frame_address {
                return Err(SyntheticFrameError::WrongFrame);
            }
            destination.copy_from_slice(&self.bytes[offset..end]);
            Ok(())
        }

        fn copy_to_frame(
            &mut self,
            frame: &Frame,
            offset: usize,
            source: &[u8],
        ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
            let end = offset
                .checked_add(source.len())
                .filter(|end| *end <= self.bytes.len())
                .ok_or(SyntheticFrameError::OutOfBounds)?;
            if frame.address() != self.frame_address {
                return Err(SyntheticFrameError::WrongFrame);
            }
            self.bytes[offset..end].copy_from_slice(source);
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_static_x86_64_load_segments_and_exposes_file_bytes() {
        let bytes = valid_elf();
        let image = Elf64Image::parse(&bytes, 48).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(image.entry_point(), 0x4000_0000);
        assert_eq!(image.segment_count(), 2);
        assert_eq!(image.load_page_count(), 3);
        let mut segments = image.segments();
        let code = segments.next().unwrap();
        let data = segments.next().unwrap();
        assert!(segments.next().is_none());
        assert_eq!(code.virtual_start(), 0x4000_0000);
        assert!(code.executable());
        assert!(!code.writable());
        assert_eq!(data.virtual_start(), 0x4000_1000);
        assert!(data.writable());
        assert!(!data.executable());
        assert_eq!(data.virtual_end(), 0x4000_2800);
        assert_eq!(data.memory_size(), 0x1800);
        assert_eq!(data.page_end(), 0x4000_3000);
        assert_eq!(image.segment_file_bytes(1).unwrap(), &[0x5a; 128]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn populates_file_bytes_and_zero_fills_each_segment_page() {
        let bytes = valid_elf();
        let image = Elf64Image::parse(&bytes, 48).unwrap();
        let memory_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
            base: 0x10_0000,
            length: PAGE_SIZE * 2,
            kind: 0,
        }])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&memory_map).unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let mut user_memory = SyntheticFrameMemory {
            frame_address: frame.address(),
            bytes: [0xa5; PAGE_SIZE as usize],
        };

        image
            .populate_segment_page(1, 0, &frame, &mut user_memory)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(&user_memory.bytes[..128], &[0x5a; 128]);
        assert!(user_memory.bytes[128..].iter().all(|byte| *byte == 0));

        user_memory.bytes.fill(0xa5);
        image
            .populate_segment_page(1, 1, &frame, &mut user_memory)
            .unwrap();
        assert!(user_memory.bytes.iter().all(|byte| *byte == 0));
        assert_eq!(
            image.populate_segment_page(1, 2, &frame, &mut user_memory),
            Err(ElfPagePopulationError::InvalidPage)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            image.populate_segment_page(16, 0, &frame, &mut user_memory),
            Err(ElfPagePopulationError::InvalidSegment)
        );
    }

    #[test]
```

```
//! Checked x86_64 mapping policy and a bounded owned page-table builder.
//!
//! Pure helpers validate addresses, permissions, and cache policy. Candidate
//! table access is delegated to an unsafe backend contract. This module never
//! writes CR3; callers may activate a validated hierarchy through the explicit
//! unsafe ownership marker after performing their architecture-specific switch.

use crate::frame::{Frame, FrameAllocator, FrameError};
use crate::memory::{
    is_canonical_virtual_address, physical_range_fits_address_width, HhdmAddressError, MemoryMap,
    RegionKind, ValidatedAcpiSpan, ValidatedMmioSpan,
};

/// Base page size supported by the initial Rustix mapping policy.
pub const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;

/// The physical root address and interpretation of CR3's low bits.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Cr3Root {
    physical_address: u64,
    low_bits: Cr3LowBits,
}

impl Cr3Root {
    pub const fn physical_address(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_address
    }

    pub const fn low_bits(self) -> Cr3LowBits {
        self.low_bits
    }
}

/// CR3's low bits are either a PCID or the paging-structure cache controls.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3LowBits {
    Pcid(u16),
    CacheControls {
        page_level_write_through: bool,
        page_level_cache_disable: bool,
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3Error {
    UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth,
    InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth,
    InvalidRootAddress,
    ReservedBits,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3RootAccessError {
    NotBootloaderReclaimable,
    Hhdm(HhdmAddressError),
}

/// Decode the currently active CR3 value without dereferencing its root table.
///
/// The caller supplies the reported physical-address width and whether CR4.PCIDE
/// is active, since those determine the valid address and low-bit encodings.
/// Encode a replacement CR3 value while preserving the active low-bit mode.
///
/// PCID is retained but the no-flush bit is always cleared so the selected PCID
/// is invalidated on load. Legacy PWT/PCD controls are preserved unchanged.
pub fn encode_cr3_value(
    root_physical_address: u64,
    low_bits: Cr3LowBits,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<u64, Cr3Error> {
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
    }
    let root_end = root_physical_address
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(Cr3Error::InvalidRootAddress)?;
    if root_physical_address & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
        || !physical_range_fits_address_width(
            root_physical_address,
            root_end,
            physical_address_bits,
        )
    {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidRootAddress);
    }
    let low = match low_bits {
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid(pcid) if pcid <= 0x0fff => u64::from(pcid),
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid(_) => return Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits),
        Cr3LowBits::CacheControls {
            page_level_write_through,
            page_level_cache_disable,
        } => {
            (u64::from(page_level_write_through) << 3) | (u64::from(page_level_cache_disable) << 4)
        }
    };
    Ok(root_physical_address | low)
}

pub fn parse_cr3_root(
    raw: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    pcid_enabled: bool,
) -> Result<Cr3Root, Cr3Error> {
    let physical_address_bits =
        physical_address_bits.ok_or(Cr3Error::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)?;
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
    }

    let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
    let low_mask = if pcid_enabled {
        PAGE_SIZE - 1
    } else {
        (1 << 3) | (1 << 4)
    };
    if raw & !(physical_mask | low_mask) != 0 {
        return Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits);
    }

    let low_bits = if pcid_enabled {
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid((raw & (PAGE_SIZE - 1)) as u16)
    } else {
        Cr3LowBits::CacheControls {
            page_level_write_through: raw & (1 << 3) != 0,
            page_level_cache_disable: raw & (1 << 4) != 0,
        }
    };

    Ok(Cr3Root {
        physical_address: raw & physical_mask,
        low_bits,
    })
}

/// Calculate the protocol-backed HHDM address of Limine's inherited root page.
///
/// This requires the root page to be wholly contained in bootloader-reclaimable
/// memory, as specified for Limine page tables. It does not dereference the page
/// or prove that the active hierarchy contains the HHDM mapping.
pub fn inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
    root: Cr3Root,
    memory_map: &MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<u64, Cr3RootAccessError> {
    let physical_start = root.physical_address();
    let physical_end = physical_start
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(Cr3RootAccessError::Hhdm(HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow))?;
    if !memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
        physical_start,
        physical_end,
        RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
    ) {
        return Err(Cr3RootAccessError::NotBootloaderReclaimable);
    }
    memory_map
        .limine_hhdm_address(
            hhdm_offset,
            physical_start,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            physical_address_bits,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
        .map_err(Cr3RootAccessError::Hhdm)
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageLevel {
    Pml5,
    Pml4,
    Pdpt,
    Pd,
    Pt,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PageWalkConfig {
    pub levels: u8,
    pub physical_address_bits: u8,
    pub virtual_address_bits: u8,
    pub nx_enabled: bool,
    pub page_2m_supported: bool,
    pub page_1g_supported: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PageTranslation {
    pub physical_address: u64,
    pub leaf_physical_base: u64,
    pub page_size: u64,
    pub permissions: PagePermissions,
    pub pat_index: u8,
    pub raw_leaf_entry: u64,
}

impl PageTranslation {
    /// Compare effective mapping policy while allowing equivalent large-page splits.
    ///
    /// Physical address, permissions, PAT index, global/software flags, and
    /// other stable leaf attributes must match. Leaf size, physical base, and
    /// hardware-maintained accessed/dirty bits may differ after a page split.
    pub const fn same_effective_mapping(self, other: Self) -> bool {
        const IGNORED_LEAF_BITS: u64 = PTE_ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK | (1 << 5) | (1 << 6) | (1 << 7);

        self.physical_address == other.physical_address
            && self.permissions.writable == other.permissions.writable
            && self.permissions.executable == other.permissions.executable
            && self.permissions.user_accessible == other.permissions.user_accessible
            && self.pat_index == other.pat_index
            && self.raw_leaf_entry & !IGNORED_LEAF_BITS == other.raw_leaf_entry & !IGNORED_LEAF_BITS
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageWalkOutcome {
    NotPresent { level: PageLevel },
    Mapped(PageTranslation),
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageTableEntryError {
    PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
    NxDisabled,
    LargePageUnsupported,
    LargePageAtInvalidLevel,
    LargePageMisaligned,
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageWalkError<E> {
    InvalidConfiguration,
    NonCanonicalAddress,
    InvalidRoot,
    InvalidEntry {
        level: PageLevel,
        error: PageTableEntryError,
    },
    Reader(E),
}

/// Read one raw entry from a table at a validated physical page address.
pub trait PageTableReader {
    type Error;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error>;
}

/// Translate one virtual address by following at most five page-table entries.
///
/// The reader owns all physical-memory access policy. This walker does not turn
/// physical addresses into pointers, modify tables, or infer effective cache
/// types from the leaf PAT selector.
pub fn walk_virtual_address<R: PageTableReader>(
    reader: &R,
    root: Cr3Root,
    virtual_address: u64,
    config: PageWalkConfig,
) -> Result<PageWalkOutcome, PageWalkError<R::Error>> {
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&config.physical_address_bits)
        || (config.levels != 4 && config.levels != 5)
        || config.virtual_address_bits != if config.levels == 4 { 48 } else { 57 }
    {
        return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidConfiguration);
    }
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(virtual_address, config.virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(PageWalkError::NonCanonicalAddress);
    }
    let root_physical = root.physical_address();
    let root_end = root_physical
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(PageWalkError::InvalidRoot)?;
    if root_physical & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
        || !physical_range_fits_address_width(root_physical, root_end, config.physical_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidRoot);
    }

    const PRESENT: u64 = 1;
    const WRITABLE: u64 = 1 << 1;
    const USER: u64 = 1 << 2;
    const WRITE_THROUGH: u64 = 1 << 3;
    const CACHE_DISABLE: u64 = 1 << 4;
    const PAGE_SIZE_OR_PAT: u64 = 1 << 7;
    const LARGE_PAGE_PAT: u64 = 1 << 12;
    const NO_EXECUTE: u64 = 1 << 63;
    const ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK: u64 = 0x000f_ffff_ffff_f000;

    let physical_mask = ((1u64 << config.physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
    let mut table_physical = root_physical;
    let mut writable = true;
    let mut user_accessible = true;
    let mut executable = true;
    let mut level_number = config.levels;

    loop {
        let shift = 12 + 9 * (level_number - 1);
        let index = ((virtual_address >> shift) & 0x1ff) as u16;
        let entry = reader
```
