    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_reject_root_frames_outside_the_configured_width() {
        let high_address = 1u64 << 40;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
            base: high_address,
            length: PAGE_SIZE,
            kind: 0,
        }])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&map).unwrap();
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let failure =
            match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config()) {
                Err(error) => error,
                Ok(_) => panic!("candidate creation accepted an out-of-range root frame"),
            };
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateCreateErrorKind::RootFrameOutOfRange);
        let frame = failure
            .frame
            .expect("root token is returned on validation failure");
        assert_eq!(frame.address(), high_address);
        allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_mapping_rejects_out_of_width_table_frames_transactionally() {
        let high_address = 1u64 << 40;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_1000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: high_address,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&map).unwrap();
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(frame.address(), 0x10_1000);
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            0xffff_9000_0000_1000,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::TableFrameOutOfRange);
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_walk_rejects_intermediate_tables_without_owned_tokens() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(2);
        let foreign_frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let root_index = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4)[0];
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        memory.foreign_child = Some((root_index, foreign_frame.address()));
        let candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address),
            Err(PageWalkError::Reader(
                CandidatePageTableReadError::UnownedTable
            ))
        );
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        allocator.deallocate(foreign_frame).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_release_failure_retains_owned_frames_for_retry() {
        const TOTAL_FRAMES: usize = 513;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(TOTAL_FRAMES);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let mut remaining_frames: [Option<Frame>; TOTAL_FRAMES - 1] =
            core::array::from_fn(|_| Some(allocator.allocate().unwrap()));
        for index in (1..remaining_frames.len()).step_by(2) {
            allocator
                .deallocate(remaining_frames[index].take().unwrap())
                .unwrap();
        }

        let failure = match candidate.release(&mut allocator) {
            Err(failure) => failure,
            Ok(()) => panic!("release unexpectedly fit a full range table"),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            failure.error,
            CandidateReleaseError::Frame(FrameError::RangeTableFull)
        );
        assert_eq!(failure.candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(failure.candidate.mapping_count(), 0);

        allocator
            .deallocate(remaining_frames[0].take().unwrap())
            .unwrap();
        failure.candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        for frame in remaining_frames.into_iter().flatten() {
            allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), TOTAL_FRAMES as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn active_candidate_rejects_mutation_and_release_until_deactivated() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(4);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
        // SAFETY: This is a synthetic test of the active-state guard; no CPU
        // actually uses the test candidate's root.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        assert!(candidate.is_active());
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.unmap_owned_page(0xffff_9000_0000_1000),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::Active)
        ));

        let failure = candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.error, CandidateReleaseError::ActiveRoot);
        let mut candidate = failure.candidate;
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), root);
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test never installed this root in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn active_owned_mapping_invalidates_before_returning_frame_ownership() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(8);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let physical_address = frame.address();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            virtual_address,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: true,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        candidate.memory.record_events = true;
        // SAFETY: The host backend records invalidations and no hardware CR3 is
        // changed; this tests active API state and ownership ordering only.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        // SAFETY: Synthetic active-root ownership is established above, and the
        // backend's invalidation operation records this leaf address.
        unsafe {
            candidate
                .map_owned_page_active(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
                .unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidation_count, 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidated_pages[0], virtual_address);
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[3],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::PageWrite { value, .. }) if value & 1 != 0
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[4],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::Invalidate { virtual_address })
        );
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address),
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
                if translation.physical_address == physical_address
        ));

        // SAFETY: The synthetic root remains the candidate's current test root;
        // unmap invalidates the address before the frame token is returned.
        let frame = unsafe { candidate.unmap_owned_page_active(virtual_address) }.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidation_count, 2);
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidated_pages[1], virtual_address);
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[5],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::PageWrite { value: 0, .. })
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[6],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::Invalidate { virtual_address })
        );
        allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        // SAFETY: No real CPU installed this host-test candidate in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_clone_preserves_inherited_entries_and_shared_tables() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let indexes = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4);
        let source_root = 0x8000;
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0], 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0] + 1, 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0x9000, indexes[1], 0xa000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xa000, indexes[2], 0xb000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xb000, indexes[3], 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 63));

        let root = parse_cr3_root(source_root, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        candidate
            .clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut allocator, &reader, root)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 4);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: 0x20_0000,
                leaf_physical_base: 0x20_0000,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions: PagePermissions {
                    writable: true,
                    executable: false,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 63),
            })
        );

        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn inherited_large_page_permission_change_splits_and_preserves_cache_type() {
        let total_frames = 16;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let indexes = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4);
        let source_root = 0x8000;
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0], 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0x9000, indexes[1], 0xa000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xa000, indexes[2], 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 7) | (1 << 12));
        let root = parse_cr3_root(source_root, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        candidate
            .clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut allocator, &reader, root)
            .unwrap();

        candidate
            .set_inherited_page_permissions(
                &mut allocator,
                virtual_address,
                0x20_1000,
                PagePermissions {
                    writable: false,
                    executable: false,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
            )
            .unwrap();
        let protected = match candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("split mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(protected.physical_address, 0x20_1000);
        assert_eq!(protected.page_size, PAGE_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(
            protected.permissions,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(protected.pat_index, 4);

        let neighbor = match candidate.walk(virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("neighbor mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(neighbor.physical_address, 0x20_2000);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.page_size, PAGE_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.permissions.writable, true);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.permissions.executable, true);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.pat_index, 4);

        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]

        let root = parse_cr3_root(source_root, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        candidate
            .clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut allocator, &reader, root)
            .unwrap();

        candidate
            .set_inherited_page_permissions(

                    executable: false,

    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_borrowed_acpi_without_owning_its_frame() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let acpi_physical = 0x20_0000;
        let acpi_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE * total_frames as u64,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: acpi_physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let span = acpi_map
            .validate_acpi_span(acpi_physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            acpi_physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x0606_0606_0606_0606).unwrap();
        let mtrrs = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64)
            .validated_layout(40)
            .unwrap();
        let attributes = mapping
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map - 3);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: acpi_physical,
                leaf_physical_base: acpi_physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions: KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: acpi_physical | 1 | (1 << 63),
            })
        );
        let duplicate_virtual = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            duplicate_virtual.cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::MappingAlreadyPresent
        );
        let other_virtual = virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE;
        let other_mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            other_virtual,
            acpi_physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let duplicate_physical = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, other_mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            duplicate_physical.cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::PhysicalPageAlreadyMapped
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::OwnershipMismatch)
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        // SAFETY: This synthetic test checks the inactive-only guard; the CPU
        // never installs the candidate's root.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_acpi_page(virtual_address),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::Active)
        );
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test never installed this root in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.unmap_acpi_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_explicit_uncacheable_mmio_without_frame_ownership() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let mmio_physical = 0xfee0_0000;
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_d000_0000_0000;
        let mmio_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
            base: 0x10_0000,
            length: PAGE_SIZE * total_frames as u64,
            kind: 0,
        }])
        .unwrap();
        let mmio_span = mmio_map
            .validate_mmio_page(mmio_physical, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            mmio_physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            permissions,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let attributes = super::SelectedCacheAttributes {
            physical_start: mmio_physical,
            physical_end: mmio_physical + PAGE_SIZE,
            pat_index: 3,
            effective_type: EffectiveMemoryType::Uncacheable,
        };
        let before = allocator.free_frames();
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test treats this as a device page and never
        // dereferences it; the API's map authorization, range, permissions, and
        // UC requirements apply.
        unsafe {
            candidate
                .map_mmio_page(&mut allocator, mmio_span, mapping, attributes)
                .unwrap()
        };
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), before - 3);
        let translation = match candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("MMIO mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(translation.physical_address, mmio_physical);
        assert_eq!(translation.permissions, permissions);
        assert_eq!(translation.pat_index, 3);
        assert_eq!(translation.raw_leaf_entry & (1 << 63), 1 << 63);

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_mmio_page(virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::NotMapped)
        );
        candidate.unmap_mmio_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_reject_invalid_borrowed_acpi_mappings() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(8);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let physical = 0x20_0000;
        let other_physical = 0x30_0000;
        let memory_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE * 8,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: other_physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let span = memory_map
            .validate_acpi_span(physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let writable = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: true,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x0606_0606_0606_0606).unwrap();
        let mtrrs = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64)
            .validated_layout(40)
            .unwrap();
        let attributes = writable
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        let failure = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, writable, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping);
        let executable = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            PagePermissions {
                executable: true,
                ..KERNEL_READ_ONLY
            },
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let executable_attributes = executable
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate
                .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, executable, executable_attributes)
                .unwrap_err()
                .cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping
        );
        let user = validate_mapping_range(
            0x4000,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            PagePermissions {
                user_accessible: true,
                ..KERNEL_READ_ONLY
            },
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let user_attributes = user
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate
                .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, user, user_attributes)
                .unwrap_err()
                .cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping
        );
        let wrong_span = memory_map
            .validate_acpi_span(other_physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let read_only = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let read_only_attributes = read_only
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate
                .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, wrong_span, read_only, read_only_attributes)
                .unwrap_err()
                .cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn borrowed_acpi_mapping_rolls_back_new_tables_on_frame_exhaustion() {
        let total_frames = 3;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let physical = 0x20_0000;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE * total_frames as u64,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let span = map
            .validate_acpi_span(physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0xffff_9000_0000_1000,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x0606_0606_0606_0606).unwrap();
        let mtrrs = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64)
            .validated_layout(40)
            .unwrap();
        let attributes = mapping
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::OutOfFrames);
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_unmap_and_release_owned_frames() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), Some(root));
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let physical = frame.address();
        let virtual_address = 0x0000_4000_0000_1000;
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        };
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(&frame, virtual_address, permissions);

        candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 4);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: physical,
                leaf_physical_base: physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: physical | 0x3 | (1 << 2) | (1 << 63),
            })
        );

        let duplicate_frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let (duplicate_mapping, duplicate_attributes) =
            candidate_mapping(&duplicate_frame, virtual_address, permissions);
        let free_before_duplicate = allocator.free_frames();
        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(
                &mut allocator,
                duplicate_frame,
                duplicate_mapping,
                duplicate_attributes,
            )
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::MappingAlreadyPresent);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_duplicate);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();

        let returned = candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(returned.address(), physical);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent {
                level: PageLevel::Pt,
            }
        );
        allocator.deallocate(returned).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    fn candidate_page_tables_support_five_level_virtual_paths() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let config = PageWalkConfig {
            levels: 5,
            virtual_address_bits: 57,
            ..four_level_walk_config()

        let virtual_address = 0xff00_0000_0020_1000;
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            virtual_address,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: true,
                user_accessible: false,
            },

        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 5);

                leaf_physical_base: physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions: PagePermissions {
                    writable: false,

                    user_accessible: false,

        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_arithmetic_overflow_and_writable_executable_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                0,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );

        let writable_executable = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: true,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x2000, PAGE_SIZE, writable_executable, Some(52), 48),
            Err(MappingError::WritableExecutable)
        );
    }

```
//! Fixed-capacity process identity and parent/child exit-state policy.
//!
//! This module does not own address spaces or block in the scheduler. Callers
//! must pair each process ID with its root and retry `try_wait` after a child
//! state change; a `Running` result means a syscall caller still has to block.

pub const MAX_PROCESSES: usize = 4;

/// ID zero belongs to the kernel supervisor and is never assigned to userspace.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, Ord, PartialEq, PartialOrd)]
pub struct ProcessId(u64);

impl ProcessId {
    pub const fn get(self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }
}

pub const KERNEL_PROCESS_ID: ProcessId = ProcessId(0);

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ProcessState {
    Running,
    Exited(i32),
}

/// A nonblocking observation of a child. `Exited` is returned once and reaps it.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum WaitResult {
    Running { pid: ProcessId },
    Exited { pid: ProcessId, status: i32 },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ProcessTableError {
    Capacity,
    InitialProcessAlreadyExists,
    InvalidProcess,
    InvalidParent,
    ParentExited,
    AlreadyExited,
    NoChild,
    ProcessIdExhausted,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct ProcessRecord {
    pid: ProcessId,
    parent: ProcessId,
    state: ProcessState,
}

/// Bounded, allocation-free process lifecycle records for the first user slice.
///
/// Exited records remain waitable zombies until their parent calls `try_wait`.
/// If a parent exits first, its children are reparented to the kernel supervisor
/// so their exit records remain reapable. Process roots and descriptor tables are
/// owned by a future runtime layer, not by this policy table.
pub struct ProcessTable {
    records: [Option<ProcessRecord>; MAX_PROCESSES],
    next_pid: Option<u64>,
}

impl ProcessTable {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            records: [None; MAX_PROCESSES],
            next_pid: Some(1),
        }
    }

    /// Register the one boot-created process under the kernel supervisor.
    pub fn create_initial(&mut self) -> Result<ProcessId, ProcessTableError> {
        if self
            .records
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .any(|record| record.parent == KERNEL_PROCESS_ID)
        {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::InitialProcessAlreadyExists);
        }
        self.insert(KERNEL_PROCESS_ID)
    }

    /// Register a child of a currently running process.
    pub fn spawn(&mut self, parent: ProcessId) -> Result<ProcessId, ProcessTableError> {
        let parent_record = self
            .record(parent)
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::InvalidParent)?;
        if parent_record.state != ProcessState::Running {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::ParentExited);
        }
        self.insert(parent)
    }

    /// Record an exit status without reclaiming the process identity.
    pub fn exit(&mut self, pid: ProcessId, status: i32) -> Result<(), ProcessTableError> {
        let index = self
            .records
            .iter()
            .position(|record| record.is_some_and(|record| record.pid == pid))
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::InvalidProcess)?;
        let record = self.records[index]
            .as_mut()
            .expect("process slot was found");
        if record.state != ProcessState::Running {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::AlreadyExited);
        }
        record.state = ProcessState::Exited(status);
        for child in self.records.iter_mut().flatten() {
            if child.parent == pid {
                child.parent = KERNEL_PROCESS_ID;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Inspect or reap a matching child without blocking.
    ///
    /// `child_pid == 0` selects any child, preferring the lowest-PID exited child
    /// so a wait-any caller never sleeps while a zombie is ready to reap.
    pub fn try_wait(
        &mut self,
        parent: ProcessId,
        child_pid: u64,
    ) -> Result<WaitResult, ProcessTableError> {
        if parent != KERNEL_PROCESS_ID {
            let parent_record = self
                .record(parent)
                .ok_or(ProcessTableError::InvalidParent)?;
            if parent_record.state != ProcessState::Running {
                return Err(ProcessTableError::ParentExited);
            }
        }

        let mut found_child = false;
        let mut running: Option<(usize, ProcessId)> = None;
        let mut exited: Option<(usize, ProcessId, i32)> = None;
        for (index, record) in self.records.iter().enumerate() {
            let Some(record) = record.filter(|record| {
                record.parent == parent && (child_pid == 0 || record.pid.get() == child_pid)
            }) else {
                continue;
            };
            found_child = true;
            match record.state {
                ProcessState::Running => {
                    if running.is_none_or(|(_, pid)| record.pid < pid) {
                        running = Some((index, record.pid));
                    }
                }
                ProcessState::Exited(status) => {
                    if exited.is_none_or(|(_, pid, _)| record.pid < pid) {
                        exited = Some((index, record.pid, status));
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        if let Some((index, pid, status)) = exited {
            self.records[index] = None;
            return Ok(WaitResult::Exited { pid, status });
        }
        if let Some((_, pid)) = running {
            return Ok(WaitResult::Running { pid });
        }
        if found_child {
            unreachable!("a matching child must be running or exited");
        }
        Err(ProcessTableError::NoChild)
    }

    pub fn state(&self, pid: ProcessId) -> Option<ProcessState> {
        self.record(pid).map(|record| record.state)
    }

    pub fn live_records(&self) -> usize {
        self.records.iter().flatten().count()
    }

    fn insert(&mut self, parent: ProcessId) -> Result<ProcessId, ProcessTableError> {
        let slot = self
            .records
            .iter()
            .position(Option::is_none)
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::Capacity)?;
        let pid = self.next_pid.ok_or(ProcessTableError::ProcessIdExhausted)?;
        self.next_pid = pid.checked_add(1);
        let pid = ProcessId(pid);
        self.records[slot] = Some(ProcessRecord {
            pid,
            parent,
            state: ProcessState::Running,
        });
        Ok(pid)
    }

    fn record(&self, pid: ProcessId) -> Option<&ProcessRecord> {
        self.records
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .find(|record| record.pid == pid)
    }
}

impl Default for ProcessTable {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{
        ProcessState, ProcessTable, ProcessTableError, WaitResult, KERNEL_PROCESS_ID, MAX_PROCESSES,
    };

    #[test]
    fn child_exit_status_is_retained_until_exact_wait_reaps_it() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let init = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        let child = processes.spawn(init).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(init, child.get()),
            Ok(WaitResult::Running { pid: child })
        );
        processes.exit(child, -17).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(processes.state(child), Some(ProcessState::Exited(-17)));
        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(init, child.get()),
            Ok(WaitResult::Exited {
                pid: child,
                status: -17,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(processes.state(child), None);
        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(init, child.get()),
            Err(ProcessTableError::NoChild)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn wait_any_prefers_the_lowest_pid_zombie_and_keeps_running_children() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let init = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        let first = processes.spawn(init).unwrap();
        let second = processes.spawn(init).unwrap();
        processes.exit(second, 23).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(init, 0),
            Ok(WaitResult::Exited {
                pid: second,
                status: 23,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(init, 0),
            Ok(WaitResult::Running { pid: first })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn exiting_parent_reparents_children_to_kernel_supervisor() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let init = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        let child = processes.spawn(init).unwrap();
        processes.exit(init, 0).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(KERNEL_PROCESS_ID, 0),
            Ok(WaitResult::Exited {
                pid: init,
                status: 0,
            })
        );
        processes.exit(child, 7).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(KERNEL_PROCESS_ID, child.get()),
            Ok(WaitResult::Exited {
                pid: child,
                status: 7,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn capacity_and_invalid_lifecycle_operations_are_explicit() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        assert_eq!(
            processes.spawn(KERNEL_PROCESS_ID),
            Err(ProcessTableError::InvalidParent)
        );
        let init = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            processes.create_initial(),
            Err(ProcessTableError::InitialProcessAlreadyExists)
        );
        let children: [Option<super::ProcessId>; MAX_PROCESSES - 1] =
            core::array::from_fn(|_| None);
        let mut children = children;
        for child in &mut children {
            *child = Some(processes.spawn(init).unwrap());
        }
        assert_eq!(processes.live_records(), MAX_PROCESSES);
        assert_eq!(processes.spawn(init), Err(ProcessTableError::Capacity));

        let child = children[0].unwrap();
        processes.exit(child, 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            processes.exit(child, 2),
            Err(ProcessTableError::AlreadyExited)
        );
        assert_eq!(processes.spawn(child), Err(ProcessTableError::ParentExited));
    }
}

# Unix-like process and syscall direction

**Status: partial address-space construction, host-tested syscall ABI decoding, and bounded static ELF64 loading into an inactive process root. No syscall entry/dispatch, process lifecycle, or Ring 3 execution is implemented.**

Rustix aims to expose a small, versioned syscall surface that can support Unix-like processes and tools. The kernel must own this interface rather than inherit an ABI accidentally from a bootloader or emulator.

## Proposed compatibility principles

- Processes have independent virtual address spaces and explicit lifecycle states.
- File descriptors are per-process integer handles to kernel-managed objects; descriptor inheritance, close-on-exec, duplication, and sharing semantics must be specified together.
- Syscalls use one documented error convention and stable numeric identifiers. New operations must not silently repurpose old numbers.
- Arguments crossing privilege boundaries are copied or validated using narrowly scoped helpers. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::copy_from_user` and `copy_to_user` preflight the complete lower-half mapped range, check writable metadata for kernel-to-user copies, and operate only on owned frame tokens through `UserFrameMemory`; they never form a Rust reference from a user virtual address. Backend copy faults report the completed prefix; hardware fault recovery is not yet implemented.
- Blocking, interruption, cancellation, and restart behavior are explicit for each syscall class.
- A compatibility layer (for example, POSIX-shaped libc behavior) remains separate from internal kernel APIs.

## Initial syscall ABI v1 contract (specified; register decoding implemented)

ABI version `1.0` is identified by `abi_version()`, syscall number `0`, returning `0x0001_0000` in `RAX`. The first entry path uses the register convention below. In v1, `RAX` returns a signed 64-bit result: nonnegative values are success (including byte counts and PIDs); errors are negative stable error numbers. ABI versioning is append-only: existing syscall numbers, argument meanings, layouts, and error values never change or get reused. There is no POSIX compatibility claim. `src/syscall.rs` currently implements the stable number/error constants and host-tested decoding of these register-level requests; it does not perform them or install an entry path.

| Number | Call | Register arguments | Result / behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `abi_version` | none | `0x0001_0000` (major 1, minor 0). |
| 1 | `exit` | `RDI`: signed 32-bit status in the low 32 bits (upper bits ignored) | Does not return; status is retained exactly by the parent wait record. |
| 2 | `write` | `RDI`: fd, `RSI`: user buffer, `RDX`: byte length | Returns bytes accepted; a short positive result is valid. Initial descriptors 1 and 2 are stdout/stderr console streams; other descriptors return `-EBADF`. Maximum request is 4096 bytes; zero length returns 0 without validating the pointer. |
| 3 | `wait` | `RDI`: child PID (0 means any child), `RSI`: optional user pointer to signed 32-bit exit status | Blocks until a matching child exits and returns its PID. A non-null status output must be writable before the child is reaped; no matching child returns `-ECHILD`. |

All other numbers are unassigned and return `-ENOSYS`; assigning a number later is an additive extension, never a reinterpretation. Descriptor 0 is reserved for input but v1 has no `read`, `open`, `close`, or `dup` call. Standard descriptors exist for the process lifetime; inheritance and general file-object semantics are not yet exposed. The initial process is created by the kernel loader, not a syscall.

Stable v1 error numbers (returned negated in `RAX`) are: `1 EINVAL`, `2 EBADF`, `3 EFAULT`, `4 ENOMEM`, `5 ECHILD`, `6 EINTR`, `7 EIO`, `8 ENOSYS`, `9 E2BIG`, `10 EOVERFLOW`, and `11 ENOTSUP`. Unknown syscall numbers return `-ENOSYS`. Pointer-plus-length ranges use checked arithmetic and must lie wholly in a mapped lower-half user range. `write` preflights the whole input range before output; a later endpoint failure may return a short count, and an error before progress returns `-EIO`. A copy fault after progress returns the completed prefix; unrecoverable hardware faults remain process-fatal until user-mode exception handling is implemented. `wait` validates its optional output range before blocking and keeps the child waitable if copying the exit status fails. V1 has no signals, asynchronous interruption, or automatic syscall restart; wait is uninterruptible.

All ABI integers are fixed-width little-endian x86_64 values. The wait status is one signed 32-bit integer with no implicit padding or extra fields. No other user-visible structs exist in v1.

## Initial x86_64 entry design (Milestone 4; not implemented)

The first single-vCPU user-mode slice will enter the kernel with `int $0x80` through a dedicated IDT interrupt gate at DPL 3 and return with `IRETQ`. This intentionally avoids `SYSCALL`/`SYSRET`, `STAR`/`LSTAR`/`FMASK`, and `SWAPGS` state transitions in the first userspace path. It is a provisional architecture decision, not a published or implemented syscall ABI.

- **Vector ownership:** `0x80` lies inside the device-vector range (`0x20..=0xef`) and is now reserved by `InterruptVectorAllocator`; generic IRQ allocation/release cannot claim it. The dedicated syscall stub and gate are not installed yet. Install a dedicated syscall stub rather than the generic device-IRQ stub. The gate must be an interrupt gate, so maskable interrupts are disabled on entry before Rust dispatch.
- **Selectors:** the current GDT uses `0x08` for kernel code, `0x10` for kernel data, and `0x18` for the two-slot TSS descriptor. Ring-3 data and 64-bit code descriptors are appended at GDT indexes 5 and 6, with compile-time selector assertions for user data `0x2b` and user code `0x33` (RPL 3); the data selector is loaded into user `SS` on return. They are installed at bootstrap but remain unused until a validated return path exists.
- **Privilege stack:** a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt uses `TSS.RSP0`; it must point to the top of the current process's mapped, writable kernel-entry stack before user execution is resumed. The bootstrap TSS initially points to one static ring-0 stack. `interrupts::set_kernel_entry_stack` validates canonical upper-half address shape and alignment before updating `RSP0`, but no per-process stack is allocated and no scheduler path calls it yet. Callers must disable local interrupts and guarantee the stack is mapped writable in every address space that can run until the next update. A future SMP design needs per-CPU TSS and entry-stack state.
- **Entry frame and state:** the assembly stub must preserve the complete user register state and construct a separately specified syscall frame; it must not assume the existing fatal-exception frame is interchangeable. Kernel code must run with the direction flag clear. Preserve user x87/SSE state across kernel handling; AVX remains disabled under the current CPU-state policy. Do not form Rust references from user pointers.
- **Initial register convention:** `RAX` carries the syscall number; arguments use `RDI`, `RSI`, `RDX`, `R10`, `R8`, and `R9`; `RAX` carries the result. This is only a proposed register convention. It becomes stable only together with ABI version discovery, syscall numbers, errors, and transfer semantics below.
- **Return validation:** use `IRETQ`, not `SYSRET`. Before returning, validate that the saved `CS` and `SS` are exactly the ring-3 selectors, `RIP` and `RSP` are canonical and within the process's executable/code and stack regions respectively, and `RFLAGS` contains no privileged or unsupported bits. Construct a safe flags value rather than echoing user-controlled flags. A malformed frame terminates the process with a reported status; never attempt the return and rely on a ring-0 `#GP` to catch it.
- **NMI and interrupt policy:** no GS-base swap is needed on this entry path. An NMI can still arrive during entry; the current NMI/exception path is fatal-only, and this design does not claim to recover from it. Keep that behavior explicit until user-origin exception/NMI policy is implemented and tested. Ordinary maskable IRQs may resume only after the entry state and scheduler ownership are consistent.

This design depends on a process-owned address space that maps the syscall entry/return code, IDT, GDT, TSS, and the active kernel stack safely. No Ring 3 execution should be enabled until the address-space implementation is reviewed and validated.

### Process address spaces (design; root construction partially implemented)

Use a separate four- or five-level root per process. The initial source is the retained active clone of Limine's hierarchy, not a curated clean-room root. Each process root owns its root page, all lower-half intermediate tables, and every user leaf frame. Keep the kernel-root owner alive for the lifetime of every process root. Copy only upper-half top-level entries from that owner into each process root; these entries are non-owning references to shared kernel subtrees, not deep copies, and must never be released by a process teardown. Do not copy lower-half entries from the kernel root.

Before publishing a shared kernel subtree, validate its page-table structure and physical bounds and reject any effectively user-accessible leaf. U/S permission is the conjunction of every entry on a path, so a U/S bit on one non-leaf alone does not grant user access. When copying upper-half root entries, clear their U/S bit as defense in depth; a user leaf then cannot become accessible if a lower entry changes. `paging::validate_supervisor_kernel_half` implements the bounded, read-only structural/effective-permission preflight, but it does not install roots or prove physical backing is readable; the supplied reader must provide that access guarantee. Sharing the active clone means every accepted upper-half supervisor mapping and alias is present in every process CR3. This is not a curated kernel map or kernel-page-table isolation, and it provides no transient-execution protection. User mappings remain private to one process, are confined to the lower canonical half, preserve W^X, and are non-global in the first implementation.

The kernel address-space owner is the only authority allowed to modify shared upper-half tables. Mutations must be serialized with local interrupts disabled on the current single-vCPU system and invalidate the affected local translation before the mapping change is relied on. A process root may not edit or reclaim shared tables. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::destroy` releases only private user leaves, intermediate tables, and the root; the caller must first switch CR3 to a different live root and invalidate this root's local non-global translations. Keep the shared kernel owner alive. PCID-aware invalidation and SMP shootdown remain unsupported and need a separate design.

The current `CandidatePageTables` deep-clones the inherited hierarchy, tracks all cloned tables as owned, and holds an exclusive mutable borrow of one memory backend; it is not itself the process-address-space abstraction. `SharedKernelHalf` validates and snapshots the sanitized upper root entries while borrowing the kernel owner. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` uses one exclusive backend borrow for multiple private roots, maps allocator-owned user 4 KiB leaves only in inactive lower halves, retains writable/executable permission metadata, validates that an initial instruction pointer is executable and its stack pointer resolves to a writable NX page, offers one-page-bounded range-preflighted copy-in/copy-out through a separate `UserFrameMemory` backend, and destroys private leaf/table/root frames without freeing shared subtrees. The copy helpers are unsafe because the caller must provide kernel buffers that do not alias the process's mapped user frames. Host tests cover four- and five-level sharing, U/S sanitization, independent roots/mappings, initial user-state permission checks, copy permissions and cross-page copies, unmap ownership return, active-root release rejection, and allocation/prepare-failure rollback. The target Limine HHDM `UserFrameMemory` adapter is currently compiled only for the opt-in frame probe; `just frame-smoke` exercises bounded copy, zero-length, and out-of-range behavior on an allocator-owned frame. It is not yet connected to process-root copies. This is still not executable process support: callers must perform CR3 transitions and local TLB invalidation before marking a root inactive; no process scheduler, syscall entry, loader, or fault policy is integrated. Keep the kernel owner alive and immutable for the shared view's lifetime; callers must use a distinct page-table backend for process-owned tables.

### Static ELF64 image validation and page initialization (partial)

`src/elf.rs` parses little-endian x86_64 `ET_EXEC` images without allocation. It bounds the program-header count, load-segment count, and total mapped pages; checks file and virtual arithmetic, page alignment and `p_align` congruence, lower-half canonical ranges, non-overlapping page spans, readable segment flags, W^X, and that the entry point lies in a non-writable executable `PT_LOAD`. It rejects dynamic/interpreter and TLS segments and executable-stack requests. This initial format intentionally requires page-aligned load offsets/addresses and supports at most 64 program headers, 16 load segments, and 64 load pages. `populate_segment_page` copies one load page into an allocator-owned frame through `UserFrameMemory`, zero-filling bytes beyond the file payload. `load_into_process_root` now allocates, populates, selects cache attributes for, and maps every load page into an inactive `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` root. On failure, previously mapped pages remain owned by the root, the failure reports their count, and any unmapped frame is returned to the caller; destroying the newly created root is the recommended cleanup. Boot integration, stack allocation, activation, process lifecycle, and execution are not integrated.

## ABI decisions still pending beyond v1

The initial v1 versioning, error encoding, syscall numbers, and register-level request decoding are implemented in `src/syscall.rs`; pointer/length validation, partial-write behavior, wait status transfer, and no-restart policy are specified but not integrated into a syscall dispatcher. `src/process.rs` adds a host-tested fixed-capacity identity/exit-state policy with parent/child tracking and nonblocking `try_wait`; scheduler blocking, address-space ownership, descriptor tables, and syscall integration remain unimplemented. Still to be specified before adding those operations are process-creation/exec and file-action semantics, general descriptor sharing/duplication/inheritance, read/open/close behavior, signal-like asynchronous delivery, clocks, and any additional structure layouts.

## Suggested first user-visible slice

After address spaces, scheduler, and storage primitives exist, implement a controlled `init` process with a small syscall subset: process exit, read/write through descriptors, open/close, and wait. Add end-to-end tests for invalid pointers, partial transfers, descriptor lifetime, process exit status, and ABI version negotiation before describing it as Unix-compatible.

# Rustix roadmap

This roadmap describes an incremental path from the current bare-metal kernel to a useful Unix-like operating system. It is a dependency plan, not a schedule or a claim of compatibility. Features become current only after the implementation, tests, and exit criteria below agree.

## How to read status

- A checked box means the source/design work exists; it does **not** imply the code compiled, linked, booted, or passed an integration test.
- A milestone is not complete until its stated exit criteria are met and the evidence is recorded.
- Hardware work needs target build and emulator evidence. Host tests cannot validate privileged instructions, bootloader pointers, page tables, device I/O, or exception-entry assembly.
- Future work is intentionally not represented by placeholder APIs or dummy implementations.

## Current status

- **Milestone 0: local exit criteria met from a clean detached worktree; hosted CI observed.** On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 from both the working tree and a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory. On 2026-11-06, GitHub Actions run [#5](https://github.com/JustEthanCodes/rustix/actions/runs/42288095710) completed successfully on `dev` at `770f9c742dd07a00f6b53274ea05a1eca010d146`; its `kernel-and-boot-smoke` job ran `just verify`. This verifies hosted CI on that remote commit, not today’s uncommitted changes.
- **Milestone 1: validation criteria met for the current Limine path.** The bounded boot snapshot, memory-range classification, and CPUID reporting were covered by host tests and QEMU reporting; the Limine pointer-readability trust boundary remains explicit.
- **Milestone 2: local exit criteria met on 2026-10-24; hosted CI observed, physical-hardware validation pending.** The boot path owns and activates a clone of Limine's reachable page-table hierarchy, preserves inherited mappings, hardens kernel HHDM aliases to R/NX or RW/NX while retaining PAT attributes, invalidates stale translations on CR3 transitions, and retains table-frame tokens. `just verify`, `just frame-smoke`, and `just fault-smoke` passed after final review; QEMU exercised the active-PCID/CR3 invalidation path with CR4.PGE clear. The PGE-toggle path is statically reviewed but was not exercised by this QEMU configuration. The successful 2026-11-06 hosted `just verify` run covers the published Milestone 2 state, but not today's uncommitted changes. Broad mapping policy, reclamation, IRQ-safe allocation, and physical-hardware validation remain outside this milestone's completed scope.
- **Milestone 3: single-vCPU exit criteria met locally on 2026-11-13; hosted CI and physical-hardware validation remain pending.** `just verify` passed with 130 host tests, target check/build, BIOS and OVMF boot smokes, active-map/TLB invalidation, IRQ-save lock checks, timer preemption of non-yielding workers with x87/SSE state preservation, cooperative wait/input behavior, and UART/PS/2 IRQ wakeup. SMP and physical-hardware validation remain deferred. See the evidence and limits below. **Milestones 4 and later: planned.** There is no ARM64 platform support, userspace, syscall ABI, persistent filesystem, GUI, or networking stack.

## Dependency path

```text
Reliable boot
    -> validated boot state
    -> owned mappings + frame allocation + heap + fault diagnostics
    -> timer/IRQ model + scheduler + IRQ-safe locking + timer preemption
    -> isolated processes + syscall ABI
    -> M5a PCI/DMA + block I/O + read-only/basic VFS
    -> M5b writable filesystem + permissions + platform services
    -> userland utilities
    -> graphical terminal and other optional services
```

Some device-driver work can proceed in parallel after the core ownership, locking, and testing rules exist. It must not bypass them with direct, unreviewed hardware access.

---

## Milestone 0 — repeatable Rust kernel boot (DONE)

### Implementation present

- [x] `no_std` Rust kernel binary for `x86_64-unknown-none` with its own ELF linker layout and `_start`.
- [x] Limine boot requests and documented external-loader boundary.
- [x] COM1 serial output/input, startup reporting, and panic/fatal halt path.
- [x] Narrow x86 port-I/O helpers and raw non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling.
- [x] `just` tasks for formatting, host tests, target checks, ELF/image builds, and QEMU smoke/run workflows.
- [x] Pinned Limine v12.9.3 binary archive with SHA-256 verification, BIOS/UEFI hybrid image recipe, and CI workflow.
- [x] Separate allocation-free Crabshell parser, kernel serial frontend, and bounded volatile RAM filesystem.

### Validation evidence and remaining proof

- [x] Current source passed formatting, host tests, target check, and optimized build through `just verify`.
- [x] The pinned image built and the bounded QEMU smoke test reached the Crabshell prompt in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 on 2026-10-16.
- [x] A separate interactive QEMU session exercised `help`, `ls`, `meminfo`, directory navigation, and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove operations; `cp` replaced an existing destination, `rmdir` refused a nonempty directory, and unsupported `memtest` was rejected as expected.
- [x] Repeat verification from a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory and uncached build/tool state; fresh Limine download/host-tool compilation, image creation, and QEMU prompt smoke test all passed on 2026-10-16.
- [x] Observe the hosted CI workflow; GitHub Actions run #5 completed successfully on the published `dev` commit on 2026-11-06 (see run #5 above).

The QEMU serial log showed the startup banner, HHDM offset, validated memory-map summary, frame counts, CPUID report, and initial prompt. The interactive command check is a focused manual test, not exhaustive shell coverage or a persistence test. `cat` returned `hello Rustix from QEMU`, `cp` replaced an existing destination with source data, `rmdir` refused a nonempty directory, and `pwd` returned to `/home/rustix` after cleanup. If a future smoke test fails, preserve `target/rustix-qemu-serial.log` as failure evidence.

**Exit criteria:** met locally. A clean detached worktree with uncached build/tool state built the image, reached `_start`, reported the expected startup state, and reached the Crabshell prompt in the automated QEMU test. Hosted CI was also observed passing on the published commit noted above; it does not imply that later uncommitted changes passed CI.

## Milestone 2 — memory ownership, paging, heap, and exceptions (DONE)

This milestone establishes a safe basis for future allocation and kernel services. HHDM access is limited to checked full-frame token paths that rely on Limine's documented contract. The boot path clones the complete reachable inherited hierarchy and activates it only after validating the requested stack span, kernel segments, candidate-root HHDM alias, and kernel-image HHDM permissions.

### Source work present

- [x] Fixed-capacity frame allocator over validated `Usable` ranges, with page alignment, first-MiB reservation, deallocation, coalescing, bounded metadata, and host tests (`src/frame.rs`).
- [x] Initialize allocator metadata from the boot snapshot and expose counts through Crabshell `meminfo`.
- [x] Specify frame-token ownership and failure semantics: `Frame` is non-copyable, failed deallocation returns the token without changing allocator state, and the current API documents (but does not enforce) one allocator instance per physical map.
- [x] Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT and fatal handlers for exception vectors 0–31.
- [x] Give double faults a dedicated IST stack; report saved register/error context and CR2/error bits for page faults.
- [x] Keep maskable IRQ delivery disabled; current exception handling is fatal-only.

### Required memory-management work

- [x] Read `CR4.LA57` and `CPUID.80000008H` when available to report active/max address widths; validate Limine pointers against active canonical width and host-test 48-/57-bit boundaries.
- [x] Document base revision 3 HHDM region coverage, page-boundary behavior, and x86 permissions/cache attributes. HHDM access is limited to opt-in, checked frame and candidate-table probes relying on the protocol contract; there is no general physical-memory service.
- [x] Reject physical map ranges outside the reported CPUID width when available; validate page-rounded HHDM address arithmetic/canonicality for base revision 3 mapped types. This is protocol-derived validation, not a page-table walk or proof of pointer readability.
- [x] Record current transition-critical objects, their mapping sources/permissions, and unresolved bounds in `docs/architecture/memory.md`.
- [x] Capture Limine's executable physical/virtual bases and resolve the complete linker-defined half-open kernel-image span in `BootInfo`; validate the linker/loader base agreement, canonical virtual span, arithmetic, and reported physical width.
- [x] Capture and validate the linker-defined page-aligned text, rodata, and data segment bounds in `BootInfo`; host-test their ordering, contiguity, rounded image coverage, and derived physical ranges. `just verify` reported all three in QEMU on 2026-10-21. This metadata does not prove inherited page-table coverage or live permissions.
- [x] Request a 256 KiB Limine x86_64 stack, require its response, and capture/validate the requested span from entry `RSP`; verify its HHDM translation and `BootloaderReclaimable` backing. `just frame-smoke` walked all 64 pages in QEMU. This request fixed stack-frame overflow in the diagnostic path.
- [x] Record that Limine guarantees at least the requested stack size but does not report the larger allocation's exact bounds or guard status; preserve the requested 256 KiB span and do not infer a guard page.
- [x] Decode the inherited CR3 root address and interpret its low bits using the reported physical-address width and active `CR4.PCIDE` state; host-test reserved-bit and width rejection. `just frame-smoke` reads the root, walks kernel segments and the requested stack span, compares effective PAT/MTRR types for kernel-image/HHDM aliases, and exercises the active-root transition.
- [x] Document the active clone's kernel alias W^X policy, inherited cache behavior, MMIO limits, huge-page splitting, stack bounds, and inherited-root preservation in `docs/architecture/memory.md`.
- [x] Clone every reachable present inherited page-table hierarchy entry into allocator-owned table frames, preserving inherited leaves and non-present entries. Validate kernel segments, the full requested stack span, candidate-root HHDM access, and critical paths; keep the inherited root and backing frames untouched.
- [x] Add pure host-tested 4 KiB mapping-range validation and leaf-PTE bit encoding. Validation requires alignment, checked bounds, known physical width, canonical virtual ranges, and W^X; encoding bounds the physical width and PAT index and requires NXE for non-executable entries. These helpers alone do not prove frame ownership, mapping coverage, or PAT cache semantics, and do not touch tables.
- [x] Implement a bounded candidate-root builder for 4 KiB mappings backed by allocator-issued table and leaf tokens. It requires NXE, uses range-bound PAT attributes, restricts walks to owned tables, and holds a unique mutable backend borrow. Mapping preflights the path and prepares all missing tables before linking them; host tests cover 4-/5-level paths, W^X, ownership rejection, and rollback. An active-state guard prevents candidate mutation/release while CR3 names its root.
- [x] Ensure candidate mapping failure (including frame exhaustion and prepare failure) rolls back partial page-table allocations without changing the active root. Host tests cover rollback and retryable release failure; `just frame-smoke` maps, walks, unmaps, and releases a separate candidate mapping in QEMU.
- [x] Validate and activate the cloned root in QEMU, preserving CR3 low-bit mode, invalidating the active PCID, and flushing global translations when CR4.PGE is enabled; verify the active CR3 plus critical translations after the switch. On failure, restore and verify the inherited root with the same TLB invalidation before releasing the inactive candidate.
- [x] Add host tests for raw PTE-bit encoding and parsing a supplied PAT layout to find WB/UC/WC indexes.
- [x] Read EFER.NXE only when NX is supported and read `IA32_PAT` only when PAT is supported; report these read-only values and recognized PAT indexes at boot.
- [x] Host-test that rejected deallocations preserve free-range state and return the frame token for unaligned, unmanaged, already-free, and range-table-full cases.
- [x] Add a pure host-tested MTRR decoder/resolver for supplied fixed and variable register values, including disabled-MTRR behavior and overlap rules. Host tests and `just verify` passed on 2026-10-21.
- [x] Capture supported MTRR capability, default-type, fixed-range, and variable-range registers read-only at boot. Retain at most 32 variable pairs; report capacity overflow explicitly without a partial snapshot. Host tests cover feature gating, supported fixed/variable register reads, unsupported fixed ranges, and capacity overflow. `just verify` passed on 2026-10-22; the QEMU serial log reported the live MTRR summary.
- [x] Validate captured MTRR capability/default-type bits, register counts and fixed-range availability, WC support, and variable-range mask/alignment; resolve the Intel SDM Table 11-7 PAT/MTRR combinations for one physical address only when `CR0.CD=0` and `CR0.NW=0`. Host tests cover all 30 documented type pairs and malformed inputs. Boot validates the captured PAT/MTRR state and prints a diagnostic resolution at PA 0; `just verify` passed on 2026-10-22. This policy helper does not establish the cache type of an inherited mapping.
- [x] Add a pure range-level PAT selector that returns an index only when it yields the requested effective type across every fixed/variable MTRR transition in the aligned physical range. Host tests cover variable boundaries, fixed-range transitions, no-uniform-index failure, and malformed range inputs. This remains policy-only and does not inspect live PTEs or aliases.
- [x] Compose range-level PAT selection with validated mapping metadata; bind the selected attributes to the physical extent and use them to encode individual 4 KiB leaves. Host tests cover a range crossing variable-MTRR types, width mismatch, and rejecting attributes for a different extent. This does not inspect inherited PTEs, establish frame ownership, or detect cache aliases.
- [x] Calculate HHDM addresses only for allocator-issued frame tokens whose complete page remains in a validated `Usable` region, with known physical width and checked protocol bounds. `just frame-smoke` passed in QEMU: one frame was written, read, cleared, and returned to the allocator. This relies on Limine's base revision 3 HHDM guarantee and does not inspect live PTEs or validate arbitrary physical addresses.
- [x] Validate the inherited CR3 root's numeric HHDM location only when its page lies wholly in a validated `BootloaderReclaimable` region and address-width arithmetic passes. Host tests reject unknown widths and other region types; `just frame-smoke` reads the 512 root entries in QEMU and confirms the HHDM access.
- [x] Add a bounded read-only 4-/5-level page-table walker with synthetic host tests for translations, permissions, PAT selection bits, 2 MiB pages, and absent entries. The opt-in QEMU probe follows every page in linker-defined text/rodata/data spans and the requested stack span, checking translations and effective cache types for kernel-image/HHDM aliases.
- [x] Add host-tested candidate page-table mapping/unmapping and transactional ownership handling; `just frame-smoke` verifies a separate candidate root can map, walk, unmap, and release one frame without changing CR3. The default boot path separately activates an inherited-root clone after critical translation and kernel-alias permission/cache checks.
- [x] Harden kernel-image HHDM aliases before activation: text/rodata become R/NX and data/BSS become RW/NX. Split inherited 1 GiB/2 MiB mappings as needed while preserving translation and PAT bits. Host tests cover both large-page splits; QEMU verifies every kernel-image alias retains its physical translation, desired permissions, and PAT index.
- [x] Add a 256 KiB BSS-backed global heap with 128 allocation records, first-fit aligned placement, exact-layout free/reuse, deterministic arena/metadata exhaustion, and an explicit prohibition on interrupt-context allocation. Host tests cover alignment, reuse, exhaustion, and invalid frees; the QEMU boot probe exercises the global allocator before entering the shell. The arena is fixed and does not grow from physical frames.

### Required exception/descriptor validation

- [x] Source contains GDT/TSS/IDT setup and normalized stubs for architectural exception vectors 0–31; double fault uses IST1.
- [x] Target-assemble/link and inspect the stubs and descriptor setup; ELF disassembly confirms call-stack alignment and the error-code normalization paths, while compile-time size assertions pin the IDT, TSS, and exception-context layouts.
- [x] Add QEMU fault-injection tests for a controlled page fault and invalid opcode. `just fault-smoke` verifies vector diagnostics, the exact CR2 address, no shell prompt or return marker, and that QEMU remains halted until its timeout; it then restores the default release kernel and ISO.
- [x] Boot the descriptor setup and both tested exception paths in QEMU. These checks cover only the injected page fault and invalid opcode, not all vectors or physical hardware.

**Exit criteria:** met locally on 2026-10-24. `just verify`, `just frame-smoke`, and `just fault-smoke` passed after final review, covering host tests, the target build, active cloned-root boot, frame and candidate-map probes, heap behavior, and fatal page-fault/invalid-opcode diagnostics. The QEMU configuration reported CR4.PGE clear and exercised the CR3 reload path; the PGE-toggle global-TLB path is statically reviewed but was not exercised in QEMU. The active hierarchy preserves Limine's complete reachable mapping graph and hardens the kernel-image HHDM aliases; it is not a clean-room address-space policy, does not reclaim the old root or leaf frames, and has no general active mapping service. Hosted CI passed on the published `dev` state on 2026-11-06; physical-hardware validation remains pending, and the hosted run does not cover today's uncommitted changes.
