//! Stable, host-testable decoding for the initial Rustix syscall ABI.
//!
//! This module defines ABI values, validates register-level request shape,
//! sanitizes user return frames, and provides a host-testable bounded write
//! service. It does not install an entry gate or dispatch requests from hardware.

pub const ABI_MAJOR: u16 = 1;
pub const ABI_MINOR: u16 = 0;
pub const ABI_VERSION: u64 = (ABI_MAJOR as u64) << 16 | ABI_MINOR as u64;
pub const MAX_WRITE_BYTES: u64 = 4096;
pub const USER_DATA_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x2b;
pub const USER_CODE_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x33;
pub const SAFE_USER_RFLAGS: u64 = 1 << 1;

const RFLAGS_IOPL: u64 = 3 << 12;
const RFLAGS_NESTED_TASK: u64 = 1 << 14;
const RFLAGS_VIRTUAL_8086: u64 = 1 << 17;

pub mod number {
    pub const ABI_VERSION: u64 = 0;
    pub const EXIT: u64 = 1;
    pub const WRITE: u64 = 2;
    pub const WAIT: u64 = 3;
}

/// Stable v1 error numbers. Syscall returns encode these as negative `i64`s.
#[repr(i64)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum SyscallError {
    InvalidArgument = 1,
    BadFileDescriptor = 2,
    Fault = 3,
    OutOfMemory = 4,
    NoChild = 5,
    Interrupted = 6,
    Io = 7,
    NoSys = 8,
    TooBig = 9,
    Overflow = 10,
    NotSupported = 11,
}

impl SyscallError {
    pub const fn return_value(self) -> i64 {
        -(self as i64)
    }
}

/// The six argument registers reserved by the x86_64 v1 calling convention.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct SyscallArguments {
    pub rdi: u64,
    pub rsi: u64,
    pub rdx: u64,
    pub r10: u64,
    pub r8: u64,
    pub r9: u64,
}

/// The five-word privilege-return frame consumed by `IRETQ` in long mode.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct UserIretFrame {
    pub instruction_pointer: u64,
    pub code_selector: u64,
    pub flags: u64,
    pub stack_pointer: u64,
    pub stack_selector: u64,
}

/// A user return frame with validated selectors/addresses and kernel-chosen flags.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct ValidatedUserIretFrame(UserIretFrame);

impl ValidatedUserIretFrame {
    pub const fn into_raw(self) -> UserIretFrame {
        self.0
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserIretFrameError {
    InvalidAddressWidth,
    InvalidSelectors,
    InvalidFlags,
    InvalidInstructionPointer,
    InvalidStackPointer,
}

/// Validate the privilege-sensitive portion of an `IRETQ` frame and replace
/// user-supplied flags with a conservative kernel-selected value.
///
/// The safe flags deliberately leave IF clear until a process-aware interrupt
/// scheduler is installed. The caller must separately verify that RIP names an
/// executable process mapping and RSP names a writable stack mapping.
pub fn sanitize_user_iret_frame(
    frame: UserIretFrame,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<ValidatedUserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidAddressWidth);
    }
    if frame.code_selector != u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR)
        || frame.stack_selector != u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR)
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidSelectors);
    }
    if frame.flags & (1 << 1) == 0
        || frame.flags & (RFLAGS_IOPL | RFLAGS_NESTED_TASK | RFLAGS_VIRTUAL_8086) != 0
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidFlags);
    }

    let lower_half_end = 1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1);
    if frame.instruction_pointer >= lower_half_end
        || !crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(
            frame.instruction_pointer,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidInstructionPointer);
    }
    let stack_last = frame
        .stack_pointer
        .checked_sub(1)
        .filter(|address| *address < lower_half_end)
        .filter(|address| {
            crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(*address, virtual_address_bits)
        });
    if stack_last.is_none() || frame.stack_pointer & 0xf != 0 {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidStackPointer);
    }

    Ok(ValidatedUserIretFrame(UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: frame.instruction_pointer,
        code_selector: u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR),
        flags: SAFE_USER_RFLAGS,
        stack_pointer: frame.stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR),
    }))
}

/// A syscall whose number and register-level arguments have been decoded.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum SyscallRequest {
    AbiVersion,
    Exit {
        status: i32,
    },
    Write {
        fd: u64,
        user_buffer: u64,
        length: usize,
    },
    Wait {
        child_pid: u64,
        status_address: Option<u64>,
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ConsoleStream {
    Stdout,
    Stderr,
}

/// The kernel-side sink for the v1 console descriptors.
pub trait ConsoleOutput {
    type Error;

    fn write(&mut self, stream: ConsoleStream, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, Self::Error>;
}

/// Copy and write one bounded v1 user buffer through a process root.
///
/// The complete user range is preflighted by `copy_from_user` before output.
/// If the frame backend faults after copying a prefix, that prefix is still
/// offered to the console and a positive short write is returned when accepted.
///
/// # Safety
/// The current kernel stack, including this function's fixed scratch buffer,
/// must not be mapped as a user frame in `process`. The boot allocator enforces
/// this by excluding the kernel image and bootstrap-stack spans from usable
/// frame allocation; future kernel stacks must preserve the same invariant.
pub unsafe fn write_user_buffer<M, U, O>(
    roots: &crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
    process: crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
    fd: u64,
    user_buffer: u64,
    length: usize,
    user_memory: &mut U,
    output: &mut O,
) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>
where
    M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory,
    U: crate::paging::UserFrameMemory,
    O: ConsoleOutput,
{
    use crate::paging::{ProcessUserCopyError, MAX_PROCESS_USER_COPY_BYTES};

    let stream = match fd {
        1 => ConsoleStream::Stdout,
        2 => ConsoleStream::Stderr,
        _ => return Err(SyscallError::BadFileDescriptor),
    };
    if length > MAX_WRITE_BYTES as usize {
        return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
    }
    if length == 0 {
        return Ok(0);
    }

    let mut scratch = [0; MAX_PROCESS_USER_COPY_BYTES];
    let copied = match unsafe {
        roots.copy_from_user(process, user_buffer, &mut scratch[..length], user_memory)
    } {
        Ok(copied) if copied <= length => copied,
        Ok(_) => return Err(SyscallError::Fault),
        Err(failure) if failure.transferred > 0 && failure.transferred <= length => {
            failure.transferred
        }
        Err(failure) => {
            return Err(match failure.cause {
                ProcessUserCopyError::LengthTooLarge => SyscallError::TooBig,
                ProcessUserCopyError::Memory(_) => SyscallError::Io,
                ProcessUserCopyError::InvalidHandle
                | ProcessUserCopyError::Releasing
                | ProcessUserCopyError::InvalidRange
                | ProcessUserCopyError::Unmapped
                | ProcessUserCopyError::PermissionDenied => SyscallError::Fault,
            });
        }
    };
    if copied == 0 {
        return Err(SyscallError::Io);
    }

    let written = output
        .write(stream, &scratch[..copied])
        .map_err(|_| SyscallError::Io)?;
    if written == 0 || written > copied {
        return Err(SyscallError::Io);
    }
    Ok(written)
}

/// Decode a v1 syscall number and its register arguments without touching user memory.
///
/// The exit status uses the low 32 bits of RDI, interpreted as a signed value.
/// A zero-length write preserves the supplied pointer without validating it; the
/// eventual syscall implementation must return zero before inspecting that pointer.
pub const fn decode_syscall(
    syscall_number: u64,
    arguments: SyscallArguments,
) -> Result<SyscallRequest, SyscallError> {
    match syscall_number {
        number::ABI_VERSION => Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion),
        number::EXIT => Ok(SyscallRequest::Exit {
            status: arguments.rdi as u32 as i32,
        }),
        number::WRITE => {
            if arguments.rdx > MAX_WRITE_BYTES {
                return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
            }
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Write {
                fd: arguments.rdi,
                user_buffer: arguments.rsi,
                length: arguments.rdx as usize,
            })
        }
        number::WAIT => Ok(SyscallRequest::Wait {
            child_pid: arguments.rdi,
            status_address: if arguments.rsi == 0 {
                None
            } else {
                Some(arguments.rsi)
            },
        }),
        _ => Err(SyscallError::NoSys),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{
        decode_syscall, number, sanitize_user_iret_frame, SyscallArguments, SyscallError,
        SyscallRequest, UserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError, ABI_VERSION, MAX_WRITE_BYTES,
        SAFE_USER_RFLAGS, USER_CODE_SELECTOR, USER_DATA_SELECTOR,
    };

    const EMPTY_ARGUMENTS: SyscallArguments = SyscallArguments {
        rdi: 0,
        rsi: 0,
        rdx: 0,
        r10: 0,
        r8: 0,
        r9: 0,
    };

    fn valid_iret_frame() -> UserIretFrame {
        UserIretFrame {
            instruction_pointer: 0x4000_0000,
            code_selector: u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR),
            flags: 0x202,
            stack_pointer: 0x7fff_fff0,
            stack_selector: u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn abi_version_and_syscall_numbers_are_stable() {
        assert_eq!(ABI_VERSION, 0x0001_0000);
        assert_eq!(number::ABI_VERSION, 0);
        assert_eq!(number::EXIT, 1);
        assert_eq!(number::WRITE, 2);
        assert_eq!(number::WAIT, 3);
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::ABI_VERSION, EMPTY_ARGUMENTS),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn error_numbers_encode_as_negative_i64_results() {
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::InvalidArgument.return_value(), -1);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::BadFileDescriptor.return_value(), -2);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::Fault.return_value(), -3);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::OutOfMemory.return_value(), -4);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::NoChild.return_value(), -5);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::Interrupted.return_value(), -6);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::Io.return_value(), -7);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::NoSys.return_value(), -8);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::TooBig.return_value(), -9);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::Overflow.return_value(), -10);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::NotSupported.return_value(), -11);
    }

    #[test]
    fn exit_status_is_the_signed_low_32_bits_of_rdi() {
        let arguments = SyscallArguments {
            rdi: 0xfeed_beef_ffff_fffe,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::EXIT, arguments),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Exit { status: -2 })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_decoding_accepts_zero_and_maximum_lengths_without_pointer_access() {
        let zero_length = SyscallArguments {
            rdi: 1,
            rsi: u64::MAX,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::WRITE, zero_length),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Write {
                fd: 1,
                user_buffer: u64::MAX,
                length: 0,
            })
        );

        let maximum = SyscallArguments {
            rdi: 2,
            rsi: 0x4000,
            rdx: MAX_WRITE_BYTES,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::WRITE, maximum),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Write {
                fd: 2,
                user_buffer: 0x4000,
                length: MAX_WRITE_BYTES as usize,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_larger_than_the_v1_limit_is_rejected() {
        let arguments = SyscallArguments {
            rdx: MAX_WRITE_BYTES + 1,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::WRITE, arguments),
            Err(SyscallError::TooBig)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn wait_decoding_distinguishes_optional_status_pointer() {
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::WAIT, EMPTY_ARGUMENTS),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Wait {
                child_pid: 0,
                status_address: None,
            })
        );

        let arguments = SyscallArguments {
            rdi: 42,
            rsi: 0x7000,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::WAIT, arguments),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Wait {
                child_pid: 42,
                status_address: Some(0x7000),
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn user_iret_frame_checks_selectors_addresses_and_sanitizes_flags() {
        let mut frame = valid_iret_frame();
        let sanitized = sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48).unwrap().into_raw();
        assert_eq!(sanitized.instruction_pointer, frame.instruction_pointer);
        assert_eq!(sanitized.code_selector, u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR));
        assert_eq!(sanitized.stack_selector, u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR));
        assert_eq!(sanitized.flags, SAFE_USER_RFLAGS);
        assert_eq!(sanitized.stack_pointer, frame.stack_pointer);

        frame.code_selector = 0x08;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidSelectors)
        );
        frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.stack_selector = 0x10;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidSelectors)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn user_iret_frame_rejects_bad_flags_and_non_user_addresses() {
        let mut frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.flags |= 3 << 12;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidFlags)
        );
        frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.flags &= !(1 << 1);
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidFlags)
        );
        frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.instruction_pointer = 1 << 47;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidInstructionPointer)
        );
        frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.stack_pointer = 0x7fff_fff8;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidStackPointer)
        );
        frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.stack_pointer = 0x0000_8000_0000_0000;
        assert!(sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48).is_ok());
        frame.stack_pointer += 16;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidStackPointer)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(valid_iret_frame(), 52),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidAddressWidth)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn unassigned_numbers_return_enosys() {
        assert_eq!(decode_syscall(4, EMPTY_ARGUMENTS), Err(SyscallError::NoSys));
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(u64::MAX, EMPTY_ARGUMENTS),
            Err(SyscallError::NoSys)
        );
    }
}

//! Bounded, allocation-free ACPI structure validation and MADT parsing.
//!
//! Parsers consume byte slices, and bounded table traversal uses an explicit
//! platform reader contract. This module never maps or dereferences physical
//! addresses and does not initialize APICs.

pub const MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE: usize = 64 * 1024;
const RSDP_V1_SIZE: usize = 20;
const RSDP_V2_MIN_SIZE: usize = 36;
const SDT_HEADER_SIZE: usize = 36;
const MADT_FIXED_SIZE: usize = 44;
const MAX_MADT_ENTRIES: usize = 256;
pub const MAX_ACPI_ROOT_ENTRIES: usize = 1024;
const MAX_LOCAL_APICS: usize = 16;
const MAX_IO_APICS: usize = 8;
const MAX_INTERRUPT_OVERRIDES: usize = 16;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AcpiError {
    StructureTooShort,
    StructureTooLarge,
    InvalidRsdpSignature,
    InvalidRsdpChecksum,
    InvalidExtendedRsdpLength,
    InvalidExtendedRsdpChecksum,
    UnsupportedRsdpRevision(u8),
    InvalidSdtLength,
    InvalidSdtChecksum,
    NotRootPointerTable,
    InvalidRootPointerTableLength,
    TooManyRootPointers,
    NullRootPointer,
    NotMadt,
    InvalidMadtLength,
    InvalidMadtEntryLength,
    TooManyMadtEntries,
    MadtCapacityExceeded,
    UnsupportedMadtEntryType(u8),
    InvalidLocalApicFlags,
    DuplicateLocalApic,
    InvalidIoApicAddress,
    DuplicateIoApicId,
    InvalidInterruptOverrideFlags,
    DuplicateInterruptOverride,
    InvalidLocalApicAddress,
    DuplicateLocalApicAddressOverride,
}

/// Physical-memory access supplied by the platform-specific ACPI integration.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// Implementations of `read` must validate every requested physical extent
/// against ACPI table memory-map metadata before reading it. `read_rsdp` may
/// additionally support the bounded legacy x86 reserved firmware window for
/// the RSDP itself; it must not extend that exception to root or child tables.
/// Both methods must copy only from checked, read-only, non-executable mappings,
/// ensure the complete extent is readable, and initialize all of `output` before
/// returning `Ok`. This module never creates mappings or dereferences physical
/// addresses itself.
pub unsafe trait AcpiPhysicalReader {
    type Error;

    fn read(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error>;

    fn read_rsdp(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        self.read(physical_start, output)
    }
}

/// Failure while traversing ACPI tables from a physical RSDP address.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AcpiReadError<E> {
    Reader(E),
    Parse(AcpiError),
    InvalidPhysicalExtent,
    ZeroRootPointer,
    MissingMadt,
}

/// Validated root-system-description pointer fields copied out of the ACPI bytes.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Rsdp {
    pub revision: u8,
    pub rsdt_address: u32,
    pub xsdt_address: Option<u64>,
}

impl Rsdp {
    /// Validate an RSDP byte slice and copy its table addresses.
    ///
    /// ACPI 1.0 (revision 0) structures use the 20-byte legacy checksum. ACPI
    /// 2.0+ structures must include and pass the extended checksum.
    pub fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, AcpiError> {
        if bytes.len() < RSDP_V1_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::StructureTooShort);
        }
        if bytes[..8] != *b"RSD PTR " {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidRsdpSignature);
        }
        if !checksum_is_valid(&bytes[..RSDP_V1_SIZE]) {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidRsdpChecksum);
        }

        let revision = bytes[15];
        let rsdt_address = read_u32(bytes, 16);
        if revision == 0 {
            return Ok(Self {
                revision,
                rsdt_address,
                xsdt_address: None,
            });
        }
        if revision < 2 {
            return Err(AcpiError::UnsupportedRsdpRevision(revision));
        }
        if bytes.len() < RSDP_V2_MIN_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::StructureTooShort);
        }

        let length = read_u32(bytes, 20) as usize;
        if !(RSDP_V2_MIN_SIZE..=MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE).contains(&length) || length > bytes.len() {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidExtendedRsdpLength);
        }
        if !checksum_is_valid(&bytes[..length]) {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidExtendedRsdpChecksum);
        }

        Ok(Self {
            revision,
            rsdt_address,
            xsdt_address: Some(read_u64(bytes, 24)),
        })
    }
}

/// A system-description table whose advertised length and checksum were checked.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Sdt<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    pub signature: [u8; 4],
    pub revision: u8,
}

impl<'a> Sdt<'a> {
    /// Validate an SDT header, bounded length, and checksum.
    ///
    /// Bytes following the advertised table length are ignored. The caller must
    /// still ensure that the complete advertised table is in the supplied slice.
    pub fn parse(bytes: &'a [u8]) -> Result<Self, AcpiError> {
        if bytes.len() < SDT_HEADER_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::StructureTooShort);
        }
        let length = read_u32(bytes, 4) as usize;
        if length < SDT_HEADER_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidSdtLength);
        }
        if length > MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::StructureTooLarge);
        }
        if length > bytes.len() {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidSdtLength);
        }
        if !checksum_is_valid(&bytes[..length]) {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidSdtChecksum);
        }

        Ok(Self {
            bytes: &bytes[..length],
            signature: [bytes[0], bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3]],
            revision: bytes[8],
        })
    }

    pub const fn length(&self) -> usize {
        self.bytes.len()
    }

    pub fn root_pointer_table(self) -> Result<RootPointerTable<'a>, AcpiError> {
        RootPointerTable::parse(self)
    }
}

/// Bounded, zero-allocation view of an ACPI RSDT or XSDT address array.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RootPointerTable<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    entry_width: usize,
    entry_count: usize,
}

impl<'a> RootPointerTable<'a> {
    pub fn parse(table: Sdt<'a>) -> Result<Self, AcpiError> {
        let entry_width = match table.signature {
            [b'R', b'S', b'D', b'T'] => 4,
            [b'X', b'S', b'D', b'T'] => 8,
            _ => return Err(AcpiError::NotRootPointerTable),
        };
        let payload_length = table.bytes.len() - SDT_HEADER_SIZE;
        if !payload_length.is_multiple_of(entry_width) {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidRootPointerTableLength);
        }
        let entry_count = payload_length / entry_width;
        if entry_count > MAX_ACPI_ROOT_ENTRIES {
            return Err(AcpiError::TooManyRootPointers);
        }
        let pointers = &table.bytes[SDT_HEADER_SIZE..];
        for index in 0..entry_count {
            let offset = index * entry_width;
            let address = if entry_width == 4 {
                read_u32(pointers, offset) as u64
            } else {
                read_u64(pointers, offset)
            };
            if address == 0 {
                return Err(AcpiError::NullRootPointer);
            }
        }
        Ok(Self {
            bytes: pointers,
            entry_width,
            entry_count,
        })
    }

    pub const fn is_xsdt(&self) -> bool {
        self.entry_width == 8
    }

    pub const fn entry_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.entry_count
    }

    pub fn address_at(&self, index: usize) -> Option<u64> {
        if index >= self.entry_count {
            return None;
        }
        let offset = index.checked_mul(self.entry_width)?;
        Some(if self.entry_width == 4 {
            read_u32(self.bytes, offset) as u64
        } else {
            read_u64(self.bytes, offset)
        })
    }
}

/// Read, validate, and parse the MADT reachable from a physical RSDP address.
///
/// The caller provides fixed-size scratch storage; no allocation or physical
/// mapping is performed here. Root tables are limited by
/// [`MAX_ACPI_ROOT_ENTRIES`], and each individual ACPI structure is limited by
/// [`MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE`].
pub fn read_madt<R: AcpiPhysicalReader>(
    reader: &mut R,
    rsdp_physical: u64,
    scratch: &mut [u8; MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE],
) -> Result<Madt, AcpiReadError<R::Error>> {
    read_rsdp(reader, rsdp_physical, &mut scratch[..RSDP_V1_SIZE])?;
    let revision = scratch[15];
    let rsdp = if revision >= 2 {
        read_rsdp(reader, rsdp_physical, &mut scratch[..RSDP_V2_MIN_SIZE])?;
        let advertised_length = read_u32(scratch, 20) as usize;
        if !(RSDP_V2_MIN_SIZE..=MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE).contains(&advertised_length) {
            return Err(AcpiReadError::Parse(AcpiError::InvalidExtendedRsdpLength));
        }
        read_rsdp(reader, rsdp_physical, &mut scratch[..advertised_length])?;
        Rsdp::parse(&scratch[..advertised_length]).map_err(AcpiReadError::Parse)?
    } else {
        Rsdp::parse(&scratch[..RSDP_V1_SIZE]).map_err(AcpiReadError::Parse)?
    };

    let (root_physical, expect_xsdt) = match rsdp.xsdt_address {
        Some(address) if address != 0 => (address, true),
        _ if rsdp.rsdt_address != 0 => (u64::from(rsdp.rsdt_address), false),
        _ => return Err(AcpiReadError::ZeroRootPointer),
    };

    read_physical(reader, root_physical, &mut scratch[..SDT_HEADER_SIZE])?;
    let root_length = checked_sdt_length(scratch)?;
    read_physical(reader, root_physical, &mut scratch[..root_length])?;
    let root_sdt = Sdt::parse(&scratch[..root_length]).map_err(AcpiReadError::Parse)?;
    let root_table = root_sdt
        .root_pointer_table()
        .map_err(AcpiReadError::Parse)?;
    if root_table.is_xsdt() != expect_xsdt {
        return Err(AcpiReadError::Parse(AcpiError::NotRootPointerTable));
    }

    let mut child_addresses = [0u64; MAX_ACPI_ROOT_ENTRIES];
    let child_count = root_table.entry_count();
    for (index, address) in child_addresses[..child_count].iter_mut().enumerate() {
        *address = root_table.address_at(index).ok_or(AcpiReadError::Parse(
            AcpiError::InvalidRootPointerTableLength,
        ))?;
    }

    for child_physical in child_addresses[..child_count].iter().copied() {
        read_physical(reader, child_physical, &mut scratch[..SDT_HEADER_SIZE])?;
        if scratch[..4] != *b"APIC" {
            continue;
        }
        let child_length = checked_sdt_length(scratch)?;
        read_physical(reader, child_physical, &mut scratch[..child_length])?;
        let child_sdt = Sdt::parse(&scratch[..child_length]).map_err(AcpiReadError::Parse)?;
        return Madt::parse(child_sdt).map_err(AcpiReadError::Parse);
    }

    Err(AcpiReadError::MissingMadt)
}

fn read_rsdp<R: AcpiPhysicalReader>(
    reader: &mut R,
    physical_start: u64,
    output: &mut [u8],
) -> Result<(), AcpiReadError<R::Error>> {
    let length = u64::try_from(output.len()).map_err(|_| AcpiReadError::InvalidPhysicalExtent)?;
    physical_start
        .checked_add(length)
        .ok_or(AcpiReadError::InvalidPhysicalExtent)?;
    reader
        .read_rsdp(physical_start, output)
        .map_err(AcpiReadError::Reader)
}

fn read_physical<R: AcpiPhysicalReader>(
    reader: &mut R,
    physical_start: u64,
    output: &mut [u8],
) -> Result<(), AcpiReadError<R::Error>> {
    let length = u64::try_from(output.len()).map_err(|_| AcpiReadError::InvalidPhysicalExtent)?;
    physical_start
        .checked_add(length)
        .ok_or(AcpiReadError::InvalidPhysicalExtent)?;
    reader
        .read(physical_start, output)
        .map_err(AcpiReadError::Reader)
}

fn checked_sdt_length<E>(header: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, AcpiReadError<E>> {
    if header.len() < SDT_HEADER_SIZE {
        return Err(AcpiReadError::Parse(AcpiError::StructureTooShort));
    }
    let length = read_u32(header, 4) as usize;
    if length < SDT_HEADER_SIZE {
        return Err(AcpiReadError::Parse(AcpiError::InvalidSdtLength));
    }
    if length > MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE {
        return Err(AcpiReadError::Parse(AcpiError::StructureTooLarge));
    }
    Ok(length)
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct LocalApic {
    pub processor_uid: u8,
    pub apic_id: u8,
    pub flags: u32,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct IoApic {
    pub apic_id: u8,
    pub physical_address: u32,
    pub global_system_interrupt_base: u32,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct InterruptSourceOverride {
    pub bus: u8,
    pub source: u8,
    pub global_system_interrupt: u32,
    pub flags: u16,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum InterruptPolarity {
    ActiveHigh,
    ActiveLow,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum InterruptTrigger {
    Edge,
    Level,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ResolvedIsaInterrupt {
    pub source: u8,
    pub global_system_interrupt: u32,
    pub polarity: InterruptPolarity,
    pub trigger: InterruptTrigger,
}

/// Fixed-capacity, copied data from an xAPIC-compatible MADT.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Madt {
    pub local_apic_address: u64,
    pub flags: u32,
    local_apics: [Option<LocalApic>; MAX_LOCAL_APICS],
    local_apic_count: usize,
    io_apics: [Option<IoApic>; MAX_IO_APICS],
    io_apic_count: usize,
    interrupt_overrides: [Option<InterruptSourceOverride>; MAX_INTERRUPT_OVERRIDES],
    interrupt_override_count: usize,
}

impl Madt {
    /// Parse the known xAPIC MADT records into bounded owned arrays.
    ///
    /// Unknown record types are skipped after validating their common header.
    /// x2APIC processor records are rejected because this parser does not yet
    /// establish x2APIC mode or destination-ID policy.
    pub fn parse(table: Sdt<'_>) -> Result<Self, AcpiError> {
        if table.signature != *b"APIC" {
            return Err(AcpiError::NotMadt);
        }
        if table.bytes.len() < MADT_FIXED_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidMadtLength);
        }

        let mut madt = Self {
            local_apic_address: read_u32(table.bytes, SDT_HEADER_SIZE) as u64,
            flags: read_u32(table.bytes, SDT_HEADER_SIZE + 4),
            local_apics: [None; MAX_LOCAL_APICS],
            local_apic_count: 0,
            io_apics: [None; MAX_IO_APICS],
            io_apic_count: 0,
            interrupt_overrides: [None; MAX_INTERRUPT_OVERRIDES],
            interrupt_override_count: 0,
        };

        let mut local_apic_address_override_seen = false;
        let mut offset = MADT_FIXED_SIZE;
        let mut entry_count = 0;
        while offset < table.bytes.len() {
            if table.bytes.len() - offset < 2 {
                return Err(AcpiError::InvalidMadtEntryLength);
            }
            let entry_type = table.bytes[offset];
            let entry_length = table.bytes[offset + 1] as usize;
            if entry_length < 2 || entry_length > table.bytes.len() - offset {
                return Err(AcpiError::InvalidMadtEntryLength);
            }
            entry_count += 1;
            if entry_count > MAX_MADT_ENTRIES {
                return Err(AcpiError::TooManyMadtEntries);
            }

            let entry = &table.bytes[offset..offset + entry_length];
            match entry_type {
                0 => {
                    require_entry_length(entry_length, 8)?;
                    let processor_uid = entry[2];
                    let apic_id = entry[3];
                    let flags = read_u32(entry, 4);
                    if flags & !0x3 != 0 {
                        return Err(AcpiError::InvalidLocalApicFlags);
                    }
                    if madt
                        .local_apics()
                        .any(|cpu| cpu.processor_uid == processor_uid || cpu.apic_id == apic_id)
                    {
                        return Err(AcpiError::DuplicateLocalApic);
                    }
                    push(
                        &mut madt.local_apics,
                        &mut madt.local_apic_count,
                        LocalApic {
                            processor_uid,
                            apic_id,
                            flags,
                        },
                    )?;
                }
                1 => {
                    require_entry_length(entry_length, 12)?;
                    let apic_id = entry[2];
                    let physical_address = read_u32(entry, 4);
                    if physical_address == 0 || physical_address & 0xfff != 0 {
                        return Err(AcpiError::InvalidIoApicAddress);
                    }
                    if madt.io_apics().any(|io_apic| io_apic.apic_id == apic_id) {
                        return Err(AcpiError::DuplicateIoApicId);
                    }
                    push(
                        &mut madt.io_apics,
                        &mut madt.io_apic_count,
                        IoApic {
                            apic_id,
                            physical_address,
                            global_system_interrupt_base: read_u32(entry, 8),
                        },
                    )?;
                }
                2 => {
                    require_entry_length(entry_length, 10)?;
                    let bus = entry[2];
                    let source = entry[3];
                    let flags = read_u16(entry, 8);
                    if flags & !0x000f != 0 || flags & 0x3 == 0x2 || (flags >> 2) & 0x3 == 0x2 {
                        return Err(AcpiError::InvalidInterruptOverrideFlags);
                    }
                    if madt.interrupt_overrides().any(|override_entry| {
                        override_entry.bus == bus && override_entry.source == source
                    }) {
                        return Err(AcpiError::DuplicateInterruptOverride);
                    }
                    push(
                        &mut madt.interrupt_overrides,
                        &mut madt.interrupt_override_count,
                        InterruptSourceOverride {
                            bus,
                            source,
                            global_system_interrupt: read_u32(entry, 4),
                            flags,
                        },
                    )?;
                }
                5 => {
                    require_entry_length(entry_length, 12)?;
                    if local_apic_address_override_seen {
                        return Err(AcpiError::DuplicateLocalApicAddressOverride);
                    }
                    local_apic_address_override_seen = true;
                    madt.local_apic_address = read_u64(entry, 4);
                }
                9 => return Err(AcpiError::UnsupportedMadtEntryType(entry_type)),
                _ => {}
            }
            offset += entry_length;
        }
        if madt.local_apic_address == 0 || madt.local_apic_address & 0xfff != 0 {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidLocalApicAddress);
        }

        Ok(madt)
    }

    pub fn local_apics(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = LocalApic> + '_ {
        self.local_apics[..self.local_apic_count]
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|entry| *entry)
    }

    pub fn io_apics(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = IoApic> + '_ {
        self.io_apics[..self.io_apic_count]
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|entry| *entry)
    }

    pub fn interrupt_overrides(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = InterruptSourceOverride> + '_ {
        self.interrupt_overrides[..self.interrupt_override_count]
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|entry| *entry)
    }

    /// Resolve an ISA IRQ source using its MADT override or ISA defaults.
    /// Conforming ISA flags default to active-high, edge-triggered delivery.
    pub fn resolve_isa_interrupt(&self, source: u8) -> ResolvedIsaInterrupt {
        let override_entry = self
            .interrupt_overrides()
            .find(|entry| entry.bus == 0 && entry.source == source);
        let (global_system_interrupt, flags) = override_entry
            .map(|entry| (entry.global_system_interrupt, entry.flags))
            .unwrap_or((u32::from(source), 0));
        let polarity = match flags & 0x3 {
            3 => InterruptPolarity::ActiveLow,
            _ => InterruptPolarity::ActiveHigh,
        };
        let trigger = match (flags >> 2) & 0x3 {
            3 => InterruptTrigger::Level,
            _ => InterruptTrigger::Edge,
        };
        ResolvedIsaInterrupt {
            source,
            global_system_interrupt,
            polarity,
            trigger,
        }
    }
}

fn require_entry_length(actual: usize, expected: usize) -> Result<(), AcpiError> {
    if actual == expected {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(AcpiError::InvalidMadtEntryLength)
    }
}

fn push<T: Copy, const N: usize>(
    entries: &mut [Option<T>; N],
    count: &mut usize,
    value: T,
) -> Result<(), AcpiError> {
    let Some(slot) = entries.get_mut(*count) else {
        return Err(AcpiError::MadtCapacityExceeded);
    };
    *slot = Some(value);
    *count += 1;
    Ok(())
}

fn checksum_is_valid(bytes: &[u8]) -> bool {
    bytes.iter().fold(0u8, |sum, byte| sum.wrapping_add(*byte)) == 0
}

fn read_u16(bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> u16 {
    u16::from_le_bytes([bytes[offset], bytes[offset + 1]])
}

fn read_u32(bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::from_le_bytes([
        bytes[offset],
        bytes[offset + 1],
        bytes[offset + 2],
        bytes[offset + 3],
    ])
}

fn read_u64(bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> u64 {
    u64::from_le_bytes([
        bytes[offset],
        bytes[offset + 1],
        bytes[offset + 2],
        bytes[offset + 3],
        bytes[offset + 4],
        bytes[offset + 5],
        bytes[offset + 6],
        bytes[offset + 7],
    ])
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{
        read_madt, AcpiError, AcpiPhysicalReader, AcpiReadError, Madt, Rsdp, Sdt,
        MAX_ACPI_ROOT_ENTRIES, MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE, RSDP_V1_SIZE,
    };
    use core::assert_eq;
    extern crate std;

    fn set_checksum(bytes: &mut [u8], checksum_offset: usize, covered_length: usize) {
        bytes[checksum_offset] = 0;
        let sum = bytes[..covered_length]
            .iter()
            .fold(0u8, |sum, byte| sum.wrapping_add(*byte));
        bytes[checksum_offset] = 0u8.wrapping_sub(sum);
    }

    fn make_sdt(signature: [u8; 4], body: &[u8]) -> std::vec::Vec<u8> {
        let length = 36 + body.len();
        let mut bytes = std::vec![0; length];
        bytes[..4].copy_from_slice(&signature);
        bytes[4..8].copy_from_slice(&(length as u32).to_le_bytes());
        bytes[8] = 1;
        bytes[10..16].copy_from_slice(b"RUSTIX");
        bytes[16..24].copy_from_slice(b"RUSTIX01");
        bytes[24..28].copy_from_slice(&1u32.to_le_bytes());
        bytes[28..32].copy_from_slice(b"RUST");
        bytes[32..36].copy_from_slice(&1u32.to_le_bytes());
        bytes[36..].copy_from_slice(body);
        set_checksum(&mut bytes, 9, length);
        bytes
    }

    #[derive(Default)]
    struct FakeReader {
        regions: std::vec::Vec<(u64, std::vec::Vec<u8>)>,
        fail_address: Option<u64>,
    }

    impl FakeReader {
        fn add_region(&mut self, address: u64, bytes: std::vec::Vec<u8>) {
            self.regions.push((address, bytes));
        }
    }

    // The fixture regions stand in for memory-map-validated, readable ACPI extents.
    unsafe impl AcpiPhysicalReader for FakeReader {
        type Error = &'static str;

        fn read(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
            if self.fail_address == Some(physical_start) {
                return Err("injected read failure");
            }
            for (base, bytes) in &self.regions {
                let Some(offset) = physical_start.checked_sub(*base) else {
                    continue;
                };
                let Ok(offset) = usize::try_from(offset) else {
                    continue;
                };
                let Some(end) = offset.checked_add(output.len()) else {
                    continue;
                };
                if end <= bytes.len() {
                    output.copy_from_slice(&bytes[offset..end]);
                    return Ok(());
                }
            }
            Err("unmapped fixture address")
        }
    }

    fn make_rsdp(root_address: u64, xsdt: bool) -> std::vec::Vec<u8> {
        if xsdt {
            let mut bytes = std::vec![0; 36];
            bytes[..8].copy_from_slice(b"RSD PTR ");
            bytes[9..15].copy_from_slice(b"RUSTIX");
            bytes[15] = 2;
            bytes[16..20].copy_from_slice(&0x7000u32.to_le_bytes());
            bytes[20..24].copy_from_slice(&36u32.to_le_bytes());
            bytes[24..32].copy_from_slice(&root_address.to_le_bytes());
            set_checksum(&mut bytes, 8, RSDP_V1_SIZE);
            let length = bytes.len();
            set_checksum(&mut bytes, 32, length);
            bytes
        } else {
            let mut bytes = std::vec![0; RSDP_V1_SIZE];
            bytes[..8].copy_from_slice(b"RSD PTR ");
            bytes[9..15].copy_from_slice(b"RUSTIX");
            bytes[16..20].copy_from_slice(&(root_address as u32).to_le_bytes());
            set_checksum(&mut bytes, 8, RSDP_V1_SIZE);
            bytes
        }
    }

    fn traversal_fixture(xsdt: bool, child_signature: [u8; 4]) -> FakeReader {
        let rsdp_address = 0x1000;
        let root_address = if xsdt { 0x2_0000_0000 } else { 0x2000 };
        let child_address = 0x3000;
        let mut child_body = std::vec![0; 8];
        child_body[..4].copy_from_slice(&0xfee0_0000u32.to_le_bytes());
        let child = make_sdt(child_signature, &child_body);
        let root_body = if xsdt {
            root_address_entry_u64(child_address)
        } else {
            root_address_entry_u32(child_address)
        };
        let root = make_sdt(if xsdt { *b"XSDT" } else { *b"RSDT" }, &root_body);

        let mut reader = FakeReader::default();
        reader.add_region(rsdp_address, make_rsdp(root_address, xsdt));
        reader.add_region(root_address, root);
        reader.add_region(child_address, child);
        reader
    }

    fn root_address_entry_u32(address: u64) -> std::vec::Vec<u8> {
        (address as u32).to_le_bytes().to_vec()
    }

    fn root_address_entry_u64(address: u64) -> std::vec::Vec<u8> {
        address.to_le_bytes().to_vec()
    }

    #[test]
    fn traverses_rsdt_and_xsdt_to_madt() {
        for xsdt in [false, true] {
            let mut reader = traversal_fixture(xsdt, *b"APIC");
            let mut scratch = [0; MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE];
            let madt = read_madt(&mut reader, 0x1000, &mut scratch).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(madt.local_apic_address, 0xfee0_0000);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_madt_traversal_failures() {
        let mut reader = traversal_fixture(false, *b"APIC");
        reader.regions[2].1[9] ^= 1;
        let mut scratch = [0; MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE];
        assert_eq!(
            read_madt(&mut reader, 0x1000, &mut scratch),
            Err(AcpiReadError::Parse(AcpiError::InvalidSdtChecksum))
        );

        let mut reader = traversal_fixture(true, *b"SSDT");
        assert_eq!(
            read_madt(&mut reader, 0x1000, &mut scratch),
            Err(AcpiReadError::MissingMadt)
        );

        let mut reader = traversal_fixture(false, *b"APIC");
        reader.fail_address = Some(0x2000);
        assert_eq!(
            read_madt(&mut reader, 0x1000, &mut scratch),
            Err(AcpiReadError::Reader("injected read failure"))
        );

        let mut reader = FakeReader::default();
        assert_eq!(
            read_madt(&mut reader, u64::MAX - 10, &mut scratch),
            Err(AcpiReadError::InvalidPhysicalExtent)
        );

        reader.add_region(0x1000, make_rsdp(0, false));
        assert_eq!(
            read_madt(&mut reader, 0x1000, &mut scratch),
            Err(AcpiReadError::ZeroRootPointer)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_and_checksums_acpi_10_rsdp() {
        let mut bytes = [0u8; 20];
        bytes[..8].copy_from_slice(b"RSD PTR ");
        bytes[9..15].copy_from_slice(b"RUSTIX");
        bytes[15] = 0;
        bytes[16..20].copy_from_slice(&0x1234_5000u32.to_le_bytes());
        set_checksum(&mut bytes, 8, RSDP_V1_SIZE);

        assert_eq!(
            Rsdp::parse(&bytes),
            Ok(Rsdp {
                revision: 0,
                rsdt_address: 0x1234_5000,
                xsdt_address: None,
            })
        );
        bytes[10] ^= 1;
        assert_eq!(Rsdp::parse(&bytes), Err(AcpiError::InvalidRsdpChecksum));
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_extended_rsdp_length_and_checksum() {
        let mut bytes = [0u8; 36];
        bytes[..8].copy_from_slice(b"RSD PTR ");
        bytes[9..15].copy_from_slice(b"RUSTIX");
        bytes[15] = 2;
        bytes[16..20].copy_from_slice(&0x1234_5000u32.to_le_bytes());
        bytes[20..24].copy_from_slice(&36u32.to_le_bytes());
        bytes[24..32].copy_from_slice(&0x1234_5678_9000u64.to_le_bytes());
        set_checksum(&mut bytes, 8, RSDP_V1_SIZE);
        set_checksum(&mut bytes, 32, 36);

        assert_eq!(
            Rsdp::parse(&bytes),
            Ok(Rsdp {
                revision: 2,
                rsdt_address: 0x1234_5000,
                xsdt_address: Some(0x1234_5678_9000),
            })
        );
        bytes[20..24].copy_from_slice(&(MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE as u32 + 1).to_le_bytes());
        assert_eq!(
            Rsdp::parse(&bytes),
            Err(AcpiError::InvalidExtendedRsdpLength)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_sdt_length_and_checksum() {
        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"TEST", &[1, 2, 3]);
        let table = Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(table.signature, *b"TEST");
        assert_eq!(table.length(), 39);

        let mut corrupt = bytes;
        corrupt[36] ^= 1;
        assert_eq!(Sdt::parse(&corrupt), Err(AcpiError::InvalidSdtChecksum));
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_bounded_rsdt_and_xsdt_pointer_arrays() {
        let mut rsdt_body = std::vec::Vec::new();
        rsdt_body.extend_from_slice(&0x1234_5000u32.to_le_bytes());
        rsdt_body.extend_from_slice(&0x2345_6000u32.to_le_bytes());
        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"RSDT", &rsdt_body);
        let pointers = Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap().root_pointer_table().unwrap();
        assert!(!pointers.is_xsdt());
        assert_eq!(pointers.entry_count(), 2);
        assert_eq!(pointers.address_at(0), Some(0x1234_5000));
        assert_eq!(pointers.address_at(1), Some(0x2345_6000));
        assert_eq!(pointers.address_at(2), None);

        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"XSDT", &0x1_2345_6000u64.to_le_bytes());
        let pointers = Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap().root_pointer_table().unwrap();
        assert!(pointers.is_xsdt());
        assert_eq!(pointers.address_at(0), Some(0x1_2345_6000));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_malformed_rsdt_xsdt_pointers_and_capacity_overflow() {
        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"RSDT", &[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]);
        assert_eq!(
            Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap().root_pointer_table(),
            Err(AcpiError::InvalidRootPointerTableLength)
        );

        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"XSDT", &0u64.to_le_bytes());
        assert_eq!(
            Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap().root_pointer_table(),
            Err(AcpiError::NullRootPointer)
        );

        let mut pointers = std::vec![0x1000u32; MAX_ACPI_ROOT_ENTRIES + 1];
        let body = pointers
            .drain(..)
            .flat_map(u32::to_le_bytes)
            .collect::<std::vec::Vec<_>>();
        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"RSDT", &body);
        assert_eq!(
            Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap().root_pointer_table(),
            Err(AcpiError::TooManyRootPointers)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_madt_devices_overrides_and_address_override() {
        let mut body = std::vec![0; 8];
        body[0..4].copy_from_slice(&0xfee0_0000u32.to_le_bytes());
        body[4..8].copy_from_slice(&1u32.to_le_bytes());

//! Fixed-capacity physical frame allocator built from validated memory regions.
//!
//! This module assigns physical frame addresses only. It does not map or access
//! them, and it never promotes loader- or firmware-reclaimable memory to free RAM.

use crate::memory::{HhdmAddressError, MemoryMap, RegionKind, MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS};

/// The current x86_64 base page size used by Rustix.
pub const FRAME_SIZE: u64 = 4096;
/// Keep the first MiB unavailable even if a loader labels it usable.
pub const LOW_MEMORY_RESERVED_END: u64 = 0x10_0000;
/// Maximum number of disjoint ranges kept in each fixed range table.
pub const MAX_FRAME_RANGES: usize = MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS;

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Frame(u64);

impl Frame {
    /// Physical address of the beginning of this frame.
    pub const fn address(&self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }

    /// Calculate this owned frame's Limine HHDM address from validated metadata.
    ///
    /// This returns a numeric address only. Dereferencing it still relies on the
    /// Limine base-revision-3 HHDM guarantee and a narrow unsafe access boundary.
    pub fn hhdm_address(
        &self,
        memory_map: &MemoryMap,
        hhdm_offset: u64,
        physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
        virtual_address_bits: u8,
    ) -> Result<u64, HhdmAddressError> {
        memory_map.usable_hhdm_address(
            hhdm_offset,
            self.0,
            FRAME_SIZE,
            physical_address_bits,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    #[cfg(test)]
    const fn from_address(address: u64) -> Self {
        Self(address)
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FrameError {
    RangeTableFull,
    RangeOverlap,
    UnalignedFrame,
    NotManaged,
    AlreadyFree,
    AccountingOverflow,
    /// A half-open exclusion span was empty, inverted, or exceeded the
    /// supported exclusion count.
    InvalidExclusion,
}

/// A rejected deallocation that returns ownership of the frame to the caller.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct DeallocationError {
    pub error: FrameError,
    pub frame: Frame,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct FrameRange {
    start: u64,
    end: u64,
}

impl FrameRange {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self { start: 0, end: 0 };
}

/// A bounded allocator over only validated `Usable` memory-map ranges.
///
/// For a given physical map, callers must use only one allocator instance as
/// the allocation authority; the type does not enforce this uniqueness. Within
/// that instance, each eligible frame is owned by the allocator while free, or
/// by the non-copyable `Frame` token returned by `allocate` while allocated. A
/// frame address is an identifier only; this allocator does not map or access it.
/// Both range tables are sorted, disjoint, page-aligned half-open ranges. The
/// allocator returns `None` on frame exhaustion and reports metadata exhaustion
/// explicitly without changing state or consuming the caller's frame token.
pub struct FrameAllocator {
    managed: [FrameRange; MAX_FRAME_RANGES],
    managed_count: usize,
    free: [FrameRange; MAX_FRAME_RANGES],
    free_count: usize,
    managed_frames: u64,
    free_frames: u64,
}

impl FrameAllocator {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        managed: [FrameRange::EMPTY; MAX_FRAME_RANGES],
        managed_count: 0,
        free: [FrameRange::EMPTY; MAX_FRAME_RANGES],
        free_count: 0,
        managed_frames: 0,
        free_frames: 0,
    };

    /// Build allocator metadata without allocating or touching physical memory.
    ///
    /// The caller must ensure there is only one allocator instance per physical
    /// map; constructing multiple instances would duplicate allocation authority.
    pub fn from_memory_map(map: &MemoryMap) -> Result<Self, FrameError> {
        Self::from_memory_map_excluding(map, &[])
    }

    /// Build allocator metadata like [`Self::from_memory_map`], additionally
    /// excluding half-open physical spans that must never be handed out as free
    /// frames.
    ///
    /// This exists to defend the kernel against a loader that mislabels
    /// kernel-owned pages (for example the kernel image or the boot stack) as
    /// `Usable`; such spans are subtracted from every otherwise-usable region
    /// before frames are accounted. Up to seven exclusions are supported;
    /// each must satisfy `start < end` with checked arithmetic.
    pub fn from_memory_map_excluding(
        map: &MemoryMap,
        exclusions: &[(u64, u64)],
    ) -> Result<Self, FrameError> {
        const MAX_EXCLUSIONS: usize = 7;
        const MAX_PIECES: usize = MAX_EXCLUSIONS + 1;

        if exclusions.len() > MAX_EXCLUSIONS {
            return Err(FrameError::RangeTableFull);
        }
        for &(start, end) in exclusions {
            if start >= end {
                return Err(FrameError::InvalidExclusion);
            }
        }

        let mut allocator = Self::EMPTY;
        let page_mask = !(FRAME_SIZE - 1);

        for region in map.regions() {
            if region.kind() != RegionKind::Usable {
                continue;
            }

            let region_start = region.start().max(LOW_MEMORY_RESERVED_END);
            let region_end = region.end();

            let mut pieces = [(0u64, 0u64); MAX_PIECES];
            pieces[0] = (region_start, region_end);
            let mut piece_count = 1usize;
            for &(exclusion_start, exclusion_end) in exclusions {
                let mut next = [(0u64, 0u64); MAX_PIECES];
                let mut next_count = 0usize;
                for &(piece_start, piece_end) in pieces.iter().take(piece_count) {
                    if exclusion_end <= piece_start || exclusion_start >= piece_end {
                        next[next_count] = (piece_start, piece_end);
                        next_count += 1;
                        continue;
                    }
                    if piece_start < exclusion_start && next_count < MAX_PIECES {
                        next[next_count] = (piece_start, exclusion_start);
                        next_count += 1;
                    }
                    if exclusion_end < piece_end && next_count < MAX_PIECES {
                        next[next_count] = (exclusion_end, piece_end);
                        next_count += 1;
                    }
                }
                pieces[..next_count].copy_from_slice(&next[..next_count]);
                piece_count = next_count;
            }

            for &(piece_start, piece_end) in pieces.iter().take(piece_count) {
                let Some(start) = piece_start
                    .checked_add(FRAME_SIZE - 1)
                    .map(|address| address & page_mask)
                else {
                    continue;
                };
                let end = piece_end & page_mask;
                if start >= end {
                    continue;
                }

                let range = FrameRange { start, end };
                Self::insert_range(&mut allocator.managed, &mut allocator.managed_count, range)?;
                Self::insert_range(&mut allocator.free, &mut allocator.free_count, range)?;

                let frames = (end - start) / FRAME_SIZE;
                allocator.managed_frames = allocator
                    .managed_frames
                    .checked_add(frames)
                    .ok_or(FrameError::AccountingOverflow)?;
                allocator.free_frames = allocator
                    .free_frames
                    .checked_add(frames)
                    .ok_or(FrameError::AccountingOverflow)?;
            }
        }

        Ok(allocator)
    }

    /// Number of complete frames inside eligible usable regions.
    pub const fn managed_frames(&self) -> u64 {
        self.managed_frames
    }

    /// Number of currently unallocated frames.
    pub const fn free_frames(&self) -> u64 {
        self.free_frames
    }

    /// Allocate the lowest-address available frame, or return `None` on exhaustion.
    pub fn allocate(&mut self) -> Option<Frame> {
        if self.free_count == 0 {
            return None;
        }

        let address = self.free[0].start;
        self.free[0].start += FRAME_SIZE;
        debug_assert!(self.free_frames > 0);
        self.free_frames = self.free_frames.saturating_sub(1);
        if self.free[0].start == self.free[0].end {
            Self::remove_range(&mut self.free, &mut self.free_count, 0);
        }
        Some(Frame(address))
    }

    /// Return a frame to the allocator, merging adjacent free ranges.
    ///
    /// On error, the returned `DeallocationError` retains the frame token so the
    /// caller can retry or otherwise preserve ownership. Failed returns do not
    /// change allocator state.
    pub fn deallocate(&mut self, frame: Frame) -> Result<(), DeallocationError> {
        let address = frame.address();
        if address & (FRAME_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
            return Err(DeallocationError {
                error: FrameError::UnalignedFrame,
                frame,
            });
        }
        let Some(end) = address.checked_add(FRAME_SIZE) else {
            return Err(DeallocationError {
                error: FrameError::NotManaged,
                frame,
            });
        };
        if !self
            .managed
            .iter()
            .take(self.managed_count)
            .any(|range| range.start <= address && end <= range.end)
        {
            return Err(DeallocationError {
                error: FrameError::NotManaged,
                frame,
            });
        }
        if self
            .free
            .iter()
            .take(self.free_count)
            .any(|range| address < range.end && range.start < end)
        {
            return Err(DeallocationError {
                error: FrameError::AlreadyFree,
                frame,
            });
        }

        let Some(new_free_count) = self.free_frames.checked_add(1) else {
            return Err(DeallocationError {
                error: FrameError::AccountingOverflow,
                frame,
            });
        };
        if let Err(error) = Self::insert_range(
            &mut self.free,
            &mut self.free_count,
            FrameRange {
                start: address,
                end,
            },
        ) {
            return Err(DeallocationError { error, frame });
        }
        self.free_frames = new_free_count;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn insert_range(
        ranges: &mut [FrameRange; MAX_FRAME_RANGES],
        count: &mut usize,
        incoming: FrameRange,
    ) -> Result<(), FrameError> {
        let mut index = 0;
        while index < *count && ranges[index].start < incoming.start {
            index += 1;
        }

        if (index > 0 && ranges[index - 1].end > incoming.start)
            || (index < *count && incoming.end > ranges[index].start)
        {
            return Err(FrameError::RangeOverlap);
        }

        let joins_previous = index > 0 && ranges[index - 1].end == incoming.start;
        let joins_next = index < *count && incoming.end == ranges[index].start;
        match (joins_previous, joins_next) {
            (true, true) => {
                ranges[index - 1].end = ranges[index].end;
                Self::remove_range(ranges, count, index);
            }
            (true, false) => ranges[index - 1].end = incoming.end,
            (false, true) => ranges[index].start = incoming.start,
            (false, false) => {
                if *count == MAX_FRAME_RANGES {
                    return Err(FrameError::RangeTableFull);
                }
                for move_index in (index..*count).rev() {
                    ranges[move_index + 1] = ranges[move_index];
                }
                ranges[index] = incoming;
                *count += 1;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn remove_range(ranges: &mut [FrameRange; MAX_FRAME_RANGES], count: &mut usize, index: usize) {
        for move_index in index..(*count - 1) {
            ranges[move_index] = ranges[move_index + 1];
        }
        debug_assert!(*count > 0);
        *count -= 1;
        ranges[*count] = FrameRange::EMPTY;
    }
}

        let neighbor = core::mem::replace(
            &mut allocated[MAX_FRAME_RANGES * 2 - 1],
            Frame::from_address(0),
        );
        allocator.deallocate(neighbor).unwrap();
        allocator.deallocate(rejected.unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), MAX_FRAME_RANGES as u64 + 2);
    }

//! A bounded kernel heap with a static bootstrap arena and optional frame-backed growth.
//!
//! The bootstrap arena is 256 KiB and tracks at most 128 allocations. An optional
//! extension maps pages on demand inside a caller-reserved virtual range, with
//! its own fixed allocation table and a caller-supplied transactional mapper.
//! Growth is bounded; allocation fails when either arena or metadata is full.
//!
//! The global wrapper serializes access with an IRQ-save spin lock. The lock
//! prevents a local interrupt from re-entering a held allocator lock; allocation
//! remains forbidden in IRQ/exception context to keep handlers bounded and
//! allocation-free.

use crate::sync::{IrqSpinLock, IrqSpinLockGuard};
use core::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout};
use core::cell::UnsafeCell;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

/// Fixed capacity of the initial BSS-backed kernel heap.
pub const KERNEL_HEAP_CAPACITY: usize = 256 * 1024;
/// Maximum number of live allocations tracked by the initial kernel heap.
pub const KERNEL_HEAP_MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize = 128;

/// The statically allocated heap type used by the kernel binary.
pub type KernelHeap = LockedHeap<KERNEL_HEAP_CAPACITY, KERNEL_HEAP_MAX_ALLOCATIONS>;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum HeapError {
    ZeroSizedAllocation,
    AllocationTableFull,
    OutOfMemory,
    AddressOverflow,
    InvalidPointer,
    LayoutMismatch,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Allocation {
    start: usize,
    size: usize,
    alignment: usize,
}

struct FixedHeap<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> {
    arena: [u8; HEAP_SIZE],
    allocations: [Option<Allocation>; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
}

impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> FixedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS> {
    const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            arena: [0; HEAP_SIZE],
            allocations: [None; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
        }
    }

    fn allocate(&mut self, layout: Layout) -> Result<NonNull<u8>, HeapError> {
        if layout.size() == 0 {
            return Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation);
        }
        let slot = self
            .allocations
            .iter()
            .position(Option::is_none)
            .ok_or(HeapError::AllocationTableFull)?;
        let start = self.find_gap(layout)?;
        self.allocations[slot] = Some(Allocation {
            start,
            size: layout.size(),
            alignment: layout.align(),
        });

        let pointer = self.arena.as_mut_ptr().wrapping_add(start);
        NonNull::new(pointer).ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)
    }

    fn deallocate(&mut self, pointer: NonNull<u8>, layout: Layout) -> Result<(), HeapError> {
        if layout.size() == 0 {
            return Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation);
        }
        let arena_start = self.arena.as_ptr() as usize;
        let allocation_start = (pointer.as_ptr() as usize)
            .checked_sub(arena_start)
            .filter(|offset| *offset < HEAP_SIZE)
            .ok_or(HeapError::InvalidPointer)?;

        for allocation in &mut self.allocations {
            let Some(active) = *allocation else {
                continue;
            };
            if active.start != allocation_start {
                continue;
            }
            if active.size != layout.size() || active.alignment != layout.align() {
                return Err(HeapError::LayoutMismatch);
            }
            *allocation = None;
            return Ok(());
        }
        Err(HeapError::InvalidPointer)
    }

    fn find_gap(&self, layout: Layout) -> Result<usize, HeapError> {
        let arena_start = self.arena.as_ptr() as usize;
        let mut candidate = 0usize;

        loop {
            let candidate_address = arena_start
                .checked_add(candidate)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let aligned_address = candidate_address
                .checked_add(layout.align() - 1)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?
                & !(layout.align() - 1);
            let start = aligned_address
                .checked_sub(arena_start)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let end = start
                .checked_add(layout.size())
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            if end > HEAP_SIZE {
                return Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory);
            }

            let mut conflicting_end = None;
            for allocation in self.allocations.iter().flatten() {
                let allocation_end = allocation
                    .start
                    .checked_add(allocation.size)
                    .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
                if start < allocation_end && allocation.start < end {
                    conflicting_end = Some(
                        conflicting_end
                            .map_or(allocation_end, |end: usize| end.max(allocation_end)),
                    );
                }
            }

            match conflicting_end {
                Some(end) => candidate = end,
                None => return Ok(start),
            }
        }
    }
}

pub type HeapPageMapper = unsafe fn(context: *mut (), first_page: usize, page_count: usize) -> bool;

struct FrameBackedHeap<const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> {
    base: usize,
    capacity_pages: usize,
    mapped_pages: usize,
    allocations: [Option<Allocation>; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
    context: *mut (),
    map_pages: Option<HeapPageMapper>,
}

impl<const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> FrameBackedHeap<MAX_ALLOCATIONS> {
    const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            base: 0,
            capacity_pages: 0,
            mapped_pages: 0,
            allocations: [None; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
            context: core::ptr::null_mut(),
            map_pages: None,

    }

        capacity_pages: usize,
        context: *mut (),
        map_pages: HeapPageMapper,

            .checked_mul(PAGE_BYTES)
            .and_then(|bytes| base.checked_add(bytes));

            || !base.is_multiple_of(PAGE_BYTES)

/// Errors reported while installing the optional frame-backed heap region.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FrameHeapInitError {
    InvalidRange,
    AlreadyConfigured,
}

/// A `GlobalAlloc` wrapper for the fixed bootstrap arena and bounded growth region.
///
/// The bootstrap arena and callback context must remain at stable addresses for
/// the lifetime of allocations. The growth callback must map the complete page
/// range transactionally and must not allocate or call this heap recursively.
pub struct LockedHeap<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> {
    lock: IrqSpinLock<()>,
    heap: UnsafeCell<FixedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>>,
    growth: UnsafeCell<FrameBackedHeap<MAX_ALLOCATIONS>>,
}

// SAFETY: `heap` and `growth` are accessed mutably only while the IRQ-save
// spin lock is held. Allocation remains prohibited in interrupt context.
unsafe impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> Sync
    for LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>
{
}

impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS> {
    /// Construct an empty allocator. The backing arena is zero-initialized BSS.
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            lock: IrqSpinLock::new(()),
            heap: UnsafeCell::new(FixedHeap::new()),
            growth: UnsafeCell::new(FrameBackedHeap::new()),
        }
    }

    /// Configure one reserved virtual range for demand-mapped heap growth.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The caller must reserve the complete range exclusively, keep `context`
    /// alive and stable until the allocator is no longer used, and provide a
    /// mapper that atomically maps all requested pages or leaves the range
    /// unchanged. The mapper must not allocate or re-enter this allocator.
    pub unsafe fn initialize_frame_backed_region(
        &self,
        base: usize,
        capacity_pages: usize,
        context: *mut (),
        map_pages: HeapPageMapper,
    ) -> Result<(), FrameHeapInitError> {
        let _lock = self.acquire();
        // SAFETY: The lock grants exclusive access to the growth configuration.
        let growth = unsafe { &mut *self.growth.get() };
        growth.configure(base, capacity_pages, context, map_pages)
    }

    fn acquire(&self) -> IrqSpinLockGuard<'_, ()> {
        self.lock.lock()
    }
}

impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> Default
    for LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>
{
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

unsafe impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> GlobalAlloc
    for LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>
{
    unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        // Allocation from interrupt/exception context can deadlock the only
        // CPU with IF masked; the allocator contract forbids it. Enforced in
        // debug builds; release builds document the contract instead.
        debug_assert!(
            crate::sync::INTERRUPT_DEPTH.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) == 0,
            "kernel heap allocation from interrupt/exception context"
        );
        let _lock = self.acquire();
        // SAFETY: The lock grants exclusive access to both allocator regions.
        let heap = unsafe { &mut *self.heap.get() };
        // SAFETY: The same lock exclusively protects the growth metadata and
        // callback configuration. Its mapper contract forbids allocator reentry.
        let growth = unsafe { &mut *self.growth.get() };
        heap.allocate(layout)
            .or_else(|_| growth.allocate(layout))
            .map(NonNull::as_ptr)
            .unwrap_or(core::ptr::null_mut())
    }

    unsafe fn dealloc(&self, pointer: *mut u8, layout: Layout) {
        let Some(pointer) = NonNull::new(pointer) else {
            return;
        };
        let _lock = self.acquire();
        // SAFETY: The lock grants exclusive access to both allocator regions. The
        // GlobalAlloc caller must provide a live allocation and its original layout.
        let heap = unsafe { &mut *self.heap.get() };
        // SAFETY: The same lock exclusively protects growth allocation metadata.
        let growth = unsafe { &mut *self.growth.get() };
        if growth.contains_pointer(pointer.as_ptr() as usize) {
            let result = growth.deallocate(pointer, layout);
            debug_assert!(
                result.is_ok(),
                "frame-backed dealloc failed; possible double-free or layout mismatch"
            );
        } else {
            let result = heap.deallocate(pointer, layout);
            debug_assert!(
                result.is_ok(),
                "arena dealloc failed; possible double-free or layout mismatch"
            );
        }
    }
}

        unsafe { allocation.as_ptr().write_bytes(0xa5, layout.size()) };

            assert_eq!(unsafe { allocation.as_ptr().add(index).read() }, 0xa5);
        }

        let reused = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(reused, allocation);
        heap.deallocate(reused, layout).unwrap();
    }

        let first = heap.allocate(full_layout).unwrap();
        let second = heap.allocate(full_layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            heap.allocate(Layout::from_size_align(1, 1).unwrap()),
            Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory)
        );

        heap.deallocate(first, full_layout).unwrap();
        let smaller_layout = Layout::from_size_align(32, 1).unwrap();
        let reused = heap.allocate(smaller_layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(reused, first);
        heap.deallocate(reused, smaller_layout).unwrap();

        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(8, 1).unwrap();
        let allocation = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(heap.allocate(layout), Err(HeapError::AllocationTableFull));
        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();

use rustix_kernel::paging::{capture_mtrr_registers, MtrrState};

const IA32_PAT: u32 = 0x0000_0277;

const CR0_EM: u64 = 1 << 2;
const CR0_TS: u64 = 1 << 3;
const CR0_NE: u64 = 1 << 5;
const CR4_PGE: u64 = 1 << 7;
const CR4_OSFXSR: u64 = 1 << 9;
const CR4_OSXMMEXCPT: u64 = 1 << 10;
const CR4_OSXSAVE: u64 = 1 << 18;

    MissingX87,

    MissingSse2,

/// Enable the x87/SSE state required by the x86_64 kernel ABI and FXSAVE contexts.
///
/// AVX/XSAVE state is intentionally disabled; any future target feature change
/// must extend the context-switch save format before it can be enabled.
pub fn initialize_fpu_state() -> Result<(), CpuStateError> {
    let features = __cpuid(1).edx;
    if features & (1 << 0) == 0 {
        return Err(CpuStateError::MissingX87);
    }
    if features & (1 << 24) == 0 {
        return Err(CpuStateError::MissingFxsave);
    }
    if features & (1 << 25) == 0 {
        return Err(CpuStateError::MissingSse);
    }
    if features & (1 << 26) == 0 {
        return Err(CpuStateError::MissingSse2);
    }

    let cr0 = (read_cr0_raw() | CR0_MP | CR0_NE) & !(CR0_EM | CR0_TS);
    // SAFETY: This only enables the architectural x87 state and native error
    // reporting, clearing EM/TS so the kernel can use its required FP state.
    unsafe { write_cr0_raw(cr0) };

    let cr4 = (read_cr4_raw() | CR4_OSFXSR | CR4_OSXMMEXCPT) & !CR4_OSXSAVE;
    // SAFETY: Preserve all existing CR4 controls except enabling OS support for
    // FXSAVE/SSE and disabling XSAVE/AVX until that state is explicitly managed.
    unsafe { write_cr4_raw(cr4) };
    Ok(())
}

pub fn identify() -> CpuInfo {
    // CPUID is part of the x86_64 architectural baseline.
    let basic = __cpuid(0);
    let mut vendor = [0; 12];
    vendor[0..4].copy_from_slice(&basic.ebx.to_le_bytes());
    vendor[4..8].copy_from_slice(&basic.edx.to_le_bytes());
    vendor[8..12].copy_from_slice(&basic.ecx.to_le_bytes());

    let basic_features = if basic.eax >= 1 {
        Some(__cpuid(1))
    } else {
        None
    };
    let extended = __cpuid(0x8000_0000);
    let extended_features = if extended.eax >= 0x8000_0001 {
        Some(__cpuid(0x8000_0001))
    } else {
        None
    };
    let structured_features = if basic.eax >= 7 {
        Some(__cpuid_count(7, 0))
    } else {
        None
    };
    let address_widths = if extended.eax >= 0x8000_0008 {
        Some(__cpuid(0x8000_0008).eax)
    } else {
        None
    };
    let cr0 = read_cr0_raw();
    let cr4 = read_cr4_raw();
    let has_nx = extended_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 20) != 0);
    let nx_enabled = if has_nx {
        // SAFETY: EFER is available in x86_64 long mode; CPUID confirms NX support,
        // and this boot-time code executes at CPL 0. The read does not change state.
        unsafe { read_msr(IA32_EFER) & EFER_NXE != 0 }
    } else {
        false
    };
    let has_pat = basic_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 16) != 0);
    let pat_msr_value = if has_pat {
        // SAFETY: CPUID reports PAT support and boot-time kernel code runs at CPL 0.
        Some(unsafe { read_msr(IA32_PAT) })
    } else {
        None
    };
    let has_mtrr = basic_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 12) != 0);
    let mtrr = capture_mtrr_registers(has_mtrr, |index| {
        // SAFETY: CPUID reports MTRR support; the capture helper only requests
        // architectural MTRR MSRs after that feature check.
        unsafe { read_msr(index) }
    });

    CpuInfo {
        vendor,
        max_basic_leaf: basic.eax,
        max_extended_leaf: extended.eax,
        has_sse2: basic_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 26) != 0),
        has_nx,
        nx_enabled,
        normal_caching: cr0 & ((1 << 30) | (1 << 29)) == 0,
        has_pat,
        pat_msr_value,
        mtrr,
        has_1g_pages: extended_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 26) != 0),
        has_long_mode: extended_features.is_some_and(|features| features.edx & (1 << 29) != 0),
        has_la57: structured_features.is_some_and(|features| features.ecx & (1 << 16) != 0),
        physical_address_bits: address_widths.map(|eax| (eax & 0xff) as u8),
        max_linear_address_bits: address_widths.map(|eax| ((eax >> 8) & 0xff) as u8),
        active_linear_address_bits: if cr4 & (1 << 12) != 0 { 57 } else { 48 },
        pcid_enabled: cr4 & (1 << 17) != 0,
    }
}

///
/// Callers must separately verify that the CPU and platform support xAPIC.
pub fn bootstrap_apic_id() -> u8 {
    (__cpuid(1).ebx >> 24) as u8
}

/// Read the current raw CR3 value without changing page-table state.
pub fn read_cr3_raw() -> u64 {
    let cr3: u64;
    // SAFETY: Rustix runs at CPL 0; reading CR3 is privileged but non-mutating.
    unsafe { asm!("mov {}, cr3", out(reg) cr3, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
    cr3

/// Install a pre-validated CR3 value.
///
/// # Safety
/// The root must name a complete, valid page-table hierarchy that preserves the
/// current instruction, stack, data, exception, and HHDM mappings. Paging mode
/// and address-width controls must already match the hierarchy, and interrupts
/// must remain disabled during the transition.
pub unsafe fn write_cr3_raw(value: u64) {

    unsafe { asm!("mov cr3, {}", in(reg) value, options(nostack, preserves_flags)) };
}

/// Replace CR3 while invalidating global translations when CR4.PGE is enabled.
///
/// Returns whether PGE was toggled. With PGE clear, the CR3 write still
/// invalidates the active PCID (or all non-global translations when PCID is
/// disabled); global translations cannot be retained while PGE is clear.
///
/// # Safety
/// `value` must satisfy [`write_cr3_raw`]'s safety requirements, and interrupts
/// must remain disabled until the target root and translations are verified.
pub unsafe fn write_cr3_with_global_flush(value: u64) -> bool {
    let cr4 = read_cr4_raw();
    if cr4 & CR4_PGE == 0 {
        // SAFETY: The caller supplies the same validated root required by
        // `write_cr3_raw`; with PGE already clear there are no global entries.
        unsafe { write_cr3_raw(value) };
        return false;
    }

    // A 1-to-0 PGE transition invalidates cached global translations. Keep PGE
    // clear across the CR3 write so the target context starts without stale
    // global translations, then restore the original control-register state.
    // SAFETY: Only CR4.PGE is modified, and the original value is restored.
    unsafe { write_cr4_raw(cr4 & !CR4_PGE) };
