            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_translation.physical_address != physical
            || hhdm_translation.physical_address != physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias probe failed: {} physical {:#018x} has inconsistent translations",
                label,
                physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        let kernel_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            kernel_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            hhdm_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_type != hhdm_type {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias conflict: {} PA {:#018x}, kernel {:?} vs HHDM {:?}",
                label,
                physical,
                kernel_type,
                hhdm_type
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    kprintln!(
        "cache-alias probe passed: {} ({} pages; effective types match)",
        label,
        pages
    );
}

fn release_probe_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!(
            "HHDM frame probe failed to return its frame: {:?}",
            error.error
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-page-fault")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately reads an unmapped
    // low virtual address; the installed page-fault handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov rax, 0xdeadbeef",
            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack)
        );
    }
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-invalid-opcode")]
fn run_fault_injection() {

    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately raises #UD; the

    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("ud2", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");

/// Set once the fatal panic path has started. A panic from inside the fatal
/// path stops silently instead of recursively printing or looping diagnostics.
static FATAL_PANIC_ACTIVE: core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool =
    core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    // Mask maskable interrupts before any diagnostics run: another kernel
    // thread must not resume after a panic is declared, and the fatal report
    // must not be preempted mid-print.
    //
    // SAFETY: Kernel panic path runs at CPL 0; masking IF is always sound.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    if FATAL_PANIC_ACTIVE.swap(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire) {
        loop {
            // SAFETY: Re-entrant panics are deliberately silent.
            unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
        }
    }
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

//! Bounded parser for statically linked x86_64 ELF64 executables.
//!
//! This validates image metadata only. It does not allocate frames, apply
//! relocations, or install mappings into a process address space.

use core::convert::TryFrom;

pub const ELF64_HEADER_SIZE: usize = 64;
pub const ELF64_PROGRAM_HEADER_SIZE: usize = 56;
pub const MAX_ELF_PROGRAM_HEADERS: usize = 64;
pub const MAX_ELF_LOAD_SEGMENTS: usize = 16;
pub const MAX_ELF_LOAD_PAGES: usize = 64;
pub const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;

const ET_EXEC: u16 = 2;
const EM_X86_64: u16 = 62;
const PT_LOAD: u32 = 1;
const PT_DYNAMIC: u32 = 2;
const PT_INTERP: u32 = 3;
const PT_TLS: u32 = 7;
const PT_GNU_STACK: u32 = 0x6474_e551;
const PF_EXECUTE: u32 = 1;
const PF_WRITE: u32 = 2;
const PF_READ: u32 = 4;
const PF_MASK: u32 = PF_EXECUTE | PF_WRITE | PF_READ;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ElfError {
    TruncatedHeader,
    InvalidMagic,
    UnsupportedClass,
    UnsupportedByteOrder,
    UnsupportedVersion,
    UnsupportedObjectType,
    UnsupportedMachine,
    InvalidAddressWidth,
    InvalidHeaderSize,
    InvalidProgramHeaderSize,
    TooManyProgramHeaders,
    InvalidProgramHeaderTable,
    UnsupportedDynamicSegment,
    UnsupportedTlsSegment,
    ExecutableStackUnsupported,
    UnsupportedSegmentFlags,
    SegmentNotReadable,
    TooManyLoadSegments,
    InvalidSegmentSize,
    InvalidFileRange,
    InvalidVirtualRange,
    InvalidAlignment,
    WritableExecutableSegment,
    OverlappingLoadSegments,
    ImageTooLarge,
    NoLoadSegments,
    EntryNotExecutable,
}

#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ElfPagePopulationError<E> {
    InvalidSegment,
    InvalidPage,
    FrameMemory(E),
}

#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ElfLoadError<CacheError, TableError, FrameMemoryError> {
    OutOfFrames,
    Mapping(crate::paging::MappingError),
    CachePolicy(CacheError),
    Populate(ElfPagePopulationError<FrameMemoryError>),
    Map(crate::paging::ProcessPageMapError<TableError>),
}

/// A loader failure may leave earlier pages mapped in the inactive process root.
/// The caller owns `frame`, if present, and must reclaim it. Destroy the newly
/// created process root to reclaim `mapped_pages` and any retained page tables.
#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct ElfLoadFailure<CacheError, TableError, FrameMemoryError> {
    pub cause: ElfLoadError<CacheError, TableError, FrameMemoryError>,
    pub frame: Option<crate::frame::Frame>,
    pub mapped_pages: usize,
    pub rollback_retained_table_frames: usize,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct LoadedElf {

    pub mapped_pages: usize,
}

/// One validated, page-aligned PT_LOAD segment in a static executable.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct Elf64LoadSegment {
    virtual_start: u64,
    virtual_end: u64,
    file_offset: usize,
    file_size: usize,
    memory_size: usize,
    page_end: u64,
    flags: u32,
}

impl Elf64LoadSegment {
    pub const fn virtual_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.virtual_start
    }

    pub const fn virtual_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.virtual_end
    }

    pub const fn file_offset(self) -> usize {
        self.file_offset
    }

    pub const fn file_size(self) -> usize {
        self.file_size
    }

    pub const fn memory_size(self) -> usize {
        self.memory_size
    }

    pub const fn page_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.page_end
    }

    pub const fn page_count(self) -> usize {
        ((self.page_end - self.virtual_start) / PAGE_SIZE) as usize
    }

    pub const fn writable(self) -> bool {
        self.flags & PF_WRITE != 0
    }

    pub const fn executable(self) -> bool {
        self.flags & PF_EXECUTE != 0
    }
}

/// A validated view into a static ELF64 image with fixed-capacity PT_LOAD metadata.
#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct Elf64Image<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    entry_point: u64,
    segments: [Option<Elf64LoadSegment>; MAX_ELF_LOAD_SEGMENTS],
    segment_count: usize,
    load_page_count: usize,
}

impl<'a> Elf64Image<'a> {
    pub fn parse(bytes: &'a [u8], virtual_address_bits: u8) -> Result<Self, ElfError> {
        if bytes.len() < ELF64_HEADER_SIZE {
            return Err(ElfError::TruncatedHeader);
        }
        if bytes.get(0..4) != Some(&b"\x7fELF"[..]) {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidMagic);
        }
        if bytes[4] != 2 {
            return Err(ElfError::UnsupportedClass);
        }
        if bytes[5] != 1 {
            return Err(ElfError::UnsupportedByteOrder);
        }
        if bytes[6] != 1 || read_u32(bytes, 20) != Some(1) {
            return Err(ElfError::UnsupportedVersion);
        }
        if read_u16(bytes, 16) != Some(ET_EXEC) {
            return Err(ElfError::UnsupportedObjectType);
        }
        if read_u16(bytes, 18) != Some(EM_X86_64) {
            return Err(ElfError::UnsupportedMachine);
        }
        if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidAddressWidth);
        }
        if read_u16(bytes, 52) != Some(ELF64_HEADER_SIZE as u16) {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidHeaderSize);
        }
        if read_u16(bytes, 54) != Some(ELF64_PROGRAM_HEADER_SIZE as u16) {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderSize);
        }

        let entry_point = read_u64(bytes, 24).ok_or(ElfError::TruncatedHeader)?;
        let program_header_offset = read_u64(bytes, 32).ok_or(ElfError::TruncatedHeader)?;
        let program_header_count =
            usize::from(read_u16(bytes, 56).ok_or(ElfError::TruncatedHeader)?);
        if program_header_count > MAX_ELF_PROGRAM_HEADERS {
            return Err(ElfError::TooManyProgramHeaders);
        }
        let program_header_offset = usize::try_from(program_header_offset)
            .map_err(|_| ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
        let program_header_bytes = program_header_count
            .checked_mul(ELF64_PROGRAM_HEADER_SIZE)
            .ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
        let program_header_end = program_header_offset
            .checked_add(program_header_bytes)
            .filter(|end| *end <= bytes.len())
            .ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;

        let lower_half_end = 1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1);
        let mut image = Self {
            bytes,
            entry_point,
            segments: [None; MAX_ELF_LOAD_SEGMENTS],
            segment_count: 0,
            load_page_count: 0,
        };

        for header_offset in
            (program_header_offset..program_header_end).step_by(ELF64_PROGRAM_HEADER_SIZE)
        {
            let kind = read_u32(bytes, header_offset).ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
            match kind {
                PT_DYNAMIC | PT_INTERP => return Err(ElfError::UnsupportedDynamicSegment),
                PT_TLS => return Err(ElfError::UnsupportedTlsSegment),
                PT_GNU_STACK => {
                    let flags = read_u32(bytes, header_offset + 4)
                        .ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
                    if flags & PF_EXECUTE != 0 {
                        return Err(ElfError::ExecutableStackUnsupported);
                    }
                }
                PT_LOAD => {
                    image.add_load_segment(header_offset, virtual_address_bits, lower_half_end)?
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }

        if image.segment_count == 0 {
            return Err(ElfError::NoLoadSegments);
        }
        if !image.segments().any(|segment| {
            segment.executable()
                && !segment.writable()
                && entry_point >= segment.virtual_start
                && entry_point < segment.virtual_end
        }) {
            return Err(ElfError::EntryNotExecutable);
        }
        Ok(image)
    }

    fn add_load_segment(
        &mut self,
        header_offset: usize,
        virtual_address_bits: u8,
        lower_half_end: u64,
    ) -> Result<(), ElfError> {
        if self.segment_count == MAX_ELF_LOAD_SEGMENTS {
            return Err(ElfError::TooManyLoadSegments);
        }
        let flags =
            read_u32(self.bytes, header_offset + 4).ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
        if flags & !PF_MASK != 0 {
            return Err(ElfError::UnsupportedSegmentFlags);
        }
        if flags & PF_READ == 0 {
            return Err(ElfError::SegmentNotReadable);
        }
        if flags & (PF_WRITE | PF_EXECUTE) == (PF_WRITE | PF_EXECUTE) {
            return Err(ElfError::WritableExecutableSegment);
        }

        let file_offset =
            read_u64(self.bytes, header_offset + 8).ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
        let virtual_start =
            read_u64(self.bytes, header_offset + 16).ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
        let file_size =
            read_u64(self.bytes, header_offset + 32).ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
        let memory_size =
            read_u64(self.bytes, header_offset + 40).ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;
        let alignment =
            read_u64(self.bytes, header_offset + 48).ok_or(ElfError::InvalidProgramHeaderTable)?;

        if file_size > memory_size {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidSegmentSize);
        }
        if memory_size == 0 {
            if file_size == 0 {
                return Ok(());
            }
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidSegmentSize);
        }
        if (file_offset | virtual_start) & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidAlignment);
        }
        if alignment > 1
            && (!alignment.is_power_of_two()
                || file_offset % alignment != virtual_start % alignment)
        {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidAlignment);
        }

        let file_offset = usize::try_from(file_offset).map_err(|_| ElfError::InvalidFileRange)?;
        let file_size = usize::try_from(file_size).map_err(|_| ElfError::InvalidFileRange)?;
        if file_offset
            .checked_add(file_size)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > self.bytes.len())
        {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidFileRange);
        }

        let virtual_end = virtual_start
            .checked_add(memory_size)
            .ok_or(ElfError::InvalidVirtualRange)?;
        let last_virtual = virtual_end - 1;
        if virtual_start < PAGE_SIZE
            || virtual_start >= lower_half_end
            || last_virtual >= lower_half_end
            || !is_canonical(virtual_start, virtual_address_bits)
            || !is_canonical(last_virtual, virtual_address_bits)
        {
            return Err(ElfError::InvalidVirtualRange);
        }
        let page_end = virtual_end
            .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE - 1)
            .map(|end| end & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1))
            .filter(|end| *end <= lower_half_end)
            .ok_or(ElfError::InvalidVirtualRange)?;
        let page_count_u64 = (page_end - virtual_start) / PAGE_SIZE;
        let page_count = usize::try_from(page_count_u64).map_err(|_| ElfError::ImageTooLarge)?;
        self.load_page_count = self
            .load_page_count
            .checked_add(page_count)
            .filter(|count| *count <= MAX_ELF_LOAD_PAGES)
            .ok_or(ElfError::ImageTooLarge)?;
        if self
            .segments()
            .any(|segment| virtual_start < segment.page_end && segment.virtual_start < page_end)
        {
            return Err(ElfError::OverlappingLoadSegments);
        }

        let memory_size = usize::try_from(memory_size).map_err(|_| ElfError::ImageTooLarge)?;
        self.segments[self.segment_count] = Some(Elf64LoadSegment {
            virtual_start,
            virtual_end,
            file_offset,
            file_size,
            memory_size,
            page_end,
            flags,
        });
        self.segment_count += 1;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub const fn entry_point(&self) -> u64 {
        self.entry_point
    }

    pub const fn segment_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.segment_count
    }

    pub const fn load_page_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.load_page_count
    }

    pub fn segments(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = Elf64LoadSegment> + '_ {
        self.segments[..self.segment_count]
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .copied()
    }

    pub fn segment_file_bytes(&self, index: usize) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
        let segment = self.segments.get(index)?.as_ref()?;
        let end = segment.file_offset.checked_add(segment.file_size)?;
        self.bytes.get(segment.file_offset..end)
    }

    /// Populate one page of a validated load segment, zero-filling bytes not
    /// covered by the segment's file payload (including BSS).
    pub fn populate_segment_page<U: crate::paging::UserFrameMemory>(
        &self,
        segment_index: usize,
        page_index: usize,
        frame: &crate::frame::Frame,
        user_memory: &mut U,
    ) -> Result<(), ElfPagePopulationError<U::Error>> {
        let segment = self
            .segments
            .get(segment_index)
            .and_then(Option::as_ref)
            .copied()
            .ok_or(ElfPagePopulationError::InvalidSegment)?;
        if page_index >= segment.page_count() {
            return Err(ElfPagePopulationError::InvalidPage);
        }

        let page_offset = page_index
            .checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE as usize)
            .ok_or(ElfPagePopulationError::InvalidPage)?;
        let file_end = page_offset
            .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE as usize)
            .ok_or(ElfPagePopulationError::InvalidPage)?
            .min(segment.file_size);
        let file_start = page_offset.min(file_end);
        let mut page = [0; PAGE_SIZE as usize];
        if file_start < file_end {
            let bytes = self
                .segment_file_bytes(segment_index)
                .ok_or(ElfPagePopulationError::InvalidSegment)?;
            let source = bytes
                .get(file_start..file_end)
                .ok_or(ElfPagePopulationError::InvalidSegment)?;
            page[..source.len()].copy_from_slice(source);
        }
        user_memory
            .copy_to_frame(frame, 0, &page)
            .map_err(ElfPagePopulationError::FrameMemory)
    }

    /// Allocate, populate, and map every validated PT_LOAD page into an inactive
    /// process root. Cache attributes are selected separately for each exact
    /// physical page by `select_cache_attributes`.
    ///
    /// On failure, pages already installed remain owned by the process root and
    /// are reported in `mapped_pages`; any returned frame remains caller-owned.
    /// Destroy a newly created root to reclaim partial mappings and retained page
    /// tables before abandoning a failed load.
    pub fn load_into_process_root<M, U, F, CacheError>(
        &self,
        roots: &mut crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
        allocator: &mut crate::frame::FrameAllocator,
        handle: crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
        user_memory: &mut U,
        mut select_cache_attributes: F,
    ) -> Result<LoadedElf, ElfLoadFailure<CacheError, M::Error, U::Error>>
    where
        M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory,
        U: crate::paging::UserFrameMemory,
        F: FnMut(
            crate::paging::ValidatedMappingRange,
        ) -> Result<crate::paging::SelectedCacheAttributes, CacheError>,
    {
        use crate::paging::{validate_mapping_range, PagePermissions, PAGE_SIZE};

        let config = roots.page_walk_config();
        let mut mapped_pages = 0;
        for (segment_index, segment) in self.segments().enumerate() {
            let permissions = PagePermissions {
                writable: segment.writable(),
                executable: segment.executable(),
                user_accessible: true,
            };
            for page_index in 0..segment.page_count() {
                let virtual_address = u64::try_from(page_index)
                    .ok()
                    .and_then(|index| index.checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE))
                    .and_then(|offset| segment.virtual_start().checked_add(offset));
                let Some(virtual_address) = virtual_address else {
                    return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                        cause: ElfLoadError::Mapping(crate::paging::MappingError::AddressOverflow),
                        frame: None,
                        mapped_pages,
                        rollback_retained_table_frames: 0,
                    });
                };
                let Some(frame) = allocator.allocate() else {
                    return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                        cause: ElfLoadError::OutOfFrames,
                        frame: None,
                        mapped_pages,
                        rollback_retained_table_frames: 0,
                    });
                };
                let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
                    virtual_address,
                    frame.address(),
                    PAGE_SIZE,
                    permissions,
                    Some(config.physical_address_bits),
                    config.virtual_address_bits,
                ) {
                    Ok(mapping) => mapping,
                    Err(error) => {
                        return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                            cause: ElfLoadError::Mapping(error),
                            frame: Some(frame),
                            mapped_pages,
                            rollback_retained_table_frames: 0,
                        });
                    }
                };
                let cache_attributes = match select_cache_attributes(mapping) {
                    Ok(attributes) => attributes,
                    Err(error) => {
                        return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                            cause: ElfLoadError::CachePolicy(error),
                            frame: Some(frame),
                            mapped_pages,
                            rollback_retained_table_frames: 0,
                        });
                    }
                };
                if let Err(error) =
                    self.populate_segment_page(segment_index, page_index, &frame, user_memory)
                {
                    return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                        cause: ElfLoadError::Populate(error),
                        frame: Some(frame),
                        mapped_pages,
                        rollback_retained_table_frames: 0,
                    });
                }
                if let Err(failure) =
                    roots.map_user_page(allocator, handle, frame, mapping, cache_attributes)
                {
                    return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                        cause: ElfLoadError::Map(failure.cause),
                        frame: Some(failure.frame),
                        mapped_pages,
                        rollback_retained_table_frames: failure.rollback_retained_table_frames,
                    });
                }
                mapped_pages += 1;
            }
        }
        Ok(LoadedElf {
            entry_point: self.entry_point(),
            mapped_pages,
        })
    }
}

fn is_canonical(address: u64, address_bits: u8) -> bool {
    let sign_bit = (address >> (address_bits - 1)) & 1;
    let upper_bits = address >> address_bits;
    let expected_upper_bits = if sign_bit == 0 {
        0
    } else {
        u64::MAX >> address_bits
    };
    upper_bits == expected_upper_bits
}

fn read_u16(bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Option<u16> {
    let end = offset.checked_add(2)?;
    let bytes = bytes.get(offset..end)?;
    Some(u16::from_le_bytes([bytes[0], bytes[1]]))
}

fn read_u32(bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    let end = offset.checked_add(4)?;
    let bytes = bytes.get(offset..end)?;
    Some(u32::from_le_bytes([bytes[0], bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3]]))
}

fn read_u64(bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Option<u64> {
    let end = offset.checked_add(8)?;
    let bytes = bytes.get(offset..end)?;
    Some(u64::from_le_bytes([
        bytes[0], bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3], bytes[4], bytes[5], bytes[6], bytes[7],
    ]))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{Elf64Image, ElfError, ElfPagePopulationError, MAX_ELF_LOAD_PAGES, PAGE_SIZE};

    const FILE_SIZE: usize = 0x3000;
    const CODE_PH: usize = 64;
    const DATA_PH: usize = CODE_PH + 56;

    fn valid_elf() -> [u8; FILE_SIZE] {
        let mut bytes = [0; FILE_SIZE];
        bytes[..4].copy_from_slice(b"\x7fELF");
        bytes[4] = 2;
        bytes[5] = 1;
        bytes[6] = 1;
        put_u16(&mut bytes, 16, 2);
        put_u16(&mut bytes, 18, 62);
        put_u32(&mut bytes, 20, 1);
        put_u64(&mut bytes, 24, 0x4000_0000);
        put_u64(&mut bytes, 32, CODE_PH as u64);
        put_u16(&mut bytes, 52, 64);
        put_u16(&mut bytes, 54, 56);
        put_u16(&mut bytes, 56, 2);
        set_load_segment(&mut bytes, CODE_PH, 5, 0x1000, 0x4000_0000, 64, 128, 0x1000);
        set_load_segment(
            &mut bytes,
            DATA_PH,
            6,
            0x2000,
            0x4000_1000,
            128,
            0x1800,
            0x1000,
        );
        bytes[0x1000..0x1040].fill(0x90);
        bytes[0x2000..0x2080].fill(0x5a);
        bytes
    }

    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    fn set_load_segment(
        bytes: &mut [u8],
        header: usize,
        flags: u32,
        file_offset: u64,
        virtual_address: u64,
        file_size: u64,
        memory_size: u64,
        alignment: u64,
    ) {
        put_u32(bytes, header, 1);
        put_u32(bytes, header + 4, flags);
        put_u64(bytes, header + 8, file_offset);
        put_u64(bytes, header + 16, virtual_address);
        put_u64(bytes, header + 32, file_size);
        put_u64(bytes, header + 40, memory_size);
        put_u64(bytes, header + 48, alignment);
    }

    fn put_u16(bytes: &mut [u8], offset: usize, value: u16) {
        bytes[offset..offset + 2].copy_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
    }

    fn put_u32(bytes: &mut [u8], offset: usize, value: u32) {
        bytes[offset..offset + 4].copy_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
    }

    fn put_u64(bytes: &mut [u8], offset: usize, value: u64) {
        bytes[offset..offset + 8].copy_from_slice(&value.to_le_bytes());
    }

    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
    enum SyntheticFrameError {
        WrongFrame,
        OutOfBounds,
    }

    struct SyntheticFrameMemory {
        frame_address: u64,
        bytes: [u8; PAGE_SIZE as usize],
    }

    // SAFETY: This test backend accesses only its matching synthetic frame token
    // and enforces page bounds for every operation.
    unsafe impl crate::paging::UserFrameMemory for SyntheticFrameMemory {
        type Error = SyntheticFrameError;

        fn copy_from_frame(
            &mut self,
            frame: &Frame,
            offset: usize,
            destination: &mut [u8],
        ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
            let end = offset
                .checked_add(destination.len())
                .filter(|end| *end <= self.bytes.len())
                .ok_or(SyntheticFrameError::OutOfBounds)?;
            if frame.address() != self.frame_address {
                return Err(SyntheticFrameError::WrongFrame);
            }
            destination.copy_from_slice(&self.bytes[offset..end]);
            Ok(())
        }

        fn copy_to_frame(
            &mut self,
            frame: &Frame,
            offset: usize,
            source: &[u8],
        ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
            let end = offset
                .checked_add(source.len())
                .filter(|end| *end <= self.bytes.len())
                .ok_or(SyntheticFrameError::OutOfBounds)?;
            if frame.address() != self.frame_address {
                return Err(SyntheticFrameError::WrongFrame);
            }
            self.bytes[offset..end].copy_from_slice(source);
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_static_x86_64_load_segments_and_exposes_file_bytes() {
        let bytes = valid_elf();
        let image = Elf64Image::parse(&bytes, 48).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(image.entry_point(), 0x4000_0000);
        assert_eq!(image.segment_count(), 2);
        assert_eq!(image.load_page_count(), 3);
        let mut segments = image.segments();
        let code = segments.next().unwrap();
        let data = segments.next().unwrap();
        assert!(segments.next().is_none());
        assert_eq!(code.virtual_start(), 0x4000_0000);
        assert!(code.executable());
        assert!(!code.writable());
        assert_eq!(data.virtual_start(), 0x4000_1000);
        assert!(data.writable());
        assert!(!data.executable());
        assert_eq!(data.virtual_end(), 0x4000_2800);
        assert_eq!(data.memory_size(), 0x1800);
        assert_eq!(data.page_end(), 0x4000_3000);
        assert_eq!(image.segment_file_bytes(1).unwrap(), &[0x5a; 128]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn populates_file_bytes_and_zero_fills_each_segment_page() {
        let bytes = valid_elf();
        let image = Elf64Image::parse(&bytes, 48).unwrap();
        let memory_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
            base: 0x10_0000,
            length: PAGE_SIZE * 2,
            kind: 0,
        }])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&memory_map).unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let mut user_memory = SyntheticFrameMemory {
            frame_address: frame.address(),
            bytes: [0xa5; PAGE_SIZE as usize],
        };

        image
            .populate_segment_page(1, 0, &frame, &mut user_memory)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(&user_memory.bytes[..128], &[0x5a; 128]);
        assert!(user_memory.bytes[128..].iter().all(|byte| *byte == 0));

        user_memory.bytes.fill(0xa5);
        image
            .populate_segment_page(1, 1, &frame, &mut user_memory)
            .unwrap();
        assert!(user_memory.bytes.iter().all(|byte| *byte == 0));
        assert_eq!(
            image.populate_segment_page(1, 2, &frame, &mut user_memory),
            Err(ElfPagePopulationError::InvalidPage)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            image.populate_segment_page(16, 0, &frame, &mut user_memory),
            Err(ElfPagePopulationError::InvalidSegment)
        );
    }

//! Allocation-free validation for virtual addresses and physical memory maps.

/// Limine's memory-map type for ordinary usable RAM.
pub const MEMORY_MAP_USABLE: u64 = 0;
/// Maximum number of memory regions retained in the boot snapshot.
pub const MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS: usize = 256;
/// Minimum x86_64 initial stack size guaranteed by the Limine protocol.
pub const LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE: u64 = 64 * 1024;

/// Check whether an address is canonical for a sign-extended virtual width.
///
/// Widths outside `1..=64` are rejected. A 64-bit width accepts every address.
pub const fn is_canonical_virtual_address(address: u64, address_bits: u8) -> bool {
    if address_bits == 0 || address_bits > 64 {
        return false;
    }
    if address_bits == 64 {
        return true;
    }

    let sign_bit = (address >> (address_bits - 1)) & 1;
    let upper_bits = address >> address_bits;
    let expected_upper_bits = if sign_bit == 0 {
        0
    } else {
        u64::MAX >> address_bits
    };
    upper_bits == expected_upper_bits
}

/// Check that a non-empty half-open physical range fits an address width.
pub const fn physical_range_fits_address_width(start: u64, end: u64, address_bits: u8) -> bool {
    if start >= end || address_bits == 0 || address_bits > 64 {
        return false;
    }
    address_bits == 64 || end <= (1u64 << address_bits)
}

/// Return the physical end of the linker-defined kernel image span, if valid.
///
/// Limine reports the load bases while the linker supplies the virtual span.
/// This validates that both sources agree on the virtual base and that the
/// relocated half-open physical range fits the known address widths.
pub const fn kernel_image_physical_end(
    physical_base: u64,
    reported_virtual_base: u64,
    linked_virtual_start: u64,
    linked_virtual_end: u64,
    physical_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_bits: u8,
) -> Option<u64> {
    if linked_virtual_start != reported_virtual_base
        || linked_virtual_start >= linked_virtual_end
        || physical_base & 0xfff != 0
        || linked_virtual_start & 0xfff != 0
    {
        return None;
    }

    let virtual_last = linked_virtual_end - 1;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(linked_virtual_start, virtual_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address(virtual_last, virtual_bits)
    {
        return None;
    }
    let sign_bit = 1u64 << (virtual_bits - 1);
    if linked_virtual_start & sign_bit != virtual_last & sign_bit {
        return None;
    }

    let image_size = linked_virtual_end - linked_virtual_start;
    let Some(physical_end) = physical_base.checked_add(image_size) else {
        return None;
    };
    if let Some(bits) = physical_bits {
        if !physical_range_fits_address_width(physical_base, physical_end, bits) {
            return None;
        }
    }
    Some(physical_end)
}

pub struct KernelImageVirtualSegments {
    pub text: (u64, u64),
    pub rodata: (u64, u64),
    pub data: (u64, u64),
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]

    pub virtual_start: u64,
    pub virtual_end: u64,
    pub physical_start: u64,
    pub physical_end: u64,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct KernelImageSegments {
    pub text: KernelImageSegment,

/// Validate page-aligned PT_LOAD mapping spans and translate them to physical ranges.
///
/// The three spans must be contiguous, ordered text/rodata/data ranges that cover
/// the linker-defined image after rounding its final byte to a 4 KiB boundary.
/// This validates linker metadata; it does not prove that inherited page tables
/// map these ranges or that their backing frames are owned by Rustix.
pub const fn kernel_image_segments(
    physical_base: u64,
    reported_virtual_base: u64,
    image_virtual_start: u64,
    image_virtual_end: u64,
    virtual_segments: KernelImageVirtualSegments,
    physical_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_bits: u8,
) -> Option<KernelImageSegments> {
    let Some(_) = kernel_image_physical_end(
        physical_base,
        reported_virtual_base,
        image_virtual_start,
        image_virtual_end,
        physical_bits,
        virtual_bits,
    ) else {
        return None;
    };

    let (text_start, text_end) = virtual_segments.text;
    let (rodata_start, rodata_end) = virtual_segments.rodata;
    let (data_start, data_end) = virtual_segments.data;
    if text_start != image_virtual_start
        || text_start >= text_end
        || text_end != rodata_start
        || rodata_start >= rodata_end
        || rodata_end != data_start
        || data_start >= image_virtual_end
        || image_virtual_end > data_end
    {
        return None;
    }

    let Some(rounded_image_end) = image_virtual_end.checked_add(0xfff) else {
        return None;
    };
    let rounded_image_end = rounded_image_end & !0xfff;
    if data_end != rounded_image_end
        || text_start & 0xfff != 0
        || text_end & 0xfff != 0
        || rodata_start & 0xfff != 0
        || rodata_end & 0xfff != 0
        || data_start & 0xfff != 0
        || data_end & 0xfff != 0
    {
        return None;
    }

    let mapped_last_virtual = data_end - 1;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(image_virtual_start, virtual_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address(mapped_last_virtual, virtual_bits)
    {
        return None;
    }
    if virtual_bits < 64
        && ((image_virtual_start ^ mapped_last_virtual) & (1u64 << (virtual_bits - 1))) != 0
    {
        return None;
    }

    let Some(mapped_physical_end) = physical_base.checked_add(data_end - image_virtual_start)
    else {
        return None;
    };
    if let Some(bits) = physical_bits {
        if !physical_range_fits_address_width(physical_base, mapped_physical_end, bits) {
            return None;
        }
    }

    let Some(text_physical_start) = physical_base.checked_add(text_start - image_virtual_start)
    else {
        return None;
    };
    let Some(text_physical_end) = physical_base.checked_add(text_end - image_virtual_start) else {
        return None;
    };
    let Some(rodata_physical_start) = physical_base.checked_add(rodata_start - image_virtual_start)
    else {
        return None;
    };
    let Some(rodata_physical_end) = physical_base.checked_add(rodata_end - image_virtual_start)
    else {
        return None;
    };
    let Some(data_physical_start) = physical_base.checked_add(data_start - image_virtual_start)
    else {
        return None;
    };

    Some(KernelImageSegments {
        text: KernelImageSegment {
            virtual_start: text_start,
            virtual_end: text_end,
            physical_start: text_physical_start,
            physical_end: text_physical_end,
        },
        rodata: KernelImageSegment {
            virtual_start: rodata_start,
            virtual_end: rodata_end,
            physical_start: rodata_physical_start,
            physical_end: rodata_physical_end,
        },
        data: KernelImageSegment {
            virtual_start: data_start,
            virtual_end: data_end,
            physical_start: data_physical_start,
            physical_end: mapped_physical_end,
        },
    })
}

/// Derive the requested initial x86_64 stack span below Limine's entry RSP.
///
/// The SysV entry stack has an 8-byte return-address slot, so `entry_rsp + 8`
/// is the exclusive top. The requested span must be at least the protocol's
/// 64 KiB minimum; callers should pass the size actually requested from Limine.
pub const fn limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(
    entry_rsp: u64,
    virtual_bits: u8,
    stack_size: u64,
) -> Option<(u64, u64)> {
    if entry_rsp & 0xf != 8 {
        return None;
    }
    let Some(stack_end) = entry_rsp.checked_add(8) else {
        return None;
    };
    if stack_size < LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE {
        return None;
    }
    let Some(stack_start) = stack_end.checked_sub(stack_size) else {
        return None;
    };
    let stack_last = stack_end - 1;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(stack_start, virtual_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address(stack_last, virtual_bits)
    {
        return None;
    }
    let sign_bit = 1u64 << (virtual_bits - 1);
    if stack_start & sign_bit != stack_last & sign_bit {
        return None;
    }
    Some((stack_start, stack_end))
}

/// Validate the page-rounded HHDM span for one Limine base-revision-3 region.
///
/// `physical_bits` is `None` only when CPUID does not report the width. This
/// checks arithmetic and canonicality, not whether the inherited page tables
/// actually contain the mapping.
pub const fn limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
    offset: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    physical_end: u64,
    physical_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_bits: u8,
) -> bool {
    const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;
    const PAGE_MASK: u64 = !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);

    if physical_start >= physical_end
        || offset & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
        || (virtual_bits != 48 && virtual_bits != 57)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address(offset, virtual_bits)
    {
        return false;
    }
    if let Some(bits) = physical_bits {
        if !physical_range_fits_address_width(physical_start, physical_end, bits) {
            return false;
        }
    }

    let mapped_start = physical_start & PAGE_MASK;
    let Some(rounded_end) = physical_end.checked_add(PAGE_SIZE - 1) else {
        return false;
    };
    let mapped_end = rounded_end & PAGE_MASK;
    if mapped_start >= mapped_end {
        return false;
    }
    if let Some(bits) = physical_bits {
        if !physical_range_fits_address_width(mapped_start, mapped_end, bits) {
            return false;
        }
    }

    let Some(virtual_start) = offset.checked_add(mapped_start) else {
        return false;
    };
    let Some(virtual_last) = offset.checked_add(mapped_end - 1) else {
        return false;
    };
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(virtual_start, virtual_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address(virtual_last, virtual_bits)
    {
        return false;
    }

    let sign_bit = 1u64 << (virtual_bits - 1);
    virtual_start & sign_bit == virtual_last & sign_bit
}

/// Classification of a physical memory region from the Limine memory map.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RegionKind {
    Usable,
    Reserved,
    AcpiReclaimable,
    AcpiNvs,
    BadMemory,
    BootloaderReclaimable,
    ExecutableAndModules,
    Framebuffer,
    Unknown(u64),
}

impl RegionKind {
    /// Whether Limine base revision 3 includes this type in the HHDM.
    pub const fn is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm(self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self,
            Self::Usable
                | Self::BootloaderReclaimable
                | Self::ExecutableAndModules
                | Self::Framebuffer
        )
    }

    const fn from_limine(kind: u64) -> Self {
        match kind {
            0 => Self::Usable,
            1 => Self::Reserved,
            2 => Self::AcpiReclaimable,
            3 => Self::AcpiNvs,
            4 => Self::BadMemory,
            5 => Self::BootloaderReclaimable,
            6 => Self::ExecutableAndModules,
            7 => Self::Framebuffer,
            unknown => Self::Unknown(unknown),
        }
    }
}

/// Unvalidated region fields copied from a boot protocol response.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RawMemoryRegion {
    pub base: u64,
    pub length: u64,
    pub kind: u64,
}

/// Validated half-open physical address range `[start, end)`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PhysicalRegion {
    start: u64,
    end: u64,
    kind: RegionKind,
}

impl PhysicalRegion {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        start: 0,
        end: 0,
        kind: RegionKind::Unknown(0),
    };

    pub const fn start(&self) -> u64 {
        self.start
    }

    pub const fn end(&self) -> u64 {
        self.end
    }

    pub const fn length(&self) -> u64 {
        self.end - self.start
    }

    pub const fn kind(&self) -> RegionKind {
        self.kind
    }
}

/// Errors produced when a memory map is malformed or exceeds kernel capacity.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MemoryMapError {
    EmptyMap,
    TooManyRegions,
    EmptyRegion { index: usize },
    AddressOverflow { index: usize },
    OverlappingRegions { first: usize, second: usize },
    UsableTotalOverflow,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum HhdmAddressError {
    UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth,
    EmptyRange,
    UnalignedRange,
    AddressOverflow,
    NotUsable,
    NotLimineMapped,
    InvalidHhdmRange,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AcpiSpanError {
    EmptyRange,
    AddressOverflow,
    SpanTooLarge,
    PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds,
    NotFullyAcpiBacked,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum AcpiSpanAuthorization {
    AcpiTableMemory,
    LegacyRsdpReserved,
}

/// A physical ACPI-related byte span whose complete 4 KiB mapping extent has
/// explicit memory-map authorization and fits the known physical-address width.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ValidatedAcpiSpan {
    byte_start: u64,
    byte_end: u64,
    mapping_start: u64,
    mapping_end: u64,
    authorization: AcpiSpanAuthorization,
}

impl ValidatedAcpiSpan {
    pub const fn byte_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.byte_start
    }

    pub const fn byte_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.byte_end
    }

    pub const fn mapping_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.mapping_start
    }

    pub const fn mapping_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.mapping_end
    }

    /// Whether one aligned 4 KiB physical page is fully covered by this span's
    /// validated page-rounded mapping extent.
    pub fn contains_mapping_page(self, physical_page: u64) -> bool {
        if physical_page & 0xfff != 0 {
            return false;
        }
        let Some(page_end) = physical_page.checked_add(4096) else {
            return false;
        };
        let authorization_contains_page = match self.authorization {
            AcpiSpanAuthorization::AcpiTableMemory => true,
            AcpiSpanAuthorization::LegacyRsdpReserved => {
                physical_page >= 0x80_000 && page_end <= 0x10_0000
            }
        };
        authorization_contains_page
            && physical_page >= self.mapping_start
            && page_end <= self.mapping_end
    }
}

/// Errors from validating a physical page span for MMIO mapping.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MmioSpanError {
    Misaligned,
    AddressOverflow,
    PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds,
    /// The page overlaps a known memory-map region not permitted for MMIO.
    OverlapsNonMmioMemory,
}

/// A physical page authorized for MMIO mapping: 4 KiB aligned, fits the known
/// physical-address width, and does not intersect a known memory-map region
/// other than `Reserved` or `Unknown`. Unreported ranges are also permitted.
///
/// This does not prove the page is a device register (firmware could omit a
/// RAM range from the map); callers must only use it with addresses from
/// validated platform data (MADT, CPUID).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ValidatedMmioSpan {
    mapping_start: u64,
    mapping_end: u64,
}

impl ValidatedMmioSpan {
    pub const fn mapping_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.mapping_start
    }

    pub const fn mapping_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.mapping_end
    }

    /// Whether one aligned 4 KiB physical page equals this validated span.
    pub fn contains_mapping_page(self, physical_page: u64) -> bool {
        physical_page == self.mapping_start
    }
}

/// Validated, allocation-free snapshot of the physical memory map.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MemoryMap {
    regions: [PhysicalRegion; MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS],
    region_count: usize,
    usable_bytes: u64,
}

impl MemoryMap {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        regions: [PhysicalRegion::EMPTY; MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS],
        region_count: 0,
        usable_bytes: 0,
    };

    pub fn from_raw(regions: &[RawMemoryRegion]) -> Result<Self, MemoryMapError> {
        let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
        for region in regions {
            builder.push(region.base, region.length, region.kind)?;
        }
        builder.finish()
    }

    pub fn regions(&self) -> &[PhysicalRegion] {
        &self.regions[..self.region_count]
    }

    pub fn range_is_within_region_kind(&self, start: u64, end: u64, kind: RegionKind) -> bool {
        start < end
            && self
                .regions()
                .iter()
                .any(|region| region.start <= start && end <= region.end && region.kind == kind)
    }

    /// Validate one aligned 4 KiB physical page as an MMIO page. The page must
    /// fit the known physical-address width and must not intersect any known
    /// memory-map region except `Reserved` or `Unknown`. Device registers are
    /// expected to lie in reserved, unknown, or unreported address space.
    pub fn validate_mmio_page(
        &self,
        physical_address: u64,
        physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    ) -> Result<ValidatedMmioSpan, MmioSpanError> {
        const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;

        if physical_address & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
            return Err(MmioSpanError::Misaligned);
        }
        let mapping_end = physical_address
            .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(MmioSpanError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if physical_address_bits.is_some_and(|bits| {
            !physical_range_fits_address_width(physical_address, mapping_end, bits)
        }) {
            return Err(MmioSpanError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds);
        }
        for region in self.regions() {
            if region.start < mapping_end
                && physical_address < region.end
                && !matches!(region.kind, RegionKind::Reserved | RegionKind::Unknown(_))
            {
                return Err(MmioSpanError::OverlapsNonMmioMemory);
            }
        }

        Ok(ValidatedMmioSpan {
            mapping_start: physical_address,
            mapping_end,
        })
    }

    /// Check that a non-empty physical span is covered only by ACPI reclaimable
    /// or ACPI NVS regions, optionally enforcing the reported physical width.
    /// Adjacent ACPI regions may jointly cover the span; gaps and other region
    /// kinds are rejected. This checks metadata only and does not authorize a
    /// dereference or imply that the span is mapped.
    pub fn validate_acpi_span(
        &self,
        start: u64,
        length: u64,
        physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    ) -> Result<ValidatedAcpiSpan, AcpiSpanError> {
        const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;
        const MAX_SPAN_SIZE: u64 = 64 * 1024;

        if length == 0 {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::EmptyRange);
        }
        if length > MAX_SPAN_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::SpanTooLarge);
        }
        let end = start
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if physical_address_bits
            .is_some_and(|bits| !physical_range_fits_address_width(start, end, bits))
        {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds);
        }
        let mapping_start = start & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        let mapping_end = end
            .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE - 1)
            .ok_or(AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow)?
            & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        if mapping_end <= mapping_start {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow);
        }
        if physical_address_bits.is_some_and(|bits| {
            !physical_range_fits_address_width(mapping_start, mapping_end, bits)
        }) {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds);
        }
        if !self.range_is_within_acpi_regions(mapping_start, mapping_end, physical_address_bits) {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::NotFullyAcpiBacked);
        }

        Ok(ValidatedAcpiSpan {
            byte_start: start,
            byte_end: end,
            mapping_start,
            mapping_end,
            authorization: AcpiSpanAuthorization::AcpiTableMemory,
        })
    }

    /// Validate an RSDP span in ACPI memory or in the bounded legacy x86
    /// firmware window `[0x80000, 0x100000)`. The legacy exception is only for
    /// the RSDP itself; table addresses must use `validate_acpi_span`.
    pub fn validate_rsdp_span(
        &self,
        start: u64,
        length: u64,
        physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    ) -> Result<ValidatedAcpiSpan, AcpiSpanError> {
        if let Ok(span) = self.validate_acpi_span(start, length, physical_address_bits) {
            return Ok(span);
        }
        const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;
        const LEGACY_RSDP_START: u64 = 0x80_000;
        const LEGACY_RSDP_END: u64 = 0x10_0000;
        const MAX_SPAN_SIZE: u64 = 64 * 1024;

        if length == 0 {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::EmptyRange);
        }
        if length > MAX_SPAN_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::SpanTooLarge);
        }
        let end = start
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if physical_address_bits
            .is_some_and(|bits| !physical_range_fits_address_width(start, end, bits))
        {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds);
        }
        let mapping_start = start & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        let mapping_end = end
            .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE - 1)
            .ok_or(AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow)?
            & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        if mapping_end <= mapping_start {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow);
        }
        if mapping_start < LEGACY_RSDP_START
            || mapping_end > LEGACY_RSDP_END
            || physical_address_bits.is_some_and(|bits| {
                !physical_range_fits_address_width(mapping_start, mapping_end, bits)
            })
            || !self.range_is_covered_by_kind(mapping_start, mapping_end, RegionKind::Reserved)
        {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::NotFullyAcpiBacked);
        }

        Ok(ValidatedAcpiSpan {
            byte_start: start,
            byte_end: end,
            mapping_start,
            mapping_end,
            authorization: AcpiSpanAuthorization::LegacyRsdpReserved,
        })
    }

    fn range_is_covered_by_kind(&self, start: u64, end: u64, kind: RegionKind) -> bool {
        if start >= end {
            return false;
        }
        let mut covered_until = start;
        for region in self.regions() {
            if region.end <= covered_until {
                continue;
            }
            if region.start > covered_until || region.kind != kind {
                return false;
            }
            covered_until = region.end.min(end);
            if covered_until == end {
                return true;
            }
        }
        false
    }

    pub fn range_is_within_acpi_regions(
        &self,
        start: u64,
        end: u64,
        physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    ) -> bool {
        if start >= end
            || physical_address_bits
                .is_some_and(|bits| !physical_range_fits_address_width(start, end, bits))
        {
            return false;
        }

        let mut covered_until = start;
        for region in self.regions() {
            if region.end <= covered_until {
                continue;
            }
            if region.start > covered_until
                || !matches!(
                    region.kind,
                    RegionKind::AcpiReclaimable | RegionKind::AcpiNvs
                )
            {
                return false;
            }
            covered_until = region.end.min(end);
            if covered_until == end {
                return true;
            }
        }
        false
    }

    /// Calculate the Limine base-revision-3 HHDM address of a page-aligned
    /// extent wholly contained in one region that Limine maps into the HHDM.
    ///
    /// This validates metadata and relies on the Limine handoff contract for the
    /// actual mapping; it does not inspect inherited page tables or make the
    /// returned integer safe to dereference by itself.
    pub fn limine_hhdm_address(
        &self,
        hhdm_offset: u64,
        physical_start: u64,
        length: u64,
        physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
        virtual_address_bits: u8,
    ) -> Result<u64, HhdmAddressError> {
        const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;

        let physical_address_bits =
            physical_address_bits.ok_or(HhdmAddressError::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)?;
        if length == 0 {
            return Err(HhdmAddressError::EmptyRange);
        }
        if (physical_start | length) & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
            return Err(HhdmAddressError::UnalignedRange);
        }
        let physical_end = physical_start
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.regions().iter().any(|region| {
            region.start <= physical_start
                && physical_end <= region.end
                && region.kind.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm()
        }) {
            return Err(HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        if !limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
            hhdm_offset,
            physical_start,
            physical_end,
            Some(physical_address_bits),
            virtual_address_bits,
        ) {
            return Err(HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        hhdm_offset
            .checked_add(physical_start)
            .ok_or(HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange)
    }

    /// Calculate the HHDM address of a page-aligned extent wholly contained in
    /// validated `Usable` memory.
    pub fn usable_hhdm_address(
        &self,
        hhdm_offset: u64,
        physical_start: u64,
        length: u64,
        physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
        virtual_address_bits: u8,
    ) -> Result<u64, HhdmAddressError> {
        const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;

        if length == 0 {
            return Err(HhdmAddressError::EmptyRange);
        }
        if (physical_start | length) & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
            return Err(HhdmAddressError::UnalignedRange);
        }
        let physical_end = physical_start
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.range_is_within_region_kind(physical_start, physical_end, RegionKind::Usable) {
            return Err(HhdmAddressError::NotUsable);
        }
        self.limine_hhdm_address(
            hhdm_offset,
            physical_start,
            length,
            physical_address_bits,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    pub const fn usable_bytes(&self) -> u64 {
        self.usable_bytes
    }
}

/// Incremental validator used to copy loader entries without an intermediate heap.
pub struct MemoryMapBuilder {
    map: MemoryMap,
}

impl MemoryMapBuilder {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            map: MemoryMap::EMPTY,
        }
    }

    pub fn push(&mut self, base: u64, length: u64, raw_kind: u64) -> Result<(), MemoryMapError> {
        let index = self.map.region_count;
        if index == MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
            return Err(MemoryMapError::TooManyRegions);
        }
        if length == 0 {
            return Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyRegion { index });
        }
        let end = base
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(MemoryMapError::AddressOverflow { index })?;
        let kind = RegionKind::from_limine(raw_kind);

        for (other_index, other) in self.map.regions().iter().enumerate() {
            if base < other.end && other.start < end {
                return Err(MemoryMapError::OverlappingRegions {
                    first: other_index,
                    second: index,
                });
            }
        }

        let usable_bytes = if kind == RegionKind::Usable {
            self.map
                .usable_bytes
                .checked_add(length)
                .ok_or(MemoryMapError::UsableTotalOverflow)?
        } else {
            self.map.usable_bytes
        };

        self.map.regions[index] = PhysicalRegion {
            start: base,
            end,
            kind,
        };
        self.map.region_count += 1;
        self.map.usable_bytes = usable_bytes;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn finish(self) -> Result<MemoryMap, MemoryMapError> {
        if self.map.region_count == 0 {
            Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyMap)
        } else {
            Ok(self.map)
        }
    }
}

impl Default for MemoryMapBuilder {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

/// Add an already-validated usable region length to a running total.
///
/// Non-usable regions leave the total unchanged. `None` signals arithmetic
/// overflow so callers can report malformed or unrepresentable maps.
pub const fn add_usable_bytes(total: u64, region_kind: u64, region_length: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    if region_kind == MEMORY_MAP_USABLE {
        total.checked_add(region_length)
    } else {
        Some(total)
    }
}

        );
        assert_eq!(
            limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(0x0000_7fff_ffff_fff8, 48, LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE,),
            Some((0x0000_7fff_ffff_0000, 0x0000_8000_0000_0000))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(entry_rsp, 57, LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE),
            Some((0xffff_8000_0001_0000, 0xffff_8000_0002_0000))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(entry_rsp, 48, LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE - 1),
            None
        );
        let large_stack_top = 0xffff_8000_0006_0000;
        assert_eq!(
            limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(large_stack_top - 8, 48, 256 * 1024),
            Some((0xffff_8000_0002_0000, large_stack_top))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(entry_rsp & !0xf, 48, LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(
            limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(u64::MAX - 7, 64, LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(
            limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(0x0000_8000_0000_0008, 48, LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(
            limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(0x10008, 48, LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE),
            Some((0x10, 0x10010))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn calculates_usable_hhdm_addresses_only_for_validated_owned_ranges() {
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: 0x3000,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_3000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 1,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let offset = 0xffff_8000_0000_0000;

        assert_eq!(
            map.usable_hhdm_address(offset, 0x10_1000, 0x1000, Some(40), 48),
            Ok(offset + 0x10_1000)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.usable_hhdm_address(offset, 0x10_3000, 0x1000, Some(40), 48),
            Err(HhdmAddressError::NotUsable)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.usable_hhdm_address(offset, 0x10_0001, 0x1000, Some(40), 48),
            Err(HhdmAddressError::UnalignedRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.usable_hhdm_address(offset, 0x10_0000, 0, Some(40), 48),
            Err(HhdmAddressError::EmptyRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.usable_hhdm_address(offset, 0x10_0000, 0x1000, None, 48),
            Err(HhdmAddressError::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.usable_hhdm_address(offset, !0xfff, 0x1000, Some(64), 48),
            Err(HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.usable_hhdm_address(0x0000_8000_0000_0000, 0x10_0000, 0x1000, Some(40), 48),
            Err(HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange)
        );
    }

        assert!(RegionKind::ExecutableAndModules.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(RegionKind::Framebuffer.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(!RegionKind::Reserved.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(!RegionKind::AcpiReclaimable.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(!RegionKind::AcpiNvs.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(!RegionKind::BadMemory.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(!RegionKind::Unknown(99).is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());

    #[test]
    fn validates_acpi_spans_against_region_kinds_and_physical_width() {
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x1000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 2,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x2000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 3,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x4000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 0,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();

        assert!(map.range_is_within_acpi_regions(0x1800, 0x2800, Some(16)));
        assert!(map.range_is_within_acpi_regions(0x1000, 0x3000, None));
        assert!(!map.range_is_within_acpi_regions(0x1800, 0x4000, None));
        assert!(!map.range_is_within_acpi_regions(0x1800, 0x2800, Some(12)));
        assert!(!map.range_is_within_acpi_regions(0x1000, 0x1000, None));

        let span = map.validate_acpi_span(0x1800, 0x900, Some(14)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(span.byte_start(), 0x1800);
        assert_eq!(span.byte_end(), 0x2100);
        assert_eq!(span.mapping_start(), 0x1000);
        assert_eq!(span.mapping_end(), 0x3000);
        assert!(span.contains_mapping_page(0x1000));
        assert!(span.contains_mapping_page(0x2000));
        assert!(!span.contains_mapping_page(0x3000));
        assert!(!span.contains_mapping_page(0x1800));
        assert_eq!(
            map.validate_acpi_span(0x2ff0, 0x20, None),
            Err(super::AcpiSpanError::NotFullyAcpiBacked)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.validate_acpi_span(0x1800, 0x900, Some(13)),
            Err(super::AcpiSpanError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.validate_acpi_span(u64::MAX - 15, 16, None),
            Err(super::AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.validate_acpi_span(0x1000, 64 * 1024 + 1, None),
            Err(super::AcpiSpanError::SpanTooLarge)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn mmio_page_validation_rejects_ram_and_accepts_device_space() {
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 0, // Usable
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x20_0000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 6, // ExecutableAndModules
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x30_0000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 5, // BootloaderReclaimable
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x40_0000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 2, // AcpiReclaimable
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x50_0000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 3, // AcpiNvs
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x60_0000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 7, // Framebuffer
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x70_0000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 4, // BadMemory
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x80_0000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 42, // Unknown
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0xfee0_0000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 1, // Reserved (device space)
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            map.validate_mmio_page(0x10_0000, Some(52)),
            Err(MmioSpanError::OverlapsNonMmioMemory)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.validate_mmio_page(0x20_0000, Some(52)),
            Err(MmioSpanError::OverlapsNonMmioMemory)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.validate_mmio_page(0x30_0000, Some(52)),
            Err(MmioSpanError::OverlapsNonMmioMemory)
        );
        for address in [0x40_0000, 0x50_0000, 0x60_0000, 0x70_0000] {
            assert_eq!(
                map.validate_mmio_page(address, Some(52)),
                Err(MmioSpanError::OverlapsNonMmioMemory),
                "known non-MMIO region at {address:#x} must not be authorized"
            );
        }
        assert!(map.validate_mmio_page(0x80_0000, Some(52)).is_ok());
        assert!(map.validate_mmio_page(0xfee0_0000, Some(52)).is_ok());
        // A page beyond every reported region (device space) is acceptable.
        assert!(map.validate_mmio_page(0x1000_0000_0000, Some(52)).is_ok());
        // Misaligned pages and pages beyond the physical width are rejected.
        assert_eq!(
            map.validate_mmio_page(0xfee0_0001, Some(52)),
            Err(MmioSpanError::Misaligned)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.validate_mmio_page(0xfee0_0000, Some(12)),
            Err(MmioSpanError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn accepts_adjacent_ranges_and_rejects_excess_entries() {
        let adjacent = [
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x1000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x2000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 1,
            },
        ];
        assert!(MemoryMap::from_raw(&adjacent).is_ok());

        let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
        for index in 0..MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
            builder.push((index as u64) * 0x2000, 0x1000, 1).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(
            builder.push(0x1_0000_0000, 0x1000, 1),
            Err(MemoryMapError::TooManyRegions)
        );
    }
