```
    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_reject_root_frames_outside_the_configured_width() {
        let high_address = 1u64 << 40;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
            base: high_address,
            length: PAGE_SIZE,
            kind: 0,
        }])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&map).unwrap();
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let failure =
            match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config()) {
                Err(error) => error,
                Ok(_) => panic!("candidate creation accepted an out-of-range root frame"),
            };
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateCreateErrorKind::RootFrameOutOfRange);
        let frame = failure
            .frame
            .expect("root token is returned on validation failure");
        assert_eq!(frame.address(), high_address);
        allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_mapping_rejects_out_of_width_table_frames_transactionally() {
        let high_address = 1u64 << 40;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_1000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: high_address,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&map).unwrap();
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(frame.address(), 0x10_1000);
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            0xffff_9000_0000_1000,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::TableFrameOutOfRange);
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_walk_rejects_intermediate_tables_without_owned_tokens() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(2);
        let foreign_frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let root_index = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4)[0];
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        memory.foreign_child = Some((root_index, foreign_frame.address()));
        let candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address),

                CandidatePageTableReadError::UnownedTable
            ))
        );

        allocator.deallocate(foreign_frame).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_release_failure_retains_owned_frames_for_retry() {
        const TOTAL_FRAMES: usize = 513;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(TOTAL_FRAMES);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let mut remaining_frames: [Option<Frame>; TOTAL_FRAMES - 1] =
            core::array::from_fn(|_| Some(allocator.allocate().unwrap()));
        for index in (1..remaining_frames.len()).step_by(2) {
            allocator
                .deallocate(remaining_frames[index].take().unwrap())
                .unwrap();
        }

        let failure = match candidate.release(&mut allocator) {
            Err(failure) => failure,
            Ok(()) => panic!("release unexpectedly fit a full range table"),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            failure.error,
            CandidateReleaseError::Frame(FrameError::RangeTableFull)
        );
        assert_eq!(failure.candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(failure.candidate.mapping_count(), 0);

        allocator
            .deallocate(remaining_frames[0].take().unwrap())
            .unwrap();
        failure.candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        for frame in remaining_frames.into_iter().flatten() {
            allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), TOTAL_FRAMES as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn active_candidate_rejects_mutation_and_release_until_deactivated() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(4);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
        // SAFETY: This is a synthetic test of the active-state guard; no CPU
        // actually uses the test candidate's root.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        assert!(candidate.is_active());
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.unmap_owned_page(0xffff_9000_0000_1000),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::Active)
        ));

        let failure = candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.error, CandidateReleaseError::ActiveRoot);
        let mut candidate = failure.candidate;
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), root);
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test never installed this root in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn active_owned_mapping_invalidates_before_returning_frame_ownership() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(8);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let physical_address = frame.address();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            virtual_address,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: true,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        candidate.memory.record_events = true;
        // SAFETY: The host backend records invalidations and no hardware CR3 is
        // changed; this tests active API state and ownership ordering only.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        // SAFETY: Synthetic active-root ownership is established above, and the
        // backend's invalidation operation records this leaf address.
        unsafe {
            candidate
                .map_owned_page_active(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
                .unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidation_count, 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidated_pages[0], virtual_address);
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[3],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::PageWrite { value, .. }) if value & 1 != 0
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[4],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::Invalidate { virtual_address })
        );
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address),
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
                if translation.physical_address == physical_address
        ));

        // SAFETY: The synthetic root remains the candidate's current test root;
        // unmap invalidates the address before the frame token is returned.
        let frame = unsafe { candidate.unmap_owned_page_active(virtual_address) }.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidation_count, 2);
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidated_pages[1], virtual_address);
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[5],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::PageWrite { value: 0, .. })
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[6],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::Invalidate { virtual_address })
        );
        allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        // SAFETY: No real CPU installed this host-test candidate in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_clone_preserves_inherited_entries_and_shared_tables() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let indexes = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4);
        let source_root = 0x8000;
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0], 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0] + 1, 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0x9000, indexes[1], 0xa000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xa000, indexes[2], 0xb000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xb000, indexes[3], 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 63));

        let root = parse_cr3_root(source_root, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        candidate
            .clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut allocator, &reader, root)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 4);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: 0x20_0000,
                leaf_physical_base: 0x20_0000,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions: PagePermissions {
                    writable: true,
                    executable: false,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 63),
            })
        );

        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn inherited_large_page_permission_change_splits_and_preserves_cache_type() {
        let total_frames = 16;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let indexes = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4);
        let source_root = 0x8000;
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0], 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0x9000, indexes[1], 0xa000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xa000, indexes[2], 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 7) | (1 << 12));
        let root = parse_cr3_root(source_root, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        candidate
            .clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut allocator, &reader, root)
            .unwrap();

        candidate
            .set_inherited_page_permissions(
                &mut allocator,
                virtual_address,
                0x20_1000,
                PagePermissions {
                    writable: false,
                    executable: false,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
            )
            .unwrap();
        let protected = match candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("split mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(protected.physical_address, 0x20_1000);
        assert_eq!(protected.page_size, PAGE_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(
            protected.permissions,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(protected.pat_index, 4);

        let neighbor = match candidate.walk(virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("neighbor mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(neighbor.physical_address, 0x20_2000);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.page_size, PAGE_SIZE);
        assert!(neighbor.permissions.writable);
        assert!(neighbor.permissions.executable);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.pat_index, 4);

        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_borrowed_acpi_without_owning_its_frame() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let acpi_physical = 0x20_0000;
        let acpi_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE * total_frames as u64,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: acpi_physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let span = acpi_map
            .validate_acpi_span(acpi_physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            acpi_physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x0606_0606_0606_0606).unwrap();
        let mtrrs = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64)
            .validated_layout(40)
            .unwrap();
        let attributes = mapping
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map - 3);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: acpi_physical,
                leaf_physical_base: acpi_physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions: KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: acpi_physical | 1 | (1 << 63),
            })
        );
        let duplicate_virtual = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            duplicate_virtual.cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::MappingAlreadyPresent
        );
        let other_virtual = virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE;
        let other_mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            other_virtual,
            acpi_physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let duplicate_physical = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, other_mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            duplicate_physical.cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::PhysicalPageAlreadyMapped
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::OwnershipMismatch)
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        // SAFETY: This synthetic test checks the inactive-only guard; the CPU
        // never installs the candidate's root.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_acpi_page(virtual_address),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::Active)
        );
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test never installed this root in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.unmap_acpi_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_explicit_uncacheable_mmio_without_frame_ownership() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);

        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();

        let virtual_address = 0xffff_d000_0000_0000;

            base: 0x10_0000,
            length: PAGE_SIZE * total_frames as u64,
            kind: 0,
        }])
        .unwrap();
        let mmio_span = mmio_map
            .validate_mmio_page(mmio_physical, Some(40))
            .unwrap();

            writable: true,
            executable: false,

            permissions,

        .unwrap();
        let attributes = super::SelectedCacheAttributes {
            physical_start: mmio_physical,
            physical_end: mmio_physical + PAGE_SIZE,
            pat_index: 3,
            effective_type: EffectiveMemoryType::Uncacheable,
        };
        let before = allocator.free_frames();
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test treats this as a device page and never
        // dereferences it; the API's map authorization, range, permissions, and
        // UC requirements apply.
        unsafe {
            candidate
                .map_mmio_page(&mut allocator, mmio_span, mapping, attributes)
                .unwrap()

        };
        assert_eq!(translation.physical_address, mmio_physical);
        assert_eq!(translation.permissions, permissions);
        assert_eq!(translation.pat_index, 3);
        assert_eq!(translation.raw_leaf_entry & (1 << 63), 1 << 63);

        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_reject_invalid_borrowed_acpi_mappings() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(8);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let physical = 0x20_0000;
        let other_physical = 0x30_0000;
        let memory_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE * 8,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: other_physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let span = memory_map
            .validate_acpi_span(physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let writable = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: true,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x0606_0606_0606_0606).unwrap();
        let mtrrs = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64)
            .validated_layout(40)
            .unwrap();
        let attributes = writable
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        let failure = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, writable, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping);
        let executable = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            PagePermissions {
                executable: true,
                ..KERNEL_READ_ONLY
            },
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let executable_attributes = executable
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate
                .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, executable, executable_attributes)
                .unwrap_err()
                .cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping
        );
        let user = validate_mapping_range(
            0x4000,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            PagePermissions {
                user_accessible: true,
                ..KERNEL_READ_ONLY
            },
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let user_attributes = user
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate
                .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, user, user_attributes)
                .unwrap_err()
                .cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping
        );
        let wrong_span = memory_map
            .validate_acpi_span(other_physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let read_only = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let read_only_attributes = read_only
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate
                .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, wrong_span, read_only, read_only_attributes)
                .unwrap_err()
                .cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn borrowed_acpi_mapping_rolls_back_new_tables_on_frame_exhaustion() {
        let total_frames = 3;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let physical = 0x20_0000;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE * total_frames as u64,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let span = map
            .validate_acpi_span(physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0xffff_9000_0000_1000,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x0606_0606_0606_0606).unwrap();
        let mtrrs = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64)
            .validated_layout(40)
            .unwrap();
        let attributes = mapping
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::OutOfFrames);
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_unmap_and_release_owned_frames() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), Some(root));
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let physical = frame.address();
        let virtual_address = 0x0000_4000_0000_1000;
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        };
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(&frame, virtual_address, permissions);

        candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 4);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: physical,
                leaf_physical_base: physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: physical | 0x3 | (1 << 2) | (1 << 63),
            })
        );

        let duplicate_frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let (duplicate_mapping, duplicate_attributes) =
            candidate_mapping(&duplicate_frame, virtual_address, permissions);
        let free_before_duplicate = allocator.free_frames();
        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(
                &mut allocator,
                duplicate_frame,
                duplicate_mapping,
                duplicate_attributes,
            )
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::MappingAlreadyPresent);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_duplicate);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();

        let returned = candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(returned.address(), physical);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent {
                level: PageLevel::Pt,
            }
        );
        allocator.deallocate(returned).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_table_mapping_rolls_back_on_frame_exhaustion() {
        let total_frames = 4;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            virtual_address,

                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::OutOfFrames);
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_table_mapping_rolls_back_after_prepare_failure() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        memory.fail_prepare_at = Some(3);
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            virtual_address,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            failure.cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::TableMemory(CandidateTestMemoryError::InjectedPrepareFailure)
        );
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_support_five_level_virtual_paths() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let config = PageWalkConfig {
            levels: 5,
            virtual_address_bits: 57,
            ..four_level_walk_config()
        };
        let mut candidate = CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, config).unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), Some(root));
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let physical = frame.address();
        let virtual_address = 0xff00_0000_0020_1000;
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            virtual_address,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: true,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );

        candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 5);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: physical,
                leaf_physical_base: physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions: PagePermissions {
                    writable: false,
                    executable: true,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: physical | 0x1,
            })
        );
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_arithmetic_overflow_and_writable_executable_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                0,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );

        let writable_executable = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: true,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x2000, PAGE_SIZE, writable_executable, Some(52), 48),
            Err(MappingError::WritableExecutable)
        );
    }
}
```

```rustix/docs/architecture/syscall-abi.md
     1	# Unix-like process and syscall direction
     2	
     3	**Status: partial address-space construction, host-tested syscall ABI decoding/write service, sanitized user IRETQ frames, bounded static ELF64 loading into an inactive process root, and fixed-capacity lifecycle policy. No syscall entry/dispatch, process-root runtime, or Ring 3 execution is implemented.**
     4	
     5	Rustix aims to expose a small, versioned syscall surface that can support Unix-like processes and tools. The kernel must own this interface rather than inherit an ABI accidentally from a bootloader or emulator.
     6	
     7	## Proposed compatibility principles
     8	
     9	- Processes have independent virtual address spaces and explicit lifecycle states.
    10	- File descriptors are per-process integer handles to kernel-managed objects; descriptor inheritance, close-on-exec, duplication, and sharing semantics must be specified together.
    11	- Syscalls use one documented error convention and stable numeric identifiers. New operations must not silently repurpose old numbers.
    12	- Arguments crossing privilege boundaries are copied or validated using narrowly scoped helpers. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::copy_from_user` and `copy_to_user` preflight the complete lower-half mapped range, check writable metadata for kernel-to-user copies, and operate only on owned frame tokens through `UserFrameMemory`; they never form a Rust reference from a user virtual address. Backend copy faults report the completed prefix; hardware fault recovery is not yet implemented.
    13	- Blocking, interruption, cancellation, and restart behavior are explicit for each syscall class.
    14	- A compatibility layer (for example, POSIX-shaped libc behavior) remains separate from internal kernel APIs.
    15	
    16	## Initial syscall ABI v1 contract (specified; register decoding implemented)
    17	
    18	ABI version `1.0` is identified by `abi_version()`, syscall number `0`, returning `0x0001_0000` in `RAX`. The first entry path uses the register convention below. In v1, `RAX` returns a signed 64-bit result: nonnegative values are success (including byte counts and PIDs); errors are negative stable error numbers. ABI versioning is append-only: existing syscall numbers, argument meanings, layouts, and error values never change or get reused. There is no POSIX compatibility claim. `src/syscall.rs` currently implements the stable number/error constants and host-tested decoding of these register-level requests; it does not perform them or install an entry path.
    19	
    20	| Number | Call | Register arguments | Result / behavior |
    21	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
    22	| 0 | `abi_version` | none | `0x0001_0000` (major 1, minor 0). |
    23	| 1 | `exit` | `RDI`: signed 32-bit status in the low 32 bits (upper bits ignored) | Does not return; status is retained exactly by the parent wait record. |
    24	| 2 | `write` | `RDI`: fd, `RSI`: user buffer, `RDX`: byte length | Returns bytes accepted; a short positive result is valid. Initial descriptors 1 and 2 are stdout/stderr console streams; other descriptors return `-EBADF`. Maximum request is 4096 bytes; zero length returns 0 without validating the pointer. |
    25	| 3 | `wait` | `RDI`: child PID (0 means any child), `RSI`: optional user pointer to signed 32-bit exit status | Blocks until a matching child exits and returns its PID. A non-null status output must be writable before the child is reaped; no matching child returns `-ECHILD`. |
    26	
    27	All other numbers are unassigned and return `-ENOSYS`; assigning a number later is an additive extension, never a reinterpretation. Descriptor 0 is reserved for input but v1 has no `read`, `open`, `close`, or `dup` call. Standard descriptors exist for the process lifetime; inheritance and general file-object semantics are not yet exposed. The initial process is created by the kernel loader, not a syscall.
    28	
    29	Stable v1 error numbers (returned negated in `RAX`) are: `1 EINVAL`, `2 EBADF`, `3 EFAULT`, `4 ENOMEM`, `5 ECHILD`, `6 EINTR`, `7 EIO`, `8 ENOSYS`, `9 E2BIG`, `10 EOVERFLOW`, and `11 ENOTSUP`. Unknown syscall numbers return `-ENOSYS`. Pointer-plus-length ranges use checked arithmetic and must lie wholly in a mapped lower-half user range. `write` preflights the whole input range before output; a later endpoint failure may return a short count, and an error before progress returns `-EIO`. A copy fault after progress returns the completed prefix; unrecoverable hardware faults remain process-fatal until user-mode exception handling is implemented. `wait` validates its optional output range before blocking and keeps the child waitable if copying the exit status fails. V1 has no signals, asynchronous interruption, or automatic syscall restart; wait is uninterruptible.
    30	
    31	All ABI integers are fixed-width little-endian x86_64 values. The wait status is one signed 32-bit integer with no implicit padding or extra fields. No other user-visible structs exist in v1.
    32	
    33	## Initial x86_64 entry design (Milestone 4; not implemented)
    34	
    35	The first single-vCPU user-mode slice will enter the kernel with `int $0x80` through a dedicated IDT interrupt gate at DPL 3 and return with `IRETQ`. This intentionally avoids `SYSCALL`/`SYSRET`, `STAR`/`LSTAR`/`FMASK`, and `SWAPGS` state transitions in the first userspace path. It is a provisional architecture decision, not a published or implemented syscall ABI.
    36	
    37	- **Vector ownership:** `0x80` lies inside the device-vector range (`0x20..=0xef`) and is now reserved by `InterruptVectorAllocator`; generic IRQ allocation/release cannot claim it. The dedicated syscall stub and gate are not installed yet. Install a dedicated syscall stub rather than the generic device-IRQ stub. The gate must be an interrupt gate, so maskable interrupts are disabled on entry before Rust dispatch.
    38	- **Selectors:** the current GDT uses `0x08` for kernel code, `0x10` for kernel data, and `0x18` for the two-slot TSS descriptor. Ring-3 data and 64-bit code descriptors are appended at GDT indexes 5 and 6, with compile-time selector assertions for user data `0x2b` and user code `0x33` (RPL 3); the data selector is loaded into user `SS` on return. They are installed at bootstrap but remain unused until a validated return path exists.
    39	- **Privilege stack:** a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt uses `TSS.RSP0`; it must point to the top of the current process's mapped, writable kernel-entry stack before user execution is resumed. The bootstrap TSS initially points to one static ring-0 stack. `interrupts::set_kernel_entry_stack` validates canonical upper-half address shape and alignment before updating `RSP0`, but no per-process stack is allocated and no scheduler path calls it yet. Callers must disable local interrupts and guarantee the stack is mapped writable in every address space that can run until the next update. A future SMP design needs per-CPU TSS and entry-stack state.
    40	- **Entry frame and state:** the assembly stub must preserve the complete user register state and construct a separately specified syscall frame; it must not assume the existing fatal-exception frame is interchangeable. Kernel code must run with the direction flag clear. Preserve user x87/SSE state across kernel handling; AVX remains disabled under the current CPU-state policy. Do not form Rust references from user pointers.
    41	- **Initial register convention:** `RAX` carries the syscall number; arguments use `RDI`, `RSI`, `RDX`, `R10`, `R8`, and `R9`; `RAX` carries the result. This is only a proposed register convention. It becomes stable only together with ABI version discovery, syscall numbers, errors, and transfer semantics below.
    42	- **Return validation:** use `IRETQ`, not `SYSRET`. Before returning, validate that the saved `CS` and `SS` are exactly the ring-3 selectors, `RIP` and `RSP` are canonical and within the process's executable/code and stack regions respectively, and `RFLAGS` contains no privileged or unsupported bits. `src/syscall.rs` now provides a host-tested five-word frame sanitizer that checks selectors, address shape/alignment, and privileged flags, then replaces user flags with the fixed reserved-bit value `0x2` (IF remains clear until process-aware interrupt scheduling is integrated). The caller must still verify executable and writable mappings through the process root. A malformed frame terminates the process with a reported status; never attempt the return and rely on a ring-0 `#GP` to catch it.
    43	- **NMI and interrupt policy:** no GS-base swap is needed on this entry path. An NMI can still arrive during entry; the current NMI/exception path is fatal-only, and this design does not claim to recover from it. Keep that behavior explicit until user-origin exception/NMI policy is implemented and tested. Ordinary maskable IRQs may resume only after the entry state and scheduler ownership are consistent.
    44	
    45	This design depends on a process-owned address space that maps the syscall entry/return code, IDT, GDT, TSS, and the active kernel stack safely. No Ring 3 execution should be enabled until the address-space implementation is reviewed and validated.
    46	
    47	### Process address spaces (design; root construction partially implemented)
    48	
    49	Use a separate four- or five-level root per process. The initial source is the retained active clone of Limine's hierarchy, not a curated clean-room root. Each process root owns its root page, all lower-half intermediate tables, and every user leaf frame. Keep the kernel-root owner alive for the lifetime of every process root. Copy only upper-half top-level entries from that owner into each process root; these entries are non-owning references to shared kernel subtrees, not deep copies, and must never be released by a process teardown. Do not copy lower-half entries from the kernel root.
    50	
    51	Before publishing a shared kernel subtree, validate its page-table structure and physical bounds and reject any effectively user-accessible leaf. U/S permission is the conjunction of every entry on a path, so a U/S bit on one non-leaf alone does not grant user access. When copying upper-half root entries, clear their U/S bit as defense in depth; a user leaf then cannot become accessible if a lower entry changes. `paging::validate_supervisor_kernel_half` implements the bounded, read-only structural/effective-permission preflight, but it does not install roots or prove physical backing is readable; the supplied reader must provide that access guarantee. Sharing the active clone means every accepted upper-half supervisor mapping and alias is present in every process CR3. This is not a curated kernel map or kernel-page-table isolation, and it provides no transient-execution protection. User mappings remain private to one process, are confined to the lower canonical half, preserve W^X, and are non-global in the first implementation.
    52	
    53	The kernel address-space owner is the only authority allowed to modify shared upper-half tables. Mutations must be serialized with local interrupts disabled on the current single-vCPU system and invalidate the affected local translation before the mapping change is relied on. A process root may not edit or reclaim shared tables. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::destroy` releases only private user leaves, intermediate tables, and the root; the caller must first switch CR3 to a different live root and invalidate this root's local non-global translations. Keep the shared kernel owner alive. PCID-aware invalidation and SMP shootdown remain unsupported and need a separate design.
    54	
    55	The current `CandidatePageTables` deep-clones the inherited hierarchy, tracks all cloned tables as owned, and holds an exclusive mutable borrow of one memory backend; it is not itself the process-address-space abstraction. `SharedKernelHalf` validates and snapshots the sanitized upper root entries while borrowing the kernel owner. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` uses one exclusive backend borrow for multiple private roots, maps allocator-owned user 4 KiB leaves only in inactive lower halves, retains writable/executable permission metadata, validates that an initial instruction pointer is executable and its stack pointer resolves to a writable NX page, offers one-page-bounded range-preflighted copy-in/copy-out through a separate `UserFrameMemory` backend, and destroys private leaf/table/root frames without freeing shared subtrees. The copy helpers are unsafe because the caller must provide kernel buffers that do not alias the process's mapped user frames. Host tests cover four- and five-level sharing, U/S sanitization, independent roots/mappings, initial user-state permission checks, copy permissions and cross-page copies, unmap ownership return, active-root release rejection, and allocation/prepare-failure rollback. The target Limine HHDM `UserFrameMemory` adapter is currently compiled only for the opt-in frame probe; `just frame-smoke` exercises bounded copy, zero-length, and out-of-range behavior on an allocator-owned frame. It is not yet connected to process-root copies. This is still not executable process support: callers must perform CR3 transitions and local TLB invalidation before marking a root inactive; no process scheduler, syscall entry, loader, or fault policy is integrated. Keep the kernel owner alive and immutable for the shared view's lifetime; callers must use a distinct page-table backend for process-owned tables.
    56	
    57	### Static ELF64 image validation and page initialization (partial)
    58	
    59	`src/elf.rs` parses little-endian x86_64 `ET_EXEC` images without allocation. It bounds the program-header count, load-segment count, and total mapped pages; checks file and virtual arithmetic, page alignment and `p_align` congruence, lower-half canonical ranges, non-overlapping page spans, readable segment flags, W^X, and that the entry point lies in a non-writable executable `PT_LOAD`. It rejects dynamic/interpreter and TLS segments and executable-stack requests. This initial format intentionally requires page-aligned load offsets/addresses and supports at most 64 program headers, 16 load segments, and 64 load pages. `populate_segment_page` copies one load page into an allocator-owned frame through `UserFrameMemory`, zero-filling bytes beyond the file payload. `load_into_process_root` now allocates, populates, selects cache attributes for, and maps every load page into an inactive `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` root. On failure, previously mapped pages remain owned by the root, the failure reports their count, and any unmapped frame is returned to the caller; destroying the newly created root is the recommended cleanup. Boot integration, stack allocation, activation, process lifecycle, and execution are not integrated.
    60	
    61	## ABI decisions still pending beyond v1
    62	
    63	The initial v1 versioning, error encoding, syscall numbers, and register-level request decoding are implemented in `src/syscall.rs`. Its host-tested `write_user_buffer` service validates descriptors 1/2, bypasses pointer validation for zero-length writes, preflights bounded user copies, and preserves short writes/partial-copy progress through a console-output interface; it is not called by a syscall dispatcher, and the target HHDM frame backend is not wired to a running process. Wait status transfer and no-restart behavior remain specified but unintegrated. `src/process.rs` adds a host-tested fixed-capacity identity/exit-state policy with parent/child tracking and nonblocking `try_wait`; scheduler blocking, address-space ownership, descriptor tables, and syscall integration remain unimplemented. Still to be specified before adding those operations are process-creation/exec and file-action semantics, general descriptor sharing/duplication/inheritance, read/open/close behavior, signal-like asynchronous delivery, clocks, and any additional structure layouts.
    64	
    65	## Suggested first user-visible slice
    66	
    67	After address spaces, scheduler, and storage primitives exist, implement a controlled `init` process with a small syscall subset: process exit, read/write through descriptors, open/close, and wait. Add end-to-end tests for invalid pointers, partial transfers, descriptor lifetime, process exit status, and ABI version negotiation before describing it as Unix-compatible.
```

```rustix/docs/architecture/interrupts.md
     1	# Interrupts and IRQ vector allocation
     2	
     3	## Current implementation
     4	
     5	`src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` installs the bootstrap GDT, TSS, exception gates for vectors 0–31, device IRQ stubs, and the APIC spurious-vector gate. Exceptions remain fatal-only. Maskable interrupts start disabled and are enabled only after the validated APIC route, registered handler, and acknowledgement path are ready.
     6	
     7	`src/irq.rs` provides a host-tested, allocation-free token allocator for device vectors `0x20..=0xef` except reserved syscall vector `0x80`; exception vectors and the reserved upper range are also excluded. The allocator now prevents generic device allocation/release of `0x80`, but no syscall gate or stub is installed yet. `rustix_irq_dispatch` invokes the registered handler, returns for the APIC spurious vector without EOI, and halts on unregistered/unexpected vectors. Device handlers own their EOI. Vector registration is performed with IF clear before the corresponding I/O APIC source is unmasked.
     8	
     9	The initial hardware target is single-vCPU QEMU `q35`: validated ACPI/MADT topology, local APIC and I/O APIC, masked legacy PIC routing, MADT-resolved ISA routes, and a periodic 8254 PIT tick near 100 Hz. OVMF smokes validate PIT delivery/EOI, non-yielding timer preemption, x87/SSE state preservation, and UART/keyboard IRQ delivery. Host tests cover vector ownership and PIT/time arithmetic; they do not replace privileged QEMU coverage.
    10	
    11	The scheduler is single-vCPU and supports cooperative waits/yields plus PIT-driven timer preemption. The timer handler advances ticks and sends APIC EOI before any scheduling switch. The common IRQ stub saves the interrupted x87/SSE state before Rust dispatch and restores the selected context before `IRETQ`; the context switch keeps aligned per-context FXSAVE areas. IRQ-safe spin locks save and restore the prior IF state, and the global heap uses one; scheduler mutations are separately serialized by masking local interrupts. IRQ/exception handlers remain bounded and allocation-free, and no current IRQ handler acquires the heap lock. SMP, per-CPU state, and physical-hardware validation remain future work.
```

```rustix/docs/architecture/memory.md
     1	# Memory-management direction
     2	
     3	## What exists now
     4	
     5	`src/memory.rs` contains an allocation-free `MemoryMapBuilder` that copies Limine ranges into validated half-open physical regions. It rejects empty ranges, `base + length` overflow, overlapping ranges, empty maps, and maps exceeding the fixed 256-region capacity. Known Limine types remain distinct, and unknown type values are preserved. Host-side tests cover range validation/classification, canonical-address boundaries, physical-width bounds, HHDM range arithmetic, and page-rounded ACPI span authorization. `MemoryMap::validate_acpi_span` accepts at most 64 KiB of requested ACPI bytes and validates the entire 4 KiB-rounded physical extent against contiguous ACPI-reclaimable/NVS regions; this is metadata only, not a mapping or dereference grant. `src/boot.rs` stores the resulting map in an owned boot snapshot and reports usable bytes.
     6	
     7	`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and coalesces adjacent free ranges. The boot path additionally subtracts the validated kernel-image and boot-stack physical spans (`from_memory_map_excluding`) so a loader mislabeling them as usable cannot cause the allocator to hand out own-kernel pages. The ownership contract assumes one allocator instance per physical map: within that instance, each eligible frame is owned either by its free-range table or by a non-copyable `Frame` token while allocated. The public constructor does not enforce unique instances, so callers must not initialize multiple allocators for the same physical map; the boot path retains one allocator in `BootInfo`. `allocate` returns `None` when no free frame remains. `deallocate` consumes the token only on success; on any error, including free-range-table exhaustion, it returns a `DeallocationError` containing the original token and leaves allocator state unchanged. The range tables each have a fixed `MAX_FRAME_RANGES` capacity, so fragmentation can prevent a frame from being returned until nearby ranges coalesce. The active cloned page-table hierarchy owns its page-table frames; the frame allocator is otherwise not yet a general-purpose virtual-memory service.
     8	
     9	`Frame::address()` is a physical address value, not a dereferenceable pointer and not a proof that the frame is mapped. CPU diagnostics now read `CR4.LA57` to report the active linear-address width (48 or 57 bits) and query `CPUID.80000008H` for physical and maximum linear-address widths when available. Boot-protocol pointers are checked against the active width, with host tests for 48- and 57-bit canonical boundaries. These facts do not prove that any physical address is mapped.
    10	
    11	`src/paging.rs` contains host-tested mapping and cache policy plus a bounded candidate-root builder. The CR3 decoder validates physical-address width and reserved bits and interprets its low 12 bits according to active `CR4.PCIDE`; it does not dereference the root. The mapping-range validator requires known physical width, checked aligned bounds, canonical virtual endpoints in one canonical half, and rejects writable-executable permissions. It can encode one 4 KiB leaf PTE with supervisor/user and write permissions, NX when EFER.NXE is confirmed, and a bounded PAT index. `PatLayout` parses supplied `IA32_PAT` values and selects WB, UC, or WC indexes. `MtrrMemoryType`, `VariableMtrr`, `FixedMtrrRanges`, and `MtrrLayout` resolve address-specific MTRR types, including fixed-range priority and defined variable-overlap rules; undefined overlaps fail closed. `MtrrRegisters::validated_layout` validates captured capability/default-type bits, register counts and fixed-range presence, WC support, and variable-mask shape/alignment before producing an owned layout. Rustix supports contiguous power-of-two variable masks and explicitly rejects unsupported discontinuous masks. The layout combines address-specific MTRR type and PAT selection according to Intel SDM Table 11-7 only when `CR0.CD` and `CR0.NW` are clear. Host tests cover all 30 documented MTRR/PAT pairs and malformed inputs. A pure range selector chooses an index only when its effective type is uniform throughout all fixed/variable MTRR boundaries in an aligned extent; selected attributes remain bound to that physical extent. The selector itself does not inspect PTEs, aliases, or frame ownership. Boot reads CR0 without modifying it, validates captured MTRR/PAT state, and reports a diagnostic PA 0 resolution; this does not assert the live PTE's type. MTRR capture is bounded to 32 variable pairs and rejects excess capacity without partial state.
    12

Both paths require NXE, support four- and five-level paths, and hold one exclusive mutable borrow of the unsafe memory backend so prepared handles cannot be mixed across backends. Borrowed ACPI mappings can only be installed and removed while the candidate is inactive. The boot-only ACPI reader performs temporary CR3 switches to read validated pages and removes them before permanent activation. The default boot path clones the complete reachable Limine hierarchy, hardens kernel HHDM aliases to text/rodata R/NX and data RW/NX while preserving PAT bits, verifies critical translations, activates the cloned CR3, and retains the candidate tokens for the active root's lifetime. The CR3 transition invalidates the active PCID and toggles CR4.PGE when enabled; the same invalidation is used if verification restores the inherited root. General candidate mutation and release are rejected while active, but narrow owned-page active map/unmap operations are supported under the single-CPU, IF-disabled contract and invalidate the local TLB before ownership is returned. Host tests cover transactional rollback and ownership; `just active-map-smoke` validates active mapping, access, invalidation, and reclamation in QEMU. The type never writes CR3. The HHDM adapter derives table pointers only from complete allocator-owned `Usable` frames through checked arithmetic.
    14

The kernel and HHDM aliases retain the same PAT index; MTRR state is unchanged. This is not a fresh address-space policy or a hardware-level exhaustive inventory, and it does not reclaim the inherited root or bootloader memory.
    16	
    17	The effective-type resolver follows [Intel SDM Vol. 3A §11.5.2.2, Table 11-7](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/671447/325384-sdm-vol-3abcd.pdf), which applies when normal caching is enabled (`CR0.CD=0`, `CR0.NW=0`). Its footnotes distinguish UC selected by an MTRR from UC selected by a page-table entry (the latter involves cache snooping and aliasing concerns); they also identify combinations that older manual editions called undefined but current processors supporting both PAT and MTRRs resolve as shown. Arbitrary physical access is not permitted: validated ACPI pages use the bounded read-only/NX reader; HHDM table access is limited to checked full-frame paths. Rustix-owned mappings should be non-executable by default; MMIO requires an explicit device range and cache policy, and guard regions must remain unmapped. The APIC MMIO validator rejects every known memory-map class except `Reserved` and `Unknown`; unreported ranges remain dependent on validated platform data. The active clone owns its page-table frames but leaves inherited leaf frames and the old root unreclaimed. The global heap begins with a 256 KiB BSS arena and can demand-map up to 1 MiB of allocator-backed pages in its reserved virtual range. Its IRQ-save lock prevents local interrupt reentrancy, but allocation remains forbidden in IRQ/exception handlers. Bootstrap exceptions remain fatal, while selected maskable IRQs are enabled only after APIC routes and handlers are ready.
    22	
    23	## Active-root preservation and remaining limits
    24	
    25	The transition clones the complete reachable inherited hierarchy rather than building a clean address space. It preserves all reachable present leaves and non-present entries, owns each cloned intermediate table, and fails closed on malformed entries, unsupported page sizes, cross-level table aliases, or fixed-capacity exhaustion. Kernel text/rodata/data HHDM aliases are then adjusted to avoid writable-executable aliases. Limine's original root and leaf frames remain intact.
    26	
    27	- **Kernel ELF image:** `linker.ld` places `.text`, `.rodata`, `.limine_requests`, `.data`, `.bss`, and `.got` in three `PT_LOAD` segments: RX text, read-only rodata, and RW data/BSS. It exports `__kernel_start` and `__kernel_end` around the complete loadable image, plus page-aligned bounds for each segment. `BootInfo` checks that Limine's reported virtual base matches the linker start, validates ordered contiguous segment bounds covering the rounded image, derives corresponding half-open physical ranges from the executable physical base with checked arithmetic, and validates canonical virtual and reported physical address widths. The release ELF and QEMU runtime report both showed the three aligned ranges on 2026-10-21. The RX, R/NX, and RW/NX labels describe the linker segment intent; these are linker/boot metadata, not proof that the inherited page tables map every page or enforce those permissions, nor proof that loader pointers are readable. The memory-map `ExecutableAndModules` entries remain illustrative, not an authoritative kernel-image extent.
    28	- **Active stack and `BootInfo`:** The assembly `_start` shim captures Limine's entry `RSP` before any Rust prologue. Under the SysV entry convention the synthetic return slot occupies 8 bytes, so `RSP + 8` is the exclusive stack top. Rustix requests a 256 KiB Limine stack and requires the stack-size response; `BootInfo` records and validates that requested span through the HHDM, including its `BootloaderReclaimable` backing. The loader may allocate more, and no guard page is inferred. QEMU transition tests walk all 64 requested stack pages.
    29	- **Kernel static data:** `RAM_FILESYSTEM`, GDT, IDT, TSS, the ring-0 stack, and double-fault IST stack are static BSS/data in the kernel image. Exception entry also requires the handler code and the TSS/IDT references to remain mapped. Preserve the complete relevant data/BSS pages and stack pages.
    30	- **Limine request data:** request records are in the kernel's writable `.limine_requests` segment. Response objects and the memory-map pointer array are bootloader-reclaimable; `capture_boot_information` copies the values used later, and the shell does not retain those pointers. Keep them mapped until the copy and validation finish; any later reclaim must be explicit rather than reclaiming the whole bootloader-reclaimable class.
    31	- **Inherited page tables:** Limine places its page tables in bootloader-reclaimable memory, but their layout is unspecified. `BootInfo` captures raw CR3 and validates the decoded root address and active low-bit mode. It verifies kernel segments, the requested stack span, and the candidate-root HHDM alias before switching; afterward it verifies CR3 and the critical paths again. The inherited root and its backing pages remain untouched and are not reclaimed.
    32	- **Devices:** COM1 uses x86 port I/O and needs no MMIO virtual mapping. Rustix does not currently request or use a framebuffer. Any future framebuffer or device-register mapping needs an explicit physical range and cache policy.
    33	
    34	## Permissions and cache policy of the active clone
    35	
    36	The active root preserves Limine's inherited kernel virtual mappings and their cache attributes. Before switching, Rustix requires NXE and enforces the linker permissions for every kernel-image HHDM alias: text and rodata are read-only/NX, and data/BSS/GOT are RW/NX. This prevents writable-executable aliases without discarding the HHDM alias. Huge-page leaves are split as necessary; unaffected entries retain their mappings and PAT/MTRR effective types. The remainder of the HHDM and all non-kernel aliases remain as Limine supplied them, so this is not yet a comprehensive Rustix mapping policy.
    37	
    38	Preserve the inherited PAT/MTRR configuration during the first transition. The boot report validates captured registers and computes a diagnostic effective type from the active PAT/MTRR values under normal caching. A separate pure selector can choose an index whose effective type remains uniform across an aligned physical range; the selector itself does not inspect PTEs or aliases. The opt-in `just frame-smoke` probe now compares effective types of the inherited kernel and HHDM aliases for kernel-image pages, but it is not a full alias inventory. The pure combination follows Intel SDM Table 11-7; it is not a generic rule for legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations. The active transition retains the inherited PAT and MTRR state and changes no cache-selection bits. The page-table split copies large-page PAT selection to the equivalent 4 KiB/2 MiB entries. Future MMIO mappings must still use explicit device ranges and a verified cache policy; do not infer MMIO from generic reserved memory-map entries. COM1 uses port I/O and requires no MMIO mapping.
    39	
    40	Do not use huge pages in the first root; add them only when physical coverage, permissions, and cache attributes are uniform across the entire huge-page extent. Future Rustix-owned downward-growing stacks should have at least one 4 KiB unmapped guard page below them. The Limine bootstrap stack has no known guard, so none may be assumed there.
    41	
    42	Never modify Limine's active page tables in place. `src/paging.rs` builds an owned clone in allocator-issued frames, can split inherited large pages to update leaf permissions, and supports transactional 4 KiB map/unmap operations before activation. The default boot path validates critical translations and kernel alias permissions, switches CR3 while invalidating stale global translations via a CR4.PGE toggle when needed, verifies the active root, and retains its frame tokens for the active lifetime. The inherited root and backing memory remain intact. This preserves inherited mappings rather than constructing a new address space; broader mapping inventory, non-kernel permission policy, reclamation, and a general mapping service remain future work.
    43	
    44	## Planned memory layers
    45	
    46	1. **Validated physical regions:** implemented as a fixed-capacity owned snapshot; allocator ownership and reclaim policy remain future work.
    47	2. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; table and leaf mappings use allocator-issued tokens. The active mapping smoke validates one owned page's map/access/unmap/reclamation path.
    48	3. **Kernel virtual memory:** Rustix runs on an active clone of Limine's hierarchy and hardens kernel-image HHDM aliases. Narrow active owned-page map/unmap operations invalidate the local TLB; this is not a clean-room address-space policy or general MMIO subsystem.

The view borrows the kernel-root owner, which must remain alive and immutable; the root set uses one exclusive backend borrow for its roots. `destroy` is permitted only after the caller switches away and invalidates the root's local non-global translations; PCID-aware teardown is unsupported. The caller still owns CR3 transitions. Mapping metadata retains writable and executable permissions, and `validate_initial_user_state` requires an executable non-writable entry page plus a writable non-executable stack page before a future transition. Generic copy-in/copy-out helpers preflight lower-half mapped ranges and permissions and access owned frames through a separate `UserFrameMemory` contract. `Elf64Image::load_into_process_root` now allocates, populates, cache-selects, and maps bounded ELF load pages; on failure the caller must reclaim the reported unconsumed frame and partial root state. This is not a curated kernel mapping policy or kernel-page-table isolation.
    51	
    52	## Invariants to preserve
    53	
    54	- Physical ranges use checked arithmetic and the half-open convention `[start, end)`.
    55	- Only complete frames in validated `Usable` regions enter the allocator; the first MiB remains reserved. Firmware and loader-reclaimable regions are not silently promoted to free memory.
    56	- Under the single-allocator-per-physical-map contract, a frame is represented by one allocator-free range or one caller-owned, non-copyable `Frame` token. Only a successful `deallocate` transfers the token back to the allocator; errors return the token and leave allocator ranges and accounting unchanged. The current public constructor relies on callers to enforce unique allocator instances.
    57	- `allocate` returns `None` on frame exhaustion. Metadata-capacity exhaustion is an explicit error, never silent loss of a frame.
    58	- A `Frame` address is physical, not directly dereferenceable. HHDM translation and table access are limited to checked full-frame token-based paths that rely on Limine's documented mapping contract. Candidate mutations are allowed only before activation and only in owned tables. The active cloned root retains its ownership tokens and rejects mutation/release until an explicit, reviewed CR3 transition away from it.

    60	- User-controlled addresses are validated on every syscall boundary; prior validation is not a substitute for access checks during later copies.
    61	- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, exhaustion, and unchanged state/ownership on failure.
    62	
    63	The active root is a full clone of Limine's reachable hierarchy with kernel HHDM alias W^X hardening, not a clean-room Rustix address space. Heap growth is bounded to a fixed virtual reservation and 1 MiB of frame-backed pages. Broader alias/MMIO coverage, frame reclamation, and physical-hardware validation remain outstanding.
```

```rustix/src/heap.rs
     2	//!
     3	//! The bootstrap arena is 256 KiB and tracks at most 128 allocations. An optional

     5	//! its own fixed allocation table and a caller-supplied transactional mapper.

    10	//! remains forbidden in IRQ/exception context to keep handlers bounded and
```
