//! A bounded kernel heap with a static bootstrap arena and optional frame-backed growth.
//!
//! The bootstrap arena is 256 KiB and tracks at most 128 allocations. An optional
//! extension maps pages on demand inside a caller-reserved virtual range, with
//! its own fixed allocation table and a caller-supplied transactional mapper.
//! Growth is bounded; allocation fails when either arena or metadata is full.
//!
//! The global wrapper serializes access with an IRQ-save spin lock. The lock
//! prevents a local interrupt from re-entering a held allocator lock; allocation
//! remains forbidden in IRQ/exception context to keep handlers bounded and
//! allocation-free.

use crate::sync::{IrqSpinLock, IrqSpinLockGuard};
use core::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout};
use core::cell::UnsafeCell;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

/// Fixed capacity of the initial BSS-backed kernel heap.
pub const KERNEL_HEAP_CAPACITY: usize = 256 * 1024;
/// Maximum number of live allocations tracked by the initial kernel heap.
pub const KERNEL_HEAP_MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize = 128;

/// The statically allocated heap type used by the kernel binary.
pub type KernelHeap = LockedHeap<KERNEL_HEAP_CAPACITY, KERNEL_HEAP_MAX_ALLOCATIONS>;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum HeapError {
    ZeroSizedAllocation,
    AllocationTableFull,
    OutOfMemory,
    AddressOverflow,
    InvalidPointer,
    LayoutMismatch,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Allocation {
    start: usize,
    size: usize,
    alignment: usize,
}

struct FixedHeap<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> {
    arena: [u8; HEAP_SIZE],
    allocations: [Option<Allocation>; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
}

impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> FixedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS> {
    const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            arena: [0; HEAP_SIZE],
            allocations: [None; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
        }
    }

    fn allocate(&mut self, layout: Layout) -> Result<NonNull<u8>, HeapError> {
        if layout.size() == 0 {
            return Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation);
        }
        let slot = self
            .allocations
            .iter()
            .position(Option::is_none)
            .ok_or(HeapError::AllocationTableFull)?;
        let start = self.find_gap(layout)?;
        self.allocations[slot] = Some(Allocation {
            start,
            size: layout.size(),
            alignment: layout.align(),
        });

        let pointer = self.arena.as_mut_ptr().wrapping_add(start);
        NonNull::new(pointer).ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)
    }

    fn deallocate(&mut self, pointer: NonNull<u8>, layout: Layout) -> Result<(), HeapError> {
        if layout.size() == 0 {
            return Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation);
        }
        let arena_start = self.arena.as_ptr() as usize;
        let allocation_start = (pointer.as_ptr() as usize)
            .checked_sub(arena_start)
            .filter(|offset| *offset < HEAP_SIZE)
            .ok_or(HeapError::InvalidPointer)?;

        for allocation in &mut self.allocations {
            let Some(active) = *allocation else {
                continue;
            };
            if active.start != allocation_start {
                continue;
            }
            if active.size != layout.size() || active.alignment != layout.align() {
                return Err(HeapError::LayoutMismatch);
            }
            *allocation = None;
            return Ok(());
        }
        Err(HeapError::InvalidPointer)
    }

    fn find_gap(&self, layout: Layout) -> Result<usize, HeapError> {
        let arena_start = self.arena.as_ptr() as usize;
        let mut candidate = 0usize;

        loop {
            let candidate_address = arena_start
                .checked_add(candidate)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let aligned_address = candidate_address
                .checked_add(layout.align() - 1)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?
                & !(layout.align() - 1);
            let start = aligned_address
                .checked_sub(arena_start)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let end = start
                .checked_add(layout.size())
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            if end > HEAP_SIZE {
                return Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory);
            }

            let mut conflicting_end = None;
            for allocation in self.allocations.iter().flatten() {
                let allocation_end = allocation
                    .start
                    .checked_add(allocation.size)
                    .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
                if start < allocation_end && allocation.start < end {
                    conflicting_end = Some(
                        conflicting_end
                            .map_or(allocation_end, |end: usize| end.max(allocation_end)),
                    );
                }
            }

            match conflicting_end {
                Some(end) => candidate = end,
                None => return Ok(start),
            }
        }
    }
}

pub type HeapPageMapper = unsafe fn(context: *mut (), first_page: usize, page_count: usize) -> bool;

struct FrameBackedHeap<const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> {
    base: usize,
    capacity_pages: usize,
    mapped_pages: usize,
    allocations: [Option<Allocation>; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
    context: *mut (),
    map_pages: Option<HeapPageMapper>,
}

impl<const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> FrameBackedHeap<MAX_ALLOCATIONS> {
    const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            base: 0,
            capacity_pages: 0,
            mapped_pages: 0,
            allocations: [None; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
            context: core::ptr::null_mut(),
            map_pages: None,
        }
    }

    fn configure(
        &mut self,
        base: usize,
        capacity_pages: usize,
        context: *mut (),
        map_pages: HeapPageMapper,
    ) -> Result<(), FrameHeapInitError> {
        let capacity = capacity_pages
            .checked_mul(PAGE_BYTES)
            .and_then(|bytes| base.checked_add(bytes));
        if self.map_pages.is_some()
            || base == 0
            || !base.is_multiple_of(PAGE_BYTES)
            || capacity_pages == 0
            || capacity.is_none()
        {
            return Err(if self.map_pages.is_some() {
                FrameHeapInitError::AlreadyConfigured
            } else {
                FrameHeapInitError::InvalidRange
            });
        }
        self.base = base;
        self.capacity_pages = capacity_pages;
        self.context = context;
        self.map_pages = Some(map_pages);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn seal_growth(&mut self) {
        self.context = core::ptr::null_mut();
        self.map_pages = None;
    }

    fn contains_pointer(&self, pointer: usize) -> bool {
        self.capacity_pages
            .checked_mul(PAGE_BYTES)
            .and_then(|capacity| self.base.checked_add(capacity).map(|end| (capacity, end)))
            .is_some_and(|(capacity, end)| capacity != 0 && (self.base..end).contains(&pointer))
    }

    fn allocate(&mut self, layout: Layout) -> Result<NonNull<u8>, HeapError> {
        if layout.size() == 0 {
            return Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation);
        }
        let slot = self
            .allocations
            .iter()
            .position(Option::is_none)
            .ok_or(HeapError::AllocationTableFull)?;
        let start = self.find_gap(layout)?;
        let end = start
            .checked_add(layout.size())
            .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // `end` is already bounded by this heap's capacity, so this division
        // cannot overflow the page count.
        let required_pages = end
            .checked_add(PAGE_BYTES - 1)
            .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?
            / PAGE_BYTES;
        if required_pages > self.mapped_pages {
            let map_pages = self.map_pages.ok_or(HeapError::OutOfMemory)?;
            let first_page = self.mapped_pages;
            let page_count = required_pages - first_page;
            // SAFETY: Configuration is unsafe at the public boundary. The
            // mapper contract requires an all-or-nothing mapping of this range.
            if !unsafe { map_pages(self.context, first_page, page_count) } {
                return Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory);
            }
            self.mapped_pages = required_pages;
        }

        self.allocations[slot] = Some(Allocation {
            start,
            size: layout.size(),
            alignment: layout.align(),
        });
        let pointer = self
            .base
            .checked_add(start)
            .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
        NonNull::new(pointer as *mut u8).ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)
    }

    fn deallocate(&mut self, pointer: NonNull<u8>, layout: Layout) -> Result<(), HeapError> {
        if layout.size() == 0 {
            return Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation);
        }
        let allocation_start = (pointer.as_ptr() as usize)
            .checked_sub(self.base)
            .filter(|offset| *offset < self.capacity_pages.saturating_mul(PAGE_BYTES))
            .ok_or(HeapError::InvalidPointer)?;
        for allocation in &mut self.allocations {
            let Some(active) = *allocation else {
                continue;
            };
            if active.start != allocation_start {
                continue;
            }
            if active.size != layout.size() || active.alignment != layout.align() {
                return Err(HeapError::LayoutMismatch);
            }
            *allocation = None;
            return Ok(());
        }
        Err(HeapError::InvalidPointer)
    }

    fn find_gap(&self, layout: Layout) -> Result<usize, HeapError> {
        let capacity = self
            .capacity_pages
            .checked_mul(PAGE_BYTES)
            .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
        let mut candidate = 0usize;
        loop {
            let candidate_address = self
                .base
                .checked_add(candidate)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let aligned_address = candidate_address
                .checked_add(layout.align() - 1)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?
                & !(layout.align() - 1);
            let start = aligned_address
                .checked_sub(self.base)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let end = start
                .checked_add(layout.size())
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            if end > capacity {
                return Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory);
            }
            let mut conflicting_end = None;
            for allocation in self.allocations.iter().flatten() {
                let allocation_end = allocation
                    .start
                    .checked_add(allocation.size)
                    .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
                if start < allocation_end && allocation.start < end {
                    conflicting_end = Some(
                        conflicting_end
                            .map_or(allocation_end, |current: usize| current.max(allocation_end)),
                    );
                }
            }
            match conflicting_end {
                Some(end) => candidate = end,
                None => return Ok(start),
            }
        }
    }
}

const PAGE_BYTES: usize = 4096;

/// Errors reported while installing the optional frame-backed heap region.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FrameHeapInitError {
    InvalidRange,
    AlreadyConfigured,
}

/// A `GlobalAlloc` wrapper for the fixed bootstrap arena and bounded growth region.
///
/// The bootstrap arena and callback context must remain at stable addresses for
/// the lifetime of allocations. The growth callback must map the complete page
/// range transactionally and must not allocate or call this heap recursively.
pub struct LockedHeap<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> {
    lock: IrqSpinLock<()>,
    heap: UnsafeCell<FixedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>>,
    growth: UnsafeCell<FrameBackedHeap<MAX_ALLOCATIONS>>,
}

// SAFETY: `heap` and `growth` are accessed mutably only while the IRQ-save
// spin lock is held. Allocation remains prohibited in interrupt context.
unsafe impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> Sync
    for LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>
{
}

impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS> {
    /// Construct an empty allocator. The backing arena is zero-initialized BSS.
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            lock: IrqSpinLock::new(()),
            heap: UnsafeCell::new(FixedHeap::new()),
            growth: UnsafeCell::new(FrameBackedHeap::new()),
        }
    }

    /// Configure one reserved virtual range for demand-mapped heap growth.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The caller must reserve the complete range exclusively, keep `context`
    /// alive and stable until the allocator is no longer used, and provide a
    /// mapper that atomically maps all requested pages or leaves the range
    /// unchanged. The mapper must not allocate or re-enter this allocator.
    pub unsafe fn initialize_frame_backed_region(
        &self,
        base: usize,
        capacity_pages: usize,
        context: *mut (),
        map_pages: HeapPageMapper,
    ) -> Result<(), FrameHeapInitError> {
        let _lock = self.acquire();
        // SAFETY: The lock grants exclusive access to the growth configuration.
        let growth = unsafe { &mut *self.growth.get() };
        growth.configure(base, capacity_pages, context, map_pages)
    }

    /// Disable future frame-backed growth while retaining already-mapped pages and allocations.
    ///
    /// This also clears the callback context pointer, ending the heap's ownership
    /// dependency on the page-table owner. Call before creating shared process
    /// roots that immutably borrow that owner. Allocations fitting in currently
    /// mapped heap pages continue to work; requests requiring new pages fail.
    pub fn seal_frame_backed_growth(&self) {
        let _lock = self.acquire();
        // SAFETY: The IRQ-save lock gives exclusive access to growth metadata and
        // waits for any synchronous mapping callback to finish before clearing it.
        unsafe { &mut *self.growth.get() }.seal_growth();
    }

    fn acquire(&self) -> IrqSpinLockGuard<'_, ()> {
        self.lock.lock()
    }
}

impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> Default
    for LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>
{
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

unsafe impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> GlobalAlloc
    for LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>
{
    unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        // Allocation from interrupt/exception context can deadlock the only
        // CPU with IF masked; the allocator contract forbids it. Enforced in
        // debug builds; release builds document the contract instead.
        debug_assert!(
            crate::sync::INTERRUPT_DEPTH.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) == 0,
            "kernel heap allocation from interrupt/exception context"
        );
        let _lock = self.acquire();
        // SAFETY: The lock grants exclusive access to both allocator regions.
        let heap = unsafe { &mut *self.heap.get() };
        // SAFETY: The same lock exclusively protects the growth metadata and
        // callback configuration. Its mapper contract forbids allocator reentry.
        let growth = unsafe { &mut *self.growth.get() };
        heap.allocate(layout)
            .or_else(|_| growth.allocate(layout))
            .map(NonNull::as_ptr)
            .unwrap_or(core::ptr::null_mut())
    }

    unsafe fn dealloc(&self, pointer: *mut u8, layout: Layout) {
        let Some(pointer) = NonNull::new(pointer) else {
            return;
        };
        let _lock = self.acquire();
        // SAFETY: The lock grants exclusive access to both allocator regions. The
        // GlobalAlloc caller must provide a live allocation and its original layout.
        let heap = unsafe { &mut *self.heap.get() };
        // SAFETY: The same lock exclusively protects growth allocation metadata.
        let growth = unsafe { &mut *self.growth.get() };
        if growth.contains_pointer(pointer.as_ptr() as usize) {
            let result = growth.deallocate(pointer, layout);
            debug_assert!(
                result.is_ok(),
                "frame-backed dealloc failed; possible double-free or layout mismatch"
            );
        } else {
            let result = heap.deallocate(pointer, layout);
            debug_assert!(
                result.is_ok(),
                "arena dealloc failed; possible double-free or layout mismatch"
            );
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use core::alloc::Layout;
    use core::assert_eq;

    use super::{FixedHeap, FrameBackedHeap, HeapError, LockedHeap, PAGE_BYTES};

    #[repr(align(4096))]
    struct TestRegion([u8; PAGE_BYTES * 2]);

    #[derive(Default)]
    struct MapTrace {
        mapped_pages: usize,
        fail: bool,
    }

    unsafe fn test_map_pages(context: *mut (), _first_page: usize, page_count: usize) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: Tests pass a live, exclusively used `MapTrace` pointer.
        let trace = unsafe { &mut *context.cast::<MapTrace>() };
        if trace.fail {
            return false;
        }
        trace.mapped_pages += page_count;
        true
    }

    #[test]
    fn honors_layout_alignment_and_reuses_freed_allocations() {
        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<256, 4>::new();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(37, 64).unwrap();
        let allocation = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocation.as_ptr() as usize % layout.align(), 0);

        // SAFETY: The pointer names a live allocation of the requested size.
        unsafe { allocation.as_ptr().write_bytes(0xa5, layout.size()) };
        for index in 0..layout.size() {
            // SAFETY: `index` is bounded by the live allocation's size.
            assert_eq!(unsafe { allocation.as_ptr().add(index).read() }, 0xa5);
        }

        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();
        let reused = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(reused, allocation);
        heap.deallocate(reused, layout).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_arena_exhaustion_and_reuses_a_coalesced_gap() {
        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<128, 4>::new();
        let full_layout = Layout::from_size_align(64, 1).unwrap();
        let first = heap.allocate(full_layout).unwrap();
        let second = heap.allocate(full_layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            heap.allocate(Layout::from_size_align(1, 1).unwrap()),
            Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory)
        );

        heap.deallocate(first, full_layout).unwrap();
        let smaller_layout = Layout::from_size_align(32, 1).unwrap();
        let reused = heap.allocate(smaller_layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(reused, first);
        heap.deallocate(reused, smaller_layout).unwrap();
        heap.deallocate(second, full_layout).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_allocation_metadata_exhaustion() {
        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<128, 1>::new();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(8, 1).unwrap();
        let allocation = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(heap.allocate(layout), Err(HeapError::AllocationTableFull));
        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();
        assert!(heap.allocate(layout).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_invalid_pointer_and_layout_without_releasing_memory() {
        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<128, 4>::new();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(16, 8).unwrap();
        let allocation = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        let wrong_layout = Layout::from_size_align(8, 8).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            heap.deallocate(allocation, wrong_layout),
            Err(HeapError::LayoutMismatch)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            heap.deallocate(NonNull::dangling(), layout),
            Err(HeapError::InvalidPointer)
        );
        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            heap.deallocate(allocation, layout),
            Err(HeapError::InvalidPointer)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn frame_backed_heap_maps_on_demand_and_reuses_freed_allocations() {
        let mut region = TestRegion([0; PAGE_BYTES * 2]);
        let mut trace = MapTrace::default();
        let mut heap = FrameBackedHeap::<4>::new();
        heap.configure(
            region.0.as_mut_ptr() as usize,
            2,
            core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(trace).cast(),
            test_map_pages,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(5000, 16).unwrap();
        let allocation = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocation.as_ptr() as usize % layout.align(), 0);
        assert_eq!(trace.mapped_pages, 2);
        assert_eq!(heap.mapped_pages, 2);
        // SAFETY: The test mapper records a successful mapping of the complete
        // aligned in-memory region used as the backing store for this heap.
        unsafe { allocation.as_ptr().add(4999).write(0xa5) };
        // SAFETY: The final byte lies within the live 5000-byte allocation.
        assert_eq!(unsafe { allocation.as_ptr().add(4999).read() }, 0xa5);
        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();
        let reused = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(reused, allocation);
        assert_eq!(trace.mapped_pages, 2);
        heap.deallocate(reused, layout).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn sealing_frame_backed_growth_keeps_mapped_pages_and_releases_context() {
        let mut region = TestRegion([0; PAGE_BYTES * 2]);
        let mut trace = MapTrace::default();
        let heap = LockedHeap::<128, 4>::new();
        let bootstrap_layout = Layout::from_size_align(128, 1).unwrap();
        let growth_layout = Layout::from_size_align(8, 1).unwrap();
        // SAFETY: `region` and `trace` remain alive and uniquely used throughout
        // the test; the mapper records a complete successful mapping.
        unsafe {
            heap.initialize_frame_backed_region(
                region.0.as_mut_ptr() as usize,
                2,
                core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(trace).cast(),
                test_map_pages,
            )
        }
        .unwrap();
        // SAFETY: Layouts are nonzero and the heap was initialized above.
        let bootstrap = unsafe { GlobalAlloc::alloc(&heap, bootstrap_layout) };
        // SAFETY: Layouts are nonzero and the configured mapper has a live context.
        let first_growth = unsafe { GlobalAlloc::alloc(&heap, growth_layout) };
        assert!(!bootstrap.is_null());
        assert!(!first_growth.is_null());
        assert_eq!(trace.mapped_pages, 1);

        heap.seal_frame_backed_growth();
        // SAFETY: The wrapper is exclusively used in this test after sealing.
        let growth = unsafe { &*heap.growth.get() };
        assert!(growth.map_pages.is_none());
        assert!(growth.context.is_null());

        // SAFETY: `first_growth` is a live allocation with its original layout.
        unsafe { GlobalAlloc::dealloc(&heap, first_growth, growth_layout) };
        // Already-mapped pages remain available after the callback is severed.
        // SAFETY: Layout is nonzero and reuses the released mapped range.
        let reused_growth = unsafe { GlobalAlloc::alloc(&heap, growth_layout) };
        assert!(!reused_growth.is_null());
        assert_eq!(trace.mapped_pages, 1);

        let beyond_mapped_layout = Layout::from_size_align(PAGE_BYTES + 1, 1).unwrap();
        // SAFETY: The request is bounded but exceeds the two-page test region;
        // after sealing, required growth is rejected without calling the mapper.
        let beyond_mapped = unsafe { GlobalAlloc::alloc(&heap, beyond_mapped_layout) };
        assert!(beyond_mapped.is_null());
        assert_eq!(trace.mapped_pages, 1);

        // SAFETY: Both returned pointers are live allocations with matching layouts.
        unsafe {
            GlobalAlloc::dealloc(&heap, reused_growth, growth_layout);
            GlobalAlloc::dealloc(&heap, bootstrap, bootstrap_layout);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn failed_frame_backed_growth_leaves_heap_metadata_unchanged() {
        let mut region = TestRegion([0; PAGE_BYTES * 2]);
        let mut trace = MapTrace {
            mapped_pages: 0,
            fail: true,
        };
        let mut heap = FrameBackedHeap::<2>::new();
        heap.configure(
            region.0.as_mut_ptr() as usize,
            2,
            core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(trace).cast(),
            test_map_pages,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(PAGE_BYTES + 1, 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(heap.allocate(layout), Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory));
        assert_eq!(heap.mapped_pages, 0);
        assert!(heap.allocations.iter().all(Option::is_none));
        assert_eq!(trace.mapped_pages, 0);

        trace.fail = false;
        let allocation = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(heap.mapped_pages, 2);
        assert_eq!(trace.mapped_pages, 2);
        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_zero_sized_layouts() {
        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<128, 4>::new();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(0, 8).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(heap.allocate(layout), Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation));
    }

    use core::ptr::NonNull;
}

//! A bounded kernel heap with a static bootstrap arena and optional frame-backed growth.
//!
//! The bootstrap arena is 256 KiB and tracks at most 128 allocations. An optional
//! extension maps pages on demand inside a caller-reserved virtual range, with
//! its own fixed allocation table and a caller-supplied transactional mapper.
//! Growth is bounded; allocation fails when either arena or metadata is full.
//!
//! The global wrapper serializes access with an IRQ-save spin lock. The lock
//! prevents a local interrupt from re-entering a held allocator lock; allocation
//! remains forbidden in IRQ/exception context to keep handlers bounded and
//! allocation-free.

use crate::sync::{IrqSpinLock, IrqSpinLockGuard};
use core::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout};
use core::cell::UnsafeCell;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

/// Fixed capacity of the initial BSS-backed kernel heap.
pub const KERNEL_HEAP_CAPACITY: usize = 256 * 1024;
/// Maximum number of live allocations tracked by the initial kernel heap.
pub const KERNEL_HEAP_MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize = 128;

/// The statically allocated heap type used by the kernel binary.
pub type KernelHeap = LockedHeap<KERNEL_HEAP_CAPACITY, KERNEL_HEAP_MAX_ALLOCATIONS>;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum HeapError {
    ZeroSizedAllocation,
    AllocationTableFull,
    OutOfMemory,
    AddressOverflow,
    InvalidPointer,
    LayoutMismatch,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Allocation {
    start: usize,
    size: usize,
    alignment: usize,
}

struct FixedHeap<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> {
    arena: [u8; HEAP_SIZE],
    allocations: [Option<Allocation>; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
}

impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> FixedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS> {
    const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            arena: [0; HEAP_SIZE],
            allocations: [None; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
        }
    }

    fn allocate(&mut self, layout: Layout) -> Result<NonNull<u8>, HeapError> {
        if layout.size() == 0 {
            return Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation);
        }
        let slot = self
            .allocations
            .iter()
            .position(Option::is_none)
            .ok_or(HeapError::AllocationTableFull)?;
        let start = self.find_gap(layout)?;
        self.allocations[slot] = Some(Allocation {
            start,
            size: layout.size(),
            alignment: layout.align(),
        });

        let pointer = self.arena.as_mut_ptr().wrapping_add(start);
        NonNull::new(pointer).ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)
    }

    fn deallocate(&mut self, pointer: NonNull<u8>, layout: Layout) -> Result<(), HeapError> {
        if layout.size() == 0 {
            return Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation);
        }
        let arena_start = self.arena.as_ptr() as usize;
        let allocation_start = (pointer.as_ptr() as usize)
            .checked_sub(arena_start)
            .filter(|offset| *offset < HEAP_SIZE)
            .ok_or(HeapError::InvalidPointer)?;

        for allocation in &mut self.allocations {
            let Some(active) = *allocation else {
                continue;
            };
            if active.start != allocation_start {
                continue;
            }
            if active.size != layout.size() || active.alignment != layout.align() {
                return Err(HeapError::LayoutMismatch);
            }
            *allocation = None;
            return Ok(());
        }
        Err(HeapError::InvalidPointer)
    }

    fn find_gap(&self, layout: Layout) -> Result<usize, HeapError> {
        let arena_start = self.arena.as_ptr() as usize;
        let mut candidate = 0usize;

        loop {
            let candidate_address = arena_start
                .checked_add(candidate)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let aligned_address = candidate_address
                .checked_add(layout.align() - 1)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?
                & !(layout.align() - 1);
            let start = aligned_address
                .checked_sub(arena_start)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let end = start
                .checked_add(layout.size())
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            if end > HEAP_SIZE {
                return Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory);
            }

            let mut conflicting_end = None;
            for allocation in self.allocations.iter().flatten() {
                let allocation_end = allocation
                    .start
                    .checked_add(allocation.size)
                    .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
                if start < allocation_end && allocation.start < end {
                    conflicting_end = Some(
                        conflicting_end
                            .map_or(allocation_end, |end: usize| end.max(allocation_end)),
                    );
                }
            }

            match conflicting_end {
                Some(end) => candidate = end,
                None => return Ok(start),
            }
        }
    }
}

pub type HeapPageMapper = unsafe fn(context: *mut (), first_page: usize, page_count: usize) -> bool;

struct FrameBackedHeap<const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> {
    base: usize,
    capacity_pages: usize,
    mapped_pages: usize,
    allocations: [Option<Allocation>; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
    context: *mut (),
    map_pages: Option<HeapPageMapper>,
}

impl<const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> FrameBackedHeap<MAX_ALLOCATIONS> {
    const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            base: 0,
            capacity_pages: 0,
            mapped_pages: 0,
            allocations: [None; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
            context: core::ptr::null_mut(),
            map_pages: None,
        }
    }

    fn configure(
        &mut self,
        base: usize,
        capacity_pages: usize,
        context: *mut (),
        map_pages: HeapPageMapper,
    ) -> Result<(), FrameHeapInitError> {
        let capacity = capacity_pages
            .checked_mul(PAGE_BYTES)
            .and_then(|bytes| base.checked_add(bytes));
        if self.map_pages.is_some()
            || base == 0
            || !base.is_multiple_of(PAGE_BYTES)
            || capacity_pages == 0
            || capacity.is_none()
        {
            return Err(if self.map_pages.is_some() {
                FrameHeapInitError::AlreadyConfigured
            } else {
                FrameHeapInitError::InvalidRange
            });
        }
        self.base = base;
        self.capacity_pages = capacity_pages;
        self.context = context;
        self.map_pages = Some(map_pages);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn seal_growth(&mut self) {
        self.context = core::ptr::null_mut();
        self.map_pages = None;
    }

    fn contains_pointer(&self, pointer: usize) -> bool {
        self.capacity_pages
            .checked_mul(PAGE_BYTES)
            .and_then(|capacity| self.base.checked_add(capacity).map(|end| (capacity, end)))
            .is_some_and(|(capacity, end)| capacity != 0 && (self.base..end).contains(&pointer))
    }

    fn allocate(&mut self, layout: Layout) -> Result<NonNull<u8>, HeapError> {
        if layout.size() == 0 {
            return Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation);
        }
        let slot = self
            .allocations
            .iter()
            .position(Option::is_none)
            .ok_or(HeapError::AllocationTableFull)?;
        let start = self.find_gap(layout)?;
        let end = start
            .checked_add(layout.size())
            .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // `end` is already bounded by this heap's capacity, so this division
        // cannot overflow the page count.
        let required_pages = end
            .checked_add(PAGE_BYTES - 1)
            .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?
            / PAGE_BYTES;
        if required_pages > self.mapped_pages {
            let map_pages = self.map_pages.ok_or(HeapError::OutOfMemory)?;
            let first_page = self.mapped_pages;
            let page_count = required_pages - first_page;
            // SAFETY: Configuration is unsafe at the public boundary. The
            // mapper contract requires an all-or-nothing mapping of this range.
            if !unsafe { map_pages(self.context, first_page, page_count) } {
                return Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory);
            }
            self.mapped_pages = required_pages;
        }

        self.allocations[slot] = Some(Allocation {
            start,
            size: layout.size(),
            alignment: layout.align(),
        });
        let pointer = self
            .base
            .checked_add(start)
            .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
        NonNull::new(pointer as *mut u8).ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)
    }

    fn deallocate(&mut self, pointer: NonNull<u8>, layout: Layout) -> Result<(), HeapError> {
        if layout.size() == 0 {
            return Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation);
        }
        let allocation_start = (pointer.as_ptr() as usize)
            .checked_sub(self.base)
            .filter(|offset| *offset < self.capacity_pages.saturating_mul(PAGE_BYTES))
            .ok_or(HeapError::InvalidPointer)?;
        for allocation in &mut self.allocations {
            let Some(active) = *allocation else {
                continue;
            };
            if active.start != allocation_start {
                continue;
            }
            if active.size != layout.size() || active.alignment != layout.align() {
                return Err(HeapError::LayoutMismatch);
            }
            *allocation = None;
            return Ok(());
        }
        Err(HeapError::InvalidPointer)
    }

    fn find_gap(&self, layout: Layout) -> Result<usize, HeapError> {
        let capacity = self
            .capacity_pages
            .checked_mul(PAGE_BYTES)
            .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
        let mut candidate = 0usize;
        loop {
            let candidate_address = self
                .base
                .checked_add(candidate)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let aligned_address = candidate_address
                .checked_add(layout.align() - 1)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?
                & !(layout.align() - 1);
            let start = aligned_address
                .checked_sub(self.base)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let end = start
                .checked_add(layout.size())
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            if end > capacity {
                return Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory);
            }
            let mut conflicting_end = None;
            for allocation in self.allocations.iter().flatten() {
                let allocation_end = allocation
                    .start
                    .checked_add(allocation.size)
                    .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
                if start < allocation_end && allocation.start < end {
                    conflicting_end = Some(
                        conflicting_end
                            .map_or(allocation_end, |current: usize| current.max(allocation_end)),
                    );
                }
            }
            match conflicting_end {
                Some(end) => candidate = end,
                None => return Ok(start),
            }
        }
    }
}

const PAGE_BYTES: usize = 4096;

/// Errors reported while installing the optional frame-backed heap region.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FrameHeapInitError {
    InvalidRange,
    AlreadyConfigured,
}

/// A `GlobalAlloc` wrapper for the fixed bootstrap arena and bounded growth region.
///
/// The bootstrap arena and callback context must remain at stable addresses for
/// the lifetime of allocations. The growth callback must map the complete page
/// range transactionally and must not allocate or call this heap recursively.
pub struct LockedHeap<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> {
    lock: IrqSpinLock<()>,
    heap: UnsafeCell<FixedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>>,
    growth: UnsafeCell<FrameBackedHeap<MAX_ALLOCATIONS>>,
}

// SAFETY: `heap` and `growth` are accessed mutably only while the IRQ-save
// spin lock is held. Allocation remains prohibited in interrupt context.
unsafe impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> Sync
    for LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>
{
}

impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS> {
    /// Construct an empty allocator. The backing arena is zero-initialized BSS.
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            lock: IrqSpinLock::new(()),
            heap: UnsafeCell::new(FixedHeap::new()),
            growth: UnsafeCell::new(FrameBackedHeap::new()),
        }
    }

    /// Configure one reserved virtual range for demand-mapped heap growth.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The caller must reserve the complete range exclusively, keep `context`
    /// alive and stable until the allocator is no longer used, and provide a
    /// mapper that atomically maps all requested pages or leaves the range
    /// unchanged. The mapper must not allocate or re-enter this allocator.
    pub unsafe fn initialize_frame_backed_region(
        &self,
        base: usize,
        capacity_pages: usize,
        context: *mut (),
        map_pages: HeapPageMapper,
    ) -> Result<(), FrameHeapInitError> {
        let _lock = self.acquire();
        // SAFETY: The lock grants exclusive access to the growth configuration.
        let growth = unsafe { &mut *self.growth.get() };
        growth.configure(base, capacity_pages, context, map_pages)
    }

    /// Disable future frame-backed growth while retaining already-mapped pages and allocations.
    ///
    /// This also clears the callback context pointer, ending the heap's ownership
    /// dependency on the page-table owner. Call before creating shared process
    /// roots that immutably borrow that owner. Allocations fitting in currently
    /// mapped heap pages continue to work; requests requiring new pages fail.
    pub fn seal_frame_backed_growth(&self) {
        let _lock = self.acquire();
        // SAFETY: The IRQ-save lock gives exclusive access to growth metadata and
        // waits for any synchronous mapping callback to finish before clearing it.
        unsafe { &mut *self.growth.get() }.seal_growth();
    }

    fn acquire(&self) -> IrqSpinLockGuard<'_, ()> {
        self.lock.lock()
    }
}

impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> Default
    for LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>
{
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

unsafe impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> GlobalAlloc
    for LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>
{
    unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        // Allocation from interrupt/exception context can deadlock the only
        // CPU with IF masked; the allocator contract forbids it. Enforced in
        // debug builds; release builds document the contract instead.
        debug_assert!(
            crate::sync::INTERRUPT_DEPTH.load(core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) == 0,
            "kernel heap allocation from interrupt/exception context"
        );
        let _lock = self.acquire();
        // SAFETY: The lock grants exclusive access to both allocator regions.
        let heap = unsafe { &mut *self.heap.get() };
        // SAFETY: The same lock exclusively protects the growth metadata and
        // callback configuration. Its mapper contract forbids allocator reentry.
        let growth = unsafe { &mut *self.growth.get() };
        heap.allocate(layout)
            .or_else(|_| growth.allocate(layout))
            .map(NonNull::as_ptr)
            .unwrap_or(core::ptr::null_mut())
    }

    unsafe fn dealloc(&self, pointer: *mut u8, layout: Layout) {
        let Some(pointer) = NonNull::new(pointer) else {
            return;
        };
        let _lock = self.acquire();
        // SAFETY: The lock grants exclusive access to both allocator regions. The
        // GlobalAlloc caller must provide a live allocation and its original layout.
        let heap = unsafe { &mut *self.heap.get() };
        // SAFETY: The same lock exclusively protects growth allocation metadata.
        let growth = unsafe { &mut *self.growth.get() };
        if growth.contains_pointer(pointer.as_ptr() as usize) {
            let result = growth.deallocate(pointer, layout);
            debug_assert!(
                result.is_ok(),
                "frame-backed dealloc failed; possible double-free or layout mismatch"
            );
        } else {
            let result = heap.deallocate(pointer, layout);
            debug_assert!(
                result.is_ok(),
                "arena dealloc failed; possible double-free or layout mismatch"
            );
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use core::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout};
    use core::assert_eq;

    use super::{FixedHeap, FrameBackedHeap, HeapError, LockedHeap, PAGE_BYTES};

    #[repr(align(4096))]
    struct TestRegion([u8; PAGE_BYTES * 2]);

    #[derive(Default)]
    struct MapTrace {
        mapped_pages: usize,
        fail: bool,
    }

    unsafe fn test_map_pages(context: *mut (), _first_page: usize, page_count: usize) -> bool {
        // SAFETY: Tests pass a live, exclusively used `MapTrace` pointer.
        let trace = unsafe { &mut *context.cast::<MapTrace>() };
        if trace.fail {
            return false;
        }
        trace.mapped_pages += page_count;
        true
    }

    #[test]
    fn honors_layout_alignment_and_reuses_freed_allocations() {
        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<256, 4>::new();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(37, 64).unwrap();
        let allocation = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocation.as_ptr() as usize % layout.align(), 0);

        // SAFETY: The pointer names a live allocation of the requested size.
        unsafe { allocation.as_ptr().write_bytes(0xa5, layout.size()) };
        for index in 0..layout.size() {
            // SAFETY: `index` is bounded by the live allocation's size.
            assert_eq!(unsafe { allocation.as_ptr().add(index).read() }, 0xa5);
        }

        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();
        let reused = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(reused, allocation);
        heap.deallocate(reused, layout).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_arena_exhaustion_and_reuses_a_coalesced_gap() {
        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<128, 4>::new();
        let full_layout = Layout::from_size_align(64, 1).unwrap();
        let first = heap.allocate(full_layout).unwrap();
        let second = heap.allocate(full_layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            heap.allocate(Layout::from_size_align(1, 1).unwrap()),
            Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory)
        );

        heap.deallocate(first, full_layout).unwrap();
        let smaller_layout = Layout::from_size_align(32, 1).unwrap();
        let reused = heap.allocate(smaller_layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(reused, first);
        heap.deallocate(reused, smaller_layout).unwrap();
        heap.deallocate(second, full_layout).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_allocation_metadata_exhaustion() {
        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<128, 1>::new();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(8, 1).unwrap();
        let allocation = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(heap.allocate(layout), Err(HeapError::AllocationTableFull));
        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();
        assert!(heap.allocate(layout).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_invalid_pointer_and_layout_without_releasing_memory() {
        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<128, 4>::new();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(16, 8).unwrap();
        let allocation = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        let wrong_layout = Layout::from_size_align(8, 8).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            heap.deallocate(allocation, wrong_layout),
            Err(HeapError::LayoutMismatch)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            heap.deallocate(NonNull::dangling(), layout),
            Err(HeapError::InvalidPointer)
        );
        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            heap.deallocate(allocation, layout),
            Err(HeapError::InvalidPointer)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn frame_backed_heap_maps_on_demand_and_reuses_freed_allocations() {
        let mut region = TestRegion([0; PAGE_BYTES * 2]);
        let mut trace = MapTrace::default();
        let mut heap = FrameBackedHeap::<4>::new();
        heap.configure(
            region.0.as_mut_ptr() as usize,
            2,
            core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(trace).cast(),
            test_map_pages,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(5000, 16).unwrap();
        let allocation = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocation.as_ptr() as usize % layout.align(), 0);
        assert_eq!(trace.mapped_pages, 2);
        assert_eq!(heap.mapped_pages, 2);
        // SAFETY: The test mapper records a successful mapping of the complete
        // aligned in-memory region used as the backing store for this heap.
        unsafe { allocation.as_ptr().add(4999).write(0xa5) };
        // SAFETY: The final byte lies within the live 5000-byte allocation.
        assert_eq!(unsafe { allocation.as_ptr().add(4999).read() }, 0xa5);
        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();
        let reused = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(reused, allocation);
        assert_eq!(trace.mapped_pages, 2);
        heap.deallocate(reused, layout).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn sealing_frame_backed_growth_keeps_mapped_pages_and_releases_context() {
        let mut region = TestRegion([0; PAGE_BYTES * 2]);
        let mut trace = MapTrace::default();
        let heap = LockedHeap::<128, 4>::new();
        let bootstrap_layout = Layout::from_size_align(128, 1).unwrap();
        let growth_layout = Layout::from_size_align(8, 1).unwrap();
        // SAFETY: `region` and `trace` remain alive and uniquely used throughout
        // the test; the mapper records a complete successful mapping.
        unsafe {
            heap.initialize_frame_backed_region(
                region.0.as_mut_ptr() as usize,
                2,
                core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(trace).cast(),
                test_map_pages,
            )
        }
        .unwrap();
        // SAFETY: Layouts are nonzero and the heap was initialized above.
        let bootstrap = unsafe { GlobalAlloc::alloc(&heap, bootstrap_layout) };
        // SAFETY: Layouts are nonzero and the configured mapper has a live context.
        let first_growth = unsafe { GlobalAlloc::alloc(&heap, growth_layout) };
        assert!(!bootstrap.is_null());
        assert!(!first_growth.is_null());
        assert_eq!(trace.mapped_pages, 1);

        heap.seal_frame_backed_growth();
        // SAFETY: The wrapper is exclusively used in this test after sealing.
        let growth = unsafe { &*heap.growth.get() };
        assert!(growth.map_pages.is_none());
        assert!(growth.context.is_null());

        // SAFETY: `first_growth` is a live allocation with its original layout.
        unsafe { GlobalAlloc::dealloc(&heap, first_growth, growth_layout) };
        // Already-mapped pages remain available after the callback is severed.
        // SAFETY: Layout is nonzero and reuses the released mapped range.
        let reused_growth = unsafe { GlobalAlloc::alloc(&heap, growth_layout) };
        assert!(!reused_growth.is_null());
        assert_eq!(trace.mapped_pages, 1);

        let beyond_mapped_layout = Layout::from_size_align(PAGE_BYTES + 1, 1).unwrap();
        // SAFETY: The request is bounded but exceeds the two-page test region;
        // after sealing, required growth is rejected without calling the mapper.
        let beyond_mapped = unsafe { GlobalAlloc::alloc(&heap, beyond_mapped_layout) };
        assert!(beyond_mapped.is_null());
        assert_eq!(trace.mapped_pages, 1);

        // SAFETY: Both returned pointers are live allocations with matching layouts.
        unsafe {
            GlobalAlloc::dealloc(&heap, reused_growth, growth_layout);
            GlobalAlloc::dealloc(&heap, bootstrap, bootstrap_layout);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn failed_frame_backed_growth_leaves_heap_metadata_unchanged() {
        let mut region = TestRegion([0; PAGE_BYTES * 2]);
        let mut trace = MapTrace {
            mapped_pages: 0,
            fail: true,
        };
        let mut heap = FrameBackedHeap::<2>::new();
        heap.configure(
            region.0.as_mut_ptr() as usize,
            2,
            core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(trace).cast(),
            test_map_pages,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(PAGE_BYTES + 1, 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(heap.allocate(layout), Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory));
        assert_eq!(heap.mapped_pages, 0);
        assert!(heap.allocations.iter().all(Option::is_none));
        assert_eq!(trace.mapped_pages, 0);

        trace.fail = false;
        let allocation = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(heap.mapped_pages, 2);
        assert_eq!(trace.mapped_pages, 2);
        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_zero_sized_layouts() {
        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<128, 4>::new();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(0, 8).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(heap.allocate(layout), Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation));
    }

    use core::ptr::NonNull;
}

pub extern "C" fn rustix_irq_dispatch(vector: u64) {
    // SAFETY: guard records this entry frame for the heap's debug checks; it
    // decrements automatically on every return path.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    if vector == APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR as u64 {

    90	/// Validate the privilege-sensitive portion of an `IRETQ` frame and replace
    91	/// user-supplied flags with a conservative kernel-selected value.
    92	///
    93	/// The safe flags deliberately leave IF clear until a process-aware interrupt
    94	/// scheduler is installed. The caller must separately verify that RIP names an
    95	/// executable process mapping and RSP names a writable stack mapping.
    96	pub fn sanitize_user_iret_frame(
    97	    frame: UserIretFrame,
    98	    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    99	) -> Result<ValidatedUserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError> {
   100	    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
   101	        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidAddressWidth);
   102	    }
   103	    if frame.code_selector != u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR)
   104	        || frame.stack_selector != u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR)
   105	    {
   106	        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidSelectors);
   107	    }
   108	    if frame.flags & (1 << 1) == 0
   109	        || frame.flags & (RFLAGS_IOPL | RFLAGS_NESTED_TASK | RFLAGS_VIRTUAL_8086) != 0
   110	    {
   111	        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidFlags);
   112	    }
   113	
   114	    let lower_half_end = 1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1);
   115	    if frame.instruction_pointer >= lower_half_end
   116	        || !crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(
   117	            frame.instruction_pointer,
   118	            virtual_address_bits,
   119	        )
   120	    {
   121	        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidInstructionPointer);
   122	    }
   123	    let stack_last = frame
   124	        .stack_pointer
   125	        .checked_sub(1)
   126	        .filter(|address| *address < lower_half_end)
   127	        .filter(|address| {
   128	            crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(*address, virtual_address_bits)
   129	        });
   130	    if stack_last.is_none() || frame.stack_pointer & 0xf != 0 {
   131	        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidStackPointer);
   132	    }
   133	
   134	    Ok(ValidatedUserIretFrame(UserIretFrame {
   135	        instruction_pointer: frame.instruction_pointer,
   136	        code_selector: u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR),
   137	        flags: SAFE_USER_RFLAGS,
   138	        stack_pointer: frame.stack_pointer,
   139	        stack_selector: u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR),
   140	    }))
   141	}

   174	/// Copy and write one bounded v1 user buffer through a process root.
   175	///
   176	/// The complete user range is preflighted by `copy_from_user` before output.
   177	/// If the frame backend faults after copying a prefix, that prefix is still
   178	/// offered to the console and a positive short write is returned when accepted.
   179	///
   180	/// # Safety
   181	/// The current kernel stack, including this function's fixed scratch buffer,
   182	/// must not be mapped as a user frame in `process`. The boot allocator enforces
   183	/// this by excluding the kernel image and bootstrap-stack spans from usable
   184	/// frame allocation; future kernel stacks must preserve the same invariant.
   185	pub unsafe fn write_user_buffer<M, U, O>(
   186	    roots: &crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
   187	    process: crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
   188	    fd: u64,
   189	    user_buffer: u64,
   190	    length: usize,
   191	    user_memory: &mut U,
   192	    output: &mut O,
   193	) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>
   194	where
   195	    M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory,
   196	    U: crate::paging::UserFrameMemory,
   197	    O: ConsoleOutput,
   198	{
   199	    use crate::paging::{ProcessUserCopyError, MAX_PROCESS_USER_COPY_BYTES};
   200	
   201	    let stream = match fd {
   202	        1 => ConsoleStream::Stdout,
   203	        2 => ConsoleStream::Stderr,
   204	        _ => return Err(SyscallError::BadFileDescriptor),
   205	    };
   206	    if length > MAX_WRITE_BYTES as usize {
   207	        return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
   208	    }
   209	    if length == 0 {
   210	        return Ok(0);
   211	    }
   212	
   213	    let mut scratch = [0; MAX_PROCESS_USER_COPY_BYTES];
   214	    let copied = match unsafe {
   215	        roots.copy_from_user(process, user_buffer, &mut scratch[..length], user_memory)
   216	    } {
   217	        Ok(copied) if copied <= length => copied,
   218	        Ok(_) => return Err(SyscallError::Fault),
   219	        Err(failure) if failure.transferred > 0 && failure.transferred <= length => {
   220	            failure.transferred
   221	        }
   222	        Err(failure) => {
   223	            return Err(match failure.cause {
   224	                ProcessUserCopyError::LengthTooLarge => SyscallError::TooBig,
   225	                ProcessUserCopyError::Memory(_) => SyscallError::Io,
   226	                ProcessUserCopyError::InvalidHandle
   227	                | ProcessUserCopyError::Releasing
   228	                | ProcessUserCopyError::InvalidRange
   229	                | ProcessUserCopyError::Unmapped
   230	                | ProcessUserCopyError::PermissionDenied => SyscallError::Fault,
   231	            });
   232	        }
   233	    };
   234	    if copied == 0 {
   235	        return Err(SyscallError::Io);
   236	    }
   237	
   238	    let written = output
   239	        .write(stream, &scratch[..copied])
   240	        .map_err(|_| SyscallError::Io)?;
   241	    if written == 0 || written > copied {
   242	        return Err(SyscallError::Io);
   243	    }
   244	    Ok(written)
   245	}

   247	/// Decode a v1 syscall number and its register arguments without touching user memory.
   248	///
   249	/// The exit status uses the low 32 bits of RDI, interpreted as a signed value.
   250	/// A zero-length write preserves the supplied pointer without validating it; the
   251	/// eventual syscall implementation must return zero before inspecting that pointer.
   252	pub const fn decode_syscall(
   253	    syscall_number: u64,
   254	    arguments: SyscallArguments,
   255	) -> Result<SyscallRequest, SyscallError> {
   256	    match syscall_number {
   257	        number::ABI_VERSION => Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion),
   258	        number::EXIT => Ok(SyscallRequest::Exit {
   259	            status: arguments.rdi as u32 as i32,
   260	        }),
   261	        number::WRITE => {
   262	            if arguments.rdx > MAX_WRITE_BYTES {
   263	                return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
   264	            }
   265	            Ok(SyscallRequest::Write {
   266	                fd: arguments.rdi,
   267	                user_buffer: arguments.rsi,
   268	                length: arguments.rdx as usize,
   269	            })
   270	        }
   271	        number::WAIT => Ok(SyscallRequest::Wait {
   272	            child_pid: arguments.rdi,
   273	            status_address: if arguments.rsi == 0 {
   274	                None
   275	            } else {
   276	                Some(arguments.rsi)
   277	            },
   278	        }),
   279	        _ => Err(SyscallError::NoSys),
   280	    }
   281	}

//! Stable, host-testable decoding for the initial Rustix syscall ABI.
//!
//! This module defines ABI values, validates register-level request shape,
//! sanitizes user return frames, and provides a host-testable bounded write
//! service. It does not install an entry gate or dispatch requests from hardware.

pub const ABI_MAJOR: u16 = 1;
pub const ABI_MINOR: u16 = 0;
pub const ABI_VERSION: u64 = (ABI_MAJOR as u64) << 16 | ABI_MINOR as u64;
pub const MAX_WRITE_BYTES: u64 = 4096;
pub const USER_SYSCALL_VECTOR: u8 = 0x80;
pub const USER_DATA_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x2b;
pub const USER_CODE_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x33;
pub const SAFE_USER_RFLAGS: u64 = 1 << 1;

const RFLAGS_IOPL: u64 = 3 << 12;
const RFLAGS_NESTED_TASK: u64 = 1 << 14;
const RFLAGS_VIRTUAL_8086: u64 = 1 << 17;

pub mod number {
    pub const ABI_VERSION: u64 = 0;
    pub const EXIT: u64 = 1;
    pub const WRITE: u64 = 2;
    pub const WAIT: u64 = 3;
}

    NoSys = 8,

}

/// The five-word privilege-return frame consumed by `IRETQ` in long mode.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct UserIretFrame {
    pub instruction_pointer: u64,
    pub code_selector: u64,
    pub flags: u64,
    pub stack_pointer: u64,
    pub stack_selector: u64,
}

/// A user return frame with validated selectors/addresses and kernel-chosen flags.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct ValidatedUserIretFrame(UserIretFrame);

impl ValidatedUserIretFrame {
    pub const fn into_raw(self) -> UserIretFrame {
        self.0
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserIretFrameError {
    InvalidAddressWidth,
    InvalidSelectors,
    InvalidFlags,
    InvalidInstructionPointer,
    InvalidStackPointer,
}

/// Validate the privilege-sensitive portion of an `IRETQ` frame and replace
/// user-supplied flags with a conservative kernel-selected value.
///
/// The safe flags deliberately leave IF clear until a process-aware interrupt
/// scheduler is installed. The caller must separately verify that RIP names an
/// executable process mapping and RSP names a writable stack mapping.
pub fn sanitize_user_iret_frame(
    frame: UserIretFrame,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<ValidatedUserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidAddressWidth);
    }
    if frame.code_selector != u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR)
        || frame.stack_selector != u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR)
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidSelectors);
    }
    if frame.flags & (1 << 1) == 0
        || frame.flags & (RFLAGS_IOPL | RFLAGS_NESTED_TASK | RFLAGS_VIRTUAL_8086) != 0
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidFlags);
    }

    let lower_half_end = 1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1);
    if frame.instruction_pointer >= lower_half_end
        || !crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(
            frame.instruction_pointer,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidInstructionPointer);
    }
    let stack_last = frame
        .stack_pointer
        .checked_sub(1)
        .filter(|address| *address < lower_half_end)
        .filter(|address| {
            crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(*address, virtual_address_bits)
        });
    if stack_last.is_none() || frame.stack_pointer & 0xf != 0 {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidStackPointer);
    }

    Ok(ValidatedUserIretFrame(UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: frame.instruction_pointer,
        code_selector: u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR),
        flags: SAFE_USER_RFLAGS,
        stack_pointer: frame.stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR),
    }))
}

/// A syscall whose number and register-level arguments have been decoded.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum SyscallRequest {
    AbiVersion,
    Exit {
        status: i32,
    },
    Write {
        fd: u64,
        user_buffer: u64,
        length: usize,
    },
    Wait {
        child_pid: u64,
        status_address: Option<u64>,
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ConsoleStream {
    Stdout,
    Stderr,
}

/// The kernel-side sink for the v1 console descriptors.
pub trait ConsoleOutput {
    type Error;

    fn write(&mut self, stream: ConsoleStream, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, Self::Error>;
}

/// Copy and write one bounded v1 user buffer through a process root.
///
/// The complete user range is preflighted by `copy_from_user` before output.
/// If the frame backend faults after copying a prefix, that prefix is still
/// offered to the console and a positive short write is returned when accepted.
///
/// # Safety
/// The current kernel stack, including this function's fixed scratch buffer,
/// must not be mapped as a user frame in `process`. The boot allocator enforces
/// this by excluding the kernel image and bootstrap-stack spans from usable
/// frame allocation; future kernel stacks must preserve the same invariant.
pub unsafe fn write_user_buffer<M, U, O>(
    roots: &crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
    process: crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
    fd: u64,
    user_buffer: u64,
    length: usize,
    user_memory: &mut U,
    output: &mut O,
) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>
where
    M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory,
    U: crate::paging::UserFrameMemory,
    O: ConsoleOutput,
{
    use crate::paging::{ProcessUserCopyError, MAX_PROCESS_USER_COPY_BYTES};

    let stream = match fd {
        1 => ConsoleStream::Stdout,
        2 => ConsoleStream::Stderr,
        _ => return Err(SyscallError::BadFileDescriptor),
    };
    if length > MAX_WRITE_BYTES as usize {
        return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
    }
    if length == 0 {
        return Ok(0);
    }

    let mut scratch = [0; MAX_PROCESS_USER_COPY_BYTES];
    let copied = match unsafe {
        roots.copy_from_user(process, user_buffer, &mut scratch[..length], user_memory)
    } {
        Ok(copied) if copied <= length => copied,
        Ok(_) => return Err(SyscallError::Fault),
        Err(failure) if failure.transferred > 0 && failure.transferred <= length => {
            failure.transferred
        }
        Err(failure) => {
            return Err(match failure.cause {
                ProcessUserCopyError::LengthTooLarge => SyscallError::TooBig,
                ProcessUserCopyError::Memory(_) => SyscallError::Io,
                ProcessUserCopyError::InvalidHandle
                | ProcessUserCopyError::Releasing
                | ProcessUserCopyError::InvalidRange
                | ProcessUserCopyError::Unmapped
                | ProcessUserCopyError::PermissionDenied => SyscallError::Fault,
            });
        }
    };
    if copied == 0 {
        return Err(SyscallError::Io);
    }

    let written = output
        .write(stream, &scratch[..copied])
        .map_err(|_| SyscallError::Io)?;
    if written == 0 || written > copied {
        return Err(SyscallError::Io);
    }
    Ok(written)
}

/// Decode a v1 syscall number and its register arguments without touching user memory.
///
/// The exit status uses the low 32 bits of RDI, interpreted as a signed value.
/// A zero-length write preserves the supplied pointer without validating it; the
/// eventual syscall implementation must return zero before inspecting that pointer.
pub const fn decode_syscall(
    syscall_number: u64,
    arguments: SyscallArguments,
) -> Result<SyscallRequest, SyscallError> {
    match syscall_number {
        number::ABI_VERSION => Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion),
        number::EXIT => Ok(SyscallRequest::Exit {
            status: arguments.rdi as u32 as i32,
        }),
        number::WRITE => {
            if arguments.rdx > MAX_WRITE_BYTES {
                return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
            }
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Write {
                fd: arguments.rdi,
                user_buffer: arguments.rsi,
                length: arguments.rdx as usize,
            })
        }
        number::WAIT => Ok(SyscallRequest::Wait {
            child_pid: arguments.rdi,
            status_address: if arguments.rsi == 0 {
                None
            } else {
                Some(arguments.rsi)
            },
        }),
        _ => Err(SyscallError::NoSys),
    }
}

    let Some(context) = (unsafe { context.as_mut() }) else {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    };
    let address_bits = USER_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_BITS.load(Ordering::Acquire);
    if address_bits == 0 {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }
    let frame = UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: context.instruction_pointer,
        code_selector: context.code_selector,
        flags: context.flags,
        stack_pointer: context.stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: context.stack_selector,
    };
    let frame = match sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, address_bits) {
        Ok(frame) => frame.into_raw(),
        Err(_) => fatal_irq_halt(),
    };
    context.instruction_pointer = frame.instruction_pointer;
    context.code_selector = frame.code_selector;
    context.flags = frame.flags;
    context.stack_pointer = frame.stack_pointer;
    context.stack_selector = frame.stack_selector;

    let arguments = SyscallArguments {
        rdi: context.rdi,
        rsi: context.rsi,
        rdx: context.rdx,
        r10: context.r10,
        r8: context.r8,
        r9: context.r9,
    };
    let result = match decode_syscall(context.rax, arguments) {
        Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion) => ABI_VERSION as i64,
        Ok(
            SyscallRequest::Exit { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Write { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Wait { .. },
        ) => SyscallError::NotSupported.return_value(),
        Err(error) => error.return_value(),
    };
    context.rax = result as u64;
}

fn fatal_irq_halt() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: Unknown device interrupts are fatal and must not be retried.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

/// Fatal exception target called by the assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_exception_dispatch(context: *const ExceptionContext) -> ! {
    // SAFETY: guard records this entry frame; this path never returns and the
    // frame is already doomed, so the increment is intentionally retained.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    // A fault raised while this handler is running (including a #DF on the
    // IST stack) must not re-enter the printing path; stop silently instead.
    if IN_FATAL_EXCEPTION.swap(true, Ordering::Acquire) {
        loop {
            // SAFETY: Re-entrant fatal diagnostics are deliberately silent.
            unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: The common assembly stub passes a pointer to its normalized stack
    // frame, which remains live for the duration of this non-returning handler.
    let context = unsafe { &*context };
    crate::kprintln!(
        "KERNEL EXCEPTION: vector {} ({}) error={:#018x} RIP={:#018x}",
        context.vector,
        exception_name(context.vector),
        context.error_code,
        context.rip
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CS={:#06x} SS={:#06x} RFLAGS={:#018x} RSP={:#018x}",
        context.cs,
        context.ss,
        context.rflags,
        context.rsp
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RAX={:#018x} RBX={:#018x} RCX={:#018x}",
        context.rax,
        context.rbx,
        context.rcx
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RDX={:#018x} RSI={:#018x} RDI={:#018x} RBP={:#018x}",
        context.rdx,
        context.rsi,
        context.rdi,
        context.rbp
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R8={:#018x} R9={:#018x} R10={:#018x} R11={:#018x}",
        context.r8,
        context.r9,
        context.r10,
        context.r11
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R12={:#018x} R13={:#018x} R14={:#018x} R15={:#018x}",
        context.r12,
        context.r13,
        context.r14,
        context.r15
    );

    if context.vector == 14 {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "page fault: present={} write={} user={} reserved={} instruction-fetch={}",
            context.error_code & 1 != 0,
            context.error_code & 2 != 0,
            context.error_code & 4 != 0,
            context.error_code & 8 != 0,
            context.error_code & 16 != 0
        );
        let fault_address: u64;
        // SAFETY: Reading CR2 is a privileged x86_64 operation in this handler.
        unsafe {
            asm!("mov {}, cr2", out(reg) fault_address, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags))
        };
        crate::kprintln!("page fault address (CR2): {:#018x}", fault_address);
    }

    loop {
        // SAFETY: Fatal exceptions are not recoverable in the current kernel.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

fn exception_name(vector: u64) -> &'static str {
    match vector {
        0 => "divide error",
        1 => "debug",
        2 => "non-maskable interrupt",
        3 => "breakpoint",
        4 => "overflow",
        5 => "bound range",
        6 => "invalid opcode",
        7 => "device not available",
        8 => "double fault",
        9 => "coprocessor segment overrun",
        10 => "invalid TSS",
        11 => "segment not present",
        12 => "stack-segment fault",
        13 => "general protection fault",
        14 => "page fault",
        16 => "x87 floating-point",
        17 => "alignment check",
        18 => "machine check",
        19 => "SIMD floating-point",
        20 => "virtualization",
        21 => "control protection",
        28 => "hypervisor injection",
        29 => "VMM communication",
        30 => "security exception",
        _ => "reserved or architecture-specific exception",
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

// SAFETY: `prepare_table` accepts only an allocator-issued frame and validates
// its complete usable span and HHDM address. Handles are only used while the
// candidate retains the frame token and this unique backend borrow.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory for LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_> {
    type PreparedTable = u64;
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn prepare_table(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
    ) -> Result<Self::PreparedTable, Self::Error> {
        frame.hhdm_address(
            self.memory_map,
            self.hhdm_offset,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    unsafe fn read_entry(
        &self,
        table: Self::PreparedTable,
        index: u16,
    ) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let entry_address = table
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The unsafe trait contract requires `table` to be the prepared
        // HHDM address of a complete writable frame; the index is in [0, 512).
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }

    unsafe fn clear_table(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable) {
        let entries = table as *mut u64;
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a handle prepared by this backend for a
        // complete writable frame retained by its candidate.
        unsafe {
            for index in 0..512 {
                entries.add(index).write_volatile(0);
            }
        }
    }

    unsafe fn write_entry(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable, index: u16, value: u64) {
        if index >= 512 {
            return;
        }
        let entry = (table as *mut u64).wrapping_add(usize::from(index));
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a prepared complete frame and an index in
        // range; this writes one entry without creating a Rust reference.
        unsafe { entry.write_volatile(value) };
    }

    unsafe fn invalidate_page(&mut self, virtual_address: u64) {
        // SAFETY: Active mapping callers provide the current virtual page and run
        // at CPL 0 with exclusive local page-table ownership.
        unsafe {
            core::arch::asm!(
                "invlpg [{}]",
                in(reg) virtual_address,
                options(nostack, preserves_flags)
            );
        }
    }
}
