        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, EffectiveMemoryType, MtrrState,
        PagePermissions, PatLayout, PAGE_SIZE,
    fn read_rsdp(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {

// Capture Limine's entry RSP before a Rust prologue changes it. The synthetic
// return slot is part of the SysV entry stack; realign before calling Rust.
core::arch::global_asm!(
    ".section .text",
    ".code64",
    ".global _start",
    ".type _start, @function",
    "_start:",
    "mov rdi, rsp",
    "and rsp, -16",
    "call rustix_start",
    "ud2",
    ".size _start, . - _start",
);

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_start(entry_rsp: u64) -> ! {
    // Keep interrupts masked until FPU state and the IRQ save destination are ready.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    if let Err(error) = arch::x86_64::cpu::initialize_fpu_state() {
        kprintln!("required x87/SSE state unavailable: {:?}", error);
        halt_forever();
    }
    kernel_threads::initialize_fpu_context();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    kprintln!("x87/SSE context state enabled with FXSAVE/FXRSTOR; AVX disabled");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    let mut boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information(entry_rsp) {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if let Err(error) = arch::x86_64::interrupts::configure_user_address_width(
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        kprintln!("user syscall address-width setup failed: {:?}", error);
        halt_forever();
    }
    #[cfg(target_os = "none")]
    let init_image = match rustix_kernel::elf::Elf64Image::parse(
        INIT_ELF_IMAGE,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(image) => image,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("bundled init ELF rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    #[cfg(target_os = "none")]
    kprintln!(
        "bundled init ELF validated: entry={:#x}, load pages={}",
        init_image.entry_point(),
        init_image.load_page_count()
    );
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
    probe_hhdm_frame(&mut boot_info);

    #[cfg(any(feature = "inject-page-fault", feature = "inject-invalid-opcode"))]
    run_fault_injection();

    activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(&mut boot_info)
}

fn activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) -> ! {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        encode_cr3_value, CandidatePageTables, PageWalkConfig, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let inherited_root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: inherited CR3: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: NXE is not enabled");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let config = PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
            core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(heap_mapping_context).cast(),
            map_kernel_heap_pages,
        )
    } {
        kprintln!("frame-backed heap setup failed: {:?}", error);
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "frame-backed heap configured: {} KiB maximum, demand-mapped",
        KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_MAX_PAGES * PAGE_SIZE as usize / 1024
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
    if timer_verified {
        if let Err(error) = kernel_threads::smoke(
            &mut candidate,
            &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
            &boot_info.cpu_info,
            &BOOTSTRAP_TIMER_TICKS,
        ) {
            kprintln!("cooperative thread probe failed: {}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    }
    probe_kernel_heap();

    // Keep the candidate and its frame tokens alive for as long as this root is
    // active. The shell runs forever and does not return to this stack frame.
    // SAFETY: The bootstrap remains single-core. If enabled, the timer handler
    // touches only its atomic counter and APIC EOI; the shell owns the filesystem.
    let filesystem = unsafe { &mut *core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RAM_FILESYSTEM) };
    match filesystem.seed_defaults() {
        Ok(home) if input_setup.uart_ready && timer_verified => {
            let mut shell_context = ShellThreadContext {
                filesystem: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(*filesystem),
                cwd: home,
                memory_map: core::ptr::addr_of!(boot_info.memory_map),
                frame_allocator: core::ptr::addr_of!(boot_info.frame_allocator),
            };
            // SAFETY: The active root, candidate tokens, allocator, BootInfo,
            // filesystem, and callback context remain live on this non-returning
            // single-vCPU path. The allocator pointer stays raw between calls.
            kernel_threads::run_shell(
                &mut candidate,
                core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(boot_info.frame_allocator),
                &boot_info.cpu_info,
                &BOOTSTRAP_TIMER_TICKS,
                shell_thread_entry,
                core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(shell_context) as usize,
            )
        }
        Ok(home) => shell::run(
            filesystem,
            home,
            &boot_info.memory_map,
            core::ptr::addr_of!(boot_info.frame_allocator),
            core::ptr::null_mut(),
        ),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("RAM filesystem initialization failed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever()
        }
    }
}

extern "C" fn bootstrap_timer_irq() {
    BOOTSTRAP_TIMER_TICKS.tick();
    // Acknowledge before a scheduling switch so the APIC does not retain an
    // in-service timer vector while another context runs.
    arch::x86_64::apic::end_of_interrupt();
    kernel_threads::timer_interrupt();
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct InputIrqSetup {
    uart_vector: Option<rustix_kernel::irq::InterruptVector>,
    keyboard_vector: Option<rustix_kernel::irq::InterruptVector>,
    uart_ready: bool,
    keyboard_ready: bool,
}

fn configure_input_irqs(
    madt: &rustix_kernel::acpi::Madt,
    vectors: &mut rustix_kernel::irq::InterruptVectorAllocator,
) -> InputIrqSetup {
    let mut setup = InputIrqSetup::default();
    if let Some((vector, route_ready)) =
        configure_one_input_irq(madt, vectors, 4, arch::x86_64::serial::irq_handler)
    {
        let vector_number = vector.number();
        setup.uart_vector = Some(vector);
        if route_ready && arch::x86_64::serial::enable_receive_interrupts() {
            // SAFETY: The UART handler is installed, COM1 is initialized, and
            // only its previously masked MADT route is being unmasked.
            setup.uart_ready =
                unsafe { arch::x86_64::apic::unmask_isa_irq(4, vector_number).is_ok() };
            if !setup.uart_ready {
                arch::x86_64::serial::disable_receive_interrupts();
            }
        }
    }

    if let Some((vector, route_ready)) =
        configure_one_input_irq(madt, vectors, 1, arch::x86_64::keyboard::irq_handler)
    {
        let vector_number = vector.number();
        setup.keyboard_vector = Some(vector);
        if route_ready && arch::x86_64::keyboard::initialize_interrupts() {
            // SAFETY: The bounded PS/2 controller setup succeeded and its
            // registered IRQ handler is ready before unmasking the route.
            setup.keyboard_ready =
                unsafe { arch::x86_64::apic::unmask_isa_irq(1, vector_number).is_ok() };
        }
    }
    kprintln!(
        "interrupt-driven input: UART RX {}, PS/2 raw scancodes {}",
        if setup.uart_ready {
            "ready"
        } else {
            "unavailable"
        },
        if setup.keyboard_ready {
            "ready"
        } else {
            "unavailable"
        }
    );
    setup
}

fn configure_one_input_irq(
    madt: &rustix_kernel::acpi::Madt,

    kprintln!("kernel heap probe passed: bootstrap exhaustion, frame-backed growth, reuse");
}

/// leaves; mapping/unmapping is allowed only while a root is inactive. `destroy`
/// returns private frames and tables but never releases shared kernel subtrees.
/// This type does not switch CR3 or invalidate translations on behalf of callers.
pub struct ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'share, 'kernel, 'memory, M: CandidatePageTableMemory> {
    kernel_half: &'share SharedKernelHalf<'kernel>,
    memory: &'memory mut M,
    config: PageWalkConfig,
    roots: [Option<ProcessRoot<M::PreparedTable>>; MAX_PROCESS_ADDRESS_SPACES],
    generations: [u64; MAX_PROCESS_ADDRESS_SPACES],
}

impl<'share, 'kernel, 'memory, M: CandidatePageTableMemory>
    ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'share, 'kernel, 'memory, M>
{
    pub fn new(
        kernel_half: &'share SharedKernelHalf<'kernel>,
        memory: &'memory mut M,
        config: PageWalkConfig,
    ) -> Result<Self, ProcessRootCreateFailure<M::Error>> {
        if !candidate_config_is_valid(config) {
            return Err(ProcessRootCreateFailure {
                cause: ProcessRootCreateErrorKind::InvalidConfiguration,
                frame: None,
            });
        }
        if config != kernel_half.config {
            return Err(ProcessRootCreateFailure {
                cause: ProcessRootCreateErrorKind::KernelConfigurationMismatch,
                frame: None,
            });
        }
        Ok(Self {
            kernel_half,
            memory,
            config,
            roots: core::array::from_fn(|_| None),
            generations: [0; MAX_PROCESS_ADDRESS_SPACES],
        })
    }

    pub const fn page_walk_config(&self) -> PageWalkConfig {
        self.config
    }

    /// Allocate a private root and copy only sanitized upper-half root entries.
    pub fn create(
        &mut self,
        allocator: &mut FrameAllocator,
    ) -> Result<ProcessAddressSpaceHandle, ProcessRootCreateFailure<M::Error>> {
        let Some(slot) = self.roots.iter().position(Option::is_none) else {
            return Err(ProcessRootCreateFailure {
                cause: ProcessRootCreateErrorKind::Capacity,
                frame: None,
            });
        };
        let generation =
            self.generations[slot]
                .checked_add(1)
                .ok_or_else(|| ProcessRootCreateFailure {
                    cause: ProcessRootCreateErrorKind::GenerationExhausted,
                    frame: None,
                })?;
        let frame = allocator
            .allocate()
            .ok_or_else(|| ProcessRootCreateFailure {
                cause: ProcessRootCreateErrorKind::OutOfFrames,
                frame: None,
            })?;
        let frame_end = frame.address().checked_add(PAGE_SIZE);
        if !frame_end.is_some_and(|end| {
            physical_range_fits_address_width(
                frame.address(),
                end,
                self.config.physical_address_bits,
            )
        }) {
            return Err(ProcessRootCreateFailure {
                cause: ProcessRootCreateErrorKind::RootFrameOutOfRange,
                frame: Some(frame),
            });
        }
        let prepared = match self.memory.prepare_table(&frame) {
            Ok(prepared) => prepared,
            Err(error) => {
                return Err(ProcessRootCreateFailure {
                    cause: ProcessRootCreateErrorKind::TableMemory(error),
                    frame: Some(frame),
                });
            }
        };
        // SAFETY: `prepared` was returned by this backend for the root token,
        // which this root set retains until successful destruction.
        unsafe { self.memory.clear_table(prepared) };
        for index in 256..512u16 {
            let entry = self.kernel_half.entries[usize::from(index - 256)];
            if entry != 0 {
                // SAFETY: The root remains owned by this set and the index is
                // within the 512-entry top-level table.
                unsafe { self.memory.write_entry(prepared, index, entry) };
            }
        }
        self.generations[slot] = generation;
        self.roots[slot] = Some(ProcessRoot {
            frame,
            prepared,
            tables: core::array::from_fn(|_| None),
            mappings: core::array::from_fn(|_| None),
            generation,
            active: false,
            releasing: false,
        });
        Ok(ProcessAddressSpaceHandle {
            slot: slot as u8,
            generation,
        })
    }

    /// Install one private, user-accessible 4 KiB leaf into an inactive root.
    pub fn map_user_page(
        &mut self,
        allocator: &mut FrameAllocator,
        handle: ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
        frame: Frame,
        mapping: ValidatedMappingRange,
        cache_attributes: SelectedCacheAttributes,
    ) -> Result<(), ProcessPageMapFailure<M::Error>> {
        macro_rules! fail {
            ($cause:expr, $retained:expr) => {
                return Err(ProcessPageMapFailure {
                    cause: $cause,
                    frame,
                    rollback_retained_table_frames: $retained,
                })
            };
        }

        let root_slot = usize::from(handle.slot);
        let Some(root) = self
            .roots
            .get_mut(root_slot)
            .and_then(Option::as_mut)
            .filter(|root| root.generation == handle.generation)
        else {
            fail!(ProcessPageMapError::InvalidHandle, 0);
        };
        if root.active {
            fail!(
                ProcessPageMapError::Candidate(CandidateMapErrorKind::Active),
                0
            );
        }
        if root.releasing {
            fail!(
                ProcessPageMapError::Candidate(CandidateMapErrorKind::Releasing),
                0
            );
        }
        if !candidate_config_is_valid(self.config) {
            fail!(
                ProcessPageMapError::Candidate(CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidConfiguration),
                0
            );
        }
        if !mapping.permissions.user_accessible {
            fail!(ProcessPageMapError::UserMappingRequired, 0);
        }
        let physical_address = frame.address();
        let Some(physical_end) = physical_address.checked_add(PAGE_SIZE) else {
            fail!(
                ProcessPageMapError::Candidate(CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping),
                0
            );
        };
        let lower_half_end = 1u64 << (self.config.virtual_address_bits - 1);
        if mapping.length() != PAGE_SIZE
            || mapping.virtual_start & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
            || mapping.virtual_start >= lower_half_end
            || mapping.physical_start != physical_address
            || mapping.physical_end != physical_end
            || mapping.physical_address_bits != self.config.physical_address_bits
        {
            fail!(
                ProcessPageMapError::Candidate(CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping),
                0
            );
        }
        let leaf_entry = match mapping.leaf_4k_entry_with_cache_attributes(
            0,
            cache_attributes,
            self.config.nx_enabled,
        ) {
            Ok(entry) => entry.bits(),
            Err(error) => fail!(
                ProcessPageMapError::Candidate(CandidateMapErrorKind::Mapping(error)),
                0
            ),
        };
        if root
            .mappings
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .any(|entry| entry.virtual_address == mapping.virtual_start)
        {
            fail!(
                ProcessPageMapError::Candidate(CandidateMapErrorKind::MappingAlreadyPresent),
                0
            );
        }
        if root.frame.address() == physical_address
            || root
                .mappings
                .iter()
                .flatten()
                .any(|entry| entry.frame.address() == physical_address)
            || root
                .tables
                .iter()
                .flatten()
                .any(|table| table.frame.address() == physical_address)
        {
            fail!(
                indexes[usize::from(self.config.levels) - 1],
            )
        }
        .map_err(ProcessPageUnmapError::TableMemory)?;
        let mapping = root.mappings[mapping_slot]
            .as_ref()
            .expect("mapping slot was validated");
        if leaf & PTE_PRESENT == 0 || leaf & PTE_ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK != mapping.frame.address() {
            return Err(ProcessPageUnmapError::OwnershipMismatch);
        }
        // SAFETY: The validated leaf belongs to this process mapping.
        unsafe {
            self.memory.write_entry(
                current_prepared,

                0,
            )
        };
        Ok(root.mappings[mapping_slot]
            .take()

            .frame)
    }

    /// Validate the initial user instruction and stack addresses before a future
    /// privilege transition. The stack pointer names the first byte above the
    /// writable stack area, so its preceding byte must be mapped.
    pub fn validate_initial_user_state(
        &self,
        handle: ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
        instruction_pointer: u64,
        stack_pointer: u64,
    ) -> Result<(), ProcessUserEntryError> {
        let root = self
            .root(handle)
            .ok_or(ProcessUserEntryError::InvalidHandle)?;
        if root.releasing {
            return Err(ProcessUserEntryError::Releasing);
        }
        if root.active {
            return Err(ProcessUserEntryError::ActiveRoot);
        }

        let lower_half_end = 1u64 << (self.config.virtual_address_bits - 1);
        if instruction_pointer >= lower_half_end
            || !is_canonical_virtual_address(instruction_pointer, self.config.virtual_address_bits)
        {
            return Err(ProcessUserEntryError::InvalidInstructionPointer);
        }
        let instruction_page = instruction_pointer & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        let entry_mapping = root
            .mappings
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .find(|mapping| mapping.virtual_address == instruction_page)
            .ok_or(ProcessUserEntryError::EntryUnmapped)?;
        if !entry_mapping.executable || entry_mapping.writable {
            return Err(ProcessUserEntryError::EntryPermissionDenied);
        }

        let stack_last_byte = stack_pointer
            .checked_sub(1)
            .filter(|address| {
                *address < lower_half_end
                    && is_canonical_virtual_address(*address, self.config.virtual_address_bits)
            })
            .ok_or(ProcessUserEntryError::InvalidStackPointer)?;
        let stack_page = stack_last_byte & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        let stack_mapping = root
            .mappings
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .find(|mapping| mapping.virtual_address == stack_page)
            .ok_or(ProcessUserEntryError::StackUnmapped)?;
        if !stack_mapping.writable || stack_mapping.executable {
            return Err(ProcessUserEntryError::StackPermissionDenied);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Copy kernel bytes from mapped user pages without forming user pointers.
    ///
    /// The complete range is validated before the first copy. If the frame
    /// backend fails during copying, `transferred` reports the completed prefix.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    /// `destination` must not alias storage in any frame mapped by this process.
    pub unsafe fn copy_from_user<U: UserFrameMemory>(
        &self,
        handle: ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
        user_address: u64,
        destination: &mut [u8],
        user_memory: &mut U,
    ) -> Result<usize, ProcessUserCopyFailure<U::Error>> {
        let root = self.root(handle).ok_or(ProcessUserCopyFailure {
            cause: ProcessUserCopyError::InvalidHandle,
        }
        destination.copy_from_slice(&scratch[..destination.len()]);
        debug_assert_eq!(user_address + destination.len() as u64, end);
        Ok(transferred)
    }

def build_kernel(features: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> None:
    command = ["cargo", "build", "--release", "--target", "x86_64-unknown-none"]
    if features:
        command.extend(["--features", ",".join(features)])
    subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, check=True)


def frame_smoke_workflow(timeout: int) -> None:
    failure: BuildError | OSError | subprocess.SubprocessError | None = None
    try:
        build_kernel(("probe-hhdm-frame",))
        build_image()
        smoke_test(timeout)
        serial_log = TARGET_DIR / "rustix-qemu-serial.log"
        output = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
        markers = (
            "HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame",
            "inherited root HHDM probe passed: read 512 entries",
            "candidate inherited-root clone probe passed:",
            "candidate page-table probe passed: mapped, walked, unmapped, and released",
        )
        missing = [marker for marker in markers if marker not in output]
        if missing:
            raise BuildError(
                "QEMU did not report successful HHDM access probes; missing markers: "
                + ", ".join(repr(marker) for marker in missing)
                + f"\nSerial output:\n{output}"
            )
        print("QEMU HHDM, inherited-mapping, cloned-root, and candidate-map probes passed.")
    except (BuildError, OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as error:
        failure = error

    try:
        build_kernel()
        build_image()
    except (BuildError, OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as restore_error:
        if failure is not None:
            raise BuildError(
                f"HHDM frame workflow failed ({failure}); restoring the default image "
                f"also failed ({restore_error})"
            ) from restore_error
        raise

    if failure is not None:
        raise BuildError(
            f"HHDM frame workflow failed; the default release image was restored: {failure}"
        ) from failure
    print("Restored the default release kernel and ISO after the HHDM frame probe.")


def active_map_smoke_workflow(timeout: int) -> None:
    failure: BuildError | OSError | subprocess.SubprocessError | None = None
    try:
        build_kernel(("probe-active-mapping",))
        build_image()
        smoke_test(timeout)
        serial_log = TARGET_DIR / "rustix-qemu-serial.log"
        output = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""

[workspace]
members = ["crates/crabshell"]
resolver = "2"

[package]
name = "rustix-kernel"
version = "0.1.0-milestone4-delta"
edition = "2021"
build = "build.rs"
publish = false
license = "Apache-2.0"
description = "A freestanding 64-bit Rust kernel for the Rustix operating system"

[features]
default = []
inject-page-fault = []
inject-invalid-opcode = []
probe-hhdm-frame = []
probe-active-mapping = []
probe-kernel-threads = []
# Include full CPU register dumps in the fatal exception path. Off by default:
# the serial console is plaintext and unprivileged.
fatal-register-dump = []

[dependencies]
crabshell = { path = "crates/crabshell" }

[lib]
path = "src/lib.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "rustix"
path = "src/main.rs"
test = false
bench = false

[profile.dev]
panic = "abort"

[profile.release]
panic = "abort"
lto = true
codegen-units = 1
strip = false
# Wrapping on overflow silently corrupts address arithmetic in the freestanding
# kernel; fail loudly (panic) instead, matching the audit hardening.
overflow-checks = true

/// Enable the x87/SSE state required by the x86_64 kernel ABI and FXSAVE contexts.
///
/// AVX/XSAVE state is intentionally disabled; any future target feature change
/// must extend the context-switch save format before it can be enabled.
pub fn initialize_fpu_state() -> Result<(), CpuStateError> {
    let features = __cpuid(1).edx;
    if features & (1 << 0) == 0 {
        return Err(CpuStateError::MissingX87);
    }
    if features & (1 << 24) == 0 {
        return Err(CpuStateError::MissingFxsave);
    }
    if features & (1 << 25) == 0 {
        return Err(CpuStateError::MissingSse);
    }
    if features & (1 << 26) == 0 {
        return Err(CpuStateError::MissingSse2);
    }

    let cr0 = (read_cr0_raw() | CR0_MP | CR0_NE) & !(CR0_EM | CR0_TS);
    // SAFETY: This only enables the architectural x87 state and native error
    // reporting, clearing EM/TS so the kernel can use its required FP state.
    unsafe { write_cr0_raw(cr0) };

    let cr4 = (read_cr4_raw() | CR4_OSFXSR | CR4_OSXMMEXCPT) & !CR4_OSXSAVE;
    // SAFETY: Preserve all existing CR4 controls except enabling OS support for
    // FXSAVE/SSE and disabling XSAVE/AVX until that state is explicitly managed.
    unsafe { write_cr4_raw(cr4) };
    Ok(())
}

// SAFETY: `read_mapped` authorizes ordinary table reads only through validated
// ACPI map regions; its separate RSDP entry point permits only the bounded legacy
// reserved window recognized by `MemoryMap::validate_rsdp_span`.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::acpi::AcpiPhysicalReader for CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    type Error = AcpiMappingError;

    fn read(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        self.read_mapped(physical_start, output, false)
    }

    fn read_rsdp(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        self.read_mapped(physical_start, output, true)
    }
}

// Capture Limine's entry RSP before a Rust prologue changes it. The synthetic
// return slot is part of the SysV entry stack; realign before calling Rust.
core::arch::global_asm!(
    ".section .text",
    ".code64",
    ".global _start",
    ".type _start, @function",
    "_start:",
    "mov rdi, rsp",
    "and rsp, -16",
    "call rustix_start",
    "ud2",
    ".size _start, . - _start",
);

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_start(entry_rsp: u64) -> ! {
    // Keep interrupts masked until FPU state and the IRQ save destination are ready.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    if let Err(error) = arch::x86_64::cpu::initialize_fpu_state() {
        kprintln!("required x87/SSE state unavailable: {:?}", error);
        halt_forever();
    }
    kernel_threads::initialize_fpu_context();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    kprintln!("x87/SSE context state enabled with FXSAVE/FXRSTOR; AVX disabled");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    let mut boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information(entry_rsp) {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if let Err(error) = arch::x86_64::interrupts::configure_user_address_width(
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        kprintln!("user syscall address-width setup failed: {:?}", error);
        halt_forever();
    }
    #[cfg(target_os = "none")]
    let init_image = match rustix_kernel::elf::Elf64Image::parse(
        INIT_ELF_IMAGE,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(image) => image,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("bundled init ELF rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    #[cfg(target_os = "none")]
    kprintln!(
        "bundled init ELF validated: entry={:#x}, load pages={}",
        init_image.entry_point(),
        init_image.load_page_count()
    );
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
    probe_hhdm_frame(&mut boot_info);

    #[cfg(any(feature = "inject-page-fault", feature = "inject-invalid-opcode"))]
    run_fault_injection();

    activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(&mut boot_info)
}

fn activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) -> ! {
fn activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) -> ! {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        encode_cr3_value, CandidatePageTables, PageWalkConfig, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let inherited_root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: inherited CR3: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: NXE is not enabled");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let config = PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "page-table transition failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    if let Err(error) =
        candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &reader, inherited_root)
    {
        kprintln!(
            "page-table transition failed to clone inherited root: {:?}",
            error
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    );
    setup
}

fn configure_one_input_irq(
    madt: &rustix_kernel::acpi::Madt,
    vectors: &mut rustix_kernel::irq::InterruptVectorAllocator,
    isa_irq: u8,
    handler: arch::x86_64::interrupts::IrqHandler,
) -> Option<(rustix_kernel::irq::InterruptVector, bool)> {
    let vector = vectors.allocate()?;
    let vector_number = vector.number();
    // SAFETY: This function is called with IF=0. The device route is masked
    // until both the APIC redirection and its callback are installed.
    if unsafe { arch::x86_64::interrupts::register_irq_handler(vector_number, handler) }.is_err() {
        let _ = vectors.release(vector);
        return None;
    }
    // SAFETY: `madt` is the validated owned table used for APIC initialization;
    // its route is kept masked until the device and handler are ready.
    if unsafe { arch::x86_64::apic::configure_isa_irq(madt, isa_irq, vector_number) }.is_err() {
        kprintln!(
            "ISA IRQ{} route configuration failed; source remains masked",
            isa_irq
        );
        return Some((vector, false));
    }
    Some((vector, true))
}

struct ShellThreadContext {
    filesystem: *mut RamFs,
    cwd: usize,
    memory_map: *const rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    frame_allocator: *const rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
}

extern "C" fn shell_thread_entry(runtime: *mut (), context_address: usize) {
    // SAFETY: `activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run` keeps this local context,
    // the static filesystem, and boot metadata live for the non-returning runtime.
    let context = unsafe { &mut *(context_address as *mut ShellThreadContext) };
    // SAFETY: This is the sole shell thread and owns the mutable filesystem.
    let filesystem = unsafe { &mut *context.filesystem };
    // SAFETY: The memory map is immutable and retained with BootInfo. The frame
    // allocator is passed as a raw pointer so no shared reference to BootInfo's
    // allocator field remains live while heap growth mutates it.
    let memory_map = unsafe { &*context.memory_map };
    shell::run(
        filesystem,
        context.cwd,
        memory_map,
        context.frame_allocator,
        runtime,
    )

fn page_table_indexes(virtual_address: u64, levels: u8) -> [u16; 5] {
    let mut indexes = [0; 5];
    for (depth, index) in indexes.iter_mut().take(usize::from(levels)).enumerate() {

        let shift = 12 + 9 * (level_number - 1);
        *index = ((virtual_address >> shift) & 0x1ff) as u16;
    }
    indexes
}

    Stdout,
    Stderr,
}

pub trait ConsoleOutput {

}

/// this by excluding the kernel image and bootstrap-stack spans from usable
/// frame allocation; future kernel stacks must preserve the same invariant.
pub unsafe fn write_user_buffer<M, U, O>(
    roots: &crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
    process: crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
    fd: u64,
    user_buffer: u64,
    length: usize,
    user_memory: &mut U,
    EmptyRange,
    UnalignedRange,
    AddressOverflow,
    MtrrPhysicalAddressWidthMismatch,
    CachePolicy(EffectiveMemoryTypeError),
    CacheAttributesRangeMismatch,
    InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth,
    UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth,
    InvalidVirtualAddressWidth,
    PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds,
    NonCanonicalVirtualRange,
    CrossesCanonicalHole,
    UserMappingOutsideLowerHalf,
    WritableExecutable,
    UnalignedPageOffset,
    PageOffsetOutOfRange,
    InvalidPatIndex,
    NxNotEnabled,
}

/// Validate one contiguous range for a future 4 KiB page-mapping operation.
///
/// The physical-address width must be known; passing `None` is rejected rather
/// than treating an unknown bound as unbounded. User-accessible mappings must
/// remain in the lower canonical half. Successful validation does not establish
/// that physical frames are owned by a caller or mapped in the HHDM.
pub fn validate_mapping_range(
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
    permissions: PagePermissions,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<ValidatedMappingRange, MappingError> {
    if virtual_address_bits == 0 || virtual_address_bits > 64 {
        return Err(MappingError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth);
    }
    let physical_address_bits =
        physical_address_bits.ok_or(MappingError::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)?;
    if physical_address_bits == 0 || physical_address_bits > 64 {
        return Err(MappingError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
    }
    if length == 0 {
        return Err(MappingError::EmptyRange);
    }
    if (virtual_start | physical_start | length) & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
        return Err(MappingError::UnalignedRange);
    }
    if permissions.writable && permissions.executable {
        return Err(MappingError::WritableExecutable);
    }

    let virtual_end = virtual_start
        .checked_add(length)
        .ok_or(MappingError::AddressOverflow)?;
    let physical_end = physical_start
        .checked_add(length)
        .ok_or(MappingError::AddressOverflow)?;
    if !physical_range_fits_address_width(physical_start, physical_end, physical_address_bits) {
        return Err(MappingError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds);
    }

    let last_virtual_address = virtual_end - 1;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(virtual_start, virtual_address_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address(last_virtual_address, virtual_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(MappingError::NonCanonicalVirtualRange);
    }
    if virtual_address_bits < 64
        && ((virtual_start ^ last_virtual_address) & (1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1))) != 0
    {
        return Err(MappingError::CrossesCanonicalHole);
    }
    if permissions.user_accessible
        && ((virtual_start | last_virtual_address) & (1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1))) != 0
    {
        return Err(MappingError::UserMappingOutsideLowerHalf);
    }

    Ok(ValidatedMappingRange {
        virtual_start,
        virtual_end,
        physical_start,
        physical_end,
        physical_address_bits,
        permissions,
    })
}

    """An actionable error while preparing or testing the boot image."""


def require_tool(name: str) -> str:
    path = shutil.which(name)
    if path is None:
        raise BuildError(f"required tool '{name}' was not found on PATH")
    return path


def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as source:
        for block in iter(lambda: source.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def safe_extract(archive: zipfile.ZipFile, destination: Path) -> None:
    root = destination.resolve()
    for member in archive.infolist():
        name = PurePosixPath(member.filename)
        mode = member.external_attr >> 16
        if not name.parts or name.is_absolute() or ".." in name.parts or ":" in name.parts[0]:
            raise BuildError(f"unsafe path in Limine archive: {member.filename}")
        if stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
            raise BuildError(f"symlink in Limine archive is not allowed: {member.filename}")
        output = (destination / Path(*name.parts)).resolve()
        if output != root and root not in output.parents:
            raise BuildError(f"archive member escapes extraction directory: {member.filename}")
    archive.extractall(destination)


def ensure_limine() -> tuple[Path, Path]:
    cache = TARGET_DIR / "tools" / f"limine-{LIMINE_VERSION}"
    archive_path = TARGET_DIR / "tools" / LIMINE_ARCHIVE_NAME
    extracted = cache / "archive"
    cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    extracted.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if not archive_path.exists():
        print(f"Downloading Limine {LIMINE_VERSION} binary release...")
        request = urllib.request.Request(
        "256M",
        "-cdrom",
        str(ISO_PATH),
        "-boot",
        "d",
        "-display",
        "none",
        "-monitor",
        "none",
        "-serial",
        "stdio",
        "-no-reboot",
        "-no-shutdown",
    ]
    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, check=False)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise BuildError(f"QEMU exited with status {result.returncode}")


def run_debug() -> None:
    qemu = require_tool("qemu-system-x86_64")
    if not ISO_PATH.is_file():
        raise BuildError("boot image not found; run 'just debug-image' first")

    command = [
        qemu,
        "-machine",
        "q35",
        "-m",
        "256M",
        "-cdrom",
        str(ISO_PATH),
        "-boot",
        "d",
        "-display",
        "none",
        "-monitor",
        "none",
        "-serial",
        "stdio",
        "-gdb",
        "tcp:127.0.0.1:1234",
        "-S",
        "-no-reboot",
        "-no-shutdown",
    ]
    print("QEMU is paused; GDB stub listening on 127.0.0.1:1234.", flush=True)
    print("Attach with the Rustix: QEMU (CodeLLDB) debug configuration.", flush=True)
    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, check=False)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise BuildError(f"QEMU exited with status {result.returncode}")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    subparsers.add_parser("image", help="create a pinned Limine BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO")
    smoke = subparsers.add_parser("smoke", help="boot the ISO and check its serial output")
    smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    uefi_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "uefi-smoke", help="boot the ISO with installed OVMF firmware and check ACPI"
    )
    uefi_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    frame_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "frame-smoke", help="probe HHDM access and an inactive candidate root in QEMU"
    )
    frame_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    active_map_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "active-map-smoke", help="probe active owned-page mapping in QEMU, then restore the image"
    )
    active_map_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    thread_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "thread-smoke", help="test cooperative and timer-preemptive kernel threads with OVMF, then restore the default image"
    )
    thread_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    input_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "input-smoke", help="test UART and PS/2 IRQ input waking the shell with OVMF"
    )
    input_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=30, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    fault_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "fault-smoke", help="test fatal exceptions in QEMU, then restore the default image"
    )
    fault_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=10, help="per-test QEMU time limit")
    subparsers.add_parser("run", help="run the ISO with an interactive serial terminal")
    subparsers.add_parser("debug", help="run the ISO paused with a loopback GDB stub")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    try:
        if args.command == "image":
            build_image()
        elif args.command == "run":
            run_interactive()
        elif args.command == "debug":
            run_debug()
        elif args.command == "frame-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            frame_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "active-map-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            active_map_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "thread-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            thread_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "input-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            input_smoke_test(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "fault-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            fault_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "uefi-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            uefi_smoke_test(args.timeout)
        else:
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            smoke_test(args.timeout)
    except (BuildError, OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as error:
        print(f"Rustix boot workflow failed: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

/// The bootstrap arena and callback context must remain at stable addresses for
/// the lifetime of allocations. The growth callback must map the complete page
/// range transactionally and must not allocate or call this heap recursively.
pub struct LockedHeap<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> {
    lock: IrqSpinLock<()>,
    heap: UnsafeCell<FixedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>>,
    growth: UnsafeCell<FrameBackedHeap<MAX_ALLOCATIONS>>,
}

// SAFETY: `heap` and `growth` are accessed mutably only while the IRQ-save
// spin lock is held. Allocation remains prohibited in interrupt context.
unsafe impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> Sync
    for LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>
{
}

impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS> {
    /// Construct an empty allocator. The backing arena is zero-initialized BSS.
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            lock: IrqSpinLock::new(()),
            heap: UnsafeCell::new(FixedHeap::new()),
            growth: UnsafeCell::new(FrameBackedHeap::new()),
        }
    }

    /// Configure one reserved virtual range for demand-mapped heap growth.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The caller must reserve the complete range exclusively, keep `context`

    /// mapper that atomically maps all requested pages or leaves the range
    /// unchanged. The mapper must not allocate or re-enter this allocator.

        &self,
        base: usize,
        capacity_pages: usize,
        context: *mut (),
        map_pages: HeapPageMapper,
    ) -> Result<(), FrameHeapInitError> {
        let _lock = self.acquire();
        // SAFETY: The lock grants exclusive access to the growth configuration.
        let growth = unsafe { &mut *self.growth.get() };

    }

    ///
    /// This also clears the callback context pointer, ending the heap's ownership
    /// dependency on the page-table owner. Call before creating shared process
    /// roots that immutably borrow that owner. Allocations fitting in currently
    /// mapped heap pages continue to work; requests requiring new pages fail.
    pub fn seal_frame_backed_growth(&self) {
        let _lock = self.acquire();

        // waits for any synchronous mapping callback to finish before clearing it.
        unsafe { &mut *self.growth.get() }.seal_growth();
    }

    fn acquire(&self) -> IrqSpinLockGuard<'_, ()> {
        self.lock.lock()
    }

    ///
    /// On failure, pages already installed remain owned by the process root and

    /// Destroy a newly created root to reclaim partial mappings and retained page
    /// tables before abandoning a failed load.
    pub fn load_into_process_root<M, U, F, CacheError>(
        &self,
        roots: &mut crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
        allocator: &mut crate::frame::FrameAllocator,
        handle: crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
        user_memory: &mut U,
        mut select_cache_attributes: F,
    ) -> Result<LoadedElf, ElfLoadFailure<CacheError, M::Error, U::Error>>
    where
        M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory,
        U: crate::paging::UserFrameMemory,
        F: FnMut(
            crate::paging::ValidatedMappingRange,
        ) -> Result<crate::paging::SelectedCacheAttributes, CacheError>,
    {
        use crate::paging::{validate_mapping_range, PagePermissions, PAGE_SIZE};

        let config = roots.page_walk_config();
        let mut mapped_pages = 0;
        for (segment_index, segment) in self.segments().enumerate() {
            let permissions = PagePermissions {
                writable: segment.writable(),
                executable: segment.executable(),
                user_accessible: true,
            };
            for page_index in 0..segment.page_count() {
                let virtual_address = u64::try_from(page_index)
                    .ok()
                    .and_then(|index| index.checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE))
                    .and_then(|offset| segment.virtual_start().checked_add(offset));
                let Some(virtual_address) = virtual_address else {
                    return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                        cause: ElfLoadError::Mapping(crate::paging::MappingError::AddressOverflow),
                        frame: None,
                        mapped_pages,
                        rollback_retained_table_frames: 0,
                    });
                };
                let Some(frame) = allocator.allocate() else {
                    return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                        cause: ElfLoadError::OutOfFrames,
                        frame: None,
                        mapped_pages,
                        rollback_retained_table_frames: 0,
                    });
                };
                let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
                    virtual_address,
                    frame.address(),
                    PAGE_SIZE,
                    permissions,
                    Some(config.physical_address_bits),
                    config.virtual_address_bits,
                ) {
                    Ok(mapping) => mapping,
                    Err(error) => {
                        return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                            cause: ElfLoadError::Mapping(error),
                            frame: Some(frame),
                            mapped_pages,
                            rollback_retained_table_frames: 0,
                        });
                    }
                };
                let cache_attributes = match select_cache_attributes(mapping) {
                    Ok(attributes) => attributes,
                    Err(error) => {
                        return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                            cause: ElfLoadError::CachePolicy(error),
                            frame: Some(frame),
                            mapped_pages,
                            rollback_retained_table_frames: 0,
                        });
                    }
                };
                if let Err(error) =
                    self.populate_segment_page(segment_index, page_index, &frame, user_memory)
                {
                    return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                        cause: ElfLoadError::Populate(error),
                        frame: Some(frame),
                        mapped_pages,
                        rollback_retained_table_frames: 0,
                    });
                }
                if let Err(failure) =
                    roots.map_user_page(allocator, handle, frame, mapping, cache_attributes)
                {
                    return Err(ElfLoadFailure {
                        cause: ElfLoadError::Map(failure.cause),
                        frame: Some(failure.frame),
                        mapped_pages,
                        rollback_retained_table_frames: failure.rollback_retained_table_frames,
                    });
                }
                mapped_pages += 1;
            }
        }
        Ok(LoadedElf {
            entry_point: self.entry_point(),
            mapped_pages,
        })

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

// SAFETY: `prepare_table` accepts only an allocator-issued frame and validates
// its complete usable span and HHDM address. Handles are only used while the
// candidate retains the frame token and this unique backend borrow.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory for LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_> {
    type PreparedTable = u64;
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn prepare_table(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
    ) -> Result<Self::PreparedTable, Self::Error> {
        frame.hhdm_address(
            self.memory_map,
            self.hhdm_offset,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    unsafe fn read_entry(
        &self,
        table: Self::PreparedTable,
        index: u16,
    ) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let entry_address = table
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The unsafe trait contract requires `table` to be the prepared
        // HHDM address of a complete writable frame; the index is in [0, 512).
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }

    unsafe fn clear_table(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable) {
        let entries = table as *mut u64;
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a handle prepared by this backend for a
        // complete writable frame retained by its candidate.
        unsafe {
            for index in 0..512 {
                entries.add(index).write_volatile(0);
            }
        }
    }

    unsafe fn write_entry(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable, index: u16, value: u64) {
        if index >= 512 {
            return;
        }
        let entry = (table as *mut u64).wrapping_add(usize::from(index));
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a prepared complete frame and an index in
        // range; this writes one entry without creating a Rust reference.
        unsafe { entry.write_volatile(value) };
    }

    unsafe fn invalidate_page(&mut self, virtual_address: u64) {
        // SAFETY: Active mapping callers provide the current virtual page and run
        // at CPL 0 with exclusive local page-table ownership.
        unsafe {
            core::arch::asm!(
                "invlpg [{}]",
                in(reg) virtual_address,
                options(nostack, preserves_flags)
            );
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
enum LimineUserFrameMemoryError {
    OutOfBounds,
    Address(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError),
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
struct LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
impl LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'_> {
    fn frame_slice_address(
        &self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        length: usize,
    ) -> Result<*mut u8, LimineUserFrameMemoryError> {
        if offset
            .checked_add(length)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE as usize)
        {
            return Err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::OutOfBounds);
        }
        if length == 0 {
            return Ok(core::ptr::null_mut());
        }

        let base = frame
            .hhdm_address(
                self.memory_map,
                self.hhdm_offset,
                self.physical_address_bits,
                self.virtual_address_bits,
            )
            .map_err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address)?;
        let address =
            base.checked_add(offset as u64)
                .ok_or(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address(
                    rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow,
                ))?;
        Ok(address as *mut u8)
    }
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
// SAFETY: The non-copyable Frame token and checked HHDM conversion authorize a
// complete Usable page. Each operation checks its subrange, accesses only that
// page, and uses raw copies rather than forming user virtual references. The
// implementation relies on Limine's mapped-usable-memory contract; hardware
// faults from a broken mapping remain fatal and are not recoverable here.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::UserFrameMemory for LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'_> {
    type Error = LimineUserFrameMemoryError;

    fn copy_from_frame(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        destination: &mut [u8],
    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        let source = self.frame_slice_address(frame, offset, destination.len())?;
        if !destination.is_empty() {
            // SAFETY: The frame subrange was checked and the HHDM address was
            // validated for the full allocator-owned frame. `copy` permits overlap.
            unsafe { core::ptr::copy(source, destination.as_mut_ptr(), destination.len()) };
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn copy_to_frame(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        source: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        let destination = self.frame_slice_address(frame, offset, source.len())?;
        if !source.is_empty() {
            // SAFETY: The frame subrange was checked and the HHDM address was
            // validated for the full allocator-owned frame. `copy` permits overlap.
            unsafe { core::ptr::copy(source.as_ptr(), destination, source.len()) };
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

struct KernelHeapMappingContext {
    candidate: *mut (),
    allocator: *mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: *const arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
}

unsafe fn map_kernel_heap_pages(
    opaque_context: *mut (),
    first_page: usize,
    page_count: usize,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, EffectiveMemoryType, MtrrState,
        PagePermissions, PatLayout, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    if page_count == 0
        || first_page
            .checked_add(page_count)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_MAX_PAGES)
    {
        return false;
    }

    // SAFETY: The caller configures this callback only after the active root,
    // allocator, CPU snapshot, and local context are all live. The boot path is
    // single-vCPU and never returns from the stack containing that context.
    let state = unsafe { &mut *opaque_context.cast::<KernelHeapMappingContext>() };
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the retained local candidate and BootInfo
    // members. The callback is synchronous and never stores a derived reference.
    let candidate = unsafe {
        &mut *state
            .candidate
            .cast::<CandidatePageTables<'static, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'static>>>()
    };
    // SAFETY: The frame allocator and CPU snapshot remain owned by retained
    // BootInfo; this callback runs on the sole CPU with the heap lock held.
    let allocator = unsafe { &mut *state.allocator };
    // SAFETY: The CPU snapshot is immutable and remains live with BootInfo.
    let cpu_info = unsafe { &*state.cpu_info };

    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The callback runs at CPL 0; save IF before disabling local IRQs
    // while the active page tables and allocator are mutated.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", "cli", out(reg) flags) };
    let result = (|| {
        let physical_width = cpu_info.physical_address_bits?;
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(cpu_info.pat_msr_value?).ok()?;
        let mtrrs = match &cpu_info.mtrr {
            MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers.validated_layout(physical_width).ok()?,
            _ => return None,
        };
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        for (mapped, page) in (first_page..first_page + page_count).enumerate() {
            let virtual_address = KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE
                .checked_add((page as u64).checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE)?)?;
            let frame = match allocator.allocate() {
                Some(frame) => frame,
                None => {
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
                virtual_address,
                frame.address(),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                Some(physical_width),
                cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
            ) {
                Ok(mapping) => mapping,
                Err(_) => {
                    deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            let attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
                CachePolicy::WriteBack,
                pat,
                &mtrrs,
                cpu_info.normal_caching,
            ) {
                Ok(attributes) if attributes.effective_type() == EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack => {
                    attributes
                }
                _ => {
                    deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            // SAFETY: IF is clear, the current candidate owns the active root,
            // and the allocator-issued frame is mapped RW/NX with local TLB
            // invalidation before its token becomes page-table-owned.
            if let Err(failure) =
                unsafe { candidate.map_owned_page_active(allocator, frame, mapping, attributes) }
            {
                deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, failure.frame);
                rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                return None;
            }
        }
        Some(())
    })()
    .is_some();
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        // SAFETY: The mapping transaction is complete or fully rolled back.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("sti") };
    }
    result
}

fn rollback_kernel_heap_pages(
    candidate: &mut rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<
        'static,
        LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'static>,
    >,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    first_page: usize,
    mapped_pages: usize,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;

    for page in (first_page..first_page + mapped_pages).rev() {
        let Some(virtual_address) = (page as u64)
            .checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE)
            .and_then(|offset| KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE.checked_add(offset))
        else {
            halt_forever();
        };
        // SAFETY: The pages belong to this transaction in the current active
        // root; unmapping invalidates their TLB entries before token return.
        let frame = unsafe { candidate.unmap_owned_page_active(virtual_address) }
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_forever());
        deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
    }
}

fn deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if allocator.deallocate(frame).is_err() {
        halt_forever();
    }
}

// Error payloads provide boot diagnostics through the derived `Debug` output.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[derive(Debug)]
enum AcpiMappingError {
    InvalidAcpiSpan {
        physical_start: u64,
        length: usize,
        error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError,
    },
    InvalidMapping(rustix_kernel::paging::MappingError),
    CandidateMap(
        rustix_kernel::paging::CandidateMapErrorKind<rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError>,
    ),
    CandidateWalk,
    UnexpectedCurrentCr3,
}

struct CandidateAcpiReader<'candidate, 'memory, 'map> {
    candidate: &'candidate mut rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<
        'memory,
        LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'map>,
    >,
    allocator: &'candidate mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &'map rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    cache_layout: rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    normal_caching: bool,
    candidate_cr3: u64,
    previous_cr3: u64,
    virtual_address: u64,
}

impl CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    fn remove_temporary_mapping(&mut self) {
        if let Err(error) = self.candidate.unmap_acpi_page(self.virtual_address) {
            crate::kprintln!("temporary ACPI mapping could not be removed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    }
}

// The legacy-reserved authorization is accepted only for RSDP reads; all
// root and child tables require ACPI-reclaimable/NVS memory-map coverage.
impl CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    fn read_mapped(
        &mut self,
        physical_start: u64,
        output: &mut [u8],
        allow_legacy_rsdp: bool,
    ) -> Result<(), AcpiMappingError> {
        use rustix_kernel::paging::{
            validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
        };

        if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
            return Err(AcpiMappingError::UnexpectedCurrentCr3);
        }
        if output.is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let length =
            u64::try_from(output.len()).map_err(|_| AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
                physical_start,
                length: output.len(),
                error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow,
            })?;
        let span = if allow_legacy_rsdp {
            self.memory_map.validate_rsdp_span(
                physical_start,
                length,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            )
        } else {
            self.memory_map.validate_acpi_span(
                physical_start,
                length,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            )
        }
        .map_err(|error| AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
            physical_start,
            length: output.len(),
            error,
        })?;
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: false,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        let mut copied = 0usize;
        while copied < output.len() {
            let current_physical = physical_start.checked_add(copied as u64).ok_or(
                AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
                    physical_start,
                    length: output.len(),
                    error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow,
                },
            )?;
            let physical_page = current_physical & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
            let page_offset = current_physical - physical_page;
            let page_length = (PAGE_SIZE - page_offset).min((output.len() - copied) as u64);
            let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
                self.virtual_address,
                physical_page,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
                self.virtual_address_bits,
            )
            .map_err(AcpiMappingError::InvalidMapping)?;
            let cache_attributes = mapping
                .select_cache_attributes(
                    CachePolicy::Uncacheable,
                    self.pat,
                    &self.cache_layout,
                    self.normal_caching,
                )
                .map_err(AcpiMappingError::InvalidMapping)?;
            self.candidate
                .map_acpi_page(self.allocator, span, mapping, cache_attributes)
                .map_err(|failure| AcpiMappingError::CandidateMap(failure.cause))?;

            let candidate_mapping_is_valid = matches!(
                self.candidate.walk(self.virtual_address),
                Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
                    if translation.physical_address == physical_page
                        && translation.permissions == permissions
            );
            if !candidate_mapping_is_valid {
                self.remove_temporary_mapping();
                return Err(AcpiMappingError::CandidateWalk);
            }
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                halt_forever();
            }

            // SAFETY: The candidate is a complete clone of the current inherited
            // hierarchy with all critical paths verified; this temporary page is
            // supervisor R/NX and the candidate remains owned by this stack.
            unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.candidate_cr3) };
            // SAFETY: The CR3 write above installed the candidate root and maskable
            // interrupts remain disabled during this single-core bootstrap read.
            unsafe { self.candidate.mark_active() };
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.candidate_cr3 {
                // SAFETY: Restoring the previous validated root preserves all code,
                // stack, data, and exception mappings needed by this path.
                unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.previous_cr3) };
                if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                    halt_forever();
                }
                // SAFETY: The verified CR3 is no longer the candidate root.
                unsafe { self.candidate.mark_inactive() };
                self.remove_temporary_mapping();
                return Err(AcpiMappingError::UnexpectedCurrentCr3);
            }

            let source = (self.virtual_address + page_offset) as *const u8;
            for offset in 0..page_length as usize {
                // SAFETY: The exact physical page is temporarily mapped R/NX in
                // the active candidate and this byte lies within its 4 KiB leaf.
                output[copied + offset] = unsafe { source.add(offset).read_volatile() };
            }

            // SAFETY: The prior root remains allocated and its critical mappings
            // were verified before this temporary switch.
            unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.previous_cr3) };
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                halt_forever();
            }
            // SAFETY: The previous root was restored and verified above.
            unsafe { self.candidate.mark_inactive() };
            self.remove_temporary_mapping();
            copied += page_length as usize;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

// SAFETY: `read_mapped` authorizes ordinary table reads only through validated
// ACPI map regions; its separate RSDP entry point permits only the bounded legacy
// reserved window recognized by `MemoryMap::validate_rsdp_span`.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::acpi::AcpiPhysicalReader for CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    type Error = AcpiMappingError;

    fn read(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        self.read_mapped(physical_start, output, false)
    }

    fn read_rsdp(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        self.read_mapped(physical_start, output, true)
    }
}

// Capture Limine's entry RSP before a Rust prologue changes it. The synthetic
// return slot is part of the SysV entry stack; realign before calling Rust.
core::arch::global_asm!(
    ".section .text",
    ".code64",
    ".global _start",
    ".type _start, @function",
    "_start:",
    "mov rdi, rsp",
    "and rsp, -16",
    "call rustix_start",
    "ud2",
    ".size _start, . - _start",
);

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_start(entry_rsp: u64) -> ! {
    // Keep interrupts masked until FPU state and the IRQ save destination are ready.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    if let Err(error) = arch::x86_64::cpu::initialize_fpu_state() {
        kprintln!("required x87/SSE state unavailable: {:?}", error);
        halt_forever();
    }
    kernel_threads::initialize_fpu_context();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    kprintln!("x87/SSE context state enabled with FXSAVE/FXRSTOR; AVX disabled");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    let mut boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information(entry_rsp) {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if let Err(error) = arch::x86_64::interrupts::configure_user_address_width(
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        kprintln!("user syscall address-width setup failed: {:?}", error);
        halt_forever();
    }
    #[cfg(target_os = "none")]
    let init_image = match rustix_kernel::elf::Elf64Image::parse(
        INIT_ELF_IMAGE,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(image) => image,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("bundled init ELF rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    #[cfg(target_os = "none")]
    kprintln!(
        "bundled init ELF validated: entry={:#x}, load pages={}",
        init_image.entry_point(),
        init_image.load_page_count()
    );
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
    probe_hhdm_frame(&mut boot_info);

    #[cfg(any(feature = "inject-page-fault", feature = "inject-invalid-opcode"))]
    run_fault_injection();

    activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(&mut boot_info)
}

fn activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) -> ! {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        encode_cr3_value, CandidatePageTables, PageWalkConfig, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let inherited_root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: inherited CR3: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: NXE is not enabled");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let config = PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "page-table transition failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    if let Err(error) =
        candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &reader, inherited_root)
    {
        kprintln!(
            "page-table transition failed to clone inherited root: {:?}",
            error
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    let spans = [
        (
            "kernel text",
            segments.text.virtual_start,
            segments.text.physical_start,
            segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel rodata",
            segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            segments.rodata.physical_start,
            segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel data",
            segments.data.virtual_start,
            segments.data.physical_start,
            segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "active boot stack",
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        ),
    ];
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
