    #[test]
    fn rejects_invalid_effective_cache_type_ranges() {
        let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 0, 1, 4, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();
        let requested = EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack;

        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(0, 0, pat, requested, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::EmptyRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(1, PAGE_SIZE, pat, requested, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::UnalignedRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(!(PAGE_SIZE - 1), PAGE_SIZE, pat, requested, true,),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(1 << 36, PAGE_SIZE, pat, requested, true),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::Mtrr(
                MtrrError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange
            ))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            layout.select_pat_index_for_range(0, PAGE_SIZE, pat, requested, false),
            Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::NonNormalCachingMode)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_captured_mtrr_snapshot_before_resolution() {
        let registers = empty_mtrr_registers(
            (1 << 12) | (1 << 10) | (1 << 8) | 1,
            (1 << 11) | (1 << 10) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64,
        );
        let layout = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(layout.memory_type_for(0), Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack));
        assert_eq!(
            layout.memory_type_for(0x10_0000),
            Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.capability |= 1 << 9;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedCapabilityBits)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.capability |= 1 << 13;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedCapabilityBits)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.default_type |= 1 << 12;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::ReservedDefaultTypeBits)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, 1 << 11);
        invalid.variable_register_count = 1;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::VariableRegisterCountMismatch)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1 << 8, 1 << 11);
        invalid.fixed_registers = None;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::FixedRegisterSupportMismatch)
        );

        let invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining as u64);
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1 << 8, (1 << 11) | 6);
        invalid.fixed_registers.as_mut().unwrap()[0] =
            MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining as u64 * 0x0101_0101_0101_0101;
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1, (1 << 11) | 6);
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << 36) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        invalid.variable_registers[0] = MtrrRegisterPair {
            base: 0x20_0000 | MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining as u64,
            mask: (physical_mask & !(0x20_0000 - 1)) | (1 << 11),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported)
        );

        let invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | (1 << 10));
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::FixedRangesUnavailable)
        );

        let mut invalid = empty_mtrr_registers(1, 1 << 11);
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << 36) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        invalid.variable_registers[0] = MtrrRegisterPair {
            base: MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64,
            mask: (physical_mask ^ (1 << 13)) | (1 << 11),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            invalid.validated_layout(36),
            Err(MtrrError::UnsupportedDiscontinuousVariableMask)
        );
    }

    fn rejects_misaligned_variable_mtrr_bases() {

    #[test]
    fn selects_uniform_cache_attributes_for_a_mapping_range_and_encodes_each_leaf() {
        let capability = 1 | (1 << 10);
        let mut registers =
            empty_mtrr_registers(capability, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64);
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << 36) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        registers.variable_registers[0] = MtrrRegisterPair {
            base: 0x20_0000 | MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough as u64,
            mask: (physical_mask & !(0x20_0000 - 1)) | (1 << 11),
        };
        let mtrrs = registers.validated_layout(36).unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value([6, 0, 1, 4, 6, 1, 7, 0])).unwrap();
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0x4000,
            0x1f_f000,
            PAGE_SIZE * 2,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(36),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let attributes = mapping
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteCombining, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(attributes.physical_start(), 0x1f_f000);
        assert_eq!(attributes.physical_end(), 0x20_1000);
        assert_eq!(attributes.pat_index(), 2);
        assert_eq!(
            attributes.effective_type(),
            EffectiveMemoryType::WriteCombining
        );
        for offset in [0, PAGE_SIZE] {
            assert_eq!(
                mapping
                    .leaf_4k_entry_with_cache_attributes(offset, attributes, true)
                    .unwrap()
                    .bits()
                    & ((1 << 3) | (1 << 4) | (1 << 7)),
                1 << 4
            );
        }

        let other_mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0x8000,
            0x30_0000,
            PAGE_SIZE * 2,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(36),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            other_mapping.leaf_4k_entry_with_cache_attributes(0, attributes, true),
            Err(MappingError::CacheAttributesRangeMismatch)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn encodes_4k_leaf_permissions_nx_and_pat_index_bits() {
        let writable_user_page = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        };
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            0x4000,
            0x20_0000,
            PAGE_SIZE * 2,
            writable_user_page,
            Some(52),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();

        let first = mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0b101, true).unwrap().bits();
        assert_eq!(
            first,
            0x20_0000 | (1 << 0) | (1 << 1) | (1 << 2) | (1 << 3) | (1 << 7) | (1 << 63)
        );
        let second = mapping
            .leaf_4k_entry(PAGE_SIZE, 0b101, true)
            .unwrap()
            .bits();
        assert_eq!(second & 0x000f_ffff_ffff_f000, 0x20_1000);
        assert_eq!(second & (1 << 63), 1 << 63);

        let all_pat_bits = mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0b111, true).unwrap().bits()
            & ((1 << 3) | (1 << 4) | (1 << 7));
        assert_eq!(all_pat_bits, (1 << 3) | (1 << 4) | (1 << 7));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_unencodable_leaf_attributes_and_page_offsets() {
        let mapping =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(52), 48)
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 8, true),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidPatIndex)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0, false),
            Err(MappingError::NxNotEnabled)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(1, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::UnalignedPageOffset)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mapping.leaf_4k_entry(PAGE_SIZE, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::PageOffsetOutOfRange)
        );

        let too_wide =
            validate_mapping_range(0x4000, 0x20_0000, PAGE_SIZE, KERNEL_READ_ONLY, Some(53), 48)
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            too_wide.leaf_4k_entry(0, 0, true),
            Err(MappingError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_reject_root_frames_outside_the_configured_width() {
        let high_address = 1u64 << 40;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
            base: high_address,
            length: PAGE_SIZE,
            kind: 0,
        }])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&map).unwrap();
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let failure =
            match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config()) {
                Err(error) => error,
                Ok(_) => panic!("candidate creation accepted an out-of-range root frame"),
            };
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateCreateErrorKind::RootFrameOutOfRange);
        let frame = failure
            .frame
            .expect("root token is returned on validation failure");
        assert_eq!(frame.address(), high_address);
        allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_mapping_rejects_out_of_width_table_frames_transactionally() {
        let high_address = 1u64 << 40;
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_1000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: high_address,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 0,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let mut allocator = FrameAllocator::from_memory_map(&map).unwrap();
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(frame.address(), 0x10_1000);
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            0xffff_9000_0000_1000,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::TableFrameOutOfRange);
        assert_eq!(failure.rollback_retained_table_frames, 0);
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_walk_rejects_intermediate_tables_without_owned_tokens() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(2);
        let foreign_frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let root_index = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4)[0];
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        memory.foreign_child = Some((root_index, foreign_frame.address()));
        let candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address),
            Err(PageWalkError::Reader(
                CandidatePageTableReadError::UnownedTable
            ))
        );
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        allocator.deallocate(foreign_frame).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_release_failure_retains_owned_frames_for_retry() {
        const TOTAL_FRAMES: usize = 513;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(TOTAL_FRAMES);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let mut remaining_frames: [Option<Frame>; TOTAL_FRAMES - 1] =
            core::array::from_fn(|_| Some(allocator.allocate().unwrap()));
        for index in (1..remaining_frames.len()).step_by(2) {
            allocator
                .deallocate(remaining_frames[index].take().unwrap())
                .unwrap();
        }

        let failure = match candidate.release(&mut allocator) {
            Err(failure) => failure,
            Ok(()) => panic!("release unexpectedly fit a full range table"),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            failure.error,
            CandidateReleaseError::Frame(FrameError::RangeTableFull)
        );
        assert_eq!(failure.candidate.table_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(failure.candidate.mapping_count(), 0);

        allocator
            .deallocate(remaining_frames[0].take().unwrap())
            .unwrap();
        failure.candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        for frame in remaining_frames.into_iter().flatten() {
            allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), TOTAL_FRAMES as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn active_candidate_rejects_mutation_and_release_until_deactivated() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(4);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
        // SAFETY: This is a synthetic test of the active-state guard; no CPU
        // actually uses the test candidate's root.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        assert!(candidate.is_active());
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.unmap_owned_page(0xffff_9000_0000_1000),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::Active)
        ));

        let failure = candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.error, CandidateReleaseError::ActiveRoot);
        let mut candidate = failure.candidate;
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), root);
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test never installed this root in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn active_owned_mapping_invalidates_before_returning_frame_ownership() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(8);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let physical_address = frame.address();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(
            &frame,
            virtual_address,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: true,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
        );
        candidate.memory.record_events = true;
        // SAFETY: The host backend records invalidations and no hardware CR3 is
        // changed; this tests active API state and ownership ordering only.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        // SAFETY: Synthetic active-root ownership is established above, and the
        // backend's invalidation operation records this leaf address.
        unsafe {
            candidate
                .map_owned_page_active(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
                .unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidation_count, 1);
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidated_pages[0], virtual_address);
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[3],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::PageWrite { value, .. }) if value & 1 != 0
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[4],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::Invalidate { virtual_address })
        );
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address),
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
                if translation.physical_address == physical_address
        ));

        // SAFETY: The synthetic root remains the candidate's current test root;
        // unmap invalidates the address before the frame token is returned.
        let frame = unsafe { candidate.unmap_owned_page_active(virtual_address) }.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidation_count, 2);
        assert_eq!(candidate.memory.invalidated_pages[1], virtual_address);
        assert!(matches!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[5],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::PageWrite { value: 0, .. })
        ));
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.memory.event_log[6],
            Some(CandidateTestEvent::Invalidate { virtual_address })
        );
        allocator.deallocate(frame).unwrap();
        // SAFETY: No real CPU installed this host-test candidate in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_clone_preserves_inherited_entries_and_shared_tables() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let indexes = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4);
        let source_root = 0x8000;
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0], 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0] + 1, 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0x9000, indexes[1], 0xa000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xa000, indexes[2], 0xb000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xb000, indexes[3], 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 63));

        let root = parse_cr3_root(source_root, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        candidate
            .clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut allocator, &reader, root)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 4);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: 0x20_0000,
                leaf_physical_base: 0x20_0000,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions: PagePermissions {
                    writable: true,
                    executable: false,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 63),
            })
        );

        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn inherited_large_page_permission_change_splits_and_preserves_cache_type() {
        let total_frames = 16;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let indexes = super::page_table_indexes(virtual_address, 4);
        let source_root = 0x8000;
        let mut reader = SyntheticReader::new();
        reader.set(source_root, indexes[0], 0x9000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0x9000, indexes[1], 0xa000 | 0x3);
        reader.set(0xa000, indexes[2], 0x20_0000 | 0x3 | (1 << 7) | (1 << 12));
        let root = parse_cr3_root(source_root, Some(40), false).unwrap();
        candidate
            .clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut allocator, &reader, root)
            .unwrap();

        candidate
            .set_inherited_page_permissions(
                &mut allocator,
                virtual_address,
                0x20_1000,
                PagePermissions {
                    writable: false,
                    executable: false,
                    user_accessible: false,
                },
            )
            .unwrap();
        let protected = match candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("split mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(protected.physical_address, 0x20_1000);
        assert_eq!(protected.page_size, PAGE_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(
            protected.permissions,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: false,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(protected.pat_index, 4);

        let neighbor = match candidate.walk(virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("neighbor mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(neighbor.physical_address, 0x20_2000);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.page_size, PAGE_SIZE);
        assert!(neighbor.permissions.writable);
        assert!(neighbor.permissions.executable);
        assert_eq!(neighbor.pat_index, 4);

        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

        let root = parse_cr3_root(source_root, Some(40), false).unwrap();

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_require_nx_and_report_unmapped_pages() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(2);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let invalid = CandidatePageTables::new(
            &mut allocator,
            &mut memory,
            PageWalkConfig {
                nx_enabled: false,
                ..four_level_walk_config()
            },
        );
        let error = match invalid {
            Err(error) => error,
            Ok(_) => panic!("candidate creation unexpectedly accepted disabled NX"),
        };
        assert_eq!(error.cause, CandidateCreateErrorKind::InvalidConfiguration);
        assert_eq!(error.frame, None);

        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_owned_page(0xffff_9000_0000_1000),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::NotMapped)
        );
        assert!(candidate.release(&mut allocator).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_borrowed_acpi_without_owning_its_frame() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let acpi_physical = 0x20_0000;
        let acpi_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE * total_frames as u64,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: acpi_physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let span = acpi_map
            .validate_acpi_span(acpi_physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            acpi_physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x0606_0606_0606_0606).unwrap();
        let mtrrs = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64)
            .validated_layout(40)
            .unwrap();
        let attributes = mapping
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        let free_before_map = allocator.free_frames();

        candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_map - 3);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: acpi_physical,
                leaf_physical_base: acpi_physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions: KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: acpi_physical | 1 | (1 << 63),
            })
        );
        let duplicate_virtual = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            duplicate_virtual.cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::MappingAlreadyPresent
        );
        let other_virtual = virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE;
        let other_mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            other_virtual,
            acpi_physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let duplicate_physical = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, other_mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            duplicate_physical.cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::PhysicalPageAlreadyMapped
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::OwnershipMismatch)
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        // SAFETY: This synthetic test checks the inactive-only guard; the CPU
        // never installs the candidate's root.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_acpi_page(virtual_address),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::Active)
        );
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test never installed this root in CR3.
        unsafe { candidate.mark_inactive() };
        candidate.unmap_acpi_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_explicit_uncacheable_mmio_without_frame_ownership() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let mmio_physical = 0xfee0_0000;
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_d000_0000_0000;
        let mmio_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
            base: 0x10_0000,
            length: PAGE_SIZE * total_frames as u64,
            kind: 0,
        }])
        .unwrap();
        let mmio_span = mmio_map
            .validate_mmio_page(mmio_physical, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            mmio_physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            permissions,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let attributes = super::SelectedCacheAttributes {
            physical_start: mmio_physical,
            physical_end: mmio_physical + PAGE_SIZE,
            pat_index: 3,
            effective_type: EffectiveMemoryType::Uncacheable,
        };
        let before = allocator.free_frames();
        // SAFETY: The synthetic test treats this as a device page and never
        // dereferences it; the API's map authorization, range, permissions, and
        // UC requirements apply.
        unsafe {
            candidate
                .map_mmio_page(&mut allocator, mmio_span, mapping, attributes)
                .unwrap()
        };
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), before - 3);
        let translation = match candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap() {
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation) => translation,
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. } => panic!("MMIO mapping disappeared"),
        };
        assert_eq!(translation.physical_address, mmio_physical);
        assert_eq!(translation.permissions, permissions);
        assert_eq!(translation.pat_index, 3);
        assert_eq!(translation.raw_leaf_entry & (1 << 63), 1 << 63);

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.unmap_mmio_page(virtual_address + PAGE_SIZE),
            Err(CandidateUnmapError::NotMapped)
        );
        candidate.unmap_mmio_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_reject_invalid_borrowed_acpi_mappings() {
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(8);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let physical = 0x20_0000;
        let other_physical = 0x30_0000;
        let memory_map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: PAGE_SIZE * 8,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: other_physical,
                length: PAGE_SIZE,
                kind: 2,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let span = memory_map
            .validate_acpi_span(physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_0000_1000;
        let writable = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: true,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            },
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(0x0606_0606_0606_0606).unwrap();
        let mtrrs = empty_mtrr_registers(0, (1 << 11) | MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u64)
            .validated_layout(40)
            .unwrap();
        let attributes = writable
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        let failure = candidate
            .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, writable, attributes)
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping);
        let executable = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            PagePermissions {
                executable: true,
                ..KERNEL_READ_ONLY
            },
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let executable_attributes = executable
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate
                .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, executable, executable_attributes)
                .unwrap_err()
                .cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping
        );
        let user = validate_mapping_range(
            0x4000,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            PagePermissions {
                user_accessible: true,
                ..KERNEL_READ_ONLY
            },
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let user_attributes = user
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate
                .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, span, user, user_attributes)
                .unwrap_err()
                .cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping
        );
        let wrong_span = memory_map
            .validate_acpi_span(other_physical, PAGE_SIZE, Some(40))
            .unwrap();
        let read_only = validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            physical,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let read_only_attributes = read_only
            .select_cache_attributes(CachePolicy::WriteBack, pat, &mtrrs, true)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            candidate
                .map_acpi_page(&mut allocator, wrong_span, read_only, read_only_attributes)
                .unwrap_err()
                .cause,
            CandidateMapErrorKind::InvalidMapping
        );
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn candidate_page_tables_map_unmap_and_release_owned_frames() {
        let total_frames = 8;
        let mut allocator = candidate_allocator(total_frames);
        let mut memory = CandidateTestMemory::new();
        let mut candidate =
            CandidatePageTables::new(&mut allocator, &mut memory, four_level_walk_config())
                .unwrap();
        let root = candidate.root_physical_address().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.root_physical_address(), Some(root));
        let frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let physical = frame.address();
        let virtual_address = 0x0000_4000_0000_1000;
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        };
        let (mapping, attributes) = candidate_mapping(&frame, virtual_address, permissions);

        candidate
            .map_owned_page(&mut allocator, frame, mapping, attributes)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(candidate.table_count(), 4);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);

        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
                physical_address: physical,
                leaf_physical_base: physical,
                page_size: PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                pat_index: 0,
                raw_leaf_entry: physical | 0x3 | (1 << 2) | (1 << 63),
            })
        );

        let duplicate_frame = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let (duplicate_mapping, duplicate_attributes) =
            candidate_mapping(&duplicate_frame, virtual_address, permissions);
        let free_before_duplicate = allocator.free_frames();
        let failure = candidate
            .map_owned_page(
                &mut allocator,
                duplicate_frame,
                duplicate_mapping,
                duplicate_attributes,
            )
            .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.cause, CandidateMapErrorKind::MappingAlreadyPresent);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), free_before_duplicate);
        allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).unwrap();

        let returned = candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(returned.address(), physical);
        assert_eq!(candidate.mapping_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(
            candidate.walk(virtual_address).unwrap(),
            PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent {
                level: PageLevel::Pt,
            }
        );
        allocator.deallocate(returned).unwrap();
        candidate.release(&mut allocator).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.free_frames(), total_frames as u64);
    }

    fn rejects_arithmetic_overflow_and_writable_executable_ranges() {
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                0,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(
                0x1000,
                u64::MAX - (PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                KERNEL_READ_ONLY,
                Some(64),
                64
            ),
            Err(MappingError::AddressOverflow)
        );

        let writable_executable = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: true,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        assert_eq!(
            validate_mapping_range(0x1000, 0x2000, PAGE_SIZE, writable_executable, Some(52), 48),
            Err(MappingError::WritableExecutable)
        );
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

// SAFETY: `prepare_table` accepts only an allocator-issued frame and validates
// its complete usable span and HHDM address. Handles are only used while the
// candidate retains the frame token and this unique backend borrow.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory for LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_> {
    type PreparedTable = u64;
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn prepare_table(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
    ) -> Result<Self::PreparedTable, Self::Error> {
        frame.hhdm_address(
            self.memory_map,
            self.hhdm_offset,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    unsafe fn read_entry(
        &self,
        table: Self::PreparedTable,
        index: u16,
    ) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let entry_address = table
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The unsafe trait contract requires `table` to be the prepared
        // HHDM address of a complete writable frame; the index is in [0, 512).
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }

    unsafe fn clear_table(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable) {
        let entries = table as *mut u64;
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a handle prepared by this backend for a
        // complete writable frame retained by its candidate.
        unsafe {
            for index in 0..512 {
                entries.add(index).write_volatile(0);
            }
        }
    }

    unsafe fn write_entry(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable, index: u16, value: u64) {
        if index >= 512 {
            return;
        }
        let entry = (table as *mut u64).wrapping_add(usize::from(index));
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a prepared complete frame and an index in
        // range; this writes one entry without creating a Rust reference.
        unsafe { entry.write_volatile(value) };
    }

    unsafe fn invalidate_page(&mut self, virtual_address: u64) {
        // SAFETY: Active mapping callers provide the current virtual page and run
        // at CPL 0 with exclusive local page-table ownership.
        unsafe {
            core::arch::asm!(
                "invlpg [{}]",
                in(reg) virtual_address,
                options(nostack, preserves_flags)
            );
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
enum LimineUserFrameMemoryError {
    OutOfBounds,
    Address(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError),
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
struct LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
impl LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'_> {
    fn frame_slice_address(
        &self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        length: usize,
    ) -> Result<*mut u8, LimineUserFrameMemoryError> {
        if offset
            .checked_add(length)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE as usize)
        {
            return Err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::OutOfBounds);
        }
        if length == 0 {
            return Ok(core::ptr::null_mut());
        }

        let base = frame
            .hhdm_address(
                self.memory_map,
                self.hhdm_offset,
                self.physical_address_bits,
                self.virtual_address_bits,
            )
            .map_err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address)?;
        let address =
            base.checked_add(offset as u64)
                .ok_or(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address(
                    rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow,
                ))?;
        Ok(address as *mut u8)
    }
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
// SAFETY: The non-copyable Frame token and checked HHDM conversion authorize a
// complete Usable page. Each operation checks its subrange, accesses only that
// page, and uses raw copies rather than forming user virtual references. The
// implementation relies on Limine's mapped-usable-memory contract; hardware
// faults from a broken mapping remain fatal and are not recoverable here.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::UserFrameMemory for LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'_> {
    type Error = LimineUserFrameMemoryError;

    fn copy_from_frame(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        destination: &mut [u8],
    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        let source = self.frame_slice_address(frame, offset, destination.len())?;
        if !destination.is_empty() {
            // SAFETY: The frame subrange was checked and the HHDM address was
            // validated for the full allocator-owned frame. `copy` permits overlap.
            unsafe { core::ptr::copy(source, destination.as_mut_ptr(), destination.len()) };
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn copy_to_frame(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        source: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        let destination = self.frame_slice_address(frame, offset, source.len())?;
        if !source.is_empty() {
            // SAFETY: The frame subrange was checked and the HHDM address was
            // validated for the full allocator-owned frame. `copy` permits overlap.
            unsafe { core::ptr::copy(source.as_ptr(), destination, source.len()) };
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

struct KernelHeapMappingContext {
    candidate: *mut (),
    allocator: *mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: *const arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
}

unsafe fn map_kernel_heap_pages(
    opaque_context: *mut (),
    first_page: usize,
    page_count: usize,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, EffectiveMemoryType, MtrrState,
        PagePermissions, PatLayout, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    if page_count == 0
        || first_page
            .checked_add(page_count)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_MAX_PAGES)
    {
        return false;
    }

    // SAFETY: The caller configures this callback only after the active root,
    // allocator, CPU snapshot, and local context are all live. The boot path is
    // single-vCPU and never returns from the stack containing that context.
    let state = unsafe { &mut *opaque_context.cast::<KernelHeapMappingContext>() };
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the retained local candidate and BootInfo
    // members. The callback is synchronous and never stores a derived reference.
    let candidate = unsafe {
        &mut *state
            .candidate
            .cast::<CandidatePageTables<'static, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'static>>>()
    };
    // SAFETY: The frame allocator and CPU snapshot remain owned by retained
    // BootInfo; this callback runs on the sole CPU with the heap lock held.
    let allocator = unsafe { &mut *state.allocator };
    // SAFETY: The CPU snapshot is immutable and remains live with BootInfo.
    let cpu_info = unsafe { &*state.cpu_info };

    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The callback runs at CPL 0; save IF before disabling local IRQs
    // while the active page tables and allocator are mutated.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", "cli", out(reg) flags) };
    let result = (|| {
        let physical_width = cpu_info.physical_address_bits?;
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(cpu_info.pat_msr_value?).ok()?;
        let mtrrs = match &cpu_info.mtrr {
            MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers.validated_layout(physical_width).ok()?,
            _ => return None,
        };
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        for (mapped, page) in (first_page..first_page + page_count).enumerate() {
            let virtual_address = KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE
                .checked_add((page as u64).checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE)?)?;
            let frame = match allocator.allocate() {
                Some(frame) => frame,
                None => {
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
                virtual_address,
                frame.address(),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                Some(physical_width),
                cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
            ) {
                Ok(mapping) => mapping,
                Err(_) => {
                    deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            let attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
                CachePolicy::WriteBack,
                pat,
                &mtrrs,
                cpu_info.normal_caching,
            ) {
                Ok(attributes) if attributes.effective_type() == EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack => {
                    attributes
                }
                _ => {
                    deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            // SAFETY: IF is clear, the current candidate owns the active root,
            // and the allocator-issued frame is mapped RW/NX with local TLB
            // invalidation before its token becomes page-table-owned.
            if let Err(failure) =
                unsafe { candidate.map_owned_page_active(allocator, frame, mapping, attributes) }
            {
                deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, failure.frame);
                rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                return None;
            }
        }
        Some(())
    })()
    .is_some();
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        // SAFETY: The mapping transaction is complete or fully rolled back.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("sti") };
    }
    result
}

fn rollback_kernel_heap_pages(
    candidate: &mut rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<
        'static,
        LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'static>,
    >,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    first_page: usize,
    mapped_pages: usize,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;

    for page in (first_page..first_page + mapped_pages).rev() {
        let Some(virtual_address) = (page as u64)
            .checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE)
            .and_then(|offset| KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE.checked_add(offset))
        else {
            halt_forever();
        };
        // SAFETY: The pages belong to this transaction in the current active
        // root; unmapping invalidates their TLB entries before token return.
        let frame = unsafe { candidate.unmap_owned_page_active(virtual_address) }
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_forever());
        deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
    }
}

fn deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if allocator.deallocate(frame).is_err() {
        halt_forever();
    }
}

// Error payloads provide boot diagnostics through the derived `Debug` output.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[derive(Debug)]
enum AcpiMappingError {
    InvalidAcpiSpan {
        physical_start: u64,
        length: usize,
        error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError,
    },
    InvalidMapping(rustix_kernel::paging::MappingError),
    CandidateMap(
        rustix_kernel::paging::CandidateMapErrorKind<rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError>,
    ),
    CandidateWalk,
    UnexpectedCurrentCr3,
}

struct CandidateAcpiReader<'candidate, 'memory, 'map> {
    candidate: &'candidate mut rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<
        'memory,
        LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'map>,
    >,
    allocator: &'candidate mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &'map rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    cache_layout: rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    normal_caching: bool,
    candidate_cr3: u64,
    previous_cr3: u64,
    virtual_address: u64,
}

impl CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    fn remove_temporary_mapping(&mut self) {
        if let Err(error) = self.candidate.unmap_acpi_page(self.virtual_address) {
            crate::kprintln!("temporary ACPI mapping could not be removed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    }
}

// The legacy-reserved authorization is accepted only for RSDP reads; all
// root and child tables require ACPI-reclaimable/NVS memory-map coverage.
impl CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    fn read_mapped(
        &mut self,
        physical_start: u64,
        output: &mut [u8],
        allow_legacy_rsdp: bool,
    ) -> Result<(), AcpiMappingError> {
        use rustix_kernel::paging::{
            validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
        };

        if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
            return Err(AcpiMappingError::UnexpectedCurrentCr3);
        }
        if output.is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let length =
            u64::try_from(output.len()).map_err(|_| AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
                physical_start,
                length: output.len(),
                error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow,
            })?;
        let span = if allow_legacy_rsdp {
            self.memory_map.validate_rsdp_span(
                physical_start,
                length,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            )
        } else {
            self.memory_map.validate_acpi_span(
                physical_start,
                length,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            )
        }
        .map_err(|error| AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
            physical_start,
            length: output.len(),
            error,
        })?;
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: false,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        let mut copied = 0usize;
        while copied < output.len() {
            let current_physical = physical_start.checked_add(copied as u64).ok_or(
                AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
                    physical_start,
                    length: output.len(),
                    error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow,
                },
            )?;
            let physical_page = current_physical & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
            let page_offset = current_physical - physical_page;
            let page_length = (PAGE_SIZE - page_offset).min((output.len() - copied) as u64);
            let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
                self.virtual_address,
                physical_page,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
                self.virtual_address_bits,
            )
            .map_err(AcpiMappingError::InvalidMapping)?;
            let cache_attributes = mapping
                .select_cache_attributes(
                    CachePolicy::Uncacheable,
                    self.pat,
                    &self.cache_layout,
                    self.normal_caching,
                )
                .map_err(AcpiMappingError::InvalidMapping)?;
            self.candidate
                .map_acpi_page(self.allocator, span, mapping, cache_attributes)
                .map_err(|failure| AcpiMappingError::CandidateMap(failure.cause))?;

            let candidate_mapping_is_valid = matches!(
                self.candidate.walk(self.virtual_address),
                Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
                    if translation.physical_address == physical_page
                        && translation.permissions == permissions
            );
            if !candidate_mapping_is_valid {
                self.remove_temporary_mapping();
                return Err(AcpiMappingError::CandidateWalk);
            }
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                halt_forever();
            }

            // SAFETY: The candidate is a complete clone of the current inherited
            // hierarchy with all critical paths verified; this temporary page is
            // supervisor R/NX and the candidate remains owned by this stack.
            unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.candidate_cr3) };
            // SAFETY: The CR3 write above installed the candidate root and maskable
            // interrupts remain disabled during this single-core bootstrap read.
            unsafe { self.candidate.mark_active() };
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.candidate_cr3 {
                // SAFETY: Restoring the previous validated root preserves all code,
                // stack, data, and exception mappings needed by this path.
                unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.previous_cr3) };
                if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                    halt_forever();
                }
                // SAFETY: The verified CR3 is no longer the candidate root.
                unsafe { self.candidate.mark_inactive() };
                self.remove_temporary_mapping();
                return Err(AcpiMappingError::UnexpectedCurrentCr3);
            }

            let source = (self.virtual_address + page_offset) as *const u8;
            for offset in 0..page_length as usize {
                // SAFETY: The exact physical page is temporarily mapped R/NX in
                // the active candidate and this byte lies within its 4 KiB leaf.
                output[copied + offset] = unsafe { source.add(offset).read_volatile() };
            }

            // SAFETY: The prior root remains allocated and its critical mappings
            // were verified before this temporary switch.
            unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.previous_cr3) };
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                halt_forever();
            }
            // SAFETY: The previous root was restored and verified above.
            unsafe { self.candidate.mark_inactive() };
            self.remove_temporary_mapping();
            copied += page_length as usize;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

// SAFETY: `read_mapped` authorizes ordinary table reads only through validated
// ACPI map regions; its separate RSDP entry point permits only the bounded legacy
// reserved window recognized by `MemoryMap::validate_rsdp_span`.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::acpi::AcpiPhysicalReader for CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    type Error = AcpiMappingError;

    fn read(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        self.read_mapped(physical_start, output, false)
    }

    fn read_rsdp(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        self.read_mapped(physical_start, output, true)
    }
}

// Capture Limine's entry RSP before a Rust prologue changes it. The synthetic
// return slot is part of the SysV entry stack; realign before calling Rust.
core::arch::global_asm!(
    ".section .text",
    ".code64",
    ".global _start",
    ".type _start, @function",
    "_start:",
    "mov rdi, rsp",
    "and rsp, -16",
    "call rustix_start",
    "ud2",
    ".size _start, . - _start",
);

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_start(entry_rsp: u64) -> ! {
    // Keep interrupts masked until FPU state and the IRQ save destination are ready.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    if let Err(error) = arch::x86_64::cpu::initialize_fpu_state() {
        kprintln!("required x87/SSE state unavailable: {:?}", error);
        halt_forever();
    }
    kernel_threads::initialize_fpu_context();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    kprintln!("x87/SSE context state enabled with FXSAVE/FXRSTOR; AVX disabled");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    let mut boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information(entry_rsp) {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if let Err(error) = arch::x86_64::interrupts::configure_user_address_width(
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        kprintln!("user syscall address-width setup failed: {:?}", error);
        halt_forever();
    }
    #[cfg(target_os = "none")]
    let init_image = match rustix_kernel::elf::Elf64Image::parse(
        INIT_ELF_IMAGE,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(image) => image,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("bundled init ELF rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    #[cfg(target_os = "none")]
    kprintln!(
        "bundled init ELF validated: entry={:#x}, load pages={}",
        init_image.entry_point(),
        init_image.load_page_count()
    );
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
    probe_hhdm_frame(&mut boot_info);

    #[cfg(any(feature = "inject-page-fault", feature = "inject-invalid-opcode"))]
    run_fault_injection();

    activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(&mut boot_info)
}

fn activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) -> ! {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        encode_cr3_value, CandidatePageTables, PageWalkConfig, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let inherited_root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: inherited CR3: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: NXE is not enabled");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let config = PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "page-table transition failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    if let Err(error) =
        candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &reader, inherited_root)
    {
        kprintln!(
            "page-table transition failed to clone inherited root: {:?}",
            error
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    let spans = [
        (
            "kernel text",
            segments.text.virtual_start,
            segments.text.physical_start,
            segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel rodata",
            segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            segments.rodata.physical_start,
            segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel data",
            segments.data.virtual_start,
            segments.data.physical_start,
            segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "active boot stack",
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        ),
    ];
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            &reader,
            inherited_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: {} was not preserved",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    }
    if !harden_kernel_hhdm_aliases(
        &mut candidate,
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        KernelAliasHardeningContext {
            memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
            hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            physical_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
            virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
            segments: boot_info.kernel_image_segments,
            reader: &reader,
            inherited_root,
            config,
        },
    ) {
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    kprintln!("kernel HHDM aliases validated: text/rodata R/NX, data RW/NX, PAT preserved");
    let candidate_root = candidate
        .root_physical_address()
        .expect("a live candidate retains its root frame");
    let root_hhdm_address = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        candidate_root,
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let root_alias = match candidate.walk(root_hhdm_address) {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
            if translation.physical_address == candidate_root =>
        {
            translation
        }
        result => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM alias: {:?}",
                result
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    if !root_alias.permissions.writable || root_alias.permissions.user_accessible {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: candidate root alias permissions are unsafe");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let new_cr3 = match encode_cr3_value(
        candidate_root,
        inherited_root.low_bits(),
        physical_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: new CR3: {:?}", error);
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let inherited_cr3 = boot_info.inherited_cr3_raw;
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != inherited_cr3 {
        kprintln!("page-table transition aborted: active CR3 changed before switch");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    if let Some(rsdp_physical_address) = boot_info.rsdp_physical_address {
        match load_acpi_madt(
            &mut candidate,
            &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
            &boot_info.memory_map,
            &boot_info.cpu_info,
            rsdp_physical_address,
            new_cr3,
            inherited_cr3,
        ) {
            Ok(madt) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "ACPI MADT copied: LAPIC={:#x}, {} local APICs, {} I/O APICs, {} overrides",
                    madt.local_apic_address,
                    madt.local_apics().count(),
                    madt.io_apics().count(),
                    madt.interrupt_overrides().count()
                );
                boot_info.acpi_madt = Some(madt);
            }
            Err(error) => kprintln!("ACPI MADT unavailable: {:?}", error),
        }
    }
    let apic_virtual_addresses = match boot_info.acpi_madt.as_ref() {
        Some(madt) => match map_bootstrap_apic_pages(
            &mut candidate,
            &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
            &boot_info.cpu_info,
            madt,
            &boot_info.memory_map,
            (
                boot_info.kernel_physical_base,
                boot_info.kernel_physical_end,
            ),
        ) {
            Ok(addresses) => Some(addresses),
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("APIC MMIO mappings unavailable: {}", error);
                None
            }
        },
        None => None,
    };
    match candidate.validate_supervisor_kernel_half() {
        Ok(table_count) => kprintln!(
            "kernel upper-half preflight passed: {} shared supervisor tables",
            table_count
        ),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: unsafe kernel upper half: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: The candidate is a complete clone of every present inherited
    // hierarchy entry, with all referenced intermediate tables owned and the
    // critical code/data/stack paths compared before this point. The inherited
    // root's paging mode, address widths, PAT/MTRR state, and low CR3 mode are
    // preserved; interrupts remain disabled through this transition and are enabled
    // later only after the selected APIC routes and handlers are ready.
    let global_tlb_flushed = unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(new_cr3) };
    if global_tlb_flushed {
        kprintln!("page-table transition: global TLB flushed via CR4.PGE toggle");
    } else {
        kprintln!("page-table transition: CR4.PGE clear; CR3 reload flushed active translations");
    }
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != new_cr3
        || !spans
            .iter()
            .all(|(_, virtual_start, physical_start, length)| {
                candidate_span_matches_source(
                    &candidate,
                    &reader,
                    inherited_root,
                    config,
                    *virtual_start,
                    *physical_start,
                    *length,
                )
            })
    {
        // SAFETY: The inherited root and its backing memory remain untouched and
        // mapped by the candidate, so restoring its validated CR3 value is safe.
        unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(inherited_cr3) };
        if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != inherited_cr3 {
            kprintln!("page-table transition failed to restore inherited CR3; candidate retained");
            halt_forever();
        }
        kprintln!("page-table transition failed post-switch verification; restored inherited CR3");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    // SAFETY: CR3 matches `new_cr3` and post-switch translation checks passed;
    // interrupts are disabled and the candidate root must remain allocated.
    unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
    kprintln!(
        "page-table transition passed: active CR3={:#x}, cloned root={:#x}, {} owned tables",
        new_cr3,
        candidate_root,
        candidate.table_count()
    );

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-active-mapping")]
    {
        if let Err(error) = probe_active_mapping(
            &mut candidate,
            &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
            &boot_info.cpu_info,
        ) {
            kprintln!("active mapping probe failed: {}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
        kprintln!("active mapping probe passed: mapped, accessed, unmapped, reclaimed frame");
    }

    let mut vector_allocator = rustix_kernel::irq::InterruptVectorAllocator::new();
    let mut timer_vector = None;
    let mut timer_verified = false;
    if let (Some(madt), Some((local_apic_virtual, io_apic_virtual))) =
        (boot_info.acpi_madt.as_ref(), apic_virtual_addresses)
    {
        if let Some(vector) = vector_allocator.allocate() {
            let vector_number = vector.number();
            timer_vector = Some(vector);
            // SAFETY: Boot is single-core with IF=0. The cloned root is active,
            // and these virtual addresses were validated supervisor RW/NX/UC
            // mappings of the exact MADT-described APIC pages.
            match unsafe {
                arch::x86_64::apic::initialize(
                    madt,
                    local_apic_virtual,
                    io_apic_virtual,
                    arch::x86_64::cpu::bootstrap_apic_id(),
                )
            } {
                Err(error) => kprintln!(
                    "APIC initialization failed; IRQs remain disabled: {:?}",
                    error
                ),
                Ok(()) => {
                    // SAFETY: APIC initialization masked every route, including
                    // PIT IRQ0; the handler is ready before the route is armed.
                    match unsafe {
                        arch::x86_64::interrupts::register_irq_handler(
                            vector_number,
                            bootstrap_timer_irq,
                        )
                    } {
                        Err(error) => {
                            kprintln!("timer IRQ handler registration failed: {:?}", error)
                        }
                        Ok(()) => match PitRate::for_frequency(100) {
                            Err(error) => kprintln!("PIT rate selection failed: {:?}", error),
                            Ok(rate) => {
                                // SAFETY: The source remains masked through
                                // configuration and the ISR is already registered.
                                let configured = unsafe {
                                    arch::x86_64::apic::configure_pit_timer(
                                        vector_number,
                                        rate.divisor(),
                                    )
                                };
                                match configured {
                                    Err(error) => {
                                        kprintln!("PIT configuration failed: {:?}", error)
                                    }
                                    Ok(()) => {
                                        // SAFETY: Only the validated IRQ0 route is
                                        // unmasked after its handler is installed.
                                        match unsafe { arch::x86_64::apic::unmask_pit_timer() } {
                                            Err(error) => {
                                                kprintln!("PIT route unmask failed: {:?}", error)
                                            }
                                            Ok(()) => {
                                                // SAFETY: IDT/APIC/EOI/handler are
                                                // ready, every other route is masked,
                                                // and this ISR neither allocates nor
                                                // touches non-atomic shared state.
                                                unsafe {
                                                    core::arch::asm!(
                                                        "sti",
                                                        options(nomem, nostack)
                                                    );
                                                }
                                                let target =
                                                    BOOTSTRAP_TIMER_TICKS.ticks().saturating_add(3);
                                                let mut observed = false;
                                                for _ in 0..100_000_000 {
                                                    if BOOTSTRAP_TIMER_TICKS.ticks() >= target {
                                                        observed = true;
                                                        break;
                                                    }
                                                    spin_loop();
                                                }
                                                if observed {
                                                    timer_verified = true;
                                                    kprintln!("timer IRQ path passed: 3 ticks, EOI acknowledged");
                                                } else {
