        SyscallRequest::Write {
            fd,
            user_buffer,
            length,
        } => {
            let mut output = SerialProcessProbeOutput;
            // SAFETY: The kernel stack is not allocator-usable user memory; the
            // service copies via owned frame tokens and never dereferences user VA.
            match unsafe {
                rustix_kernel::syscall::write_user_buffer(
                    roots,
                    state.process,
                    fd,
                    user_buffer,
                    length,
                    user_memory,
                    &mut output,
                )
            } {
                Ok(written) => written as i64,
                Err(error) => error.return_value(),
            }
        }
        SyscallRequest::Exit { status } => {
            kprintln!("process syscall: exit status {}", status);
            finish_active_user_process(state, roots, status)
        }
        SyscallRequest::Wait { .. } => SyscallError::NotSupported.return_value(),
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
fn probe_user_process_root<M: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    candidate: &rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    memory_map: &rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: &arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
) -> Result<(), &'static str> {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, MtrrState, PagePermissions, PatLayout,
        ProcessAddressSpaceRoots, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    kprintln!("process probe: preparing isolated root");
    let init_image =
        rustix_kernel::elf::Elf64Image::parse(INIT_ELF_IMAGE, cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits)
            .map_err(|_| "bundled init ELF validation failed in process probe")?;
    let initial_free_frames = allocator.free_frames();
    let kernel_half = candidate
        .share_supervisor_kernel_half()
        .map_err(|_| "active kernel half could not be shared safely")?;
    let physical_address_bits = cpu_info
        .physical_address_bits
        .ok_or("physical address width unavailable")?;
    let pat = match cpu_info.pat_msr_value {
        Some(value) => PatLayout::from_msr_value(value)
            .map_err(|_| "PAT state is invalid for process mappings")?,
        None => return Err("PAT state unavailable for process mappings"),
    };
    let mtrr_layout = match &cpu_info.mtrr {
        MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers
            .validated_layout(physical_address_bits)
            .map_err(|_| "MTRR state is invalid for process mappings")?,
        _ => return Err("MTRR state unavailable for process mappings"),
    };
    let mut select_cache = |mapping: rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMappingRange| {
        mapping
            .select_cache_attributes(
                CachePolicy::WriteBack,
                pat,
                &mtrr_layout,
                cpu_info.normal_caching,
            )
            .map_err(|_| "no uniform write-back cache policy for process page")
    };
    let mut process_memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map,
        hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut roots = match ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::new(&kernel_half, &mut process_memory, config) {
        Ok(roots) => roots,
        Err(failure) => {
            if let Some(frame) = failure.frame {
                allocator
                    .deallocate(frame)
                    .map_err(|_| "process-root manager frame could not be reclaimed")?;
            }
            return Err("process-root manager creation failed");
        }
    };
    let process = match roots.create(allocator) {
        Ok(process) => process,
        Err(failure) => {
            if let Some(frame) = failure.frame {
                allocator
                    .deallocate(frame)
                    .map_err(|_| "process-root frame could not be reclaimed")?;
            }
            return Err("process root creation failed");
        }
    };
    let mut user_memory = LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory {
        memory_map,
        hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits: Some(physical_address_bits),
        virtual_address_bits: cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    kprintln!("process probe: root created; loading ELF segments");
    if let Err(failure) = init_image.load_into_process_root(
        &mut roots,
        allocator,
        process,
        &mut user_memory,
        &mut select_cache,
    ) {
        if let Some(frame) = failure.frame {
            allocator
                .deallocate(frame)
                .map_err(|_| "unmapped ELF frame could not be reclaimed")?;
        }
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "partially loaded process root could not be destroyed")?;
        return Err("bundled init ELF could not be loaded into the process root");
    }

    kprintln!("process probe: ELF load complete; mapping user stack");
    const USER_STACK_BASE: u64 = 0x0000_7fff_ffff_f000;
    let stack_frame = match allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, process)
                .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after stack allocation failed")?;
            return Err("no frame available for the user stack");
        }
    };
    let stack_mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
        USER_STACK_BASE,
        stack_frame.address(),
        PAGE_SIZE,
        PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        },
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(mapping) => mapping,
        Err(_) => {
            allocator
                .deallocate(stack_frame)
                .map_err(|_| "unmapped stack frame could not be reclaimed")?;
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, process)
                .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after stack validation failed")?;
            return Err("user stack mapping range was rejected");
        }
    };
    let stack_cache = match select_cache(stack_mapping) {
        Ok(attributes) => attributes,
        Err(error) => {
            allocator
                .deallocate(stack_frame)
                .map_err(|_| "unmapped stack frame could not be reclaimed")?;
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, process)
                .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after cache selection failed")?;
            return Err(error);
        }
    };
    if let Err(failure) =
        roots.map_user_page(allocator, process, stack_frame, stack_mapping, stack_cache)
    {
        allocator
            .deallocate(failure.frame)
            .map_err(|_| "unmapped stack frame could not be reclaimed")?;
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after stack mapping failed")?;
        return Err("user stack page could not be mapped");
    }

    let stack_pointer = USER_STACK_BASE + PAGE_SIZE;
    if roots
        .validate_initial_user_state(process, init_image.entry_point(), stack_pointer)
        .is_err()
    {
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after entry validation failed")?;
        return Err("ELF entry or writable NX stack validation failed");
    }

    let mut process_table = rustix_kernel::process::ProcessTable::new();
    let process_id = process_table
        .create_initial()
        .map_err(|_| "initial process record could not be created")?;
    let root_address = match roots.root_physical_address(process) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(_) => {
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, process)
                .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after root lookup failed")?;
            return Err("process root address is unavailable");
        }
    };
    let kernel_cr3 = arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw();
    let kernel_cr3_root = match rustix_kernel::paging::parse_cr3_root(
        kernel_cr3,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        cpu_info.pcid_enabled,
    ) {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(_) => {
            roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
                "process root could not be destroyed after kernel CR3 validation failed"
            })?;
            return Err("active kernel CR3 could not be validated");
        }
    };
    let process_cr3 = match rustix_kernel::paging::encode_cr3_value(
        root_address,
        kernel_cr3_root.low_bits(),
        physical_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(_) => {
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, process)
                .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after CR3 encoding failed")?;
            return Err("process CR3 encoding failed");
        }
    };
    let raw_user_frame = rustix_kernel::syscall::UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: init_image.entry_point(),
        code_selector: u64::from(arch::x86_64::interrupts::USER_CODE_SELECTOR),
        flags: rustix_kernel::syscall::SAFE_USER_RFLAGS,
        stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: u64::from(arch::x86_64::interrupts::USER_DATA_SELECTOR),
    };
    let user_frame = match rustix_kernel::syscall::sanitize_user_iret_frame(
        raw_user_frame,
        cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(frame) => frame,
        Err(_) => {
            roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
                "process root could not be destroyed after IRET frame validation failed"
            })?;
            return Err("initial user IRET frame was rejected");
        }
    };
    kprintln!("process probe: initial entry and stack validated; preparing syscall runtime");
    let mut process_context = ActiveUserProcessSyscallContext {
        roots: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(roots).cast(),
        user_memory: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(user_memory).cast(),
        process_table: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(process_table),
        process,
        process_id,
        kernel_cr3,
    };
    // SAFETY: IF was disabled by the caller; all pointer targets remain live
    // until the synchronous user entry returns through its exit syscall.
    if unsafe {
        arch::x86_64::interrupts::install_user_syscall_handler(
            dispatch_active_user_process_syscall,
            core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(process_context).cast(),
        )
    }
    .is_err()
    {
        roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
            "process root could not be destroyed after syscall handler setup failed"
        })?;
        return Err("user syscall handler setup failed");
    }
    // SAFETY: IF remains disabled, and this complete root was prevalidated.
    if unsafe { roots.mark_active(process) }.is_err() {
        // SAFETY: No user callback is in flight and the root is not installed.
        unsafe { arch::x86_64::interrupts::clear_user_syscall_handler() };
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after activation failed")?;
        return Err("process root could not be marked active");
    }
    kprintln!("process probe: activating process root and entering Ring 3");
    // SAFETY: The process root shares the validated supervisor kernel half and
    // the kernel/TSS stacks are mapped in both roots; interrupts remain disabled.
    unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(process_cr3) };
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != process_cr3 {
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The mapped entry/stack were validated above; syscall dispatch is
    // installed and maskable interrupts remain disabled through process exit.
    let exit_status = match unsafe { arch::x86_64::interrupts::enter_user(user_frame) } {
        Ok(status) => status,
        Err(_) => halt_forever(),
    };
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != kernel_cr3 {
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The exit trampoline returned to the kernel root with IF=0 and no
    // syscall callback remains in flight.
    unsafe { arch::x86_64::interrupts::clear_user_syscall_handler() };
    let wait_result =
        match process_table.try_wait(rustix_kernel::process::KERNEL_PROCESS_ID, process_id.get()) {
            Ok(result) => result,
            Err(_) => {
                roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
                    "inactive process root could not be destroyed after wait failed"
                })?;
                return Err("kernel wait could not inspect the init process");
            }
        };
    if !matches!(
        wait_result,
        rustix_kernel::process::WaitResult::Exited { pid, status }
            if pid == process_id && status == exit_status && status == 42
    ) {
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "inactive process root could not be destroyed after wait mismatch")?;
        return Err("init exit status was not retained and reaped as expected");
    }
    roots
        .destroy(allocator, process)
        .map_err(|_| "inactive process root teardown failed")?;
    if allocator.free_frames() != initial_free_frames {
        return Err("process-root teardown did not restore the frame count");
    }
    kprintln!(
        "init process exited with status {} and was reaped by kernel wait",
        exit_status
    );
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_hhdm_frame(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE;
    use rustix_kernel::paging::UserFrameMemory;

    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: no free frame");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let hhdm_address = match frame.hhdm_address(
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe rejected frame translation: {:?}", error);
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let mut user_memory = LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut expected = [0; 64];
    for (index, byte) in expected.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        *byte = index as u8 ^ 0x5a;
    }
    let mut observed = [0; 64];
    let copy_round_trip = user_memory
        .copy_to_frame(&frame, 128, &expected)
        .and_then(|()| user_memory.copy_from_frame(&frame, 128, &mut observed));
    let mut out_of_bounds = [0; 2];
    let bounds_rejected = user_memory
        .copy_from_frame(&frame, FRAME_SIZE as usize - 1, &mut out_of_bounds)
        .is_err();
    let empty_copy = user_memory
        .copy_to_frame(&frame, FRAME_SIZE as usize, &[])
        .is_ok();
    let mut verified =
        copy_round_trip.is_ok() && observed == expected && bounds_rejected && empty_copy;
    let words = (FRAME_SIZE / core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64) as usize;
    let page = hhdm_address as *mut u64;
    // SAFETY: The non-copyable `Frame` token is held exclusively; its full page
    // is within validated `Usable` memory and its HHDM arithmetic was checked.
    // Limine base revision 3 guarantees usable memory in the HHDM, and no other
    // Rustix mapping aliases this newly allocated frame. This is an opt-in QEMU
    // probe; a broken loader mapping would fault and be caught by the fatal path.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index)
                .write_volatile(0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64);
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            if page.add(index).read_volatile() != (0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64) {
                verified = false;
                break;
            }
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index).write_volatile(0);
        }
    }

    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
    if !verified {
        kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: readback mismatch");
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!("HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame");
    probe_inherited_root(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_inherited_root(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address;

    let root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: CR3 decode rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let address = match inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
        root,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: HHDM validation rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let entries = address as *const u64;
    let mut present_entries = 0;
    // SAFETY: The complete root page was validated as bootloader-reclaimable
    // and its HHDM range arithmetic was checked. The Limine base-revision-3
    // contract maps that region; this read-only opt-in probe trusts that handoff.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..512 {
            if entries.add(index).read_volatile() & 1 != 0 {
                present_entries += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    kprintln!(
        "inherited root HHDM probe passed: read 512 entries, {} present",
        present_entries
    );
    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("inherited page-table walk failed: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "active boot stack",
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
    );

    let pat_value = match boot_info.cpu_info.pat_msr_value {
        Some(value) => value,
        None => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: active PAT value unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let pat = match rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value) {
        Ok(pat) => pat,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid PAT layout: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid MTRR state: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: non-normal CR0 caching mode");
        halt_forever();
    }
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    probe_cloned_page_tables(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        [
            (
                "kernel text",
                segments.text.virtual_start,
                segments.text.physical_start,
                segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel rodata",
                segments.rodata.virtual_start,
                segments.rodata.physical_start,
                segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel data",
                segments.data.virtual_start,
                segments.data.physical_start,
                segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "active boot stack",
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            ),
        ],
    );
    probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_cloned_page_tables(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    spans: [(&str, u64, u64, u64); 4],
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables;

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map,
        hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate = match CandidatePageTables::new(allocator, &mut memory, config) {
        Ok(candidate) => candidate,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                error.cause
            );
            if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                release_probe_frame(allocator, frame);
            }
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if let Err(error) = candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(allocator, source_reader, source_root) {
        kprintln!("candidate clone probe failed: {:?}", error);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
    }
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            source_reader,
            source_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed: {} translation mismatch",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
        }
    }
    let table_count = candidate.table_count();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate clone probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate inherited-root clone probe passed: {} owned table pages preserve critical paths; CR3 unchanged",
        table_count
    );
}

fn candidate_span_matches_source(
    candidate: &rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let Some(virtual_address) = virtual_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(expected_physical) = physical_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let source_result =
            walk_virtual_address(source_reader, source_root, virtual_address, config);
        let candidate_result = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
        let (source_translation, candidate_translation) = match (source_result, candidate_result) {
            (Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(source)), Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(candidate))) => {
                (source, candidate)
            }
            (source, candidate) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate clone walk mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}",
                    virtual_address,
                    source,
                    candidate
                );
                return false;
            }
        };
        if !source_translation.same_effective_mapping(candidate_translation)
            || candidate_translation.physical_address != expected_physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone translation mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}, expected PA={:#x}",
                virtual_address,
                source_translation,
                candidate_translation,
                expected_physical
            );
            return false;
        }
        let Some(next_offset) = offset.checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE) else {
            return false;
        };
        offset = next_offset;
    }
    true
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome,
    };

    let Some(physical_address_bits) = boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits else {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: physical width unknown");
        halt_forever();
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled || !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: NXE or normal caching unavailable");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let pat_value = boot_info
        .cpu_info
        .pat_msr_value
        .expect("inherited cache-alias probe validated active PAT");
    let pat = rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value).unwrap_or_else(|error| {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid PAT: {:?}",
            error
        );
        halt_forever();
    });
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid MTRR: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: true,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_ffff_f000;
    let permissions = PagePermissions {
        writable: true,
        executable: false,
        user_accessible: false,
    };
    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: no leaf frame available");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
        virtual_address,
        frame.address(),
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        permissions,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        config.virtual_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(mapping) => mapping,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid mapping: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let cache_attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
        CachePolicy::WriteBack,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
    ) {
        Ok(attributes) => attributes,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: cache policy: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate page-table probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                if let Some(root_frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, root_frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
    let frame_address = frame.address();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.map_owned_page(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        frame,
        mapping,
        cache_attributes,
    ) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to map leaf: {:?}",
            failure.cause
        );
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, failure.frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let walk = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
    let returned_frame = match candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address) {
        Ok(frame) => frame,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed to unmap leaf: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let translation_valid = match &walk {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => {
            translation.physical_address == frame_address
                && translation.page_size == rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE
                && translation.permissions == permissions
                && translation.pat_index == cache_attributes.pat_index()
        }
        _ => false,
    };
    if returned_frame.address() != frame_address {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: unmap returned the wrong frame");
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
    if !translation_valid {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: candidate walk: {:?}",
            walk
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate page-table probe passed: mapped, walked, unmapped, and released root {:#x}; CR3 unchanged",
        root.expect("candidate retains root until release")
    );
}

fn release_candidate_after_probe_failure(
    candidate: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
) -> ! {
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table cleanup also failed: {:?}", failure);
    }
    halt_forever()
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_inherited_mapping(
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    label: &str,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    let mut first_translation: Option<rustix_kernel::paging::PageTranslation> = None;
    let mut permissions_uniform = true;
    let mut pat_index_uniform = true;
    while offset < length {
        let virtual_address = match virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let expected_physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} physical overflow",
                    label
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, virtual_address, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level }) => {
                if level == rustix_kernel::paging::PageLevel::Pml4 {
                    let pml4_index = ((virtual_address >> 39) & 0x1ff) as u16;
                    let root_entry = reader.read_entry(root.physical_address(), pml4_index);
                    kprintln!(
                        "inherited mapping PML4 detail: VA={:#018x}, index={}, root={:#x}, entry={:?}",
                        virtual_address,
                        pml4_index,
                        root.physical_address(),
                        root_entry
                    );
                }
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} absent at {:?}",
                    label,
                    level
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {}: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if translation.physical_address != expected_physical {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited mapping probe failed: {} {:#018x} mapped to {:#018x}, expected {:#018x}",
                label,
                virtual_address,
                translation.physical_address,
                expected_physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        if let Some(first) = first_translation {
            permissions_uniform &= translation.permissions == first.permissions;
            pat_index_uniform &= translation.pat_index == first.pat_index;
        } else {
            first_translation = Some(translation);
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    if let Some(first) = first_translation {
        kprintln!(
            "inherited mapping probe passed: {} ({} pages), first permissions={:?}, PAT index={}, leaf size={}, uniform permissions={}, uniform PAT index={}",
            label,
            pages,
            first.permissions,
            first.pat_index,
            first.page_size,
            permissions_uniform,
            pat_index_uniform
        );
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
    boot_info: &boot::BootInfo,
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    mtrrs: &rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    label: &str,
    kernel_virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} physical overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_virtual = match kernel_virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_virtual = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
            boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(address) => address,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM range: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, kernel_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, hhdm_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_translation.physical_address != physical
            || hhdm_translation.physical_address != physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias probe failed: {} physical {:#018x} has inconsistent translations",
                label,
                physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        let kernel_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            kernel_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            hhdm_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_type != hhdm_type {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias conflict: {} PA {:#018x}, kernel {:?} vs HHDM {:?}",
                label,
                physical,
                kernel_type,
                hhdm_type
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    kprintln!(
        "cache-alias probe passed: {} ({} pages; effective types match)",
        label,
        pages
    );
}

fn release_probe_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!(
            "HHDM frame probe failed to return its frame: {:?}",
            error.error
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-page-fault")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately reads an unmapped
    // low virtual address; the installed page-fault handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov rax, 0xdeadbeef",
            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack)
        );
    }
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-invalid-opcode")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering invalid opcode with ud2");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately raises #UD; the
    // installed invalid-opcode handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("ud2", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

/// Set once the fatal panic path has started. A panic from inside the fatal
/// path stops silently instead of recursively printing or looping diagnostics.
static FATAL_PANIC_ACTIVE: core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool =
    core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    // Mask maskable interrupts before any diagnostics run: another kernel
    // thread must not resume after a panic is declared, and the fatal report
    // must not be preempted mid-print.
    //
    // SAFETY: Kernel panic path runs at CPL 0; masking IF is always sound.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    if FATAL_PANIC_ACTIVE.swap(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire) {
        loop {
            // SAFETY: Re-entrant panics are deliberately silent.
            unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
        }
    }
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

/// user-supplied flags with a conservative kernel-selected value.
///
/// The safe flags deliberately leave IF clear until a process-aware interrupt
/// scheduler is installed. The caller must separately verify that RIP names an
/// executable process mapping and RSP names a writable stack mapping.
pub fn sanitize_user_iret_frame(
    frame: UserIretFrame,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<ValidatedUserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidAddressWidth);
    }
    if frame.code_selector != u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR)
        || frame.stack_selector != u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR)
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidSelectors);
    }
    if frame.flags & (1 << 1) == 0
        || frame.flags & (RFLAGS_IOPL | RFLAGS_NESTED_TASK | RFLAGS_VIRTUAL_8086) != 0
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidFlags);
    }

    let lower_half_end = 1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1);
    if frame.instruction_pointer >= lower_half_end
        || !crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(
            frame.instruction_pointer,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidInstructionPointer);
    }
    let stack_last = frame
        .stack_pointer
        .checked_sub(1)
        .filter(|address| *address < lower_half_end)
        .filter(|address| {
            crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(*address, virtual_address_bits)
        });
    if stack_last.is_none() || frame.stack_pointer & 0xf != 0 {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidStackPointer);
    }

    Ok(ValidatedUserIretFrame(UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: frame.instruction_pointer,
        code_selector: u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR),
        flags: SAFE_USER_RFLAGS,
        stack_pointer: frame.stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR),
    }))
}

/// A syscall whose number and register-level arguments have been decoded.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum SyscallRequest {
    AbiVersion,
//! Allocation-free validation for virtual addresses and physical memory maps.

/// Limine's memory-map type for ordinary usable RAM.
pub const MEMORY_MAP_USABLE: u64 = 0;
/// Maximum number of memory regions retained in the boot snapshot.
pub const MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS: usize = 256;
/// Minimum x86_64 initial stack size guaranteed by the Limine protocol.
pub const LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE: u64 = 64 * 1024;

/// Check whether an address is canonical for a sign-extended virtual width.
///
/// Widths outside `1..=64` are rejected. A 64-bit width accepts every address.
pub const fn is_canonical_virtual_address(address: u64, address_bits: u8) -> bool {
    if address_bits == 0 || address_bits > 64 {
        return false;
    }
    if address_bits == 64 {
        return true;
    }

    let sign_bit = (address >> (address_bits - 1)) & 1;
    let upper_bits = address >> address_bits;
    let expected_upper_bits = if sign_bit == 0 {
        0
    } else {
        u64::MAX >> address_bits
    };
    upper_bits == expected_upper_bits
}

/// Check that a non-empty half-open physical range fits an address width.
pub const fn physical_range_fits_address_width(start: u64, end: u64, address_bits: u8) -> bool {
    if start >= end || address_bits == 0 || address_bits > 64 {
        return false;
    }
    address_bits == 64 || end <= (1u64 << address_bits)
}

//!
//! Bootstrap installs exception and device-IRQ gates with maskable interrupts
//! disabled. APIC setup, route masking, handler registration, and explicit `sti`
//! are owned by the boot path; exceptions remain fatal-only.

    offset_low: u16,
    selector: u16,
    ist: u8,
    attributes: u8,
    offset_middle: u16,
    offset_high: u32,
    reserved: u32,
}

impl IdtEntry {
    const MISSING: Self = Self {
        offset_low: 0,
        selector: 0,
        ist: 0,
        attributes: 0,
        offset_middle: 0,
        offset_high: 0,
        reserved: 0,
    };

    fn interrupt_gate(handler: u64, ist: u8) -> Self {
        Self {
            offset_low: handler as u16,
            selector: KERNEL_CODE_SELECTOR,
            ist: ist & 0x07,
            attributes: 0x8e,
            offset_middle: (handler >> 16) as u16,
            offset_high: (handler >> 32) as u32,
            reserved: 0,
        }
    }

    fn user_interrupt_gate(handler: u64) -> Self {
        let mut entry = Self::interrupt_gate(handler, 0);
        entry.attributes = 0xee;
        entry

}

/// Install a private kernel GDT/TSS, exception gates, and device IRQ gates.
///
/// The bootstrap runs with maskable interrupts disabled. This routine leaves
/// them disabled and does not modify CR3 or the inherited page-table hierarchy.
pub fn initialize() {
    // SAFETY: Single-core bootstrap ownership; the descriptor tables are private
    // static storage and are initialized before any gate is loaded.
    unsafe {
        asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack));
        initialize_tss();
        initialize_gdt();
        initialize_idt();
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_tss() {
    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    let double_fault_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let double_fault_top = unsafe { double_fault_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);

    // The architectural TSS fields are packed; use unaligned raw writes rather
    // than creating references to their potentially unaligned storage.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(ring0_top);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).ist1).write_unaligned(double_fault_top);
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_gdt() {
    let tss_base = core::ptr::addr_of!(TSS) as u64;
    let tss_limit = (size_of::<TaskStateSegment>() - 1) as u64;
    let low = (tss_limit & 0xffff)
        | ((tss_base & 0x00ff_ffff) << 16)
        | (TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE << 40)
        | ((tss_limit & 0x000f_0000) << 32)
        | ((tss_base & 0xff00_0000) << 32);
    let high = tss_base >> 32;

    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[0]).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[1]).write(0x00af_9a00_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[2]).write(0x00cf_9200_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[3]).write(low);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[4]).write(high);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[5]).write(USER_DATA_DESCRIPTOR);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[6]).write(USER_CODE_DESCRIPTOR);
    }

    let gdtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<[u64; 7]>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(GDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: `GDT` and its TSS descriptor are initialized and remain live.
    unsafe { rustix_load_gdt(&gdtr) };
}

unsafe fn initialize_idt() {
    let idt_entries = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IDT.0).cast::<IdtEntry>();
    let stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(exception_stub_table).cast::<usize>();

    for vector in 0..EXCEPTION_COUNT {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains exactly 32 stub addresses.
        let handler = unsafe { stubs.add(vector).read() } as u64;
        let ist = if vector == 8 { 1 } else { 0 };
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, ist));
        }
    }

    let irq_stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(irq_stub_table).cast::<usize>();
    for vector in IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains one stub for each allocated vector.
        let handler = unsafe { irq_stubs.add(vector - IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR).read() } as u64;
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, 0));
        }
    }
    // Vector 0x80 is reserved from device allocation and uses its own DPL-3
    // interrupt gate rather than the generic device-IRQ dispatch path.
    // SAFETY: The assembly defines this dedicated entry stub in the kernel image.
    unsafe {
        idt_entries
            .add(USER_SYSCALL_VECTOR)
            .write(IdtEntry::user_interrupt_gate(
                rustix_syscall_stub as *const () as usize as u64,
            ));
    }

    // SAFETY: The final table entry is the dedicated 0xff spurious-IRQ stub.
    let spurious_handler =
        unsafe { irq_stubs.add(IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT + IRQ_UNWIRED_COUNT).read() } as u64;
    // SAFETY: The APIC spurious vector is a valid IDT index.
    unsafe {
        idt_entries
            .add(APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR)
            .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(spurious_handler, 0));
    }
    // Vectors 0xf0-0xfe have no registered source; wire them to a controlled
    // fatal stop (through the shared dispatch, which halts) instead of leaving
    // non-present gates that would cascade into #GP with no diagnostics.
    for vector in IRQ_UNWIRED_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_UNWIRED_LAST_VECTOR {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table provides one stub for each vector.
        let handler =
            unsafe { irq_stubs.add(IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT + (vector - IRQ_UNWIRED_FIRST_VECTOR)) }.read()
                as u64;
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, 0));
        }
    }

    let idtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<IdtTable>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(IDT) as u64,

    unsafe { asm!("lidt [{}]", in(reg) &idtr, options(readonly, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
}

/// Configure the active user virtual-address width used to sanitize syscall returns.
///
/// Call after boot CPU discovery and before any CPL3 code can execute.
pub fn configure_user_address_width(virtual_address_bits: u8) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth);
    }
    USER_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_BITS.store(virtual_address_bits, Ordering::Release);
    Ok(())
}

/// Errors returned while selecting the ring-0 entry stack for a user context.

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum KernelEntryStackError {
    InvalidVirtualAddressWidth,
    NonCanonical,
    NotKernelAddress,
    Misaligned,

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]

/// Select the stack used by the next privilege transition from CPL3 to CPL0.
///
/// # Safety
/// The TSS must already be initialized, local interrupts must be disabled, and
/// `stack_top` must be the aligned top of a live, writable supervisor stack that
/// is mapped in the active address space and every address space that may run
/// before this value is changed again. Callers must update it before entering a
/// different process. The function validates the address shape, not the mapping
/// or ownership of the stack memory.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn set_kernel_entry_stack(
    stack_top: u64,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth);
    }
    if stack_top & 0xf != 0 {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::Misaligned);
    }
    if !rustix_kernel::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(stack_top, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::NonCanonical);
    }
    if stack_top & (1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1)) == 0 {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::NotKernelAddress);
    }

    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);
    // SAFETY: The function contract requires initialized TSS storage; the field
    // is packed, so write without creating an aligned reference to it.
    unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(stack_top) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Install the syscall callback for one synchronously entered user process.
///
/// # Safety
/// Local interrupts must be disabled, no other CPU may access this state, and
/// `context` must remain live until the callback is cleared after user return.
pub unsafe fn install_user_syscall_handler(
    handler: UserSyscallHandler,
    context: *mut (),
) -> Result<(), UserRuntimeError> {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The temporary stack operation is balanced at CPL 0.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags)) };
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and the first implementation is single-vCPU.
    if unsafe { runtime.read() }.is_some() {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::AlreadyInstalled);
    }
    // SAFETY: The caller keeps the function context live until clearing it.
    unsafe { runtime.write(Some(UserSyscallRuntime { handler, context })) };
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and assembly reads these values only on this CPU.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_PENDING).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_STATUS).write(0);
    }

    unsafe { runtime.write(None) };

/// # Safety
/// The process root must already be active in CR3, TSS.RSP0 must point to a live
/// supervisor stack mapped in both roots, the syscall callback must be installed,
/// maskable interrupts must be disabled, and user faults must remain fatal until
/// a process-fault handler is installed.
pub unsafe fn enter_user(
    frame: rustix_kernel::syscall::ValidatedUserIretFrame,
) -> Result<i32, UserRuntimeError> {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The temporary stack operation is balanced at CPL 0.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags)) };
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and only this CPU can update the runtime slot.
    if unsafe { runtime.read() }.is_none() {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::NotInstalled);
    }
    let frame = frame.into_raw();
    // SAFETY: The caller establishes the root, stack, TSS, callback, and fault
    // policy invariants. The assembly returns only after a process exit request.
    Ok(unsafe { rustix_enter_user(&frame) })
}

/// Register one callback for an allocated device IRQ vector.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The caller must keep the IRQ source masked while registering and ensure it
/// is masked whenever this callback is dispatched. The caller must serialize
/// registration against IRQ dispatch on every CPU. `handler` must not allocate,
/// format output, block, or unwind; it runs with IF disabled and owns the EOI.
/// The source must remain masked until all handler state is ready.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn register_irq_handler(
    vector: u8,
    handler: IrqHandler,
) -> Result<(), IrqRegistrationError> {
    let vector = vector as usize;
    if !(IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR).contains(&vector) {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::InvalidVector);
    }

    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: This reads RFLAGS at CPL 0; the temporary push/pop is balanced.
    unsafe {
        asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags));
    }
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }

    // SAFETY: The API contract requires registration to be serialized with IRQ
    // dispatch, and the vector has been checked against the table bounds.
    let slot = unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IRQ_HANDLERS)
            .cast::<Option<IrqHandler>>()
            .add(vector)
    };
    // SAFETY: `slot` points into the initialized static callback table.
    if unsafe { slot.read() }.is_some() {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::AlreadyRegistered);
    }
    // SAFETY: Registration is serialized by the caller's masking/IF contract.
    unsafe { slot.write(Some(handler)) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Device IRQ target called by the normalized assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_irq_dispatch(vector: u64) {
    // SAFETY: guard records this entry frame for the heap's debug checks; it
    // decrements automatically on every return path.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    if vector == APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR as u64 {
        return;
    }

    if !(IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR as u64..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR as u64).contains(&vector) {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }

    // SAFETY: Interrupt gates clear IF, and registration's safety contract
    // serializes writes against this read. No mutable reference is created.
    let handler = unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of!(IRQ_HANDLERS)
            .cast::<Option<IrqHandler>>()
            .add(vector as usize)
            .read()
    };
    match handler {
        Some(handler) => handler(),
        None => fatal_irq_halt(),
    }
}

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_syscall_dispatch(context: *mut rustix_kernel::syscall::SyscallContext) {
    use rustix_kernel::syscall::{
        decode_syscall, sanitize_user_iret_frame, SyscallArguments, SyscallError, SyscallRequest,
        UserIretFrame, ABI_VERSION,
    };

    crate::kprintln!("syscall dispatcher entered");
    // SAFETY: The assembly entry is reached only through the DPL-3 syscall gate;
    // the stack pointer refers to its normalized GPR and hardware return frame.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    let Some(context) = (unsafe { context.as_mut() }) else {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    };
    let address_bits = USER_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_BITS.load(Ordering::Acquire);
    if address_bits == 0 {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }
    let frame = UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: context.instruction_pointer,
        code_selector: context.code_selector,
        flags: context.flags,
        stack_pointer: context.stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: context.stack_selector,
    };
    let frame = match sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, address_bits) {
        Ok(frame) => frame.into_raw(),
        Err(_) => fatal_irq_halt(),
    };
    context.instruction_pointer = frame.instruction_pointer;
    context.code_selector = frame.code_selector;
    context.flags = frame.flags;
    context.stack_pointer = frame.stack_pointer;
    context.stack_selector = frame.stack_selector;

    let arguments = SyscallArguments {
        rdi: context.rdi,
        rsi: context.rsi,
        rdx: context.rdx,
        r10: context.r10,
        r8: context.r8,
        r9: context.r9,
    };
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: Interrupt gates clear IF and runtime registration requires IF=0;
    // this is a copy of the single-vCPU callback record, not a mutable reference.
    let runtime = unsafe { runtime.read() };
    let result = if let Some(runtime) = runtime {
        (runtime.handler)(context, runtime.context)
    } else {
        match decode_syscall(context.rax, arguments) {
            Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion) => ABI_VERSION as i64,
            Ok(
                SyscallRequest::Exit { .. }
                | SyscallRequest::Write { .. }
                | SyscallRequest::Wait { .. },
            ) => SyscallError::NotSupported.return_value(),
            Err(error) => error.return_value(),
        }
    };
    context.rax = result as u64;
}

fn fatal_irq_halt() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: Unknown device interrupts are fatal and must not be retried.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

/// Fatal exception target called by the assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_exception_dispatch(context: *const ExceptionContext) -> ! {
    // SAFETY: guard records this entry frame; this path never returns and the
    // frame is already doomed, so the increment is intentionally retained.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    // A fault raised while this handler is running (including a #DF on the
    // IST stack) must not re-enter the printing path; stop silently instead.
    if IN_FATAL_EXCEPTION.swap(true, Ordering::Acquire) {
        loop {
            // SAFETY: Re-entrant fatal diagnostics are deliberately silent.
            unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: The common assembly stub passes a pointer to its normalized stack
    // frame, which remains live for the duration of this non-returning handler.
    let context = unsafe { &*context };
    crate::kprintln!(
        "KERNEL EXCEPTION: vector {} ({}) error={:#018x} RIP={:#018x}",
        context.vector,
        exception_name(context.vector),
        context.error_code,
        context.rip
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CS={:#06x} SS={:#06x} RFLAGS={:#018x} RSP={:#018x}",
        context.cs,
        context.ss,
        context.rflags,
        context.rsp
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RAX={:#018x} RBX={:#018x} RCX={:#018x}",
        context.rax,
        context.rbx,
        context.rcx
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RDX={:#018x} RSI={:#018x} RDI={:#018x} RBP={:#018x}",
        context.rdx,
        context.rsi,
        context.rdi,
        context.rbp
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R8={:#018x} R9={:#018x} R10={:#018x} R11={:#018x}",
        context.r8,
        context.r9,
        context.r10,
        context.r11
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R12={:#018x} R13={:#018x} R14={:#018x} R15={:#018x}",
        context.r12,
        context.r13,
        context.r14,
        context.r15
    );

    if context.vector == 14 {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "page fault: present={} write={} user={} reserved={} instruction-fetch={}",
            context.error_code & 1 != 0,
            context.error_code & 2 != 0,
            context.error_code & 4 != 0,
            context.error_code & 8 != 0,
            context.error_code & 16 != 0
        );
        let fault_address: u64;
        // SAFETY: Reading CR2 is a privileged x86_64 operation in this handler.
        unsafe {
            asm!("mov {}, cr2", out(reg) fault_address, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags))
        };
        crate::kprintln!("page fault address (CR2): {:#018x}", fault_address);
    }

    loop {
        // SAFETY: Fatal exceptions are not recoverable in the current kernel.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

fn exception_name(vector: u64) -> &'static str {
    match vector {
        0 => "divide error",
        1 => "debug",
        2 => "non-maskable interrupt",
        3 => "breakpoint",
        4 => "overflow",
        5 => "bound range",
        6 => "invalid opcode",
        7 => "device not available",
        8 => "double fault",
        9 => "coprocessor segment overrun",
        10 => "invalid TSS",
        11 => "segment not present",
        12 => "stack-segment fault",
        13 => "general protection fault",
        14 => "page fault",
        16 => "x87 floating-point",
        17 => "alignment check",
        18 => "machine check",
        19 => "SIMD floating-point",
        20 => "virtualization",
        21 => "control protection",
        28 => "hypervisor injection",
        29 => "VMM communication",
        30 => "security exception",
        _ => "reserved or architecture-specific exception",
    }
}

/// The five-word privilege-return frame consumed by `IRETQ` in long mode.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct UserIretFrame {
    pub instruction_pointer: u64,
    pub code_selector: u64,
    pub flags: u64,
    pub stack_pointer: u64,
    pub stack_selector: u64,
}

/// A user return frame with validated selectors/addresses and kernel-chosen flags.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct ValidatedUserIretFrame(UserIretFrame);

impl ValidatedUserIretFrame {
    pub const fn into_raw(self) -> UserIretFrame {
        self.0
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserIretFrameError {
    InvalidAddressWidth,
    InvalidSelectors,
    InvalidFlags,
    InvalidInstructionPointer,
    InvalidStackPointer,
}

/// Validate the privilege-sensitive portion of an `IRETQ` frame and replace
/// user-supplied flags with a conservative kernel-selected value.
///
/// The safe flags deliberately leave IF clear until a process-aware interrupt
/// scheduler is installed. The caller must separately verify that RIP names an
/// executable process mapping and RSP names a writable stack mapping.
pub fn sanitize_user_iret_frame(
    frame: UserIretFrame,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<ValidatedUserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidAddressWidth);
    }
    if frame.code_selector != u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR)
        || frame.stack_selector != u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR)
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidSelectors);
    }
    if frame.flags & (1 << 1) == 0
        || frame.flags & (RFLAGS_IOPL | RFLAGS_NESTED_TASK | RFLAGS_VIRTUAL_8086) != 0
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidFlags);
    }

    let lower_half_end = 1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1);
    if frame.instruction_pointer >= lower_half_end
        || !crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(
            frame.instruction_pointer,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidInstructionPointer);
    }
    let stack_last = frame
        .stack_pointer
        .checked_sub(1)
        .filter(|address| *address < lower_half_end)
        .filter(|address| {
            crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(*address, virtual_address_bits)
        });
    if stack_last.is_none() || frame.stack_pointer & 0xf != 0 {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidStackPointer);
    }

    Ok(ValidatedUserIretFrame(UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: frame.instruction_pointer,
        code_selector: u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR),
        flags: SAFE_USER_RFLAGS,
        stack_pointer: frame.stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR),
    }))
}

39:- **Privilege stack:** a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt uses `TSS.RSP0`; it must point to the top of the current process's mapped, writable kernel-entry stack before user execution is resumed. The bootstrap TSS initially points to one static ring-0 stack. `interrupts::set_kernel_entry_stack` validates canonical upper-half address shape and alignment before updating `RSP0`, but no per-process stack is allocated and no scheduler path calls it yet. Callers must disable local interrupts and guarantee the stack is mapped writable in every address space that can run until the next update. A future SMP design needs per-CPU TSS and entry-stack state.
42:- **Return validation:** use `IRETQ`, not `SYSRET`. The dispatcher applies the host-tested five-word frame sanitizer on each return: it checks exact ring-3 selectors, lower-half canonical instruction/stack address shape, stack alignment, and privileged flags, then replaces user flags with the fixed reserved-bit value `0x2` (IF remains clear). The live dispatcher cannot yet verify RIP/RSP mappings against an owning process root or convert a malformed frame into process exit; those checks and user-fault isolation must be connected before enabling Ring 3 execution.
59:`src/elf.rs` parses little-endian x86_64 `ET_EXEC` images without allocation. It bounds the program-header count, load-segment count, and total mapped pages; checks file and virtual arithmetic, page alignment and `p_align` congruence, lower-half canonical ranges, non-overlapping page spans, readable segment flags, W^X, and that the entry point lies in a non-writable executable `PT_LOAD`. It rejects dynamic/interpreter and TLS segments and executable-stack requests. This initial format intentionally requires page-aligned load offsets/addresses and supports at most 64 program headers, 16 load segments, and 64 load pages. `populate_segment_page` copies one load page into an allocator-owned frame through `UserFrameMemory`, zero-filling bytes beyond the file payload. `load_into_process_root` now allocates, populates, selects cache attributes for, and maps every load page into an inactive `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` root. On failure, previously mapped pages remain owned by the root, the failure reports their count, and any unmapped frame is returned to the caller; destroying the newly created root is the recommended cleanup. The kernel build reproducibly compiles `crates/rustix-init` as a static ELF64 payload and boot parses/validates its entry and load-page count; loading it into a process root, stack allocation, activation, process lifecycle, and execution remain pending.

//! Stable, host-testable decoding for the initial Rustix syscall ABI.
//!
//! This module defines ABI values, validates register-level request shape,
//! sanitizes user return frames, and provides a host-testable bounded write
//! service. It does not install an entry gate or dispatch requests from hardware.

pub const ABI_MAJOR: u16 = 1;
pub const ABI_MINOR: u16 = 0;
pub const ABI_VERSION: u64 = (ABI_MAJOR as u64) << 16 | ABI_MINOR as u64;
pub const MAX_WRITE_BYTES: u64 = 4096;

    pub const fn into_raw(self) -> UserIretFrame {
        self.0

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserIretFrameError {
    InvalidAddressWidth,
    InvalidSelectors,
    InvalidFlags,
    InvalidInstructionPointer,
    InvalidStackPointer,
}

/// Validate the initial privilege-return frame, including the required 16-byte
/// stack alignment, and replace user flags with a conservative kernel value.
///
/// The safe flags deliberately leave IF clear until a process-aware interrupt
/// scheduler is installed. The caller must separately verify that RIP names an
/// executable process mapping and RSP names a writable stack mapping.
pub fn sanitize_user_iret_frame(
    frame: UserIretFrame,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<ValidatedUserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError> {
    sanitize_user_frame(frame, virtual_address_bits, true)
}

/// Sanitize a syscall's saved user return frame without imposing a new stack
/// alignment on an in-function RSP. SysV permits transient stack alignment while
/// executing a function; the active process root must still validate its mapping.
pub fn sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame(
    frame: UserIretFrame,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<ValidatedUserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError> {
    sanitize_user_frame(frame, virtual_address_bits, false)
}

fn sanitize_user_frame(
    frame: UserIretFrame,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    require_aligned_stack: bool,
) -> Result<ValidatedUserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidAddressWidth);
    }
    if frame.code_selector != u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR)
        || frame.stack_selector != u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR)
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidSelectors);
    }
    if frame.flags & (1 << 1) == 0
        || frame.flags & (RFLAGS_IOPL | RFLAGS_NESTED_TASK | RFLAGS_VIRTUAL_8086) != 0
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidFlags);
    }

    let lower_half_end = 1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1);
    if frame.instruction_pointer >= lower_half_end
        || !crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(
            frame.instruction_pointer,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidInstructionPointer);
    }
    let stack_last = frame
        .stack_pointer
        .checked_sub(1)
        .filter(|address| *address < lower_half_end)
        .filter(|address| {
            crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(*address, virtual_address_bits)
        });
    if stack_last.is_none() || (require_aligned_stack && frame.stack_pointer & 0xf != 0) {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidStackPointer);
    }

    Ok(ValidatedUserIretFrame(UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: frame.instruction_pointer,
        code_selector: u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR),
        flags: SAFE_USER_RFLAGS,
        stack_pointer: frame.stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR),
    }))
}

/// A syscall whose number and register-level arguments have been decoded.
