pub enum SyscallRequest {
    AbiVersion,
    Exit {
        status: i32,
    },
    Write {
        fd: u64,
        user_buffer: u64,
        length: usize,
    },
    Wait {
        child_pid: u64,
        status_address: Option<u64>,
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ConsoleStream {
    Stdout,
    Stderr,
}

/// The kernel-side sink for the v1 console descriptors.
pub trait ConsoleOutput {
    type Error;

    fn write(&mut self, stream: ConsoleStream, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, Self::Error>;
}

/// Copy and write one bounded v1 user buffer through a process root.
///
/// The complete user range is preflighted by `copy_from_user` before output.
/// If the frame backend faults after copying a prefix, that prefix is still
/// offered to the console and a positive short write is returned when accepted.
///
/// # Safety
/// The current kernel stack, including this function's fixed scratch buffer,
/// must not be mapped as a user frame in `process`. The boot allocator enforces
/// this by excluding the kernel image and bootstrap-stack spans from usable
/// frame allocation; future kernel stacks must preserve the same invariant.
pub unsafe fn write_user_buffer<M, U, O>(
    roots: &crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
    process: crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
    fd: u64,
    user_buffer: u64,
    length: usize,
    user_memory: &mut U,
    output: &mut O,
) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>
where
    M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory,
    U: crate::paging::UserFrameMemory,
    O: ConsoleOutput,
{
    use crate::paging::{ProcessUserCopyError, MAX_PROCESS_USER_COPY_BYTES};

    let stream = match fd {
        1 => ConsoleStream::Stdout,
        2 => ConsoleStream::Stderr,
        _ => return Err(SyscallError::BadFileDescriptor),
    };
    if length > MAX_WRITE_BYTES as usize {
        return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
    }
    if length == 0 {
        return Ok(0);
    }

    let mut scratch = [0; MAX_PROCESS_USER_COPY_BYTES];
    let copied = match unsafe {
        roots.copy_from_user(process, user_buffer, &mut scratch[..length], user_memory)
    } {
        Ok(copied) if copied <= length => copied,
        Ok(_) => return Err(SyscallError::Fault),
        Err(failure) if failure.transferred > 0 && failure.transferred <= length => {
            failure.transferred
        }
        Err(failure) => {
            return Err(match failure.cause {
                ProcessUserCopyError::LengthTooLarge => SyscallError::TooBig,
                ProcessUserCopyError::Memory(_) => SyscallError::Io,
                ProcessUserCopyError::InvalidHandle
                | ProcessUserCopyError::Releasing
                | ProcessUserCopyError::InvalidRange
                | ProcessUserCopyError::Unmapped
                | ProcessUserCopyError::PermissionDenied => SyscallError::Fault,
            });
        }
    };
    if copied == 0 {
        return Err(SyscallError::Io);
    }

    let written = output
        .write(stream, &scratch[..copied])
        .map_err(|_| SyscallError::Io)?;
    if written == 0 || written > copied {
        return Err(SyscallError::Io);
    }
    Ok(written)
}

/// Decode a v1 syscall number and its register arguments without touching user memory.
///
/// The exit status uses the low 32 bits of RDI, interpreted as a signed value.
/// A zero-length write preserves the supplied pointer without validating it; the
/// eventual syscall implementation must return zero before inspecting that pointer.
pub const fn decode_syscall(
    syscall_number: u64,
    arguments: SyscallArguments,
) -> Result<SyscallRequest, SyscallError> {
    match syscall_number {
        number::ABI_VERSION => Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion),
        number::EXIT => Ok(SyscallRequest::Exit {
            status: arguments.rdi as u32 as i32,
        }),
        number::WRITE => {
            if arguments.rdx > MAX_WRITE_BYTES {
                return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
            }
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Write {
                fd: arguments.rdi,
                user_buffer: arguments.rsi,
                length: arguments.rdx as usize,
            })
        }
        number::WAIT => Ok(SyscallRequest::Wait {
            child_pid: arguments.rdi,
            status_address: if arguments.rsi == 0 {
                None
            } else {
                Some(arguments.rsi)
            },
        }),
        _ => Err(SyscallError::NoSys),
    }
}

//!
//! Bootstrap installs exception and device-IRQ gates with maskable interrupts
//! disabled. APIC setup, route masking, handler registration, and explicit `sti`
//! are owned by the boot path; exceptions remain fatal-only.

static mut GDT: [u64; 7] = [0; 7];
static mut IDT: IdtTable = IdtTable([IdtEntry::MISSING; 256]);
static mut TSS: TaskStateSegment = TaskStateSegment::EMPTY;
static mut RING0_STACK: Stack = Stack([0; STACK_SIZE]);
static mut DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK: Stack = Stack([0; STACK_SIZE]);
static mut IRQ_HANDLERS: [Option<IrqHandler>; 256] = [None; 256];
/// Whether a fatal exception diagnostic is in progress. A fault from inside
/// the fatal path stops silently instead of recursively printing.
static IN_FATAL_EXCEPTION: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
static USER_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_BITS: AtomicU8 = AtomicU8::new(0);

pub type UserSyscallHandler =
    extern "C" fn(*mut rustix_kernel::syscall::SyscallContext, *mut ()) -> i64;

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct UserSyscallRuntime {
    handler: UserSyscallHandler,
    context: *mut (),
}

static mut USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME: Option<UserSyscallRuntime> = None;
#[no_mangle]
static mut RUSTIX_USER_RESUME_RSP: u64 = 0;
#[no_mangle]
static mut RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_PENDING: u8 = 0;
#[no_mangle]
static mut RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_STATUS: i32 = 0;
#[repr(C, align(16))]
struct UserKernelFxState([u8; 512]);
#[no_mangle]
static mut RUSTIX_USER_KERNEL_FX_STATE: UserKernelFxState = UserKernelFxState([0; 512]);

/// A device interrupt callback. The callback is responsible for issuing EOI.
pub type IrqHandler = extern "C" fn();

/// Reasons an IRQ callback could not be registered.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum IrqRegistrationError {
    InvalidVector,
    InterruptsEnabled,
    AlreadyRegistered,
}

// In 64-bit mode, exception entry saves SS:RSP even for a CPL 0 fault.
#[repr(C)]
// Register dumps are only compiled with the `fatal-register-dump` feature;
// the vector/error/RIP fields are always needed for the fatal diagnostic.
#[cfg_attr(not(feature = "fatal-register-dump"), allow(dead_code))]
pub(crate) struct ExceptionContext {
    r15: u64,
    r14: u64,
    r13: u64,
    r12: u64,
    r11: u64,
    r10: u64,
    r9: u64,
    r8: u64,
    rbp: u64,
    rdi: u64,
    rsi: u64,
    rdx: u64,
    rcx: u64,
    rbx: u64,
    rax: u64,
    vector: u64,
    error_code: u64,
    rip: u64,
    cs: u64,
    rflags: u64,
    rsp: u64,
    ss: u64,
}

const _: [(); 16] = [(); size_of::<IdtEntry>()];
const _: [(); 4096] = [(); size_of::<IdtTable>()];
const _: [(); 104] = [(); size_of::<TaskStateSegment>()];
const _: [(); 176] = [(); size_of::<ExceptionContext>()];
const _: [(); 120] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, vector)];
const _: [(); 128] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, error_code)];
const _: [(); 136] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, rip)];
const _: [(); 144] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, cs)];
const _: [(); 152] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, rflags)];
const _: [(); 160] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, rsp)];
const _: [(); 168] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, ss)];

extern "C" {
    static exception_stub_table: [usize; EXCEPTION_COUNT];
    static irq_stub_table: [usize; IRQ_STUB_COUNT];
    fn rustix_load_gdt(descriptor_table_pointer: *const DescriptorTablePointer);
    fn rustix_syscall_stub();
    fn rustix_enter_user(frame: *const rustix_kernel::syscall::UserIretFrame) -> i32;
}

/// Install a private kernel GDT/TSS, exception gates, and device IRQ gates.
///
/// The bootstrap runs with maskable interrupts disabled. This routine leaves
/// them disabled and does not modify CR3 or the inherited page-table hierarchy.
pub fn initialize() {
    // SAFETY: Single-core bootstrap ownership; the descriptor tables are private
    // static storage and are initialized before any gate is loaded.
    unsafe {
        asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack));
        initialize_tss();
        initialize_gdt();
        initialize_idt();
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_tss() {
    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    let double_fault_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let double_fault_top = unsafe { double_fault_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);

    // The architectural TSS fields are packed; use unaligned raw writes rather
    // than creating references to their potentially unaligned storage.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(ring0_top);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).ist1).write_unaligned(double_fault_top);
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_gdt() {
    let tss_base = core::ptr::addr_of!(TSS) as u64;
    let tss_limit = (size_of::<TaskStateSegment>() - 1) as u64;
    let low = (tss_limit & 0xffff)
        | ((tss_base & 0x00ff_ffff) << 16)
        | (TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE << 40)
        | ((tss_limit & 0x000f_0000) << 32)
        | ((tss_base & 0xff00_0000) << 32);
    let high = tss_base >> 32;

    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[0]).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[1]).write(0x00af_9a00_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[2]).write(0x00cf_9200_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[3]).write(low);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[4]).write(high);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[5]).write(USER_DATA_DESCRIPTOR);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[6]).write(USER_CODE_DESCRIPTOR);
    }

    let gdtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<[u64; 7]>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(GDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: `GDT` and its TSS descriptor are initialized and remain live.
    unsafe { rustix_load_gdt(&gdtr) };
}

unsafe fn initialize_idt() {
    let idt_entries = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IDT.0).cast::<IdtEntry>();
    let stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(exception_stub_table).cast::<usize>();

    for vector in 0..EXCEPTION_COUNT {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains exactly 32 stub addresses.
        let handler = unsafe { stubs.add(vector).read() } as u64;
        let ist = if vector == 8 { 1 } else { 0 };
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, ist));
        }
    }

    let irq_stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(irq_stub_table).cast::<usize>();
    for vector in IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains one stub for each allocated vector.
        let handler = unsafe { irq_stubs.add(vector - IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR).read() } as u64;
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, 0));
        }
    }
    // Vector 0x80 is reserved from device allocation and uses its own DPL-3
    // interrupt gate rather than the generic device-IRQ dispatch path.
    // SAFETY: The assembly defines this dedicated entry stub in the kernel image.
    unsafe {
        idt_entries
            .add(USER_SYSCALL_VECTOR)
            .write(IdtEntry::user_interrupt_gate(
                rustix_syscall_stub as *const () as usize as u64,
            ));
    }

    // SAFETY: The final table entry is the dedicated 0xff spurious-IRQ stub.
    let spurious_handler =
        unsafe { irq_stubs.add(IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT + IRQ_UNWIRED_COUNT).read() } as u64;
    // SAFETY: The APIC spurious vector is a valid IDT index.
    unsafe {
        idt_entries
            .add(APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR)
            .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(spurious_handler, 0));
    }
    // Vectors 0xf0-0xfe have no registered source; wire them to a controlled
    // fatal stop (through the shared dispatch, which halts) instead of leaving
    // non-present gates that would cascade into #GP with no diagnostics.
    for vector in IRQ_UNWIRED_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_UNWIRED_LAST_VECTOR {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table provides one stub for each vector.
        let handler =
            unsafe { irq_stubs.add(IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT + (vector - IRQ_UNWIRED_FIRST_VECTOR)) }.read()
                as u64;
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, 0));
        }
    }

    let idtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<IdtTable>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(IDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: Every architectural exception gate is initialized in static storage.
    unsafe { asm!("lidt [{}]", in(reg) &idtr, options(readonly, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
}

/// Configure the active user virtual-address width used to sanitize syscall returns.
///
/// Call after boot CPU discovery and before any CPL3 code can execute.
pub fn configure_user_address_width(virtual_address_bits: u8) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth);
    }
    USER_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_BITS.store(virtual_address_bits, Ordering::Release);
    Ok(())
}

/// Errors returned while selecting the ring-0 entry stack for a user context.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum KernelEntryStackError {
    InvalidVirtualAddressWidth,
    NonCanonical,
    NotKernelAddress,
    Misaligned,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserRuntimeError {
    InterruptsEnabled,
    AlreadyInstalled,
    NotInstalled,
}

/// Select the stack used by the next privilege transition from CPL3 to CPL0.
///
/// # Safety
/// The TSS must already be initialized, local interrupts must be disabled, and
/// `stack_top` must be the aligned top of a live, writable supervisor stack that
/// is mapped in the active address space and every address space that may run
/// before this value is changed again. Callers must update it before entering a
/// different process. The function validates the address shape, not the mapping
/// or ownership of the stack memory.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn set_kernel_entry_stack(
    stack_top: u64,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth);
    }
    if stack_top & 0xf != 0 {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::Misaligned);
    }
    if !rustix_kernel::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(stack_top, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::NonCanonical);
    }
    if stack_top & (1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1)) == 0 {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::NotKernelAddress);
    }

    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);
    // SAFETY: The function contract requires initialized TSS storage; the field
    // is packed, so write without creating an aligned reference to it.
    unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(stack_top) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Install the syscall callback for one synchronously entered user process.
///
/// # Safety
/// Local interrupts must be disabled, no other CPU may access this state, and
/// `context` must remain live until the callback is cleared after user return.
pub unsafe fn install_user_syscall_handler(
    handler: UserSyscallHandler,
    context: *mut (),
) -> Result<(), UserRuntimeError> {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The temporary stack operation is balanced at CPL 0.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags)) };
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and the first implementation is single-vCPU.
    if unsafe { runtime.read() }.is_some() {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::AlreadyInstalled);
    }
    // SAFETY: The caller keeps the function context live until clearing it.
    unsafe { runtime.write(Some(UserSyscallRuntime { handler, context })) };
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and assembly reads these values only on this CPU.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_PENDING).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_STATUS).write(0);
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Remove the user-process syscall callback after returning to the kernel root.
///
/// # Safety
/// Local interrupts must be disabled, and no syscall callback may be in flight.
pub unsafe fn clear_user_syscall_handler() {
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: The API contract guarantees single-vCPU exclusion with IF clear.
    unsafe { runtime.write(None) };
}

/// Request the syscall/exception assembly exit path after restoring the kernel root.
///
/// # Safety
/// The kernel root must be active, the process root must no longer be active,
/// and execution must be on this single CPU with maskable interrupts disabled.
pub unsafe fn request_user_process_exit(status: i32) {
    // SAFETY: The caller satisfies the documented ordering and single-vCPU contract.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_STATUS).write(status);
        core::sync::atomic::compiler_fence(Ordering::Release);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_PENDING).write(1);
    }
}

/// Enter a validated user frame and return only through the process-exit path.
///
/// # Safety
/// The process root must already be active in CR3, TSS.RSP0 must point to a live
/// supervisor stack mapped in both roots, the syscall callback must be installed,
/// maskable interrupts must be disabled, and user faults must remain fatal until
/// a process-fault handler is installed.
pub unsafe fn enter_user(
    frame: rustix_kernel::syscall::ValidatedUserIretFrame,
) -> Result<i32, UserRuntimeError> {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The temporary stack operation is balanced at CPL 0.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags)) };
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and only this CPU can update the runtime slot.
    if unsafe { runtime.read() }.is_none() {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::NotInstalled);
    }
    let frame = frame.into_raw();
    // SAFETY: The caller establishes the root, stack, TSS, callback, and fault
    // policy invariants. The assembly returns only after a process exit request.
    Ok(unsafe { rustix_enter_user(&frame) })
}

/// Register one callback for an allocated device IRQ vector.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The caller must keep the IRQ source masked while registering and ensure it
/// is masked whenever this callback is dispatched. The caller must serialize
/// registration against IRQ dispatch on every CPU. `handler` must not allocate,
/// format output, block, or unwind; it runs with IF disabled and owns the EOI.
/// The source must remain masked until all handler state is ready.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn register_irq_handler(
    vector: u8,
    handler: IrqHandler,
) -> Result<(), IrqRegistrationError> {
    let vector = vector as usize;
    if !(IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR).contains(&vector) {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::InvalidVector);
    }

    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: This reads RFLAGS at CPL 0; the temporary push/pop is balanced.
    unsafe {
        asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags));
    }
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }

    // SAFETY: The API contract requires registration to be serialized with IRQ
    // dispatch, and the vector has been checked against the table bounds.
    let slot = unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IRQ_HANDLERS)
            .cast::<Option<IrqHandler>>()
            .add(vector)
    };
    // SAFETY: `slot` points into the initialized static callback table.
    if unsafe { slot.read() }.is_some() {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::AlreadyRegistered);
    }
    // SAFETY: Registration is serialized by the caller's masking/IF contract.
    unsafe { slot.write(Some(handler)) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Device IRQ target called by the normalized assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_irq_dispatch(vector: u64) {
    // SAFETY: guard records this entry frame for the heap's debug checks; it
    // decrements automatically on every return path.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    if vector == APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR as u64 {
        return;
    }

    if !(IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR as u64..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR as u64).contains(&vector) {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }

    // SAFETY: Interrupt gates clear IF, and registration's safety contract
    // serializes writes against this read. No mutable reference is created.
    let handler = unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of!(IRQ_HANDLERS)
            .cast::<Option<IrqHandler>>()
            .add(vector as usize)
            .read()
    };
    match handler {
        Some(handler) => handler(),
        None => fatal_irq_halt(),
    }
}

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_syscall_dispatch(context: *mut rustix_kernel::syscall::SyscallContext) {
    use rustix_kernel::syscall::{
        decode_syscall, sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame, SyscallArguments, SyscallError,
        SyscallRequest, UserIretFrame, ABI_VERSION,
    };

    crate::kprintln!("syscall dispatcher entered");
    // SAFETY: The assembly entry is reached only through the DPL-3 syscall gate;
    // the stack pointer refers to its normalized GPR and hardware return frame.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    let Some(context) = (unsafe { context.as_mut() }) else {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    };
    let address_bits = USER_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_BITS.load(Ordering::Acquire);
    if address_bits == 0 {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }
    let frame = UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: context.instruction_pointer,
        code_selector: context.code_selector,
        flags: context.flags,
        stack_pointer: context.stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: context.stack_selector,
    };
    let frame = match sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame(frame, address_bits) {
        Ok(frame) => frame.into_raw(),
        Err(_) => fatal_irq_halt(),
    };
    context.instruction_pointer = frame.instruction_pointer;
    context.code_selector = frame.code_selector;
    context.flags = frame.flags;
    context.stack_pointer = frame.stack_pointer;
    context.stack_selector = frame.stack_selector;

    let arguments = SyscallArguments {
        rdi: context.rdi,
        rsi: context.rsi,
        rdx: context.rdx,
        r10: context.r10,
        r8: context.r8,
        r9: context.r9,
    };
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: Interrupt gates clear IF and runtime registration requires IF=0;
    // this is a copy of the single-vCPU callback record, not a mutable reference.
    let runtime = unsafe { runtime.read() };
    let result = if let Some(runtime) = runtime {
        (runtime.handler)(context, runtime.context)
    } else {
        match decode_syscall(context.rax, arguments) {
            Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion) => ABI_VERSION as i64,
            Ok(
                SyscallRequest::Exit { .. }
                | SyscallRequest::Write { .. }
                | SyscallRequest::Wait { .. },
            ) => SyscallError::NotSupported.return_value(),
            Err(error) => error.return_value(),
        }
    };
    context.rax = result as u64;
}

fn fatal_irq_halt() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: Unknown device interrupts are fatal and must not be retried.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

/// Fatal exception target called by the assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_exception_dispatch(context: *const ExceptionContext) -> ! {
    // SAFETY: guard records this entry frame; this path never returns and the
    // frame is already doomed, so the increment is intentionally retained.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    // A fault raised while this handler is running (including a #DF on the
    // IST stack) must not re-enter the printing path; stop silently instead.
    if IN_FATAL_EXCEPTION.swap(true, Ordering::Acquire) {
        loop {
            // SAFETY: Re-entrant fatal diagnostics are deliberately silent.
            unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: The common assembly stub passes a pointer to its normalized stack
    // frame, which remains live for the duration of this non-returning handler.
    let context = unsafe { &*context };
    crate::kprintln!(
        "KERNEL EXCEPTION: vector {} ({}) error={:#018x} RIP={:#018x}",
        context.vector,
        exception_name(context.vector),
        context.error_code,
        context.rip
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CS={:#06x} SS={:#06x} RFLAGS={:#018x} RSP={:#018x}",
        context.cs,
        context.ss,
        context.rflags,
        context.rsp
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RAX={:#018x} RBX={:#018x} RCX={:#018x}",
        context.rax,
        context.rbx,
        context.rcx
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RDX={:#018x} RSI={:#018x} RDI={:#018x} RBP={:#018x}",
        context.rdx,
        context.rsi,
        context.rdi,
        context.rbp
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R8={:#018x} R9={:#018x} R10={:#018x} R11={:#018x}",
        context.r8,
        context.r9,
        context.r10,
        context.r11
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R12={:#018x} R13={:#018x} R14={:#018x} R15={:#018x}",
        context.r12,
        context.r13,
        context.r14,
        context.r15
    );

    if context.vector == 14 {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "page fault: present={} write={} user={} reserved={} instruction-fetch={}",
            context.error_code & 1 != 0,
            context.error_code & 2 != 0,
            context.error_code & 4 != 0,
            context.error_code & 8 != 0,
            context.error_code & 16 != 0
        );
        let fault_address: u64;
        // SAFETY: Reading CR2 is a privileged x86_64 operation in this handler.
        unsafe {
            asm!("mov {}, cr2", out(reg) fault_address, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags))
        };
        crate::kprintln!("page fault address (CR2): {:#018x}", fault_address);
    }

    loop {
        // SAFETY: Fatal exceptions are not recoverable in the current kernel.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

fn exception_name(vector: u64) -> &'static str {
    match vector {
        0 => "divide error",
        1 => "debug",
        2 => "non-maskable interrupt",
        3 => "breakpoint",
        4 => "overflow",
        5 => "bound range",
        6 => "invalid opcode",
        7 => "device not available",
        8 => "double fault",
        9 => "coprocessor segment overrun",
        10 => "invalid TSS",
        11 => "segment not present",
        12 => "stack-segment fault",
        13 => "general protection fault",
        14 => "page fault",
        16 => "x87 floating-point",
        17 => "alignment check",
        18 => "machine check",
        19 => "SIMD floating-point",
        20 => "virtualization",
        21 => "control protection",
        28 => "hypervisor injection",
        29 => "VMM communication",
        30 => "security exception",
        _ => "reserved or architecture-specific exception",
    }
}

global_asm!(
    r#"
    .section .text
    .code64

    .macro RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR name, number
    .global \name
    .type \name, @function
\name:
    push 0
    push \number
    jmp rustix_exception_common
    .endm

    .macro RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR name, number
    .global \name
    .type \name, @function
\name:

# Unix-like process and syscall direction

**Status: partial address-space construction, host-tested syscall ABI decoding/write service, sanitized user IRETQ frames, bounded static ELF64 loading into an inactive process root, fixed-capacity lifecycle policy, and a dedicated DPL-3 `int 0x80` entry/return stub. The hardware dispatcher currently implements ABI-version discovery and returns `ENOTSUP` for process operations; no process-root runtime or Ring 3 execution is integrated.**

Rustix aims to expose a small, versioned syscall surface that can support Unix-like processes and tools. The kernel must own this interface rather than inherit an ABI accidentally from a bootloader or emulator.

## Proposed compatibility principles

- Processes have independent virtual address spaces and explicit lifecycle states.
- File descriptors are per-process integer handles to kernel-managed objects; descriptor inheritance, close-on-exec, duplication, and sharing semantics must be specified together.
- Syscalls use one documented error convention and stable numeric identifiers. New operations must not silently repurpose old numbers.
- Arguments crossing privilege boundaries are copied or validated using narrowly scoped helpers. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::copy_from_user` and `copy_to_user` preflight the complete lower-half mapped range, check writable metadata for kernel-to-user copies, and operate only on owned frame tokens through `UserFrameMemory`; they never form a Rust reference from a user virtual address. Backend copy faults report the completed prefix; hardware fault recovery is not yet implemented.
- Blocking, interruption, cancellation, and restart behavior are explicit for each syscall class.
- A compatibility layer (for example, POSIX-shaped libc behavior) remains separate from internal kernel APIs.

## Initial syscall ABI v1 contract (specified; register decoding implemented)

ABI version `1.0` is identified by `abi_version()`, syscall number `0`, returning `0x0001_0000` in `RAX`. The first entry path uses the register convention below. In v1, `RAX` returns a signed 64-bit result: nonnegative values are success (including byte counts and PIDs); errors are negative stable error numbers. ABI versioning is append-only: existing syscall numbers, argument meanings, layouts, and error values never change or get reused. There is no POSIX compatibility claim. `src/syscall.rs` implements the stable number/error constants, host-tested request decoding and write service, and the assembly-matched syscall context layout. `interrupts.rs` installs the DPL-3 gate and dedicated entry stub; hardware dispatch currently returns the ABI version and reports known process operations as `ENOTSUP` until a live process runtime is connected.

| Number | Call | Register arguments | Result / behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `abi_version` | none | `0x0001_0000` (major 1, minor 0). |
| 1 | `exit` | `RDI`: signed 32-bit status in the low 32 bits (upper bits ignored) | Does not return; status is retained exactly by the parent wait record. |
| 2 | `write` | `RDI`: fd, `RSI`: user buffer, `RDX`: byte length | Returns bytes accepted; a short positive result is valid. Initial descriptors 1 and 2 are stdout/stderr console streams; other descriptors return `-EBADF`. Maximum request is 4096 bytes; zero length returns 0 without validating the pointer. |
| 3 | `wait` | `RDI`: child PID (0 means any child), `RSI`: optional user pointer to signed 32-bit exit status | Blocks until a matching child exits and returns its PID. A non-null status output must be writable before the child is reaped; no matching child returns `-ECHILD`. |

All other numbers are unassigned and return `-ENOSYS`; assigning a number later is an additive extension, never a reinterpretation. Descriptor 0 is reserved for input but v1 has no `read`, `open`, `close`, or `dup` call. Standard descriptors exist for the process lifetime; inheritance and general file-object semantics are not yet exposed. The initial process is created by the kernel loader, not a syscall.

Stable v1 error numbers (returned negated in `RAX`) are: `1 EINVAL`, `2 EBADF`, `3 EFAULT`, `4 ENOMEM`, `5 ECHILD`, `6 EINTR`, `7 EIO`, `8 ENOSYS`, `9 E2BIG`, `10 EOVERFLOW`, and `11 ENOTSUP`. Unknown syscall numbers return `-ENOSYS`. Pointer-plus-length ranges use checked arithmetic and must lie wholly in a mapped lower-half user range. `write` preflights the whole input range before output; a later endpoint failure may return a short count, and an error before progress returns `-EIO`. A copy fault after progress returns the completed prefix; unrecoverable hardware faults remain process-fatal until user-mode exception handling is implemented. `wait` validates its optional output range before blocking and keeps the child waitable if copying the exit status fails. V1 has no signals, asynchronous interruption, or automatic syscall restart; wait is uninterruptible.

All ABI integers are fixed-width little-endian x86_64 values. The wait status is one signed 32-bit integer with no implicit padding or extra fields. No other user-visible structs exist in v1.

## Initial x86_64 entry design (Milestone 4; not implemented)

The first single-vCPU user-mode slice will enter the kernel with `int $0x80` through a dedicated IDT interrupt gate at DPL 3 and return with `IRETQ`. This intentionally avoids `SYSCALL`/`SYSRET`, `STAR`/`LSTAR`/`FMASK`, and `SWAPGS` state transitions in the first userspace path. It is a provisional architecture decision, not a published or implemented syscall ABI.

- **Vector ownership:** `0x80` lies inside the device-vector range (`0x20..=0xef`) and is reserved by `InterruptVectorAllocator`; generic IRQ allocation/release cannot claim it. The IDT installs a dedicated DPL-3 interrupt gate rather than the generic device-IRQ stub. Its assembly entry rejects CPL0 invocation, saves all GPRs and x87/SSE state, clears the direction flag, and calls a normalized Rust dispatcher with IF clear. The dispatcher currently implements only ABI-version discovery; process operations remain unavailable.
- **Selectors:** the current GDT uses `0x08` for kernel code, `0x10` for kernel data, and `0x18` for the two-slot TSS descriptor. Ring-3 data and 64-bit code descriptors are appended at GDT indexes 5 and 6, with compile-time selector assertions for user data `0x2b` and user code `0x33` (RPL 3); the data selector is loaded into user `SS` on return. They are installed at bootstrap but remain unused until a validated return path exists.
- **Privilege stack:** a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt uses `TSS.RSP0`; it must point to the top of the current process's mapped, writable kernel-entry stack before user execution is resumed. The bootstrap TSS initially points to one static ring-0 stack. `interrupts::set_kernel_entry_stack` validates canonical upper-half address shape and alignment before updating `RSP0`, but no per-process stack is allocated and no scheduler path calls it yet. Callers must disable local interrupts and guarantee the stack is mapped writable in every address space that can run until the next update. A future SMP design needs per-CPU TSS and entry-stack state.
- **Entry frame and state:** the dedicated assembly stub saves all GPRs in the `SyscallContext` layout, passes the five-word privilege frame separately from the fatal-exception frame, and saves/restores x87/SSE state around the Rust dispatcher; AVX remains disabled under the current CPU-state policy. Kernel code runs with the direction flag clear. The dispatcher does not form Rust references from user pointers. Blocking/scheduler switches and syscall-side user-memory access are not yet wired.
- **Initial register convention:** `RAX` carries the syscall number; arguments use `RDI`, `RSI`, `RDX`, `R10`, `R8`, and `R9`; `RAX` carries the result. This is only a proposed register convention. It becomes stable only together with ABI version discovery, syscall numbers, errors, and transfer semantics below.
- **Return validation:** use `IRETQ`, not `SYSRET`. Initial entry uses a host-tested frame sanitizer that requires exact ring-3 selectors, a canonical lower-half instruction pointer, a lower-half stack range, 16-byte initial stack alignment, and safe flags. Syscall resume uses a separate sanitizer that keeps exact selectors, canonical lower-half address shape, and privileged-flag checks but does not impose 16-byte alignment on an in-function RSP; it replaces user flags with `0x2` (IF remains clear). Once a process is active, the dispatcher also validates the saved instruction pointer against an executable mapping and the saved stack pointer against a writable NX mapping. A malformed frame is converted into process exit rather than returned to CPL3.
- **NMI and interrupt policy:** no GS-base swap is needed on this entry path. An NMI can still arrive during entry; the current NMI/exception path is fatal-only, and this design does not claim to recover from it. Keep that behavior explicit until user-origin exception/NMI policy is implemented and tested. Ordinary maskable IRQs may resume only after the entry state and scheduler ownership are consistent.

This design depends on a process-owned address space that maps the syscall entry/return code, IDT, GDT, TSS, and the active kernel stack safely. No Ring 3 execution should be enabled until the address-space implementation is reviewed and validated.

### Process address spaces (design; root construction partially implemented)

Use a separate four- or five-level root per process. The initial source is the retained active clone of Limine's hierarchy, not a curated clean-room root. Each process root owns its root page, all lower-half intermediate tables, and every user leaf frame. Keep the kernel-root owner alive for the lifetime of every process root. Copy only upper-half top-level entries from that owner into each process root; these entries are non-owning references to shared kernel subtrees, not deep copies, and must never be released by a process teardown. Do not copy lower-half entries from the kernel root.

Before publishing a shared kernel subtree, validate its page-table structure and physical bounds and reject any effectively user-accessible leaf. U/S permission is the conjunction of every entry on a path, so a U/S bit on one non-leaf alone does not grant user access. When copying upper-half root entries, clear their U/S bit as defense in depth; a user leaf then cannot become accessible if a lower entry changes. `paging::validate_supervisor_kernel_half` implements the bounded, read-only structural/effective-permission preflight, but it does not install roots or prove physical backing is readable; the supplied reader must provide that access guarantee. Sharing the active clone means every accepted upper-half supervisor mapping and alias is present in every process CR3. This is not a curated kernel map or kernel-page-table isolation, and it provides no transient-execution protection. User mappings remain private to one process, are confined to the lower canonical half, preserve W^X, and are non-global in the first implementation.

The kernel address-space owner is the only authority allowed to modify shared upper-half tables. Mutations must be serialized with local interrupts disabled on the current single-vCPU system and invalidate the affected local translation before the mapping change is relied on. A process root may not edit or reclaim shared tables. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::destroy` releases only private user leaves, intermediate tables, and the root; the caller must first switch CR3 to a different live root and invalidate this root's local non-global translations. Keep the shared kernel owner alive. PCID-aware invalidation and SMP shootdown remain unsupported and need a separate design.

The current `CandidatePageTables` deep-clones the inherited hierarchy, tracks all cloned tables as owned, and holds an exclusive mutable borrow of one memory backend; it is not itself the process-address-space abstraction. `SharedKernelHalf` validates and snapshots the sanitized upper root entries while borrowing the kernel owner. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` uses one exclusive backend borrow for multiple private roots, maps allocator-owned user 4 KiB leaves only in inactive lower halves, retains writable/executable permission metadata, validates that an initial instruction pointer is executable and its stack pointer resolves to a writable NX page, offers one-page-bounded range-preflighted copy-in/copy-out through a separate `UserFrameMemory` backend, and destroys private leaf/table/root frames without freeing shared subtrees. The copy helpers are unsafe because the caller must provide kernel buffers that do not alias the process's mapped user frames. Host tests cover four- and five-level sharing, U/S sanitization, independent roots/mappings, initial user-state permission checks, copy permissions and cross-page copies, unmap ownership return, active-root release rejection, and allocation/prepare-failure rollback. The target Limine HHDM `UserFrameMemory` adapter is currently compiled only for the opt-in frame probe; `just frame-smoke` exercises bounded copy, zero-length, and out-of-range behavior on an allocator-owned frame. It is not yet connected to process-root copies. This is still not executable process support: callers must perform CR3 transitions and local TLB invalidation before marking a root inactive; no process scheduler, syscall entry, loader, or fault policy is integrated. Keep the kernel owner alive and immutable for the shared view's lifetime; callers must use a distinct page-table backend for process-owned tables.

### Static ELF64 image validation and page initialization (partial)

`src/elf.rs` parses little-endian x86_64 `ET_EXEC` images without allocation. It bounds the program-header count, load-segment count, and total mapped pages; checks file and virtual arithmetic, page alignment and `p_align` congruence, lower-half canonical ranges, non-overlapping page spans, readable segment flags, W^X, and that the entry point lies in a non-writable executable `PT_LOAD`. It rejects dynamic/interpreter and TLS segments and executable-stack requests. This initial format intentionally requires page-aligned load offsets/addresses and supports at most 64 program headers, 16 load segments, and 64 load pages. `populate_segment_page` copies one load page into an allocator-owned frame through `UserFrameMemory`, zero-filling bytes beyond the file payload. `load_into_process_root` now allocates, populates, selects cache attributes for, and maps every load page into an inactive `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` root. On failure, previously mapped pages remain owned by the root, the failure reports their count, and any unmapped frame is returned to the caller; destroying the newly created root is the recommended cleanup. The kernel build reproducibly compiles `crates/rustix-init` as a static ELF64 payload and boot parses/validates its entry and load-page count; loading it into a process root, stack allocation, activation, process lifecycle, and execution remain pending.

## ABI decisions still pending beyond v1

The initial v1 versioning, error encoding, syscall numbers, register-level request decoding, and assembly-matched syscall context layout are implemented in `src/syscall.rs`. The dedicated `int 0x80` dispatcher applies return-frame shape/selector/flag sanitization and serves ABI-version discovery; process calls currently return `ENOTSUP`. The host-tested `write_user_buffer` service validates descriptors 1/2, bypasses pointer validation for zero-length writes, preflights bounded user copies, and preserves short writes/partial-copy progress through a console-output interface, but is not yet connected to the hardware dispatcher. The target HHDM frame backend is not wired to a running process. Wait status transfer and no-restart behavior remain specified but unintegrated. `src/process.rs` adds a host-tested fixed-capacity identity/exit-state policy with parent/child tracking and nonblocking `try_wait`; scheduler blocking, address-space ownership, descriptor tables, and syscall integration remain unimplemented. Still to be specified before adding those operations are process-creation/exec and file-action semantics, general descriptor sharing/duplication/inheritance, read/open/close behavior, signal-like asynchronous delivery, clocks, and any additional structure layouts.

## Suggested first user-visible slice

After address spaces, scheduler, and storage primitives exist, implement a controlled `init` process with a small syscall subset: process exit, read/write through descriptors, open/close, and wait. Add end-to-end tests for invalid pointers, partial transfers, descriptor lifetime, process exit status, and ABI version negotiation before describing it as Unix-compatible.

## State
- The user’s commit is `1e3dac9`. **Do not commit, stage, reset, create branches, or alter history.** Preserve `.zed/tasks.json` and all existing staged/partially staged work.

  - Loads the bundled ELF into a process root, maps a writable NX stack, validates entry/stack mappings, activates the root, enters Ring 3, and dispatches ABI-version, write, and exit syscalls.

If routing CPL3 exceptions to the exit trampoline, **drop `InterruptContextGuard` before the trampoline** to avoid leaking interrupt nesting depth.         if record.state != ProcessState::Running {

     1	# Interrupts and IRQ vector allocation
     2	
     3	## Current implementation
     4	
     5	`src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` installs the bootstrap GDT, TSS, exception gates for vectors 0–31, device IRQ stubs, and the APIC spurious-vector gate. Exceptions remain fatal-only. Maskable interrupts start disabled and are enabled only after the validated APIC route, registered handler, and acknowledgement path are ready.
     6	
     7	`src/irq.rs` provides a host-tested, allocation-free token allocator for device vectors `0x20..=0xef` except reserved syscall vector `0x80`; exception vectors and the reserved upper range are also excluded. The IDT overrides `0x80` with a dedicated DPL-3 interrupt gate and assembly stub. The stub rejects CPL0 invocation, saves the full GPR set and x87/SSE state on the TSS entry stack, and dispatches a normalized syscall context with IF clear; the current dispatcher only returns ABI-version discovery and `ENOTSUP` for process operations. `rustix_irq_dispatch` invokes the registered handler, returns for the APIC spurious vector without EOI, and halts on unregistered/unexpected vectors. Device handlers own their EOI. Vector registration is performed with IF clear before the corresponding I/O APIC source is unmasked.
     8	
     9	The initial hardware target is single-vCPU QEMU `q35`: validated ACPI/MADT topology, local APIC and I/O APIC, masked legacy PIC routing, MADT-resolved ISA routes, and a periodic 8254 PIT tick near 100 Hz. OVMF smokes validate PIT delivery/EOI, non-yielding timer preemption, x87/SSE state preservation, and UART/keyboard IRQ delivery. Host tests cover vector ownership and PIT/time arithmetic; they do not replace privileged QEMU coverage.
    10	
    11	The scheduler is single-vCPU and supports cooperative waits/yields plus PIT-driven timer preemption. The timer handler advances ticks and sends APIC EOI before any scheduling switch. The common IRQ stub saves the interrupted x87/SSE state before Rust dispatch and restores the selected context before `IRETQ`; the context switch keeps aligned per-context FXSAVE areas. IRQ-safe spin locks save and restore the prior IF state, and the global heap uses one; scheduler mutations are separately serialized by masking local interrupts. IRQ/exception handlers remain bounded and allocation-free, and no current IRQ handler acquires the heap lock. SMP, per-CPU state, and physical-hardware validation remain future work.

//! Bootstrap GDT, TSS, and interrupt entry for x86_64.
//!
//! Bootstrap installs exception and device-IRQ gates with maskable interrupts
//! disabled. APIC setup, route masking, handler registration, and explicit `sti`
//! are owned by the boot path. Kernel exceptions and selected critical user
//! exceptions remain fatal; the diagnostic user-process path can reap other CPL3 faults.

use core::arch::{asm, global_asm};
use core::mem::size_of;
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU8, Ordering};

use rustix_kernel::sync::InterruptContextGuard;

const EXCEPTION_COUNT: usize = 32;
const IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR: usize = 0x20;
const IRQ_LAST_VECTOR: usize = 0xef;
const IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT: usize = IRQ_LAST_VECTOR - IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR + 1;
const APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR: usize = 0xff;
/// Vectors 0xf0-0xfe have no registered source or IDT-worthy meaning today.
/// They are wired to a controlled fatal stop instead of left non-present.
const IRQ_UNWIRED_FIRST_VECTOR: usize = 0xf0;
const IRQ_UNWIRED_LAST_VECTOR: usize = 0xfe;
const IRQ_UNWIRED_COUNT: usize = IRQ_UNWIRED_LAST_VECTOR - IRQ_UNWIRED_FIRST_VECTOR + 1;
const IRQ_STUB_COUNT: usize = IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT + IRQ_UNWIRED_COUNT + 1;
const USER_SYSCALL_VECTOR: usize = rustix_kernel::syscall::USER_SYSCALL_VECTOR as usize;
const KERNEL_CODE_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x08;
pub const USER_DATA_SELECTOR: u16 = rustix_kernel::syscall::USER_DATA_SELECTOR;
pub const USER_CODE_SELECTOR: u16 = rustix_kernel::syscall::USER_CODE_SELECTOR;
const USER_DATA_DESCRIPTOR: u64 = 0x00cf_f200_0000_ffff;
const USER_CODE_DESCRIPTOR: u64 = 0x00af_fa00_0000_ffff;
const _: [(); 0x2b] = [(); USER_DATA_SELECTOR as usize];
const _: [(); 0x33] = [(); USER_CODE_SELECTOR as usize];
const _: [(); 208] = [(); IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT];
const STACK_SIZE: usize = 16 * 1024;
const TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE: u64 = 0x89;

#[repr(C, packed)]
struct DescriptorTablePointer {
    limit: u16,
    base: u64,
}

#[repr(C, align(16))]
struct IdtTable([IdtEntry; 256]);

#[repr(C, packed)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct IdtEntry {
    offset_low: u16,
    selector: u16,
    ist: u8,
    attributes: u8,
    offset_middle: u16,
    offset_high: u32,
    reserved: u32,
}

impl IdtEntry {
    const MISSING: Self = Self {
        offset_low: 0,
        selector: 0,
        ist: 0,
        attributes: 0,
        offset_middle: 0,
        offset_high: 0,
        reserved: 0,
    };

    fn interrupt_gate(handler: u64, ist: u8) -> Self {
        Self {
            offset_low: handler as u16,
            selector: KERNEL_CODE_SELECTOR,
            ist: ist & 0x07,
            attributes: 0x8e,
            offset_middle: (handler >> 16) as u16,
            offset_high: (handler >> 32) as u32,
            reserved: 0,
        }
    }

    fn user_interrupt_gate(handler: u64) -> Self {
        let mut entry = Self::interrupt_gate(handler, 0);
        entry.attributes = 0xee;
        entry
    }
}

#[repr(C, packed)]

    rsp0: u64,

}

}

/// Install a private kernel GDT/TSS, exception gates, and device IRQ gates.
///
/// The bootstrap runs with maskable interrupts disabled. This routine leaves
/// them disabled and does not modify CR3 or the inherited page-table hierarchy.
pub fn initialize() {
    // SAFETY: Single-core bootstrap ownership; the descriptor tables are private
    // static storage and are initialized before any gate is loaded.
    unsafe {
        asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack));
        initialize_tss();
        initialize_gdt();
        initialize_idt();
    }

    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    let double_fault_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let double_fault_top = unsafe { double_fault_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);

    // The architectural TSS fields are packed; use unaligned raw writes rather
    // than creating references to their potentially unaligned storage.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(ring0_top);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).ist1).write_unaligned(double_fault_top);
    }

        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(GDT) as u64,
