```
        .map_err(|_| "active kernel half could not be shared safely")?;
    let physical_address_bits = cpu_info
        .physical_address_bits
        .ok_or("physical address width unavailable")?;
    let pat = match cpu_info.pat_msr_value {
        Some(value) => PatLayout::from_msr_value(value)
            .map_err(|_| "PAT state is invalid for process mappings")?,
        None => return Err("PAT state unavailable for process mappings"),
    };
    let mtrr_layout = match &cpu_info.mtrr {
        MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers
            .validated_layout(physical_address_bits)
            .map_err(|_| "MTRR state is invalid for process mappings")?,
        _ => return Err("MTRR state unavailable for process mappings"),
    };
    let mut select_cache = |mapping: rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMappingRange| {
        mapping
            .select_cache_attributes(
                CachePolicy::WriteBack,
                pat,
                &mtrr_layout,
                cpu_info.normal_caching,
            )
            .map_err(|_| "no uniform write-back cache policy for process page")
    };
    let mut process_memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map,
        hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut roots = match ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::new(&kernel_half, &mut process_memory, config) {
        Ok(roots) => roots,
        Err(failure) => {
            if let Some(frame) = failure.frame {
                allocator
                    .deallocate(frame)
                    .map_err(|_| "process-root manager frame could not be reclaimed")?;
            }
            return Err("process-root manager creation failed");
        }
    };
    let process = match roots.create(allocator) {
        Ok(process) => process,
        Err(failure) => {
            if let Some(frame) = failure.frame {
                allocator
                    .deallocate(frame)
                    .map_err(|_| "process-root frame could not be reclaimed")?;
            }
            return Err("process root creation failed");
        }
    };
    let mut user_memory = LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory {
        memory_map,
        hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits: Some(physical_address_bits),
        virtual_address_bits: cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };

    if let Err(failure) = init_image.load_into_process_root(
        &mut roots,
        allocator,
        process,
        &mut user_memory,
        &mut select_cache,
    ) {
        if let Some(frame) = failure.frame {
            allocator
                .deallocate(frame)
                .map_err(|_| "unmapped ELF frame could not be reclaimed")?;
        }
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "partially loaded process root could not be destroyed")?;
        return Err("bundled init ELF could not be loaded into the process root");
    }

    const USER_STACK_BASE: u64 = 0x0000_7fff_ffff_f000;
    let stack_frame = match allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, process)
                .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after stack allocation failed")?;
            return Err("no frame available for the user stack");
        }
    };
    let stack_mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
        USER_STACK_BASE,
        stack_frame.address(),
        PAGE_SIZE,
        PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        },
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(mapping) => mapping,
        Err(_) => {
            allocator
                .deallocate(stack_frame)
                .map_err(|_| "unmapped stack frame could not be reclaimed")?;
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, process)
                .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after stack validation failed")?;
            return Err("user stack mapping range was rejected");
        }
    };
    let stack_cache = match select_cache(stack_mapping) {
        Ok(attributes) => attributes,
        Err(error) => {
            allocator
                .deallocate(stack_frame)
                .map_err(|_| "unmapped stack frame could not be reclaimed")?;
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, process)
                .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after cache selection failed")?;
            return Err(error);
        }
    };
    if let Err(failure) =
        roots.map_user_page(allocator, process, stack_frame, stack_mapping, stack_cache)
    {
        allocator
            .deallocate(failure.frame)
            .map_err(|_| "unmapped stack frame could not be reclaimed")?;
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after stack mapping failed")?;
        return Err("user stack page could not be mapped");
    }

    let stack_pointer = USER_STACK_BASE + PAGE_SIZE;
    if roots
        .validate_initial_user_state(process, init_image.entry_point(), stack_pointer)
        .is_err()
    {
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after entry validation failed")?;
        return Err("ELF entry or writable NX stack validation failed");
    }

    let mut process_table = rustix_kernel::process::ProcessTable::new();
    let process_id = process_table
        .create_initial()
        .map_err(|_| "initial process record could not be created")?;
    let root_address = match roots.root_physical_address(process) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(_) => {
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, process)
                .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after root lookup failed")?;
            return Err("process root address is unavailable");
        }
    };
    let kernel_cr3 = arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw();
    let kernel_cr3_root = match rustix_kernel::paging::parse_cr3_root(
        kernel_cr3,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        cpu_info.pcid_enabled,
    ) {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(_) => {
            roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
                "process root could not be destroyed after kernel CR3 validation failed"
            })?;
            return Err("active kernel CR3 could not be validated");
        }
    };
    let process_cr3 = match rustix_kernel::paging::encode_cr3_value(
        root_address,
        kernel_cr3_root.low_bits(),
        physical_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(_) => {
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, process)
                .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after CR3 encoding failed")?;
            return Err("process CR3 encoding failed");
        }
    };
    let raw_user_frame = rustix_kernel::syscall::UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: init_image.entry_point(),
        code_selector: u64::from(arch::x86_64::interrupts::USER_CODE_SELECTOR),
        flags: rustix_kernel::syscall::SAFE_USER_RFLAGS,
        stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: u64::from(arch::x86_64::interrupts::USER_DATA_SELECTOR),
    };
    let user_frame = match rustix_kernel::syscall::sanitize_user_iret_frame(
        raw_user_frame,
        cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(frame) => frame,
        Err(_) => {
            roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
                "process root could not be destroyed after IRET frame validation failed"
            })?;
            return Err("initial user IRET frame was rejected");
        }
    };

    let mut process_context = ActiveUserProcessSyscallContext {
        roots: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(roots).cast(),
        user_memory: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(user_memory).cast(),
        process_table: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(process_table),
        process,
        process_id,
        kernel_cr3,
    };
    // SAFETY: IF was disabled by the caller; all pointer targets remain live
    // until the synchronous user entry returns through its exit syscall.
    if unsafe {
        arch::x86_64::interrupts::install_user_syscall_handler(
            dispatch_active_user_process_syscall,
            dispatch_active_user_process_exception,
            core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(process_context).cast(),
        )
    }
    .is_err()
    {
        roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
            "process root could not be destroyed after syscall handler setup failed"
        })?;
        return Err("user syscall handler setup failed");
    }
    // SAFETY: IF remains disabled, and this complete root was prevalidated.
    if unsafe { roots.mark_active(process) }.is_err() {
        // SAFETY: No user callback is in flight and the root is not installed.
        unsafe { arch::x86_64::interrupts::clear_user_syscall_handler() };
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after activation failed")?;
        return Err("process root could not be marked active");
    }

    // SAFETY: The process root shares the validated supervisor kernel half and
    // the kernel/TSS stacks are mapped in both roots; interrupts remain disabled.
    unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(process_cr3) };
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != process_cr3 {
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The mapped entry/stack were validated above; syscall/fault dispatch
    // are installed and maskable interrupts remain disabled through process exit.
    let exit_status = match unsafe { arch::x86_64::interrupts::enter_user(user_frame) } {
        Ok(status) => status,
        Err(_) => halt_forever(),
    };
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != kernel_cr3 {
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The exit trampoline returned to the kernel root with IF=0 and no
    // syscall callback remains in flight.
    unsafe { arch::x86_64::interrupts::clear_user_syscall_handler() };
    let wait_result =
        match process_table.try_wait(rustix_kernel::process::KERNEL_PROCESS_ID, process_id.get()) {
            Ok(result) => result,
            Err(_) => {
                roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
                    "inactive process root could not be destroyed after wait failed"
                })?;
                return Err("kernel wait could not inspect the init process");
            }
        };
    let expected_status = if cfg!(feature = "probe-user-fault") {
        128 + 6
    } else {
        42
    };
    if !matches!(
        wait_result,
        rustix_kernel::process::WaitResult::Exited { pid, status }
            if pid == process_id && status == exit_status && status == expected_status
    ) {
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "inactive process root could not be destroyed after wait mismatch")?;
        return Err("init exit status was not retained and reaped as expected");
    }
    roots
        .destroy(allocator, process)
        .map_err(|_| "inactive process root teardown failed")?;
    if allocator.free_frames() != initial_free_frames {
        return Err("process-root teardown did not restore the frame count");
    }
    #[cfg(not(feature = "probe-user-fault"))]
    kprintln!(
        "init process exited with status {} and was reaped by kernel wait",
        exit_status
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-user-fault")]
    kprintln!(
        "user #UD process exited with status {} and was reaped by kernel wait",
        exit_status
    );
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_hhdm_frame(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE;
    use rustix_kernel::paging::UserFrameMemory;

    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: no free frame");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let hhdm_address = match frame.hhdm_address(
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe rejected frame translation: {:?}", error);
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let mut user_memory = LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut expected = [0; 64];
    for (index, byte) in expected.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        *byte = index as u8 ^ 0x5a;
    }
    let mut observed = [0; 64];
    let copy_round_trip = user_memory
        .copy_to_frame(&frame, 128, &expected)
        .and_then(|()| user_memory.copy_from_frame(&frame, 128, &mut observed));
    let mut out_of_bounds = [0; 2];
    let bounds_rejected = user_memory
        .copy_from_frame(&frame, FRAME_SIZE as usize - 1, &mut out_of_bounds)
        .is_err();
    let empty_copy = user_memory
        .copy_to_frame(&frame, FRAME_SIZE as usize, &[])
        .is_ok();
    let mut verified =
        copy_round_trip.is_ok() && observed == expected && bounds_rejected && empty_copy;
    let words = (FRAME_SIZE / core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64) as usize;
    let page = hhdm_address as *mut u64;
    // SAFETY: The non-copyable `Frame` token is held exclusively; its full page
    // is within validated `Usable` memory and its HHDM arithmetic was checked.
    // Limine base revision 3 guarantees usable memory in the HHDM, and no other
    // Rustix mapping aliases this newly allocated frame. This is an opt-in QEMU
    // probe; a broken loader mapping would fault and be caught by the fatal path.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index)
                .write_volatile(0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64);
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            if page.add(index).read_volatile() != (0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64) {
                verified = false;
                break;
            }
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index).write_volatile(0);
        }
    }

    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
    if !verified {
        kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: readback mismatch");
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!("HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame");
    probe_inherited_root(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_inherited_root(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address;

    let root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: CR3 decode rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let address = match inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
        root,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: HHDM validation rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let entries = address as *const u64;
    let mut present_entries = 0;
    // SAFETY: The complete root page was validated as bootloader-reclaimable
    // and its HHDM range arithmetic was checked. The Limine base-revision-3
    // contract maps that region; this read-only opt-in probe trusts that handoff.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..512 {
            if entries.add(index).read_volatile() & 1 != 0 {
                present_entries += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    kprintln!(
        "inherited root HHDM probe passed: read 512 entries, {} present",
        present_entries
    );
    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("inherited page-table walk failed: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "active boot stack",
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
    );

    let pat_value = match boot_info.cpu_info.pat_msr_value {
        Some(value) => value,
        None => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: active PAT value unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let pat = match rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value) {
        Ok(pat) => pat,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid PAT layout: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid MTRR state: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: non-normal CR0 caching mode");
        halt_forever();
    }
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    probe_cloned_page_tables(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        [
            (
                "kernel text",
                segments.text.virtual_start,
                segments.text.physical_start,
                segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel rodata",
                segments.rodata.virtual_start,
                segments.rodata.physical_start,
                segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel data",
                segments.data.virtual_start,
                segments.data.physical_start,
                segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "active boot stack",
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            ),
        ],
    );
    probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_cloned_page_tables(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    spans: [(&str, u64, u64, u64); 4],
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables;

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map,
        hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate = match CandidatePageTables::new(allocator, &mut memory, config) {
        Ok(candidate) => candidate,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                error.cause
            );
            if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                release_probe_frame(allocator, frame);
            }
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if let Err(error) = candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(allocator, source_reader, source_root) {
        kprintln!("candidate clone probe failed: {:?}", error);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
    }
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            source_reader,
            source_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed: {} translation mismatch",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
        }
    }
    let table_count = candidate.table_count();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate clone probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate inherited-root clone probe passed: {} owned table pages preserve critical paths; CR3 unchanged",
        table_count
    );
}

fn candidate_span_matches_source(
    candidate: &rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let Some(virtual_address) = virtual_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(expected_physical) = physical_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let source_result =
            walk_virtual_address(source_reader, source_root, virtual_address, config);
        let candidate_result = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
        let (source_translation, candidate_translation) = match (source_result, candidate_result) {
            (Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(source)), Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(candidate))) => {
                (source, candidate)
            }
            (source, candidate) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate clone walk mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}",
                    virtual_address,
                    source,
                    candidate
                );
                return false;
            }
        };
        if !source_translation.same_effective_mapping(candidate_translation)
            || candidate_translation.physical_address != expected_physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone translation mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}, expected PA={:#x}",
                virtual_address,
                source_translation,
                candidate_translation,
                expected_physical
            );
            return false;
        }
        let Some(next_offset) = offset.checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE) else {
            return false;
        };
        offset = next_offset;
    }
    true
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome,
    };

    let Some(physical_address_bits) = boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits else {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: physical width unknown");
        halt_forever();
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled || !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: NXE or normal caching unavailable");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let pat_value = boot_info
        .cpu_info
        .pat_msr_value
        .expect("inherited cache-alias probe validated active PAT");
    let pat = rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value).unwrap_or_else(|error| {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid PAT: {:?}",
            error
        );
        halt_forever();
    });
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid MTRR: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: true,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_ffff_f000;
    let permissions = PagePermissions {
        writable: true,
        executable: false,
        user_accessible: false,
    };
    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: no leaf frame available");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
        virtual_address,
        frame.address(),
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        permissions,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        config.virtual_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(mapping) => mapping,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid mapping: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let cache_attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
        CachePolicy::WriteBack,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
    ) {
        Ok(attributes) => attributes,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: cache policy: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate page-table probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                if let Some(root_frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, root_frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
    let frame_address = frame.address();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.map_owned_page(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        frame,
        mapping,
        cache_attributes,
    ) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to map leaf: {:?}",
            failure.cause
        );
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, failure.frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let walk = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
    let returned_frame = match candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address) {
        Ok(frame) => frame,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed to unmap leaf: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let translation_valid = match &walk {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => {
            translation.physical_address == frame_address
                && translation.page_size == rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE
                && translation.permissions == permissions
                && translation.pat_index == cache_attributes.pat_index()
        }
        _ => false,
    };
    if returned_frame.address() != frame_address {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: unmap returned the wrong frame");
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
    if !translation_valid {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: candidate walk: {:?}",
            walk
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate page-table probe passed: mapped, walked, unmapped, and released root {:#x}; CR3 unchanged",
        root.expect("candidate retains root until release")
    );
}

fn release_candidate_after_probe_failure(
    candidate: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
) -> ! {
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table cleanup also failed: {:?}", failure);
    }
    halt_forever()
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_inherited_mapping(
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    label: &str,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    let mut first_translation: Option<rustix_kernel::paging::PageTranslation> = None;
    let mut permissions_uniform = true;
    let mut pat_index_uniform = true;
    while offset < length {
        let virtual_address = match virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let expected_physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} physical overflow",
                    label
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, virtual_address, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level }) => {
                if level == rustix_kernel::paging::PageLevel::Pml4 {
                    let pml4_index = ((virtual_address >> 39) & 0x1ff) as u16;
                    let root_entry = reader.read_entry(root.physical_address(), pml4_index);
                    kprintln!(
                        "inherited mapping PML4 detail: VA={:#018x}, index={}, root={:#x}, entry={:?}",
                        virtual_address,
                        pml4_index,
                        root.physical_address(),
                        root_entry
                    );
                }
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} absent at {:?}",
                    label,
                    level
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {}: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if translation.physical_address != expected_physical {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited mapping probe failed: {} {:#018x} mapped to {:#018x}, expected {:#018x}",
                label,
                virtual_address,
                translation.physical_address,
                expected_physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        if let Some(first) = first_translation {
            permissions_uniform &= translation.permissions == first.permissions;
            pat_index_uniform &= translation.pat_index == first.pat_index;
        } else {
            first_translation = Some(translation);
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    if let Some(first) = first_translation {
        kprintln!(
            "inherited mapping probe passed: {} ({} pages), first permissions={:?}, PAT index={}, leaf size={}, uniform permissions={}, uniform PAT index={}",
            label,
            pages,
            first.permissions,
            first.pat_index,
            first.page_size,
            permissions_uniform,
            pat_index_uniform
        );
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
    boot_info: &boot::BootInfo,
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    mtrrs: &rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    label: &str,
    kernel_virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} physical overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_virtual = match kernel_virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_virtual = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
            boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(address) => address,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM range: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, kernel_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, hhdm_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_translation.physical_address != physical
            || hhdm_translation.physical_address != physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias probe failed: {} physical {:#018x} has inconsistent translations",
                label,
                physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        let kernel_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            kernel_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            hhdm_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_type != hhdm_type {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias conflict: {} PA {:#018x}, kernel {:?} vs HHDM {:?}",
                label,
                physical,
                kernel_type,
                hhdm_type
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    kprintln!(
        "cache-alias probe passed: {} ({} pages; effective types match)",
        label,
        pages
    );
}

fn release_probe_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!(
            "HHDM frame probe failed to return its frame: {:?}",
            error.error
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-page-fault")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately reads an unmapped
    // low virtual address; the installed page-fault handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov rax, 0xdeadbeef",
            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack)
        );
    }
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-invalid-opcode")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering invalid opcode with ud2");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately raises #UD; the
    // installed invalid-opcode handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("ud2", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

/// Set once the fatal panic path has started. A panic from inside the fatal
/// path stops silently instead of recursively printing or looping diagnostics.
static FATAL_PANIC_ACTIVE: core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool =
    core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    // Mask maskable interrupts before any diagnostics run: another kernel
    // thread must not resume after a panic is declared, and the fatal report
    // must not be preempted mid-print.
    //
    // SAFETY: Kernel panic path runs at CPL 0; masking IF is always sound.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    if FATAL_PANIC_ACTIVE.swap(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire) {
        loop {
            // SAFETY: Re-entrant panics are deliberately silent.
            unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
        }
    }
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
```
```
    }
}

            exit(121);
        }

        let invalid_write = unsafe { syscall(SYS_WRITE, STDOUT, 0x5000_0000, 1, 0, 0, 0) };
        if invalid_write != -3 {
            exit(122);
        }
        let fault_message_written = unsafe {
            syscall(
                SYS_WRITE,
                STDOUT,
                FAULT_MESSAGE.as_ptr() as u64,
                FAULT_MESSAGE.len() as u64,
                0,
                0,
                0,
            )
        };
        if fault_message_written != FAULT_MESSAGE.len() as i64 {
            exit(123);
        }
        exit(42)
    }
}

fn exit(status: i32) -> ! {
    // The kernel's exit syscall must not return; spinning is a fail-closed fallback.
    let _ = unsafe { syscall(SYS_EXIT, status as u32 as u64, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) };
    loop {
        core::hint::spin_loop();
    }
}

unsafe fn syscall(
    number: u64,
    first: u64,
    second: u64,
    third: u64,
    fourth: u64,
    fifth: u64,
    sixth: u64,
) -> i64 {
    let result: u64;
    // SAFETY: The kernel installs the documented DPL-3 int 0x80 gate and saves
    // all listed registers. The Rustix syscall ABI uses RAX and six argument regs.
    unsafe {
        asm!(
            "int 0x80",
            inlateout("rax") number => result,
            in("rdi") first,
            in("rsi") second,
            in("rdx") third,
            in("r10") fourth,
            in("r8") fifth,
            in("r9") sixth,
            lateout("rcx") _,
            lateout("r11") _,
        );
    }
    result as i64
}

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(_info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    exit(127)
}
```

```
use std::env;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::process::Command;

fn main() {
    let root = PathBuf::from(env::var_os("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").expect("manifest directory"));
    let source = root.join("crates/rustix-init/src/main.rs");
    let linker_script = root.join("crates/rustix-init/linker.ld");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", source.display());
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", linker_script.display());
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=RUSTC");

    if env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS").as_deref() != Ok("none") {
        return;
    }

    let rustc = env::var_os("RUSTC").expect("Cargo provides RUSTC");
    let output = PathBuf::from(env::var_os("OUT_DIR").expect("Cargo provides OUT_DIR"))
        .join("rustix-init.elf");
    let linker_arg = format!("-T{}", linker_script.display());
    let mut command = Command::new(rustc);
    command
        .current_dir(&root)
        .arg("--crate-name")
        .arg("rustix_init")
        .arg("--edition=2021")
        .arg("--check-cfg=cfg(rustix_fault_probe)")
        .arg("--crate-type=bin")
        .arg("--target=x86_64-unknown-none")
        .arg("-Cpanic=abort")
        .arg("-Copt-level=2")
        .arg("-Ccode-model=small")
        .arg("-Crelocation-model=static")
        .arg("-Ctarget-feature=-avx,-avx2,-avx512f")
        .arg(format!("-Clink-arg={linker_arg}"))
        .arg("-Clink-arg=--build-id=none")
        .arg(&source)
        .arg("-o")
        .arg(&output);
    if env::var_os("CARGO_FEATURE_PROBE_USER_FAULT").is_some() {
        command.arg("--cfg=rustix_fault_probe");
    }
    let status = command
        .status()
        .expect("failed to invoke rustc for the init payload");
    assert!(
        status.success(),
        "failed to build the rustix-init ELF payload"
    );
}

```

   142	
   143	## Milestone 3 — IRQs, time, and kernel scheduling (DONE locally; single-vCPU, SMP deferred)
   144	
   145	Do not enable interrupts as a side effect of installing exception gates. IRQ delivery needs its own controller, acknowledgement, masking, ownership, and synchronization design.
   146	
   147	### Implementation and remaining work
   148	
   149	The current source includes host-tested bounded ACPI parsing and span authorization, a boot-only read-only/NX ACPI reader that copies MADT data into owned state, xAPIC/I/O APIC routing, allocated IRQ dispatch and acknowledgement, a PIT timer, a single-vCPU scheduler with cooperative waits and timer preemption, guarded thread stacks, bounded frame-backed heap growth, and interrupt-driven UART/PS/2 queues. `IrqSpinLock` saves/disables local interrupts and restores the prior IF state; the heap uses it, while scheduler mutations are serialized by local interrupt masking. Timer IRQ assembly saves x87/SSE state before Rust dispatch, and context switches preserve per-context FXSAVE state; AVX/XSAVE remains disabled. On 2026-11-13, `just verify` passed with 130 host tests and BIOS/OVMF coverage for active mapping, timer preemption/FPU state, locks, cooperative waits, and input. SMP is not part of this completed single-vCPU slice.
   150	
   151	**Ring 3 prerequisite gate:** the single-vCPU IRQ-safe locking and timer-preemption prerequisites in this milestone are now implemented and validated. This only establishes scheduler progress and local interrupt-safe locking; it does not provide user/kernel isolation, safe syscall entry/return, per-process kernel stacks, or any other Milestone 4 guarantee.
   152	
   153	- [x] Use the existing single-vCPU QEMU `q35` configuration with the local APIC and MADT-described I/O APIC; keep legacy PIC routing masked. OVMF smokes observed timer and device IRQ delivery.
   154	- [x] Read bounded ACPI tables through the validated read-only/NX path. The reader checks table bounds/signatures/checksums and copies the required MADT data into owned state; host tests cover malformed tables and span authorization, and OVMF reports the copied MADT.
   155	- [x] Parse the selected machine's MADT topology and interrupt-source overrides. Host parser tests and OVMF boot cover the data used by APIC routing; FADT/HPET/MCFG work remains limited to this milestone's needs.
   156	- [x] Add fixed-capacity IRQ vector ownership, masked-first controller routes, dispatch, spurious/unexpected-vector handling, and EOI. OVMF observed timer IRQ delivery and acknowledgement; input routes are also tested.
   157	- [x] Route an approximately 100 Hz 8254 PIT through the I/O APIC and maintain atomic monotonic ticks. Host tests cover divisor and elapsed-time arithmetic, including fractional-tick rounding drift; OVMF verifies live timer delivery and EOI. Wall-clock time remains separate and is not provided.
   158	- [x] Add bounded wait queues, cooperative sleep/wakeup, and event handoff; host scheduler tests and OVMF `thread-smoke` cover wakeup and timed sleep.
   159	- [x] Establish IRQ-safe lock primitives and broader context-specific locking rules before enabling timer preemption. `src/sync.rs` provides an IRQ-save spin lock that restores the prior RFLAGS.IF state; the heap uses it, while scheduler policy changes mask local interrupts and do not hold a lock across context switches. IRQ handlers remain allocation-free and do not acquire the heap lock. Host tests and the OVMF thread smoke validate lock operations and both enabled/disabled IF restoration.
   160	- [x] Implement owned-frame active map/unmap with explicit mapping/cache policy, transactional rollback, and local TLB invalidation. Host tests cover failure rollback; `active-map-smoke` passed live mapping, access, invalidation, and reclamation in QEMU.

   162	- [x] Keep allocator operations out of IRQ/exception handlers; handlers use bounded, allocation-free work, and the heap contract explicitly forbids IRQ-context allocation. The IRQ-save heap lock prevents local interrupt reentrancy, but does not make allocation appropriate in handlers. Exhaustion is fallible at the allocator boundary.
   163	- [x] Keep bootloader-reclaimable and ACPI memory, the active bootstrap stack, and Limine's inherited page-table root reserved; the active cloned root retains its owned table frames and does not reclaim the old root or inherited leaf frames.

The OVMF `thread-smoke` verifies two non-yielding workers both run, checks x87/SSE state survives asynchronous preemption, and validates the IRQ-save lock's IF behavior. Timer EOI is issued before a context switch; IRQ/exception handlers remain bounded and allocation-free. SMP remains a separate later sub-milestone.

IRQ/exception handlers remain allocation-free. SMP, physical-hardware validation, and userspace are still out of scope.

   171	
   172	## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI
   173	
   174	Userspace begins only after page tables, exception handling, scheduling, and controlled memory allocation are trustworthy. The syscall ABI is a product interface and must not emerge accidentally from internal functions. Milestone 3's single-vCPU IRQ-safe locking and timer-preemption gate is locally validated; this enables scheduler progress but does not by itself make user code isolated or safe. SMP remains outside this milestone.
   175	
   176	### Planned work
   177	
   178	- [x] Decide and document the initial x86_64 user-entry/syscall mechanism, register convention, selector/MSR setup, per-CPU state requirements, and safe return path. The current design uses a DPL-3 `int $0x80` gate and validated `IRETQ`, with no syscall MSRs or `SWAPGS`. Vector `0x80` is excluded from the device allocator, the GDT installs asserted Ring 3 selectors sourced from `syscall.rs`, a checked unsafe TSS `RSP0` setter exists, and the dedicated assembly gate/stub saves GPR and x87/SSE state before dispatch and sanitizes return flags with IF clear. The dispatcher currently implements ABI-version discovery and returns `ENOTSUP` for process operations; per-process stack ownership/scheduling, mapping-aware return validation, and Ring 3 execution remain pending. Revisit the choice if the entry model or SMP requirements change.
   179	- [x] Define per-process address-space construction without deep-cloning the entire kernel page-table tree for every process. The design shares validated supervisor-only upper-half subtrees, keeps lower-half tables and user frames process-owned, and specifies kernel-owner lifetime, teardown, permission, and local TLB rules. Implementation and validation remain pending.

Partial address-space support now snapshots validated supervisor-only kernel entries, creates multiple roots, maps/unmaps private lower-half user frames, retains executable/writable metadata, validates an initial executable entry and writable NX stack page, and releases private mappings/tables/roots only after the caller switches away. Caller-managed CR3/TLB transitions, activation integration, target copy-in/copy-out, and end-to-end isolation validation remain pending.
   181	- [ ] Implement copy-in/copy-out helpers that validate lengths, arithmetic, canonical ranges, permissions, and faults; never form a kernel reference directly from a user pointer. One-page-bounded frame-token-based copy helpers preflight full ranges and permissions and report partial backend-copy progress. The host-tested `write_user_buffer` service now uses process-root copy-in and preserves partial progress/short output; the target HHDM `UserFrameMemory` backend is exercised by `just frame-smoke` but is not yet wired to a live process/syscall path, and recoverable hardware-fault handling remains pending.
   182	- [x] Specify v1 version discovery, initial syscall numbers/argument meanings, fixed-width layouts, negative error encoding, bounded partial-write/copy behavior, wait semantics, no-restart policy, and append-only compatibility before exposing calls. The contract is documented in `docs/architecture/syscall-abi.md`; `src/syscall.rs` provides host-tested stable constants and register-level request decoding, and the dedicated hardware gate/stub now handles ABI-version discovery; live process syscall services remain unintegrated. Future read/open/close/dup, descriptor sharing, signals, and clocks still require separate specifications.
   183	- [ ] Add initial process lifecycle and descriptor-table semantics: create/load, exit, wait, close, duplication/inheritance, and process cleanup. `src/process.rs` now provides host-tested fixed-capacity PID, parent/child, exit-status, zombie-reap, and reparenting policy; it is not yet bound to process roots, blocking scheduler waits, descriptors, or syscall dispatch.

The kernel build now produces a bounded static `rustix-init` ELF payload, and QEMU boot parses/validates it; loading into a process root, stack setup, activation, execution, and failed-load teardown integration remain pending. Use `.bin` for command-line programs and `.app` for GUI applications as role-based filename suffixes for the same underlying format. `.app` is a Rustix single-file application suffix, not an Apple/macOS app bundle; initially require application resources to be embedded or absent.

   192

   199	## Milestone 5 — VFS, storage, and device ownership
   200	
   201	Keep the current RAM filesystem as a bootstrap/test implementation. Persistence and device drivers require explicit block ownership, error handling, and recovery behavior. Split this milestone into M5a (PCI/DMA, block I/O, and a read-only/basic VFS slice) and M5b (writable storage, permissions, and platform services) so each checkpoint has a bounded validation target.
   202	
   203	### M5a — PCI/DMA, block I/O, and read-only/basic VFS
   204	
   205	- [ ] Define VFS node, mount, path, metadata, and file-descriptor contracts independently of a particular disk format.
   206	- [ ] Preserve volatile RAMFS as a test backend and add tests for mount/path errors, capacity, partial I/O, and object lifetime.
   207	- [ ] Establish bounded PCI/device discovery, including checked ACPI MCFG handling where required, before adding PCI-backed devices. Keep discovery separate from individual driver policy.
   208	- [ ] Define DMA buffer ownership, address translation, cache synchronization, device reset, and error handling before any device can DMA into kernel memory. Scope and test the trust assumptions; do not equate PCI enumeration with safe DMA.
   209	- [ ] Add a narrowly scoped block-device interface with request validation, timeout/error reporting, and a QEMU-supported initial device driver (such as virtio-blk) on top of the shared PCI/DMA foundations.
   210	- [ ] Choose and document the first on-disk filesystem format before implementing writable storage. Specify partition discovery, byte order, block size, metadata limits, corruption handling, and read-only/recovery behavior; begin with a read-only mount and bounded metadata parsing.
   211	- [ ] Test read-only mount, lookup, and read behavior against reproducible images, including malformed metadata and I/O errors. Do not expose on-disk write operations in this slice; the volatile RAMFS remains available as a writable test backend.
   212	- [ ] Define file descriptors and basic process I/O semantics before exposing filesystem operations to applications.
   213	
   214	### M5b — writable filesystem, permissions, and platform services
   215	
   216	- [ ] On detected corruption, report the failure and refuse writable mounting rather than attempting automatic repair. Plan a separate offline checker/repair tool; do not repair data implicitly.
   217	- [ ] Define crash-safe atomic replacement or equivalent transactional behavior for critical files such as account metadata and credentials. Flush the new data before replacing the old file, and test interruption at each update stage.
   218	- [ ] Define explicit no-space errors and partial-write behavior. Never silently discard or overwrite existing user data to recover space.
   219	- [ ] Add persistent write/read/remount/reboot and failure-injection integration tests; never claim persistence from an in-memory cache alone.
   220	- [ ] Define the planned top-level filesystem layout: `/home`, `/root`, `/etc`, `/usr`, `/dev`, `/proc`, `/sys`, `/tmp`, `/var`, `/run`, `/mnt`, `/media`, and `/boot`, plus `/usr/sbin`. Document that `/proc` and `/sys` are future virtual interfaces, `/dev` exposes device interfaces, `/tmp` and `/run` are volatile, and mount-point and boot-file usage depends on later storage/boot design.
   221	- [ ] Specify filesystem ownership and permission metadata. Support owner/group/other read, write, and execute permissions, default creation modes/umask, and the directory sticky bit. Use sticky-directory semantics for `/tmp` (mode equivalent to `01777`) and later `/home/Public/`, so users can create entries without removing or renaming another user's files.
   222	- [ ] Specify that `/etc` and `/usr` are root-owned and writable only by root, while normal users may read configuration and execute permitted programs. Keep readable account metadata separate from a root-only credential file containing password hashes. Reserve `/usr/Apps` for globally installed `.app` GUI applications and `/usr/bin` for globally installed `.bin` command-line tools; `/usr/sbin` is reserved for system-administration tools if needed.
   223	- [ ] Provide a trustworthy CSPRNG before password hashing or security-sensitive random values. Evaluate validated entropy sources (for example, supported CPU randomness instructions or a virtio RNG device) as inputs; do not treat one hardware source alone as a complete CSPRNG. Test initialization, failure, and unavailable-entropy behavior.
   224	- [ ] Provide wall-clock time before persistent audit logs require calendar timestamps. Keep monotonic time as the source for elapsed-time and timeout calculations; define behavior when the wall clock is unavailable or invalid.
   225	- [ ] Define kernel/platform shutdown and reboot operations, including filesystem flush ordering and failure behavior. Parse and validate ACPI FADT power-control data when needed; test the supported QEMU shutdown/reboot paths.
   226	
   227	**M5a exit criteria:** bounded PCI discovery and the DMA ownership policy are validated for the supported QEMU device path; the block driver passes bounded request, timeout, and error tests; a reproducible image mounts the documented filesystem read-only, with lookup/read tests covering malformed metadata and device errors. No writable mount is implied.
   228	
   229	**M5b exit criteria:** writable filesystem behavior is validated across remount and reboot, including crash/failure injection, corruption refusal, I/O errors, and exhausted-space behavior; permission and sticky-directory rules, CSPRNG failure behavior, wall-clock fallback, and supported ACPI shutdown/reboot paths are tested. Milestone 5 validates storage through test/integration harnesses; user-space utilities are verified in Milestone 6.
