//! Stable, host-testable decoding for the initial Rustix syscall ABI.
//!
//! This module defines ABI values, validates register-level request shape,
//! sanitizes user return frames, and provides a host-testable bounded write
//! service. It does not install an entry gate or dispatch requests from hardware.

pub const ABI_MAJOR: u16 = 1;
pub const ABI_MINOR: u16 = 0;
pub const ABI_VERSION: u64 = (ABI_MAJOR as u64) << 16 | ABI_MINOR as u64;
pub const MAX_WRITE_BYTES: u64 = 4096;
pub const USER_SYSCALL_VECTOR: u8 = 0x80;
pub const USER_DATA_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x2b;
pub const USER_CODE_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x33;
pub const SAFE_USER_RFLAGS: u64 = 1 << 1;

const RFLAGS_IOPL: u64 = 3 << 12;
const RFLAGS_NESTED_TASK: u64 = 1 << 14;
const RFLAGS_VIRTUAL_8086: u64 = 1 << 17;

pub mod number {
    pub const ABI_VERSION: u64 = 0;
    pub const EXIT: u64 = 1;
    pub const WRITE: u64 = 2;
    pub const WAIT: u64 = 3;
}

/// Stable v1 error numbers. Syscall returns encode these as negative `i64`s.
#[repr(i64)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum SyscallError {
    InvalidArgument = 1,
    BadFileDescriptor = 2,
    Fault = 3,
    OutOfMemory = 4,
    NoChild = 5,
    Interrupted = 6,
    Io = 7,
    NoSys = 8,
    TooBig = 9,
    Overflow = 10,
    NotSupported = 11,
}

impl SyscallError {
    pub const fn return_value(self) -> i64 {
        -(self as i64)
    }
}

/// The six argument registers reserved by the x86_64 v1 calling convention.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct SyscallArguments {
    pub rdi: u64,
    pub rsi: u64,
    pub rdx: u64,
    pub r10: u64,
    pub r8: u64,
    pub r9: u64,
}

/// Register and privilege frame saved by the dedicated `int 0x80` entry stub.
///
/// The field order matches the assembly push sequence, followed by the five-word
/// hardware frame created by a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt transition.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct SyscallContext {
    pub r15: u64,
    pub r14: u64,
    pub r13: u64,
    pub r12: u64,
    pub r11: u64,
    pub r10: u64,
    pub r9: u64,
    pub r8: u64,
    pub rbp: u64,
    pub rdi: u64,
    pub rsi: u64,
    pub rdx: u64,
    pub rcx: u64,
    pub rbx: u64,
    pub rax: u64,
    pub instruction_pointer: u64,
    pub code_selector: u64,
    pub flags: u64,
    pub stack_pointer: u64,
    pub stack_selector: u64,
}

const _: [(); 160] = [(); core::mem::size_of::<SyscallContext>()];
const _: [(); 0] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, r15)];
const _: [(); 112] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, rax)];
const _: [(); 120] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, instruction_pointer)];
const _: [(); 128] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, code_selector)];
const _: [(); 136] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, flags)];
const _: [(); 144] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, stack_pointer)];
const _: [(); 152] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, stack_selector)];

/// The five-word privilege-return frame consumed by `IRETQ` in long mode.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct UserIretFrame {
    pub instruction_pointer: u64,
    pub code_selector: u64,
    pub flags: u64,
    pub stack_pointer: u64,
    pub stack_selector: u64,
}

/// A user return frame with validated selectors/addresses and kernel-chosen flags.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct ValidatedUserIretFrame(UserIretFrame);

impl ValidatedUserIretFrame {
    pub const fn into_raw(self) -> UserIretFrame {
        self.0
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserIretFrameError {
    InvalidAddressWidth,
    InvalidSelectors,
    InvalidFlags,
    InvalidInstructionPointer,
    InvalidStackPointer,
}

/// Validate the initial privilege-return frame, including the required 16-byte
/// stack alignment, and replace user flags with a conservative kernel value.
///
/// The safe flags deliberately leave IF clear until a process-aware interrupt
/// scheduler is installed. The caller must separately verify that RIP names an
/// executable process mapping and RSP names a writable stack mapping.
pub fn sanitize_user_iret_frame(
    frame: UserIretFrame,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<ValidatedUserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError> {
    sanitize_user_frame(frame, virtual_address_bits, true)
}

/// Sanitize a syscall's saved user return frame without imposing a new stack
/// alignment on an in-function RSP. SysV permits transient stack alignment while
/// executing a function; the active process root must still validate its mapping.
pub fn sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame(
    frame: UserIretFrame,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<ValidatedUserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError> {
    sanitize_user_frame(frame, virtual_address_bits, false)
}

fn sanitize_user_frame(
    frame: UserIretFrame,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    require_aligned_stack: bool,
) -> Result<ValidatedUserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidAddressWidth);
    }
    if frame.code_selector != u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR)
        || frame.stack_selector != u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR)
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidSelectors);
    }
    if frame.flags & (1 << 1) == 0
        || frame.flags & (RFLAGS_IOPL | RFLAGS_NESTED_TASK | RFLAGS_VIRTUAL_8086) != 0
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidFlags);
    }

    let lower_half_end = 1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1);
    if frame.instruction_pointer >= lower_half_end
        || !crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(
            frame.instruction_pointer,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidInstructionPointer);
    }
    let stack_last = frame
        .stack_pointer
        .checked_sub(1)
        .filter(|address| *address < lower_half_end)
        .filter(|address| {
            crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(*address, virtual_address_bits)
        });
    if stack_last.is_none() || (require_aligned_stack && frame.stack_pointer & 0xf != 0) {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidStackPointer);
    }

    Ok(ValidatedUserIretFrame(UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: frame.instruction_pointer,
        code_selector: u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR),
        flags: SAFE_USER_RFLAGS,
        stack_pointer: frame.stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR),
    }))
}

/// A syscall whose number and register-level arguments have been decoded.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum SyscallRequest {
    AbiVersion,
    Exit {
        status: i32,
    },
    Write {
        fd: u64,
        user_buffer: u64,
        length: usize,
    },
    Wait {
        child_pid: u64,
        status_address: Option<u64>,
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ConsoleStream {
    Stdout,
    Stderr,
}

/// The kernel-side sink for the v1 console descriptors.
pub trait ConsoleOutput {
    type Error;

    fn write(&mut self, stream: ConsoleStream, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, Self::Error>;
}

/// Copy and write one bounded v1 user buffer through a process root.
///
/// The complete user range is preflighted by `copy_from_user` before output.
/// If the frame backend faults after copying a prefix, that prefix is still
/// offered to the console and a positive short write is returned when accepted.
///
/// # Safety
/// The current kernel stack, including this function's fixed scratch buffer,
/// must not be mapped as a user frame in `process`. The boot allocator enforces
/// this by excluding the kernel image and bootstrap-stack spans from usable
/// frame allocation; future kernel stacks must preserve the same invariant.
pub unsafe fn write_user_buffer<M, U, O>(
    roots: &crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
    process: crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
    fd: u64,
    user_buffer: u64,
    length: usize,
    user_memory: &mut U,
    output: &mut O,
) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>
where
    M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory,
    U: crate::paging::UserFrameMemory,
    O: ConsoleOutput,
{
    use crate::paging::{ProcessUserCopyError, MAX_PROCESS_USER_COPY_BYTES};

    let stream = match fd {
        1 => ConsoleStream::Stdout,
        2 => ConsoleStream::Stderr,
        _ => return Err(SyscallError::BadFileDescriptor),
    };
    if length > MAX_WRITE_BYTES as usize {
        return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
    }
    if length == 0 {
        return Ok(0);
    }

    let mut scratch = [0; MAX_PROCESS_USER_COPY_BYTES];
    let copied = match unsafe {
        roots.copy_from_user(process, user_buffer, &mut scratch[..length], user_memory)
    } {
        Ok(copied) if copied <= length => copied,
        Ok(_) => return Err(SyscallError::Fault),
        Err(failure) if failure.transferred > 0 && failure.transferred <= length => {
            failure.transferred
        }
        Err(failure) => {
            return Err(match failure.cause {
                ProcessUserCopyError::LengthTooLarge => SyscallError::TooBig,
                ProcessUserCopyError::Memory(_) => SyscallError::Io,
                ProcessUserCopyError::InvalidHandle
                | ProcessUserCopyError::Releasing
                | ProcessUserCopyError::InvalidRange
                | ProcessUserCopyError::Unmapped
                | ProcessUserCopyError::PermissionDenied => SyscallError::Fault,
            });
        }
    };
    if copied == 0 {
        return Err(SyscallError::Io);
    }

    let written = output
        .write(stream, &scratch[..copied])
        .map_err(|_| SyscallError::Io)?;
    if written == 0 || written > copied {
        return Err(SyscallError::Io);
    }
    Ok(written)
}

/// Decode a v1 syscall number and its register arguments without touching user memory.
///
/// The exit status uses the low 32 bits of RDI, interpreted as a signed value.
/// A zero-length write preserves the supplied pointer without validating it; the
/// eventual syscall implementation must return zero before inspecting that pointer.
pub const fn decode_syscall(
    syscall_number: u64,
    arguments: SyscallArguments,
) -> Result<SyscallRequest, SyscallError> {
    match syscall_number {
        number::ABI_VERSION => Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion),
        number::EXIT => Ok(SyscallRequest::Exit {
            status: arguments.rdi as u32 as i32,
        }),
        number::WRITE => {
            if arguments.rdx > MAX_WRITE_BYTES {
                return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
            }
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Write {
                fd: arguments.rdi,
                user_buffer: arguments.rsi,
                length: arguments.rdx as usize,
            })
        }
        number::WAIT => Ok(SyscallRequest::Wait {
            child_pid: arguments.rdi,
            status_address: if arguments.rsi == 0 {
                None
            } else {
                Some(arguments.rsi)
            },
        }),
        _ => Err(SyscallError::NoSys),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{
        decode_syscall, number, sanitize_user_iret_frame, sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame,
        SyscallArguments, SyscallError, SyscallRequest, UserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError,
        ABI_VERSION, MAX_WRITE_BYTES, SAFE_USER_RFLAGS, USER_CODE_SELECTOR, USER_DATA_SELECTOR,
    };

    const EMPTY_ARGUMENTS: SyscallArguments = SyscallArguments {
        rdi: 0,
        rsi: 0,
        rdx: 0,
        r10: 0,
        r8: 0,
        r9: 0,
    };

    fn valid_iret_frame() -> UserIretFrame {
        UserIretFrame {
            instruction_pointer: 0x4000_0000,
            code_selector: u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR),
            flags: 0x202,
            stack_pointer: 0x7fff_fff0,
            stack_selector: u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn abi_version_and_syscall_numbers_are_stable() {
        assert_eq!(ABI_VERSION, 0x0001_0000);
        assert_eq!(number::ABI_VERSION, 0);
        assert_eq!(number::EXIT, 1);
        assert_eq!(number::WRITE, 2);
        assert_eq!(number::WAIT, 3);
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::ABI_VERSION, EMPTY_ARGUMENTS),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn error_numbers_encode_as_negative_i64_results() {
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::InvalidArgument.return_value(), -1);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::BadFileDescriptor.return_value(), -2);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::Fault.return_value(), -3);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::OutOfMemory.return_value(), -4);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::NoChild.return_value(), -5);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::Interrupted.return_value(), -6);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::Io.return_value(), -7);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::NoSys.return_value(), -8);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::TooBig.return_value(), -9);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::Overflow.return_value(), -10);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::NotSupported.return_value(), -11);
    }

    #[test]
    fn exit_status_is_the_signed_low_32_bits_of_rdi() {
        let arguments = SyscallArguments {
            rdi: 0xfeed_beef_ffff_fffe,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::EXIT, arguments),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Exit { status: -2 })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_decoding_accepts_zero_and_maximum_lengths_without_pointer_access() {
        let zero_length = SyscallArguments {
            rdi: 1,
            rsi: u64::MAX,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::WRITE, zero_length),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Write {
                fd: 1,
                user_buffer: u64::MAX,
                length: 0,
            })
        );

        let maximum = SyscallArguments {
            rdi: 2,
            rsi: 0x4000,
            rdx: MAX_WRITE_BYTES,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::WRITE, maximum),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Write {
                fd: 2,
                user_buffer: 0x4000,
                length: MAX_WRITE_BYTES as usize,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_larger_than_the_v1_limit_is_rejected() {
        let arguments = SyscallArguments {
            rdx: MAX_WRITE_BYTES + 1,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::WRITE, arguments),
            Err(SyscallError::TooBig)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn wait_decoding_distinguishes_optional_status_pointer() {
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::WAIT, EMPTY_ARGUMENTS),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Wait {
                child_pid: 0,
                status_address: None,
            })
        );

        let arguments = SyscallArguments {
            rdi: 42,
            rsi: 0x7000,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::WAIT, arguments),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Wait {
                child_pid: 42,
                status_address: Some(0x7000),
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn user_iret_frame_checks_selectors_addresses_alignment_and_sanitizes_flags() {
        let mut frame = valid_iret_frame();
        let sanitized = sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48).unwrap().into_raw();
        assert_eq!(sanitized.instruction_pointer, frame.instruction_pointer);
        assert_eq!(sanitized.code_selector, u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR));
        assert_eq!(sanitized.stack_selector, u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR));
        assert_eq!(sanitized.flags, SAFE_USER_RFLAGS);
        assert_eq!(sanitized.stack_pointer, frame.stack_pointer);

        frame.code_selector = 0x08;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidSelectors)
        );
        frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.stack_selector = 0x10;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidSelectors)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn syscall_return_frame_preserves_valid_in_function_stack_alignment() {
        let mut frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.stack_pointer = 0x7fff_fff8;
        let sanitized = sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame(frame, 48)
            .unwrap()
            .into_raw();
        assert_eq!(sanitized.stack_pointer, 0x7fff_fff8);
        assert_eq!(sanitized.flags, SAFE_USER_RFLAGS);
    }

    #[test]
    fn user_iret_frame_rejects_bad_flags_and_non_user_addresses() {
        let mut frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.flags |= 3 << 12;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidFlags)
        );
        frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.flags &= !(1 << 1);
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidFlags)
        );
        frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.instruction_pointer = 1 << 47;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidInstructionPointer)
        );
        frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.stack_pointer = 0x7fff_fff8;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidStackPointer)
        );
        frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.stack_pointer = 0x0000_8000_0000_0000;
        assert!(sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48).is_ok());
        frame.stack_pointer += 16;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidStackPointer)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(valid_iret_frame(), 52),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidAddressWidth)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn unassigned_numbers_return_enosys() {
        assert_eq!(decode_syscall(4, EMPTY_ARGUMENTS), Err(SyscallError::NoSys));
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(u64::MAX, EMPTY_ARGUMENTS),
            Err(SyscallError::NoSys)
        );
    }
}

     1	# Interrupts and IRQ vector allocation
     2	
     3	## Current implementation
     4	
     5	`src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` installs the bootstrap GDT, TSS, exception gates for vectors 0–31, device IRQ stubs, and the APIC spurious-vector gate. Kernel-origin exceptions remain fatal. In the opt-in synchronous Ring 3 process probe, noncritical CPL3 exceptions are reported and handed to the installed process callback, which records status `128 + vector`, restores the kernel CR3, and exits through the user-entry trampoline. NMI (#2), double fault (#8), and machine check (#18) remain fatal regardless of saved CPL. The only user-fault recovery path currently exercised is #UD; this is not a general exception or signal mechanism. Maskable interrupts start disabled and are enabled only after the validated APIC route, registered handler, and acknowledgement path are ready.
     6	
     7	`src/irq.rs` provides a host-tested, allocation-free token allocator for device vectors `0x20..=0xef` except reserved syscall vector `0x80`; exception vectors and the reserved upper range are also excluded. The IDT overrides `0x80` with a dedicated DPL-3 interrupt gate and assembly stub. The stub rejects CPL0 invocation, saves the full GPR set and x87/SSE state on the TSS entry stack, and dispatches a normalized syscall context with IF clear. In the opt-in process probe, the dispatcher implements ABI-version discovery, bounded write through allocator-owned user-frame copies, exit, and scheduler-independent kernel wait/reap after the synchronous entry returns; the userspace `wait` syscall remains `ENOTSUP`. The normal build only exposes ABI-version discovery. `rustix_irq_dispatch` invokes the registered handler, returns for the APIC spurious vector without EOI, and halts on unregistered/unexpected vectors. Device handlers own their EOI. Vector registration is performed with IF clear before the corresponding I/O APIC source is unmasked.
     8	
     9	The initial hardware target is single-vCPU QEMU `q35`: validated ACPI/MADT topology, local APIC and I/O APIC, masked legacy PIC routing, MADT-resolved ISA routes, and a periodic 8254 PIT tick near 100 Hz. OVMF smokes validate PIT delivery/EOI, non-yielding timer preemption, x87/SSE state preservation, and UART/keyboard IRQ delivery. Host tests cover vector ownership and PIT/time arithmetic; they do not replace privileged QEMU coverage.
    10	
    11	The scheduler is single-vCPU and supports cooperative waits/yields plus PIT-driven timer preemption. The timer handler advances ticks and sends APIC EOI before any scheduling switch. The common IRQ stub saves the interrupted x87/SSE state before Rust dispatch and restores the selected context before `IRETQ`; the context switch keeps aligned per-context FXSAVE areas. IRQ-safe spin locks save and restore the prior IF state, and the global heap uses one; scheduler mutations are separately serialized by masking local interrupts. IRQ/exception handlers remain bounded and allocation-free, and no current IRQ handler acquires the heap lock. SMP, per-CPU state, and physical-hardware validation remain future work.

     1	# Unix-like process and syscall direction
     2	
     3	**Status: Milestone 4 is in progress. The opt-in single-vCPU QEMU diagnostic path creates an isolated lower-half process root sharing the validated supervisor kernel half, loads and runs a bundled static ELF in Ring 3, serves ABI-version/write/exit syscalls, terminates user #UD with status 134, and restores/reaps the process root. The normal kernel does not launch userspace. The userspace `wait` syscall, general process scheduling/kernel stacks, broad user-fault coverage, virtual-memory allocation, and a userspace runtime remain unimplemented.**
     4	
     5	Rustix aims to expose a small, versioned syscall surface that can support Unix-like processes and tools. The kernel must own this interface rather than inherit an ABI accidentally from a bootloader or emulator.
     6	
     7	## Proposed compatibility principles
     8	
     9	- Processes have independent virtual address spaces and explicit lifecycle states.
    10	- File descriptors are per-process integer handles to kernel-managed objects; descriptor inheritance, close-on-exec, duplication, and sharing semantics must be specified together.
    11	- Syscalls use one documented error convention and stable numeric identifiers. New operations must not silently repurpose old numbers.
    12	- Arguments crossing privilege boundaries are copied or validated using narrowly scoped helpers. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::copy_from_user` and `copy_to_user` preflight the complete lower-half mapped range, check writable metadata for kernel-to-user copies, and operate only on owned frame tokens through `UserFrameMemory`; they never form a Rust reference from a user virtual address. Backend copy faults report the completed prefix; hardware fault recovery is not yet implemented.
    13	- Blocking, interruption, cancellation, and restart behavior are explicit for each syscall class.
    14	- A compatibility layer (for example, POSIX-shaped libc behavior) remains separate from internal kernel APIs.
    15	
    16	## Initial syscall ABI v1 contract (specified; register decoding implemented)
    17	
    18	ABI version `1.0` is identified by `abi_version()`, syscall number `0`, returning `0x0001_0000` in `RAX`. In v1, `RAX` returns a signed 64-bit result: nonnegative values are success (including byte counts and PIDs); errors are negative stable error numbers. ABI versioning is append-only: existing syscall numbers, argument meanings, layouts, and error values never change or get reused. There is no POSIX compatibility claim. `src/syscall.rs` implements the stable number/error constants, host-tested request decoding and write service, and the assembly-matched syscall context layout. `interrupts.rs` installs the DPL-3 gate and dedicated entry stub. The opt-in diagnostic process runtime dispatches ABI-version, bounded write, and exit; userspace `wait` and process creation are not implemented. A separate kernel-side test harness waits for the synchronous process after its exit trampoline returns.
    19	
    20	| Number | Call | Register arguments | Result / behavior |
    21	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
    22	| 0 | `abi_version` | none | `0x0001_0000` (major 1, minor 0). |
    23	| 1 | `exit` | `RDI`: signed 32-bit status in the low 32 bits (upper bits ignored) | Does not return; status is retained exactly by the parent wait record. |
    24	| 2 | `write` | `RDI`: fd, `RSI`: user buffer, `RDX`: byte length | Returns bytes accepted; a short positive result is valid. Initial descriptors 1 and 2 are stdout/stderr console streams; other descriptors return `-EBADF`. Maximum request is 4096 bytes; zero length returns 0 without validating the pointer. |
    25	| 3 | `wait` | `RDI`: child PID (0 means any child), `RSI`: optional user pointer to signed 32-bit exit status | Blocks until a matching child exits and returns its PID. A non-null status output must be writable before the child is reaped; no matching child returns `-ECHILD`. |
    26	
    27	All other numbers are unassigned and return `-ENOSYS`; assigning a number later is an additive extension, never a reinterpretation. Descriptor 0 is reserved for input but v1 has no `read`, `open`, `close`, or `dup` call. Standard descriptors exist for the process lifetime; inheritance and general file-object semantics are not yet exposed. The initial process is created by the kernel loader, not a syscall.
    28	
    29	Stable v1 error numbers (returned negated in `RAX`) are: `1 EINVAL`, `2 EBADF`, `3 EFAULT`, `4 ENOMEM`, `5 ECHILD`, `6 EINTR`, `7 EIO`, `8 ENOSYS`, `9 E2BIG`, `10 EOVERFLOW`, and `11 ENOTSUP`. Unknown syscall numbers return `-ENOSYS`. Pointer-plus-length ranges use checked arithmetic and must lie wholly in a mapped lower-half user range. `write` preflights the whole input range before output; a later endpoint failure may return a short count, and an error before progress returns `-EIO`. A copy fault after progress returns the completed prefix; unrecoverable hardware faults remain process-fatal until user-mode exception handling is implemented. `wait` validates its optional output range before blocking and keeps the child waitable if copying the exit status fails. V1 has no signals, asynchronous interruption, or automatic syscall restart; wait is uninterruptible.
    30	
    31	All ABI integers are fixed-width little-endian x86_64 values. The wait status is one signed 32-bit integer with no implicit padding or extra fields. No other user-visible structs exist in v1.
    32	
    33	## Initial x86_64 entry design (Milestone 4; diagnostic path integrated)
    34	
    35	The opt-in single-vCPU process probe enters Ring 3 with a validated five-word `IRETQ` frame and enters the kernel with `int $0x80` through a dedicated DPL-3 IDT gate. This intentionally avoids `SYSCALL`/`SYSRET`, `STAR`/`LSTAR`/`FMASK`, and `SWAPGS` state transitions in this first slice. The register and error contract below is the versioned v1 ABI, but the runtime and syscall surface are not general-purpose or enabled in the default boot path.
    36	
    37	- **Vector ownership:** `0x80` lies inside the device-vector range (`0x20..=0xef`) and is reserved by `InterruptVectorAllocator`; generic IRQ allocation/release cannot claim it. The IDT installs a dedicated DPL-3 interrupt gate rather than the generic device-IRQ stub. Its assembly entry rejects CPL0 invocation, saves all GPRs and x87/SSE state, clears the direction flag, and calls a normalized Rust dispatcher with IF clear. The dispatcher currently implements only ABI-version discovery; process operations remain unavailable.
    38	- **Selectors:** the current GDT uses `0x08` for kernel code, `0x10` for kernel data, and `0x18` for the two-slot TSS descriptor. Ring-3 data and 64-bit code descriptors are appended at GDT indexes 5 and 6, with compile-time selector assertions for user data `0x2b` and user code `0x33` (RPL 3); the data selector is loaded into user `SS` on return. They are installed at bootstrap but remain unused until a validated return path exists.
    39	- **Privilege stack:** a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt uses `TSS.RSP0`. The current synchronous QEMU probe uses the bootstrap static ring-0 stack, mapped in both the kernel and process roots; it does not allocate per-process kernel stacks or schedule among user processes. `interrupts::set_kernel_entry_stack` validates canonical upper-half address shape and alignment before updating `RSP0`, but no general process scheduler calls it. Callers must disable local interrupts and guarantee the stack is mapped writable in every address space that can run until the next update. A future SMP design needs per-CPU TSS and entry-stack state.
    40	- **Entry frame and state:** the dedicated assembly stub saves all GPRs in the `SyscallContext` layout, passes the five-word privilege frame separately from the exception frame, and saves/restores x87/SSE state around the Rust dispatcher; AVX remains disabled under the current CPU-state policy. Kernel code runs with the direction flag clear. The process probe validates saved RIP/RSP against the active process mappings and accesses user buffers only through owned frame tokens. It does not block or schedule in a syscall.
    41	- **Initial register convention:** `RAX` carries the syscall number; arguments use `RDI`, `RSI`, `RDX`, `R10`, `R8`, and `R9`; `RAX` carries the result. This is only a proposed register convention. It becomes stable only together with ABI version discovery, syscall numbers, errors, and transfer semantics below.
    42	- **Return validation:** use `IRETQ`, not `SYSRET`. Initial entry uses a host-tested frame sanitizer that requires exact ring-3 selectors, a canonical lower-half instruction pointer, a lower-half stack range, 16-byte initial stack alignment, and safe flags. Syscall resume uses a separate sanitizer that keeps exact selectors, canonical lower-half address shape, and privileged-flag checks but does not impose 16-byte alignment on an in-function RSP; it replaces user flags with `0x2` (IF remains clear). Once a process is active, the dispatcher also validates the saved instruction pointer against an executable mapping and the saved stack pointer against a writable NX mapping. A malformed frame is converted into process exit rather than returned to CPL3.
    43	- **NMI and interrupt policy:** no GS-base swap is needed on this entry path. NMI, double fault, and machine check remain fatal even when their saved CS indicates CPL3. Other user-origin exceptions terminate the process with status `128 + vector` in the diagnostic runtime; only user #UD has been exercised in QEMU so far. Kernel-origin exceptions remain fatal. Ordinary maskable IRQs stay disabled throughout the synchronous process run.
    44	
    45	This path depends on each process root sharing supervisor-only upper-half mappings that cover syscall/exception code, the IDT, GDT, TSS, and active kernel stack. The bundled process root and syscall/exception transitions are exercised by opt-in QEMU smokes, but the shared Limine-derived kernel mapping is not a curated kernel map or a general isolation policy. Do not enable normal boot-time Ring 3 execution until process scheduling, per-process kernel stacks, wait semantics, and the remaining Milestone 4 fault/teardown criteria are implemented and validated.
    46	
    47	### Process address spaces (design; root construction partially implemented)
    48	
    49	Use a separate four- or five-level root per process. The initial source is the retained active clone of Limine's hierarchy, not a curated clean-room root. Each process root owns its root page, all lower-half intermediate tables, and every user leaf frame. Keep the kernel-root owner alive for the lifetime of every process root. Copy only upper-half top-level entries from that owner into each process root; these entries are non-owning references to shared kernel subtrees, not deep copies, and must never be released by a process teardown. Do not copy lower-half entries from the kernel root.
    50	
    51	Before publishing a shared kernel subtree, validate its page-table structure and physical bounds and reject any effectively user-accessible leaf. U/S permission is the conjunction of every entry on a path, so a U/S bit on one non-leaf alone does not grant user access. When copying upper-half root entries, clear their U/S bit as defense in depth; a user leaf then cannot become accessible if a lower entry changes. `paging::validate_supervisor_kernel_half` implements the bounded, read-only structural/effective-permission preflight, but it does not install roots or prove physical backing is readable; the supplied reader must provide that access guarantee. Sharing the active clone means every accepted upper-half supervisor mapping and alias is present in every process CR3. This is not a curated kernel map or kernel-page-table isolation, and it provides no transient-execution protection. User mappings remain private to one process, are confined to the lower canonical half, preserve W^X, and are non-global in the first implementation.
    52	
    53	The kernel address-space owner is the only authority allowed to modify shared upper-half tables. Mutations must be serialized with local interrupts disabled on the current single-vCPU system and invalidate the affected local translation before the mapping change is relied on. A process root may not edit or reclaim shared tables. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::destroy` releases only private user leaves, intermediate tables, and the root; the caller must first switch CR3 to a different live root and invalidate this root's local non-global translations. Keep the shared kernel owner alive. PCID-aware invalidation and SMP shootdown remain unsupported and need a separate design.
    54	
    55	The current `CandidatePageTables` deep-clones the inherited hierarchy, tracks all cloned tables as owned, and holds an exclusive mutable borrow of one memory backend; it is not itself the process-address-space abstraction. `SharedKernelHalf` validates and snapshots the sanitized upper root entries while borrowing the kernel owner. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` uses one exclusive backend borrow for multiple private roots, maps allocator-owned user 4 KiB leaves only in inactive lower halves, retains writable/executable permission metadata, validates the initial executable entry and writable NX stack, provides range-preflighted copy-in/copy-out through a separate `UserFrameMemory` backend, and destroys private leaf/table/root frames without freeing shared subtrees. Host tests cover four-/five-level sharing, U/S sanitization, independent mappings, permission checks, cross-page copies, unmap ownership, active-root release rejection, and rollback. The opt-in `probe-user-process` target additionally constructs and activates one root, loads the bundled ELF, serves write/exit calls using token-based copies, and restores CR3 before wait/reap and teardown. The bootstrap static kernel-entry stack and Limine-derived shared kernel subtree are used; this is not a general multi-process or curated kernel-map policy. Keep the kernel owner alive and immutable for the shared view's lifetime; callers must use a distinct page-table backend for process-owned tables.
    56	
    57	### Static ELF64 image validation and page initialization (partial)
    58	
    59	`src/elf.rs` parses little-endian x86_64 `ET_EXEC` images without allocation. It bounds the program-header count, load-segment count, and total mapped pages; checks file and virtual arithmetic, page alignment and `p_align` congruence, lower-half canonical ranges, non-overlapping page spans, readable segment flags, W^X, and that the entry point lies in a non-writable executable `PT_LOAD`. It rejects dynamic/interpreter and TLS segments and executable-stack requests. This initial format intentionally requires page-aligned load offsets/addresses and supports at most 64 program headers, 16 load segments, and 64 load pages. `populate_segment_page` copies one load page into an allocator-owned frame through `UserFrameMemory`, zero-filling bytes beyond the file payload. `load_into_process_root` allocates, populates, cache-selects, and maps every load page into an inactive process root. The diagnostic build reproducibly compiles `crates/rustix-init` as a static ELF64 payload; `just process-smoke` loads and runs the normal image, and `just user-fault-smoke` builds a `ud2` entry variant and validates process termination/reaping/teardown.
    60	
    61	## ABI decisions still pending beyond v1
    62	
    63	The initial v1 versioning, error encoding, syscall numbers, register-level request decoding, and assembly-matched syscall context layout are implemented in `src/syscall.rs`. The diagnostic `int 0x80` path sanitizes return frames and serves ABI-version, bounded write, and exit calls; invalid unmapped write buffers return `EFAULT` before output. `src/process.rs` provides fixed-capacity identity/exit-state policy, and the diagnostic kernel harness performs a nonblocking kernel-side wait/reap after the user-entry trampoline returns. The userspace `wait` call still returns `ENOTSUP`; status copyout, blocking waits, child creation, scheduler integration, and descriptor tables are not implemented. User faults are process-terminating only while the opt-in callback is installed; current QEMU coverage includes #UD, not the full exception matrix. Still to be specified before broader process operations are process-creation/exec and file-action semantics, general descriptor sharing/duplication/inheritance, read/open/close behavior, signal-like asynchronous delivery, clocks, and any additional structure layouts.
    64	
    65	## Suggested first user-visible slice
    66	
    67	After address spaces, scheduler, and storage primitives exist, implement a controlled `init` process with a small syscall subset: process exit, read/write through descriptors, open/close, and wait. Add end-to-end tests for invalid pointers, partial transfers, descriptor lifetime, process exit status, and ABI version negotiation before describing it as Unix-compatible.

struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

// SAFETY: `prepare_table` accepts only an allocator-issued frame and validates
// its complete usable span and HHDM address. Handles are only used while the
// candidate retains the frame token and this unique backend borrow.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory for LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_> {
    type PreparedTable = u64;
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn prepare_table(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
    ) -> Result<Self::PreparedTable, Self::Error> {
        frame.hhdm_address(
            self.memory_map,
            self.hhdm_offset,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    unsafe fn read_entry(
        &self,
        table: Self::PreparedTable,
        index: u16,
    ) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let entry_address = table
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The unsafe trait contract requires `table` to be the prepared
        // HHDM address of a complete writable frame; the index is in [0, 512).
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }

    unsafe fn clear_table(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable) {
        let entries = table as *mut u64;
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a handle prepared by this backend for a
        // complete writable frame retained by its candidate.
        unsafe {
            for index in 0..512 {
                entries.add(index).write_volatile(0);
            }
        }
    }

    unsafe fn write_entry(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable, index: u16, value: u64) {
        if index >= 512 {
            return;
        }
        let entry = (table as *mut u64).wrapping_add(usize::from(index));
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a prepared complete frame and an index in
        // range; this writes one entry without creating a Rust reference.
        unsafe { entry.write_volatile(value) };
    }

    unsafe fn invalidate_page(&mut self, virtual_address: u64) {
        // SAFETY: Active mapping callers provide the current virtual page and run
        // at CPL 0 with exclusive local page-table ownership.
        unsafe {
            core::arch::asm!(
                "invlpg [{}]",
                in(reg) virtual_address,
                options(nostack, preserves_flags)
            );
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
enum LimineUserFrameMemoryError {
    OutOfBounds,
    Address(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError),
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
struct LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
impl LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'_> {
    fn frame_slice_address(
        &self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        length: usize,
    ) -> Result<*mut u8, LimineUserFrameMemoryError> {
        if offset
            .checked_add(length)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE as usize)
        {
            return Err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::OutOfBounds);
        }
        if length == 0 {
            return Ok(core::ptr::null_mut());
        }

        let base = frame
            .hhdm_address(
                self.memory_map,
                self.hhdm_offset,
                self.physical_address_bits,
                self.virtual_address_bits,
            )
            .map_err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address)?;
        let address =
            base.checked_add(offset as u64)
                .ok_or(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address(
                    rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow,
                ))?;
        Ok(address as *mut u8)
    }
}

// SAFETY: The non-copyable Frame token and checked HHDM conversion authorize a
// complete Usable page. Each operation checks its subrange, accesses only that
// page, and uses raw copies rather than forming user virtual references. The
// implementation relies on Limine's mapped-usable-memory contract; hardware
// faults from a broken mapping remain fatal and are not recoverable here.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::UserFrameMemory for LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'_> {
    type Error = LimineUserFrameMemoryError;

    fn copy_from_frame(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        destination: &mut [u8],
    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        let source = self.frame_slice_address(frame, offset, destination.len())?;
        if !destination.is_empty() {
            // SAFETY: The frame subrange was checked and the HHDM address was
            // validated for the full allocator-owned frame. `copy` permits overlap.
            unsafe { core::ptr::copy(source, destination.as_mut_ptr(), destination.len()) };
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn copy_to_frame(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        source: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        let destination = self.frame_slice_address(frame, offset, source.len())?;
        if !source.is_empty() {
            // SAFETY: The frame subrange was checked and the HHDM address was
            // validated for the full allocator-owned frame. `copy` permits overlap.
            unsafe { core::ptr::copy(source.as_ptr(), destination, source.len()) };
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

struct KernelHeapMappingContext {
    candidate: *mut (),
    allocator: *mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: *const arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
}

unsafe fn map_kernel_heap_pages(
    opaque_context: *mut (),
    first_page: usize,
    page_count: usize,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, EffectiveMemoryType, MtrrState,
        PagePermissions, PatLayout, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    if page_count == 0
        || first_page
            .checked_add(page_count)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_MAX_PAGES)
    {
        return false;
    }

    // SAFETY: The caller configures this callback only after the active root,
    // allocator, CPU snapshot, and local context are all live. The boot path is
    // single-vCPU and never returns from the stack containing that context.
    let state = unsafe { &mut *opaque_context.cast::<KernelHeapMappingContext>() };
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the retained local candidate and BootInfo
    // members. The callback is synchronous and never stores a derived reference.
    let candidate = unsafe {
        &mut *state
            .candidate
            .cast::<CandidatePageTables<'static, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'static>>>()
    };
    // SAFETY: The frame allocator and CPU snapshot remain owned by retained
    // BootInfo; this callback runs on the sole CPU with the heap lock held.
    let allocator = unsafe { &mut *state.allocator };
    // SAFETY: The CPU snapshot is immutable and remains live with BootInfo.
    let cpu_info = unsafe { &*state.cpu_info };

    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The callback runs at CPL 0; save IF before disabling local IRQs
    // while the active page tables and allocator are mutated.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", "cli", out(reg) flags) };
    let result = (|| {
        let physical_width = cpu_info.physical_address_bits?;
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(cpu_info.pat_msr_value?).ok()?;
        let mtrrs = match &cpu_info.mtrr {
            MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers.validated_layout(physical_width).ok()?,
            _ => return None,
        };
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        for (mapped, page) in (first_page..first_page + page_count).enumerate() {
            let virtual_address = KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE
                .checked_add((page as u64).checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE)?)?;
            let frame = match allocator.allocate() {
                Some(frame) => frame,
                None => {
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
                virtual_address,
                frame.address(),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                Some(physical_width),
                cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
            ) {
                Ok(mapping) => mapping,
                Err(_) => {
                    deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            let attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
                CachePolicy::WriteBack,
                pat,
                &mtrrs,
                cpu_info.normal_caching,
            ) {
                Ok(attributes) if attributes.effective_type() == EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack => {
                    attributes
                }
                _ => {
                    deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            // SAFETY: IF is clear, the current candidate owns the active root,
            // and the allocator-issued frame is mapped RW/NX with local TLB
            // invalidation before its token becomes page-table-owned.
            if let Err(failure) =
                unsafe { candidate.map_owned_page_active(allocator, frame, mapping, attributes) }
            {
                deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, failure.frame);
                rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                return None;
            }
        }
        Some(())
    })()
    .is_some();
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        // SAFETY: The mapping transaction is complete or fully rolled back.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("sti") };
    }
    result
}

fn rollback_kernel_heap_pages(
    candidate: &mut rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<
        'static,
        LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'static>,
    >,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    first_page: usize,
    mapped_pages: usize,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;

    for page in (first_page..first_page + mapped_pages).rev() {
        let Some(virtual_address) = (page as u64)
            .checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE)
            .and_then(|offset| KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE.checked_add(offset))
        else {
            halt_forever();
        };
        // SAFETY: The pages belong to this transaction in the current active
        // root; unmapping invalidates their TLB entries before token return.
        let frame = unsafe { candidate.unmap_owned_page_active(virtual_address) }
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_forever());
        deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
    }
}

fn deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if allocator.deallocate(frame).is_err() {
        halt_forever();
    }
}

// Error payloads provide boot diagnostics through the derived `Debug` output.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[derive(Debug)]
enum AcpiMappingError {
    InvalidAcpiSpan {
        physical_start: u64,
        length: usize,
        error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError,
    },
    InvalidMapping(rustix_kernel::paging::MappingError),
    CandidateMap(
        rustix_kernel::paging::CandidateMapErrorKind<rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError>,
    ),
    CandidateWalk,
    UnexpectedCurrentCr3,
}

struct CandidateAcpiReader<'candidate, 'memory, 'map> {
    candidate: &'candidate mut rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<
        'memory,
        LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'map>,
    >,
    allocator: &'candidate mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &'map rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    cache_layout: rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    normal_caching: bool,
    candidate_cr3: u64,
    previous_cr3: u64,
    virtual_address: u64,
}

impl CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    fn remove_temporary_mapping(&mut self) {
        if let Err(error) = self.candidate.unmap_acpi_page(self.virtual_address) {
            crate::kprintln!("temporary ACPI mapping could not be removed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    }
}

// The legacy-reserved authorization is accepted only for RSDP reads; all
// root and child tables require ACPI-reclaimable/NVS memory-map coverage.
impl CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    fn read_mapped(
        &mut self,
        physical_start: u64,
        output: &mut [u8],
        allow_legacy_rsdp: bool,
    ) -> Result<(), AcpiMappingError> {
        use rustix_kernel::paging::{
            validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
        };

        if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
            return Err(AcpiMappingError::UnexpectedCurrentCr3);
        }
        if output.is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let length =
            u64::try_from(output.len()).map_err(|_| AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
                physical_start,
                length: output.len(),
                error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow,
            })?;
        let span = if allow_legacy_rsdp {
            self.memory_map.validate_rsdp_span(
                physical_start,
                length,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            )
        } else {
            self.memory_map.validate_acpi_span(
                physical_start,
                length,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            )
        }
        .map_err(|error| AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
            physical_start,
            length: output.len(),
            error,
        })?;
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: false,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        let mut copied = 0usize;
        while copied < output.len() {
            let current_physical = physical_start.checked_add(copied as u64).ok_or(
                AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
                    physical_start,
                    length: output.len(),
                    error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow,
                },
            )?;
            let physical_page = current_physical & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
            let page_offset = current_physical - physical_page;
            let page_length = (PAGE_SIZE - page_offset).min((output.len() - copied) as u64);
            let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
                self.virtual_address,
                physical_page,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
                self.virtual_address_bits,
            )
            .map_err(AcpiMappingError::InvalidMapping)?;
            let cache_attributes = mapping
                .select_cache_attributes(
                    CachePolicy::Uncacheable,
                    self.pat,
                    &self.cache_layout,
                    self.normal_caching,
                )
                .map_err(AcpiMappingError::InvalidMapping)?;
            self.candidate
                .map_acpi_page(self.allocator, span, mapping, cache_attributes)
                .map_err(|failure| AcpiMappingError::CandidateMap(failure.cause))?;

            let candidate_mapping_is_valid = matches!(
                self.candidate.walk(self.virtual_address),
                Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
                    if translation.physical_address == physical_page
                        && translation.permissions == permissions
            );
            if !candidate_mapping_is_valid {
                self.remove_temporary_mapping();
                return Err(AcpiMappingError::CandidateWalk);
            }
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                halt_forever();
            }

            // SAFETY: The candidate is a complete clone of the current inherited
            // hierarchy with all critical paths verified; this temporary page is
            // supervisor R/NX and the candidate remains owned by this stack.
            unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.candidate_cr3) };
            // SAFETY: The CR3 write above installed the candidate root and maskable
            // interrupts remain disabled during this single-core bootstrap read.
            unsafe { self.candidate.mark_active() };
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.candidate_cr3 {
                // SAFETY: Restoring the previous validated root preserves all code,
                // stack, data, and exception mappings needed by this path.
                unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.previous_cr3) };
                if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                    halt_forever();
                }
                // SAFETY: The verified CR3 is no longer the candidate root.
                unsafe { self.candidate.mark_inactive() };
                self.remove_temporary_mapping();
                return Err(AcpiMappingError::UnexpectedCurrentCr3);
            }

            let source = (self.virtual_address + page_offset) as *const u8;
            for offset in 0..page_length as usize {
                // SAFETY: The exact physical page is temporarily mapped R/NX in
                // the active candidate and this byte lies within its 4 KiB leaf.
                output[copied + offset] = unsafe { source.add(offset).read_volatile() };
            }

            // SAFETY: The prior root remains allocated and its critical mappings
            // were verified before this temporary switch.
            unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.previous_cr3) };
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                halt_forever();
            }
            // SAFETY: The previous root was restored and verified above.
            unsafe { self.candidate.mark_inactive() };
            self.remove_temporary_mapping();
            copied += page_length as usize;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

// SAFETY: `read_mapped` authorizes ordinary table reads only through validated
// ACPI map regions; its separate RSDP entry point permits only the bounded legacy
// reserved window recognized by `MemoryMap::validate_rsdp_span`.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::acpi::AcpiPhysicalReader for CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    type Error = AcpiMappingError;

    fn read(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        self.read_mapped(physical_start, output, false)
    }

    fn read_rsdp(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        self.read_mapped(physical_start, output, true)
    }
}

// Capture Limine's entry RSP before a Rust prologue changes it. The synthetic
// return slot is part of the SysV entry stack; realign before calling Rust.
core::arch::global_asm!(
    ".section .text",
    ".code64",
    ".global _start",
    ".type _start, @function",
    "_start:",
    "mov rdi, rsp",
    "and rsp, -16",
    "call rustix_start",
    "ud2",
    ".size _start, . - _start",
);

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_start(entry_rsp: u64) -> ! {
    // Keep interrupts masked until FPU state and the IRQ save destination are ready.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    if let Err(error) = arch::x86_64::cpu::initialize_fpu_state() {
        kprintln!("required x87/SSE state unavailable: {:?}", error);
        halt_forever();
    }
    kernel_threads::initialize_fpu_context();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    kprintln!("x87/SSE context state enabled with FXSAVE/FXRSTOR; AVX disabled");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    let mut boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information(entry_rsp) {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if let Err(error) = arch::x86_64::interrupts::configure_user_address_width(
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        kprintln!("user syscall address-width setup failed: {:?}", error);
        halt_forever();
    }
    #[cfg(target_os = "none")]
    let init_image = match rustix_kernel::elf::Elf64Image::parse(
        INIT_ELF_IMAGE,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(image) => image,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("bundled init ELF rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    #[cfg(target_os = "none")]
    kprintln!(
        "bundled init ELF validated: entry={:#x}, load pages={}",
        init_image.entry_point(),
        init_image.load_page_count()
    );
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
    probe_hhdm_frame(&mut boot_info);

    #[cfg(any(feature = "inject-page-fault", feature = "inject-invalid-opcode"))]
    run_fault_injection();

    activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(&mut boot_info)
}

fn activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) -> ! {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        encode_cr3_value, CandidatePageTables, PageWalkConfig, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let inherited_root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: inherited CR3: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: NXE is not enabled");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let config = PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "page-table transition failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    if let Err(error) =
        candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &reader, inherited_root)
    {
        kprintln!(
            "page-table transition failed to clone inherited root: {:?}",
            error
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    let spans = [
        (
            "kernel text",
            segments.text.virtual_start,
            segments.text.physical_start,
            segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel rodata",
            segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            segments.rodata.physical_start,
            segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel data",
            segments.data.virtual_start,
            segments.data.physical_start,
            segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "active boot stack",
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        ),
    ];
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            &reader,
            inherited_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: {} was not preserved",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    }
    if !harden_kernel_hhdm_aliases(
        &mut candidate,
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        KernelAliasHardeningContext {
            memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
            hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            physical_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
            virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
            segments: boot_info.kernel_image_segments,
            reader: &reader,
            inherited_root,
            config,
        },
    ) {
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    kprintln!("kernel HHDM aliases validated: text/rodata R/NX, data RW/NX, PAT preserved");
    let candidate_root = candidate
        .root_physical_address()
        .expect("a live candidate retains its root frame");
    let root_hhdm_address = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        candidate_root,
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let root_alias = match candidate.walk(root_hhdm_address) {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
            if translation.physical_address == candidate_root =>
        {
            translation
        }
        result => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM alias: {:?}",
                result
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    if !root_alias.permissions.writable || root_alias.permissions.user_accessible {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: candidate root alias permissions are unsafe");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let new_cr3 = match encode_cr3_value(
        candidate_root,
        inherited_root.low_bits(),
        physical_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: new CR3: {:?}", error);
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let inherited_cr3 = boot_info.inherited_cr3_raw;
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != inherited_cr3 {
        kprintln!("page-table transition aborted: active CR3 changed before switch");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    if let Some(rsdp_physical_address) = boot_info.rsdp_physical_address {
        match load_acpi_madt(
            &mut candidate,
            &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
            &boot_info.memory_map,
            &boot_info.cpu_info,
            rsdp_physical_address,
            new_cr3,
            inherited_cr3,
        ) {
            Ok(madt) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "ACPI MADT copied: LAPIC={:#x}, {} local APICs, {} I/O APICs, {} overrides",
                    madt.local_apic_address,
                    madt.local_apics().count(),
                    madt.io_apics().count(),
                    madt.interrupt_overrides().count()
                );
                boot_info.acpi_madt = Some(madt);
            }
            Err(error) => kprintln!("ACPI MADT unavailable: {:?}", error),
        }
    }
    let apic_virtual_addresses = match boot_info.acpi_madt.as_ref() {
        Some(madt) => match map_bootstrap_apic_pages(
            &mut candidate,
            &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
            &boot_info.cpu_info,
            madt,
            &boot_info.memory_map,
            (
                boot_info.kernel_physical_base,
                boot_info.kernel_physical_end,
            ),
        ) {
            Ok(addresses) => Some(addresses),
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("APIC MMIO mappings unavailable: {}", error);
                None
            }
        },
        None => None,
    };
    match candidate.validate_supervisor_kernel_half() {
        Ok(table_count) => kprintln!(
            "kernel upper-half preflight passed: {} shared supervisor tables",
            table_count
        ),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: unsafe kernel upper half: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: The candidate is a complete clone of every present inherited
    // hierarchy entry, with all referenced intermediate tables owned and the
    // critical code/data/stack paths compared before this point. The inherited
    // root's paging mode, address widths, PAT/MTRR state, and low CR3 mode are
    // preserved; interrupts remain disabled through this transition and are enabled
    // later only after the selected APIC routes and handlers are ready.
    let global_tlb_flushed = unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(new_cr3) };
    if global_tlb_flushed {
        kprintln!("page-table transition: global TLB flushed via CR4.PGE toggle");
    } else {
        kprintln!("page-table transition: CR4.PGE clear; CR3 reload flushed active translations");
    }
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != new_cr3
        || !spans
            .iter()
            .all(|(_, virtual_start, physical_start, length)| {
                candidate_span_matches_source(
                    &candidate,
                    &reader,
                    inherited_root,
                    config,
                    *virtual_start,
                    *physical_start,
                    *length,
                )
            })
    {
        // SAFETY: The inherited root and its backing memory remain untouched and
        // mapped by the candidate, so restoring its validated CR3 value is safe.
        unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(inherited_cr3) };
        if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != inherited_cr3 {
            kprintln!("page-table transition failed to restore inherited CR3; candidate retained");
            halt_forever();
        }
        kprintln!("page-table transition failed post-switch verification; restored inherited CR3");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    // SAFETY: CR3 matches `new_cr3` and post-switch translation checks passed;
    // interrupts are disabled and the candidate root must remain allocated.
    unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
    kprintln!(
        "page-table transition passed: active CR3={:#x}, cloned root={:#x}, {} owned tables",
        new_cr3,
        candidate_root,
        candidate.table_count()
    );

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-active-mapping")]
    {
        if let Err(error) = probe_active_mapping(
            &mut candidate,
            &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
            &boot_info.cpu_info,
        ) {
            kprintln!("active mapping probe failed: {}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
        kprintln!("active mapping probe passed: mapped, accessed, unmapped, reclaimed frame");
    }

    let mut vector_allocator = rustix_kernel::irq::InterruptVectorAllocator::new();
    let mut timer_vector = None;
    let mut timer_verified = false;
    if let (Some(madt), Some((local_apic_virtual, io_apic_virtual))) =
        (boot_info.acpi_madt.as_ref(), apic_virtual_addresses)
    {
        if let Some(vector) = vector_allocator.allocate() {
            let vector_number = vector.number();
            timer_vector = Some(vector);
            // SAFETY: Boot is single-core with IF=0. The cloned root is active,
            // and these virtual addresses were validated supervisor RW/NX/UC
            // mappings of the exact MADT-described APIC pages.
            match unsafe {
                arch::x86_64::apic::initialize(
                    madt,
                    local_apic_virtual,
                    io_apic_virtual,
                    arch::x86_64::cpu::bootstrap_apic_id(),
                )
            } {
                Err(error) => kprintln!(
                    "APIC initialization failed; IRQs remain disabled: {:?}",
                    error
                ),
                Ok(()) => {
                    // SAFETY: APIC initialization masked every route, including
                    // PIT IRQ0; the handler is ready before the route is armed.
                    match unsafe {
                        arch::x86_64::interrupts::register_irq_handler(
                            vector_number,
                            bootstrap_timer_irq,
                        )
                    } {
                        Err(error) => {
                            kprintln!("timer IRQ handler registration failed: {:?}", error)
                        }
                        Ok(()) => match PitRate::for_frequency(100) {
                            Err(error) => kprintln!("PIT rate selection failed: {:?}", error),
                            Ok(rate) => {
                                // SAFETY: The source remains masked through
                                // configuration and the ISR is already registered.
                                let configured = unsafe {
                                    arch::x86_64::apic::configure_pit_timer(
                                        vector_number,
                                        rate.divisor(),
                                    )
                                };
                                match configured {
                                    Err(error) => {
                                        kprintln!("PIT configuration failed: {:?}", error)
                                    }
                                    Ok(()) => {
                                        // SAFETY: Only the validated IRQ0 route is
                                        // unmasked after its handler is installed.
                                        match unsafe { arch::x86_64::apic::unmask_pit_timer() } {
                                            Err(error) => {
                                                kprintln!("PIT route unmask failed: {:?}", error)
                                            }
                                            Ok(()) => {
                                                // SAFETY: IDT/APIC/EOI/handler are
                                                // ready, every other route is masked,
                                                // and this ISR neither allocates nor
                                                // touches non-atomic shared state.
                                                unsafe {
                                                    core::arch::asm!(
                                                        "sti",
                                                        options(nomem, nostack)
                                                    );
                                                }
                                                let target =
                                                    BOOTSTRAP_TIMER_TICKS.ticks().saturating_add(3);
                                                let mut observed = false;
                                                for _ in 0..100_000_000 {
                                                    if BOOTSTRAP_TIMER_TICKS.ticks() >= target {
                                                        observed = true;
                                                        break;
                                                    }
                                                    spin_loop();
                                                }
                                                if observed {
                                                    timer_verified = true;
                                                    kprintln!("timer IRQ path passed: 3 ticks, EOI acknowledged");
                                                } else {
                                                    // SAFETY: Stop the sole unmasked
                                                    // source before continuing without
