        user_memory: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(user_memory).cast(),
        process_table: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(process_table),
        process,
        process_id,
        kernel_cr3,
    };
    // SAFETY: IF was disabled by the caller; all pointer targets remain live
    // until the synchronous user entry returns through its exit syscall.
    if unsafe {
        arch::x86_64::interrupts::install_user_syscall_handler(
            dispatch_active_user_process_syscall,
            dispatch_active_user_process_exception,
            core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(process_context).cast(),
        )
    }
    .is_err()
    {
        roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
            "process root could not be destroyed after syscall handler setup failed"
        })?;
        return Err("user syscall handler setup failed");
    }
    // SAFETY: IF remains disabled, and this complete root was prevalidated.
    if unsafe { roots.mark_active(process) }.is_err() {
        // SAFETY: No user callback is in flight and the root is not installed.
        unsafe { arch::x86_64::interrupts::clear_user_syscall_handler() };
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after activation failed")?;
        return Err("process root could not be marked active");
    }

    // SAFETY: The process root shares the validated supervisor kernel half and
    // the kernel/TSS stacks are mapped in both roots; interrupts remain disabled.
    unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(process_cr3) };
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != process_cr3 {
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The mapped entry/stack were validated above; syscall/fault dispatch
    // are installed and maskable interrupts remain disabled through process exit.
    let exit_status = match unsafe { arch::x86_64::interrupts::enter_user(user_frame) } {
        Ok(status) => status,
        Err(_) => halt_forever(),
    };
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != kernel_cr3 {
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The exit trampoline returned to the kernel root with IF=0 and no
    // syscall callback remains in flight.
    unsafe { arch::x86_64::interrupts::clear_user_syscall_handler() };
    let wait_result =
        match process_table.try_wait(rustix_kernel::process::KERNEL_PROCESS_ID, process_id.get()) {
            Ok(result) => result,
            Err(_) => {
                roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
                    "inactive process root could not be destroyed after wait failed"
                })?;
                return Err("kernel wait could not inspect the init process");
            }
        };
    #[cfg(any(
        feature = "probe-user-fault",
        feature = "probe-user-page-fault",
        feature = "probe-user-general-protection",
        feature = "probe-user-divide-error"
    ))]
    let expected_status = 128 + PROBE_USER_FAULT_VECTOR as i32;
    #[cfg(not(any(
        feature = "probe-user-fault",
        feature = "probe-user-page-fault",
        feature = "probe-user-general-protection",
        feature = "probe-user-divide-error"
    )))]
    let expected_status = 42;
    if !matches!(
        wait_result,
        rustix_kernel::process::WaitResult::Exited { pid, status }
            if pid == process_id && status == exit_status && status == expected_status
    ) {
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "inactive process root could not be destroyed after wait mismatch")?;
        return Err("init exit status was not retained and reaped as expected");
    }
    roots
        .destroy(allocator, process)
        .map_err(|_| "inactive process root teardown failed")?;
    if allocator.free_frames() != initial_free_frames {
        return Err("process-root teardown did not restore the frame count");
    }
    #[cfg(not(any(
        feature = "probe-user-fault",
        feature = "probe-user-page-fault",
        feature = "probe-user-general-protection",
        feature = "probe-user-divide-error"
    )))]
    kprintln!(
        "init process exited with status {} and was reaped by kernel wait",
        exit_status
    );
    #[cfg(any(
        feature = "probe-user-fault",
        feature = "probe-user-page-fault",
        feature = "probe-user-general-protection",
        feature = "probe-user-divide-error"
    ))]
    kprintln!(
        "user fault vector {} exited with status {} and was reaped by kernel wait",
        PROBE_USER_FAULT_VECTOR,
        exit_status
    );
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_hhdm_frame(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE;
    use rustix_kernel::paging::UserFrameMemory;

    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: no free frame");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let hhdm_address = match frame.hhdm_address(
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe rejected frame translation: {:?}", error);
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let mut user_memory = LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut expected = [0; 64];
    for (index, byte) in expected.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        *byte = index as u8 ^ 0x5a;
    }
    let mut observed = [0; 64];
    let copy_round_trip = user_memory
        .copy_to_frame(&frame, 128, &expected)
        .and_then(|()| user_memory.copy_from_frame(&frame, 128, &mut observed));
    let mut out_of_bounds = [0; 2];
    let bounds_rejected = user_memory
        .copy_from_frame(&frame, FRAME_SIZE as usize - 1, &mut out_of_bounds)
        .is_err();
    let empty_copy = user_memory
        .copy_to_frame(&frame, FRAME_SIZE as usize, &[])
        .is_ok();
    let mut verified =
        copy_round_trip.is_ok() && observed == expected && bounds_rejected && empty_copy;
    let words = (FRAME_SIZE / core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64) as usize;
    let page = hhdm_address as *mut u64;
    // SAFETY: The non-copyable `Frame` token is held exclusively; its full page
    // is within validated `Usable` memory and its HHDM arithmetic was checked.
    // Limine base revision 3 guarantees usable memory in the HHDM, and no other
    // Rustix mapping aliases this newly allocated frame. This is an opt-in QEMU
    // probe; a broken loader mapping would fault and be caught by the fatal path.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index)
                .write_volatile(0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64);
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            if page.add(index).read_volatile() != (0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64) {
                verified = false;
                break;
            }
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index).write_volatile(0);
        }
    }

    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
    if !verified {
        kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: readback mismatch");
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!("HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame");
    probe_inherited_root(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_inherited_root(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address;

    let root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: CR3 decode rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let address = match inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
        root,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: HHDM validation rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let entries = address as *const u64;
    let mut present_entries = 0;
    // SAFETY: The complete root page was validated as bootloader-reclaimable
    // and its HHDM range arithmetic was checked. The Limine base-revision-3
    // contract maps that region; this read-only opt-in probe trusts that handoff.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..512 {
            if entries.add(index).read_volatile() & 1 != 0 {
                present_entries += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    kprintln!(
        "inherited root HHDM probe passed: read 512 entries, {} present",
        present_entries
    );
    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("inherited page-table walk failed: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "active boot stack",
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
    );

    let pat_value = match boot_info.cpu_info.pat_msr_value {
        Some(value) => value,
        None => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: active PAT value unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let pat = match rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value) {
        Ok(pat) => pat,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid PAT layout: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid MTRR state: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: non-normal CR0 caching mode");
        halt_forever();
    }
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    probe_cloned_page_tables(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        [
            (
                "kernel text",
                segments.text.virtual_start,
                segments.text.physical_start,
                segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel rodata",
                segments.rodata.virtual_start,
                segments.rodata.physical_start,
                segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel data",
                segments.data.virtual_start,
                segments.data.physical_start,
                segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "active boot stack",
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            ),
        ],
    );
    probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_cloned_page_tables(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    spans: [(&str, u64, u64, u64); 4],
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables;

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map,
        hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate = match CandidatePageTables::new(allocator, &mut memory, config) {
        Ok(candidate) => candidate,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                error.cause
            );
            if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                release_probe_frame(allocator, frame);
            }
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if let Err(error) = candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(allocator, source_reader, source_root) {
        kprintln!("candidate clone probe failed: {:?}", error);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
    }
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            source_reader,
            source_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed: {} translation mismatch",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
        }
    }
    let table_count = candidate.table_count();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate clone probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate inherited-root clone probe passed: {} owned table pages preserve critical paths; CR3 unchanged",
        table_count
    );
}

fn candidate_span_matches_source(
    candidate: &rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let Some(virtual_address) = virtual_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(expected_physical) = physical_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let source_result =
            walk_virtual_address(source_reader, source_root, virtual_address, config);
        let candidate_result = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
        let (source_translation, candidate_translation) = match (source_result, candidate_result) {
            (Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(source)), Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(candidate))) => {
                (source, candidate)
            }
            (source, candidate) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate clone walk mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}",
                    virtual_address,
                    source,
                    candidate
                );
                return false;
            }
        };
        if !source_translation.same_effective_mapping(candidate_translation)
            || candidate_translation.physical_address != expected_physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone translation mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}, expected PA={:#x}",
                virtual_address,
                source_translation,
                candidate_translation,
                expected_physical
            );
            return false;
        }
        let Some(next_offset) = offset.checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE) else {
            return false;
        };
        offset = next_offset;
    }
    true
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome,
    };

    let Some(physical_address_bits) = boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits else {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: physical width unknown");
        halt_forever();
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled || !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: NXE or normal caching unavailable");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let pat_value = boot_info
        .cpu_info
        .pat_msr_value
        .expect("inherited cache-alias probe validated active PAT");
    let pat = rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value).unwrap_or_else(|error| {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid PAT: {:?}",
            error
        );
        halt_forever();
    });
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid MTRR: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: true,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_ffff_f000;
    let permissions = PagePermissions {
        writable: true,
        executable: false,
        user_accessible: false,
    };
    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: no leaf frame available");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
        virtual_address,
        frame.address(),
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        permissions,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        config.virtual_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(mapping) => mapping,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid mapping: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let cache_attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
        CachePolicy::WriteBack,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
    ) {
        Ok(attributes) => attributes,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: cache policy: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate page-table probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                if let Some(root_frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, root_frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
    let frame_address = frame.address();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.map_owned_page(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        frame,
        mapping,
        cache_attributes,
    ) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to map leaf: {:?}",
            failure.cause
        );
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, failure.frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let walk = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
    let returned_frame = match candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address) {
        Ok(frame) => frame,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed to unmap leaf: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let translation_valid = match &walk {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => {
            translation.physical_address == frame_address
                && translation.page_size == rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE
                && translation.permissions == permissions
                && translation.pat_index == cache_attributes.pat_index()
        }
        _ => false,
    };
    if returned_frame.address() != frame_address {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: unmap returned the wrong frame");
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
    if !translation_valid {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: candidate walk: {:?}",
            walk
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate page-table probe passed: mapped, walked, unmapped, and released root {:#x}; CR3 unchanged",
        root.expect("candidate retains root until release")
    );
}

fn release_candidate_after_probe_failure(
    candidate: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
) -> ! {
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table cleanup also failed: {:?}", failure);
    }
    halt_forever()
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_inherited_mapping(
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    label: &str,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    let mut first_translation: Option<rustix_kernel::paging::PageTranslation> = None;
    let mut permissions_uniform = true;
    let mut pat_index_uniform = true;
    while offset < length {
        let virtual_address = match virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let expected_physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} physical overflow",
                    label
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, virtual_address, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level }) => {
                if level == rustix_kernel::paging::PageLevel::Pml4 {
                    let pml4_index = ((virtual_address >> 39) & 0x1ff) as u16;
                    let root_entry = reader.read_entry(root.physical_address(), pml4_index);
                    kprintln!(
                        "inherited mapping PML4 detail: VA={:#018x}, index={}, root={:#x}, entry={:?}",
                        virtual_address,
                        pml4_index,
                        root.physical_address(),
                        root_entry
                    );
                }
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} absent at {:?}",
                    label,
                    level
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {}: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if translation.physical_address != expected_physical {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited mapping probe failed: {} {:#018x} mapped to {:#018x}, expected {:#018x}",
                label,
                virtual_address,
                translation.physical_address,
                expected_physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        if let Some(first) = first_translation {
            permissions_uniform &= translation.permissions == first.permissions;
            pat_index_uniform &= translation.pat_index == first.pat_index;
        } else {
            first_translation = Some(translation);
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    if let Some(first) = first_translation {
        kprintln!(
            "inherited mapping probe passed: {} ({} pages), first permissions={:?}, PAT index={}, leaf size={}, uniform permissions={}, uniform PAT index={}",
            label,
            pages,
            first.permissions,
            first.pat_index,
            first.page_size,
            permissions_uniform,
            pat_index_uniform
        );
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
    boot_info: &boot::BootInfo,
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    mtrrs: &rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    label: &str,
    kernel_virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} physical overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_virtual = match kernel_virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_virtual = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
            boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(address) => address,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM range: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, kernel_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, hhdm_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_translation.physical_address != physical
            || hhdm_translation.physical_address != physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias probe failed: {} physical {:#018x} has inconsistent translations",
                label,
                physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        let kernel_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            kernel_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            hhdm_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_type != hhdm_type {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias conflict: {} PA {:#018x}, kernel {:?} vs HHDM {:?}",
                label,
                physical,
                kernel_type,
                hhdm_type
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    kprintln!(
        "cache-alias probe passed: {} ({} pages; effective types match)",
        label,
        pages
    );
}

fn release_probe_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!(
            "HHDM frame probe failed to return its frame: {:?}",
            error.error
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-page-fault")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately reads an unmapped
    // low virtual address; the installed page-fault handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov rax, 0xdeadbeef",
            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack)
        );
    }
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-invalid-opcode")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering invalid opcode with ud2");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately raises #UD; the
    // installed invalid-opcode handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("ud2", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-general-protection")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering general protection with invalid DS selector");
    // SAFETY: The selector index is outside the installed GDT limit, so loading
    // it into DS deliberately raises a kernel-origin #GP in QEMU.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov ax, 0xffff",
            "mov ds, ax",
            out("ax") _,
            options(nostack)
        )
    };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-divide-error")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering divide error with a zero divisor");
    // SAFETY: Integer division by zero deliberately raises kernel-origin #DE.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "xor edx, edx",
            "xor eax, eax",
            "xor ecx, ecx",
            "div ecx",
            out("eax") _,
            out("edx") _,
            out("ecx") _,
            options(nostack)
        )
    };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

/// Set once the fatal panic path has started. A panic from inside the fatal
/// path stops silently instead of recursively printing or looping diagnostics.
static FATAL_PANIC_ACTIVE: core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool =
    core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    // Mask maskable interrupts before any diagnostics run: another kernel
    // thread must not resume after a panic is declared, and the fatal report
    // must not be preempted mid-print.
    //
    // SAFETY: Kernel panic path runs at CPL 0; masking IF is always sound.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    if FATAL_PANIC_ACTIVE.swap(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire) {
        loop {
            // SAFETY: Re-entrant panics are deliberately silent.
            unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
        }
    }
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build a pinned Limine hybrid ISO and smoke-test it in QEMU.

Only Python's standard library is required. The Limine binary archive is kept
under target/ and checked against the SHA-256 published for the pinned release.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import select
import shutil
import socket
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import urllib.request
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TARGET_DIR = ROOT / "target"
LIMINE_VERSION = "12.9.3"
LIMINE_ARCHIVE_NAME = "limine-binary.zip"
# Provenance: SHA-256 of limine-binary.zip v12.9.3 as published for the
# upstream v12.9.3 release (cross-checked against the GitHub release API
# digest at pin time; the release is marked immutable upstream). The archive is
# re-hashed on every run and mismatch is fatal. The upstream PGP signature
# (limine-binary.zip.sig) is NOT verified by this script; verify it out-of-band
# whenever the pin is bumped.
LIMINE_ARCHIVE_SHA256 = "1bdbbcda650c5dba9b1eca5833d598137bf11bd6289bc89b6bcc4f8f112fa676"
LIMINE_ARCHIVE_URL = (
    "https://github.com/Limine-Bootloader/Limine/releases/download/"
    f"v{LIMINE_VERSION}/{LIMINE_ARCHIVE_NAME}"
)
KERNEL = TARGET_DIR / "x86_64-unknown-none" / "release" / "rustix"
ISO_ROOT = TARGET_DIR / "rustix-iso-root"
ISO_PATH = TARGET_DIR / "rustix.iso"

REQUIRED_LIMINE_FILES = (
    "limine-bios.sys",
    "limine-bios-cd.bin",
    "limine-uefi-cd.bin",
    "BOOTX64.EFI",
)


class BuildError(RuntimeError):
    """An actionable error while preparing or testing the boot image."""


def require_tool(name: str) -> str:
    path = shutil.which(name)
    if path is None:
        raise BuildError(f"required tool '{name}' was not found on PATH")
    return path


def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as source:
        for block in iter(lambda: source.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def safe_extract(archive: zipfile.ZipFile, destination: Path) -> None:
    root = destination.resolve()
    for member in archive.infolist():
        name = PurePosixPath(member.filename)
        mode = member.external_attr >> 16
        if not name.parts or name.is_absolute() or ".." in name.parts or ":" in name.parts[0]:
            raise BuildError(f"unsafe path in Limine archive: {member.filename}")
        if stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
            raise BuildError(f"symlink in Limine archive is not allowed: {member.filename}")
        output = (destination / Path(*name.parts)).resolve()
        if output != root and root not in output.parents:
            raise BuildError(f"archive member escapes extraction directory: {member.filename}")
    archive.extractall(destination)


def ensure_limine() -> tuple[Path, Path]:
    cache = TARGET_DIR / "tools" / f"limine-{LIMINE_VERSION}"
    archive_path = TARGET_DIR / "tools" / LIMINE_ARCHIVE_NAME
    extracted = cache / "archive"
    cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    extracted.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if not archive_path.exists():
        print(f"Downloading Limine {LIMINE_VERSION} binary release...")
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            LIMINE_ARCHIVE_URL,
            headers={"User-Agent": "Rustix-OS-build/0.1"},
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response, archive_path.open(
                "wb"
            ) as output:
                shutil.copyfileobj(response, output)
        except Exception as error:
            archive_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            raise BuildError(f"could not download pinned Limine release: {error}") from error

    actual_hash = sha256(archive_path)
    if actual_hash != LIMINE_ARCHIVE_SHA256:
        archive_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise BuildError(
            "Limine archive SHA-256 mismatch: "
            f"expected {LIMINE_ARCHIVE_SHA256}, got {actual_hash}"
        )

    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path) as archive:
            safe_extract(archive, extracted)
    except (OSError, zipfile.BadZipFile) as error:
        raise BuildError(f"could not extract the pinned Limine archive: {error}") from error

    def find_asset(name: str) -> Path:
        matches = sorted(extracted.rglob(name))
        if not matches:
            raise BuildError(f"Limine {LIMINE_VERSION} archive is missing {name}")
        return matches[0]

    if sys.platform == "win32":
        limine_tool = find_asset("limine.exe")
    else:
        limine_source = find_asset("limine.c")
        limine_tool = limine_source.with_name("limine")
        if not limine_tool.is_file():
            compiler = require_tool("cc")
            print("Building Limine host utility from the pinned source...")
            subprocess.run(
                [
                    compiler,
                    "-g",
                    "-O2",
                    "-pipe",
                    "-std=c99",
                    "-D_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64",
                    limine_source.name,
                    "-o",
                    str(limine_tool),
                ],
                cwd=limine_source.parent,
                check=True,
            )
        limine_tool.chmod(
            limine_tool.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IXUSR | stat.S_IXGRP | stat.S_IXOTH
        )
    return limine_tool, extracted


def build_image() -> None:
    if not KERNEL.is_file():
        raise BuildError("kernel ELF not found; run 'just build' first")
    xorriso = require_tool("xorriso")
    limine_tool, limine_root = ensure_limine()

    shutil.rmtree(ISO_ROOT, ignore_errors=True)
    boot_dir = ISO_ROOT / "boot" / "limine"
    efi_dir = ISO_ROOT / "EFI" / "BOOT"
    boot_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    efi_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    shutil.copy2(KERNEL, ISO_ROOT / "boot" / "rustix")
    shutil.copy2(ROOT / "limine.conf", ISO_ROOT / "limine.conf")

    for name in REQUIRED_LIMINE_FILES:
        source = next(iter(sorted(limine_root.rglob(name))), None)
        if source is None:
            raise BuildError(f"Limine archive is missing required file {name}")
        if name == "BOOTX64.EFI":
            shutil.copy2(source, efi_dir / name)
        else:
            shutil.copy2(source, boot_dir / name)

    ISO_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    xorriso_command = [
        xorriso,
        "-as",
        "mkisofs",
        "-R",
        "-r",
        "-J",
        "-b",
        "boot/limine/limine-bios-cd.bin",
        "-no-emul-boot",
        "-boot-load-size",
        "4",
        "-boot-info-table",
        "-hfsplus",
        "-apm-block-size",
        "2048",
        "--efi-boot",
        "boot/limine/limine-uefi-cd.bin",
        "-efi-boot-part",
        "--efi-boot-image",
        "--protective-msdos-label",
        str(ISO_ROOT),
        "-o",
        str(ISO_PATH),
    ]
    subprocess.run(xorriso_command, cwd=ROOT, check=True)
    subprocess.run([str(limine_tool), "bios-install", str(ISO_PATH)], cwd=ROOT, check=True)
    print(f"Created hybrid BIOS/UEFI image: {ISO_PATH.relative_to(ROOT)}")


def find_ovmf_firmware() -> tuple[Path, Path | None]:
    """Find a known installed OVMF image or CODE/VARS pair."""
    directories = (
        Path("/usr/share/ovmf"),
        Path("/usr/share/OVMF"),
        Path("/usr/share/qemu"),
        Path("/usr/share/edk2/ovmf"),
    )
    combined_names = ("OVMF.fd", "ovmf.fd")
    for directory in directories:
        for name in combined_names:
            firmware = directory / name
            if firmware.is_file():
                return firmware.resolve(), None

    for directory in directories:
        for suffix in ("", "_4M"):
            code = directory / f"OVMF_CODE{suffix}.fd"
            variables = directory / f"OVMF_VARS{suffix}.fd"
            if code.is_file() and variables.is_file():
                return code.resolve(), variables.resolve()

    raise BuildError(
        "OVMF firmware was not found in standard system locations; "
        "install the 'ovmf' package (for example, 'sudo apt install ovmf')"
    )

        def connect_until_ready(address: str | tuple[str, int], family: int) -> socket.socket:

        raise BuildError(f"kernel reached the shell after {kind} injection\nSerial output:\n{output}")
    if "fault injection unexpectedly returned" in output:
        raise BuildError(f"{kind} instruction returned instead of faulting\nSerial output:\n{output}")
    if not timed_out:
        status = result.returncode if result is not None else "unknown"
        raise BuildError(
            f"QEMU did not remain halted after {kind} (exit status {status})\n"
            f"Serial output:\n{output}"
        )

    print(f"QEMU {kind} fault-injection test passed (halt observed within {timeout}s).")
    print(f"Captured serial log: {serial_log.relative_to(ROOT)}")


def build_kernel(features: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> None:
    command = ["cargo", "build", "--release", "--target", "x86_64-unknown-none"]
    if features:
        command.extend(["--features", ",".join(features)])
    subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, check=True)

def run_interactive() -> None:
    qemu = require_tool("qemu-system-x86_64")
    if not ISO_PATH.is_file():
        raise BuildError("boot image not found; run 'just image' first")
    command = [
        qemu,
        "-machine",
        "q35",
        "-m",
        "256M",
        "-cdrom",
        str(ISO_PATH),
        "-boot",
        "d",
        "-display",
        "none",
        "-monitor",
        "none",
        "-serial",
        "stdio",
        "-no-reboot",
        "-no-shutdown",
    ]
    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, check=False)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise BuildError(f"QEMU exited with status {result.returncode}")

        "-display",
        "none",
        "-monitor",
        "none",
        "-serial",

        "-no-reboot",
        "-no-shutdown",
    ]
    print("QEMU is paused; GDB stub listening on 127.0.0.1:1234.", flush=True)
    print("Attach with the Rustix: QEMU (CodeLLDB) debug configuration.", flush=True)
    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, check=False)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise BuildError(f"QEMU exited with status {result.returncode}")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    subparsers.add_parser("image", help="create a pinned Limine BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO")
    smoke = subparsers.add_parser("smoke", help="boot the ISO and check its serial output")
    smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    uefi_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "uefi-smoke", help="boot the ISO with installed OVMF firmware and check ACPI"
    )
    uefi_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    frame_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "frame-smoke", help="probe HHDM access and an inactive candidate root in QEMU"
    )
    frame_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    process_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "process-smoke", help="run bundled init in Ring 3 and verify syscall/wait/teardown"
    )
    process_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    user_fault_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "user-fault-smoke", help="test Ring 3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE termination and process teardown"
    )
    user_fault_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    active_map_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "active-map-smoke", help="probe active owned-page mapping in QEMU, then restore the image"
    )
    active_map_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    thread_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "thread-smoke", help="test cooperative and timer-preemptive kernel threads with OVMF, then restore the default image"
    )
    thread_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    input_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "input-smoke", help="test UART and PS/2 IRQ input waking the shell with OVMF"
    )
    input_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=30, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    fault_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "fault-smoke", help="test fatal exceptions in QEMU, then restore the default image"
    )
    fault_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=10, help="per-test QEMU time limit")
    subparsers.add_parser("run", help="run the ISO with an interactive serial terminal")
    subparsers.add_parser("debug", help="run the ISO paused with a loopback GDB stub")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    try:
        if args.command == "image":
            build_image()
        elif args.command == "run":
            run_interactive()
        elif args.command == "debug":
            run_debug()
        elif args.command == "frame-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            frame_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "process-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            process_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "user-fault-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            user_fault_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "active-map-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            active_map_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "thread-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            thread_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "input-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            input_smoke_test(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "fault-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            fault_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "uefi-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            uefi_smoke_test(args.timeout)
        else:
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            smoke_test(args.timeout)
    except (BuildError, OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as error:
        print(f"Rustix boot workflow failed: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Unix-like process and syscall direction

**Status: Milestone 4 is in progress. The opt-in single-vCPU QEMU diagnostic path creates a lower-half process root sharing the validated supervisor kernel half, loads and runs a bundled static ELF in Ring 3, serves ABI-version/write/exit syscalls, terminates CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE with status `128 + vector`, and restores/reaps the root. The normal kernel does not launch userspace. The diagnostic `wait` path reaps already-exited children and preserves a zombie when status copyout fails; waiting for a running child, general process scheduling/kernel stacks, virtual-memory allocation, and a userspace runtime remain unimplemented.**

Rustix aims to expose a small, versioned syscall surface that can support Unix-like processes and tools. The kernel must own this interface rather than inherit an ABI accidentally from a bootloader or emulator.

## Proposed compatibility principles

- Processes have independent virtual address spaces and explicit lifecycle states.
- File descriptors are per-process integer handles to kernel-managed objects; descriptor inheritance, close-on-exec, duplication, and sharing semantics must be specified together.
- Syscalls use one documented error convention and stable numeric identifiers. New operations must not silently repurpose old numbers.
- Arguments crossing privilege boundaries are copied or validated using narrowly scoped helpers. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::copy_from_user` and `copy_to_user` preflight the complete lower-half mapped range, check writable metadata for kernel-to-user copies, and operate only on owned frame tokens through `UserFrameMemory`; they never form a Rust reference from a user virtual address. Backend copy faults report the completed prefix. The diagnostic user-exception path terminates a process on supported CPL3 faults; it does not make arbitrary kernel memory accesses recoverable.
- Blocking, interruption, cancellation, and restart behavior are explicit for each syscall class.
- A compatibility layer (for example, POSIX-shaped libc behavior) remains separate from internal kernel APIs.

## Initial syscall ABI v1 contract (specified; register decoding implemented)

ABI version `1.0` is identified by `abi_version()`, syscall number `0`, returning `0x0001_0000` in `RAX`. In v1, `RAX` returns a signed 64-bit result: nonnegative values are success (including byte counts and PIDs); errors are negative stable error numbers. ABI versioning is append-only: existing syscall numbers, argument meanings, layouts, and error values never change or get reused. There is no POSIX compatibility claim. `src/syscall.rs` implements the stable number/error constants, host-tested request decoding and write service, and the assembly-matched syscall context layout. `interrupts.rs` installs the DPL-3 gate and dedicated entry stub. The opt-in diagnostic process runtime dispatches ABI-version, bounded write, exit, and wait for already-exited children; a wait on a running child returns `ENOTSUP` because blocking user-process scheduling is not integrated. The QEMU init uses a kernel-seeded exited-child fixture to test wait status copyout and verifies an invalid status pointer returns `EFAULT` without reaping the child. A separate kernel-side test harness waits for the synchronous init after its exit trampoline returns.

| Number | Call | Register arguments | Result / behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `abi_version` | none | `0x0001_0000` (major 1, minor 0). |
| 1 | `exit` | `RDI`: signed 32-bit status in the low 32 bits (upper bits ignored) | Does not return; status is retained exactly by the parent wait record. |
| 2 | `write` | `RDI`: fd, `RSI`: user buffer, `RDX`: byte length | Returns bytes accepted; a short positive result is valid. Initial descriptors 1 and 2 are stdout/stderr console streams; other descriptors return `-EBADF`. Maximum request is 4096 bytes; zero length returns 0 without validating the pointer. |
| 3 | `wait` | `RDI`: child PID (0 means any child), `RSI`: optional user pointer to signed 32-bit exit status | Blocks until a matching child exits and returns its PID. A non-null status output must be writable before the child is reaped; no matching child returns `-ECHILD`. |

All other numbers are unassigned and return `-ENOSYS`; assigning a number later is an additive extension, never a reinterpretation. Descriptor 0 is reserved for input but v1 has no `read`, `open`, `close`, or `dup` call. Standard descriptors exist for the process lifetime; inheritance and general file-object semantics are not yet exposed. The initial process is created by the kernel loader, not a syscall.

Stable v1 error numbers (returned negated in `RAX`) are: `1 EINVAL`, `2 EBADF`, `3 EFAULT`, `4 ENOMEM`, `5 ECHILD`, `6 EINTR`, `7 EIO`, `8 ENOSYS`, `9 E2BIG`, `10 EOVERFLOW`, and `11 ENOTSUP`. Unknown syscall numbers return `-ENOSYS`. Pointer-plus-length ranges use checked arithmetic and must lie wholly in a mapped lower-half user range. `write` preflights the whole input range before output; a later endpoint failure may return a short count, and an error before progress returns `-EIO`. A copy fault after progress returns the completed prefix. An unmapped diagnostic `write` buffer returns `-EFAULT` before the syscall returns to userspace. `wait` validates its optional output range before blocking and keeps the child waitable if copying the exit status fails; this wait behavior is specified but not yet provided by the hardware dispatcher. V1 has no signals, asynchronous interruption, or automatic syscall restart; wait is uninterruptible.

All ABI integers are fixed-width little-endian x86_64 values. The wait status is one signed 32-bit integer with no implicit padding or extra fields. No other user-visible structs exist in v1.

## Initial x86_64 entry design (Milestone 4; diagnostic path integrated)

The opt-in single-vCPU process probe enters Ring 3 with a validated five-word `IRETQ` frame and enters the kernel with `int $0x80` through a dedicated DPL-3 IDT gate. This intentionally avoids `SYSCALL`/`SYSRET`, `STAR`/`LSTAR`/`FMASK`, and `SWAPGS` state transitions in this first slice. The register and error contract below is the versioned v1 ABI, but the runtime and syscall surface are not general-purpose or enabled in the default boot path.

- **Vector ownership:** `0x80` lies inside the device-vector range (`0x20..=0xef`) and is reserved by `InterruptVectorAllocator`; generic IRQ allocation/release cannot claim it. The IDT installs a dedicated DPL-3 interrupt gate rather than the generic device-IRQ stub. Its assembly entry rejects CPL0 invocation, saves all GPRs and x87/SSE state, clears the direction flag, and calls a normalized Rust dispatcher with IF clear. The opt-in process probe implements ABI-version discovery, write, and exit; `wait` and process creation remain unavailable to userspace.
- **Selectors:** the current GDT uses `0x08` for kernel code, `0x10` for kernel data, and `0x18` for the two-slot TSS descriptor. Ring-3 data and 64-bit code descriptors are appended at GDT indexes 5 and 6, with compile-time selector assertions for user data `0x2b` and user code `0x33` (RPL 3); the process probe uses these selectors in its validated entry frame.
- **Privilege stack:** a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt uses `TSS.RSP0`. The current synchronous QEMU probe uses the bootstrap static ring-0 stack, mapped in both the kernel and process roots; it does not allocate per-process kernel stacks or schedule among user processes. `interrupts::set_kernel_entry_stack` validates canonical upper-half address shape and alignment before updating `RSP0`, but no general process scheduler calls it. Callers must disable local interrupts and guarantee the stack is mapped writable in every address space that can run until the next update. A future SMP design needs per-CPU TSS and entry-stack state.
- **Entry frame and state:** the dedicated assembly stub saves all GPRs in the `SyscallContext` layout, passes the five-word privilege frame separately from the exception frame, and saves/restores x87/SSE state around the Rust dispatcher; AVX remains disabled under the current CPU-state policy. Kernel code runs with the direction flag clear. The process probe validates saved RIP/RSP against the active process mappings and accesses user buffers only through owned frame tokens. It does not block or schedule in a syscall.
- **Initial register convention:** `RAX` carries the syscall number; arguments use `RDI`, `RSI`, `RDX`, `R10`, `R8`, and `R9`; `RAX` carries the result. This convention and its initial numbers/errors are versioned as ABI v1. Implemented operations remain a subset of the documented contract.
- **Return validation:** use `IRETQ`, not `SYSRET`. Initial entry uses a host-tested frame sanitizer that requires exact ring-3 selectors, a canonical lower-half instruction pointer, a lower-half stack range, 16-byte initial stack alignment, and safe flags. Syscall resume uses a separate sanitizer that keeps exact selectors, canonical lower-half address shape, and privileged-flag checks but does not impose 16-byte alignment on an in-function RSP; it replaces user flags with `0x2` (IF remains clear). Once a process is active, the dispatcher also validates the saved instruction pointer against an executable mapping and the saved stack pointer against a writable NX mapping. A malformed frame is converted into process exit rather than returned to CPL3.
- **NMI and interrupt policy:** no GS-base swap is needed on this entry path. NMI, double fault, and machine check remain fatal even when their saved CS indicates CPL3. Other user-origin exceptions terminate the process with status `128 + vector` in the diagnostic runtime; QEMU exercises CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE. Kernel-origin #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE are separately tested as fatal. Ordinary maskable IRQs stay disabled throughout the synchronous process run.

This path depends on each process root sharing supervisor-only upper-half mappings that cover syscall/exception code, the IDT, GDT, TSS, and active kernel stack. The bundled process root and syscall/exception transitions are exercised by opt-in QEMU smokes, but the shared Limine-derived kernel mapping is not a curated kernel map or a general isolation policy. Do not enable normal boot-time Ring 3 execution until process scheduling, per-process kernel stacks, wait semantics, and the remaining Milestone 4 fault/teardown criteria are implemented and validated.

### Process address spaces (design; root construction partially implemented)

Use a separate four- or five-level root per process. The initial source is the retained active clone of Limine's hierarchy, not a curated clean-room root. Each process root owns its root page, all lower-half intermediate tables, and every user leaf frame. Keep the kernel-root owner alive for the lifetime of every process root. Copy only upper-half top-level entries from that owner into each process root; these entries are non-owning references to shared kernel subtrees, not deep copies, and must never be released by a process teardown. Do not copy lower-half entries from the kernel root.

Before publishing a shared kernel subtree, validate its page-table structure and physical bounds and reject any effectively user-accessible leaf. U/S permission is the conjunction of every entry on a path, so a U/S bit on one non-leaf alone does not grant user access. When copying upper-half root entries, clear their U/S bit as defense in depth; a user leaf then cannot become accessible if a lower entry changes. `paging::validate_supervisor_kernel_half` implements the bounded, read-only structural/effective-permission preflight, but it does not install roots or prove physical backing is readable; the supplied reader must provide that access guarantee. Sharing the active clone means every accepted upper-half supervisor mapping and alias is present in every process CR3. This is not a curated kernel map or kernel-page-table isolation, and it provides no transient-execution protection. User mappings remain private to one process, are confined to the lower canonical half, preserve W^X, and are non-global in the first implementation.

The kernel address-space owner is the only authority allowed to modify shared upper-half tables. Mutations must be serialized with local interrupts disabled on the current single-vCPU system and invalidate the affected local translation before the mapping change is relied on. A process root may not edit or reclaim shared tables. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::destroy` releases only private user leaves, intermediate tables, and the root; the caller must first switch CR3 to a different live root and invalidate this root's local non-global translations. Keep the shared kernel owner alive. PCID-aware invalidation and SMP shootdown remain unsupported and need a separate design.

The current `CandidatePageTables` deep-clones the inherited hierarchy, tracks all cloned tables as owned, and holds an exclusive mutable borrow of one memory backend; it is not itself the process-address-space abstraction. `SharedKernelHalf` validates and snapshots the sanitized upper root entries while borrowing the kernel owner. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` uses one exclusive backend borrow for multiple private roots, maps allocator-owned user 4 KiB leaves only in inactive lower halves, retains writable/executable permission metadata, validates the initial executable entry and writable NX stack, provides range-preflighted copy-in/copy-out through a separate `UserFrameMemory` backend, and destroys private leaf/table/root frames without freeing shared subtrees. Host tests cover four-/five-level sharing, U/S sanitization, independent mappings, permission checks, cross-page copies, unmap ownership, active-root release rejection, and rollback. The opt-in `probe-user-process` target additionally constructs and activates one root, loads the bundled ELF, serves write/exit calls using token-based copies, and restores CR3 before wait/reap and teardown. The bootstrap static kernel-entry stack and Limine-derived shared kernel subtree are used; this is not a general multi-process or curated kernel-map policy. Keep the kernel owner alive and immutable for the shared view's lifetime; callers must use a distinct page-table backend for process-owned tables.

### Static ELF64 image validation and page initialization (partial)

`src/elf.rs` parses little-endian x86_64 `ET_EXEC` images without allocation. It bounds the program-header count, load-segment count, and total mapped pages; checks file and virtual arithmetic, page alignment and `p_align` congruence, lower-half canonical ranges, non-overlapping page spans, readable segment flags, W^X, and that the entry point lies in a non-writable executable `PT_LOAD`. It rejects dynamic/interpreter and TLS segments and executable-stack requests. This initial format intentionally requires page-aligned load offsets/addresses and supports at most 64 program headers, 16 load segments, and 64 load pages. `populate_segment_page` copies one load page into an allocator-owned frame through `UserFrameMemory`, zero-filling bytes beyond the file payload. `load_into_process_root` allocates, populates, cache-selects, and maps every load page into an inactive process root. The diagnostic build reproducibly compiles `crates/rustix-init` as a static ELF64 payload; `just process-smoke` loads and runs the normal image, and `just user-fault-smoke` builds a `ud2` entry variant and validates process termination/reaping/teardown.

## ABI decisions still pending beyond v1

The initial v1 versioning, error encoding, syscall numbers, register-level request decoding, and assembly-matched syscall context layout are implemented in `src/syscall.rs`. The diagnostic `int 0x80` path sanitizes return frames and serves ABI-version, bounded write, wait-for-exited-child, and exit calls; invalid unmapped write/status buffers return `EFAULT` without corrupting the process or consuming a waitable child. `src/process.rs` provides fixed-capacity identity/exit-state policy, and the diagnostic kernel harness performs a nonblocking kernel-side wait/reap after the user-entry trampoline returns. The userspace `wait` call can reap an already-exited child; it returns `ENOTSUP` for a running child because blocking user-process scheduling is not integrated. Status copyout is frame-token-based and happens before reaping, while child creation, scheduler integration, and descriptor tables are not implemented. User faults are process-terminating only while the opt-in callback is installed; QEMU covers CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE and kernel-fatal coverage for the same four vectors. This does not make arbitrary kernel accesses recoverable. Still to be specified before broader process operations are process-creation/exec and file-action semantics, general descriptor sharing/duplication/inheritance, read/open/close behavior, signal-like asynchronous delivery, clocks, and any additional structure layouts.

## Suggested first user-visible slice

The first controlled `no_std` init process now runs only in the opt-in QEMU probe and exercises ABI-version discovery, write, EFAULT, exit, kernel-side wait/reap, and teardown. The next work is to make process execution reusable, implement a real userspace wait path and child lifecycle, define per-process kernel stacks and scheduler interaction, and expand user-fault/VM tests before considering a normal-boot userspace service. Read/write/open/close and descriptor-lifetime semantics need their own complete implementation and adversarial tests before any Unix-compatibility claim.

# Interrupts and IRQ vector allocation

## Current implementation

`src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` installs the bootstrap GDT, TSS, exception gates for vectors 0–31, device IRQ stubs, and the APIC spurious-vector gate. Kernel-origin exceptions remain fatal. In the opt-in synchronous Ring 3 process probe, noncritical CPL3 exceptions are reported and handed to the installed process callback, which records status `128 + vector`, restores the kernel CR3, and exits through the user-entry trampoline. NMI (#2), double fault (#8), and machine check (#18) remain fatal regardless of saved CPL. QEMU exercises CPL3 #PF, #GP, #UD, and #DE termination in the diagnostic runtime; this is not a general exception or signal mechanism. Maskable interrupts start disabled and are enabled only after the validated APIC route, registered handler, and acknowledgement path are ready.

`src/irq.rs` provides a host-tested, allocation-free token allocator for device vectors `0x20..=0xef` except reserved syscall vector `0x80`; exception vectors and the reserved upper range are also excluded. The IDT overrides `0x80` with a dedicated DPL-3 interrupt gate and assembly stub. The stub rejects CPL0 invocation, saves the full GPR set and x87/SSE state on the TSS entry stack, and dispatches a normalized syscall context with IF clear. In the opt-in process probe, the dispatcher implements ABI-version discovery, bounded write and wait-status copyout through allocator-owned user-frame copies, exit, and scheduler-independent kernel wait/reap after the synchronous entry returns. Userspace `wait` can reap an already-exited child; a running child returns `ENOTSUP` until blocking process scheduling exists. The normal build only exposes ABI-version discovery. `rustix_irq_dispatch` invokes the registered handler, returns for the APIC spurious vector without EOI, and halts on unregistered/unexpected vectors. Device handlers own their EOI. Vector registration is performed with IF clear before the corresponding I/O APIC source is unmasked.

The initial hardware target is single-vCPU QEMU `q35`: validated ACPI/MADT topology, local APIC and I/O APIC, masked legacy PIC routing, MADT-resolved ISA routes, and a periodic 8254 PIT tick near 100 Hz. OVMF smokes validate PIT delivery/EOI, non-yielding timer preemption, x87/SSE state preservation, and UART/keyboard IRQ delivery. Host tests cover vector ownership and PIT/time arithmetic; they do not replace privileged QEMU coverage.

The scheduler is single-vCPU and supports cooperative waits/yields plus PIT-driven timer preemption. The timer handler advances ticks and sends APIC EOI before any scheduling switch. The common IRQ stub saves the interrupted x87/SSE state before Rust dispatch and restores the selected context before `IRETQ`; the context switch keeps aligned per-context FXSAVE areas. IRQ-safe spin locks save and restore the prior IF state, and the global heap uses one; scheduler mutations are separately serialized by masking local interrupts. IRQ/exception handlers remain bounded and allocation-free, and no current IRQ handler acquires the heap lock. SMP, per-CPU state, and physical-hardware validation remain future work.
