- [x86_64 drivers and hardware boundary](architecture/drivers.md)
- [Crabshell and the volatile RAM filesystem](architecture/crabshell.md)
- [Unix-like process and syscall direction](architecture/syscall-abi.md)
- [Build and toolchain guide](development/building.md)
- [Testing and verification](development/testing.md)
- [Security and unsafe-code policy](security.md)
- [Milestones and acceptance criteria](roadmap/README.md)

## Current status

The repository contains a bare-metal `no_std` Rust kernel for `x86_64-unknown-none`. After Limine handoff it validates and copies memory-map metadata into an owned snapshot, captures the executable's physical and virtual bases, complete linker-defined image span, and page-aligned text/rodata/data segment bounds, reports baseline CPUID features, active/maximum address widths, read-only CR0 caching state, gated EFER.NXE/IA32_PAT values, and a bounded MTRR snapshot, seeds a volatile RAM filesystem, and runs Crabshell over the COM1 serial console. Boot-protocol pointers are checked for canonicality using the active 4- or 5-level paging width; physical map bounds and protocol-scoped HHDM range arithmetic are also validated. Crabshell's allocation-free parser is a separate crate; the kernel handles command execution. On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 both in the working tree and from a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory; the clean run downloaded and built the pinned Limine host utility, created the image, and passed the bounded QEMU boot to the shell prompt. The serial log showed memory-map and CPU reporting. GitHub Actions run [#5](https://github.com/JustEthanCodes/rustix/actions/runs/42288095710) passed `just verify` on the published `dev` commit on 2026-11-06; it does not cover later uncommitted changes. A separate interactive QEMU session exercised `help`, `ls`, `meminfo`, directory navigation, and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove commands. Milestone 0's local exit criteria are met, and Milestone 1's validation criteria are met for the current Limine path. This is a kernel-mode shell, not a user process. An opt-in diagnostic QEMU path runs the bundled init in Ring 3 and validates ABI version/write/EFAULT, wait-status copyout and retry against a kernel-seeded exited-child fixture, exit, kernel wait/reap, process-root teardown, and CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE exits; blocking userspace wait, child scheduling, and normal-boot userspace remain unsupported, so Milestone 4 is in progress. A bounded physical-frame allocator is initialized from the validated map and reported by `meminfo`; token ownership and failed-deallocation semantics are documented and host-tested. The boot transition owns an activated clone of Limine's reachable page-table hierarchy, and the global heap begins with a 256 KiB BSS arena and 128 allocation records, with bounded frame-backed growth up to 1 MiB. The Limine base-revision 3 HHDM scope and a conservative initial mapping/alias/cache policy are documented. Pure host-tested helpers validate mapping ranges/PTE bits, parse PAT layouts, validate captured MTRR snapshots, combine PAT/MTRR types under normal caching according to Intel SDM Table 11-7, and select a PAT index only when it yields one effective type across an aligned physical range. Boot validates the captured state and prints a diagnostic effective type at PA 0. The transition preserves inherited cache attributes, adjusts kernel-image HHDM aliases to R/NX or RW/NX, and checks the effective PAT index against the inherited mapping. `BootInfo` records raw CR3 and a validated decode of its root physical address and low-bit interpretation. Checked HHDM access is limited to complete allocator-owned usable frames and cloned table frames; the active root owns its cloned table pages while inherited leaf frames remain loader-owned. The complete linker-defined kernel-image span and requested 256 KiB initial boot-stack span are captured and validated; Limine does not report any larger allocation bounds or guard status, so Rustix does not infer a guard page. The heap has bounded frame-backed growth and an IRQ-save lock; allocation remains prohibited in IRQ/exception context. ACPI support includes bounded host-tested RSDP/SDT/RSDT/XSDT/MADT parsing and a read-only/NX boot reader that copies validated MADT data into owned state. Rustix has a tested single-vCPU APIC/PIT IRQ path, cooperative and timer-preemptive scheduling, IRQ-save locks, guarded kernel threads, bounded frame-backed heap growth, and interrupt-driven UART/PS/2 queues with a polling fallback. SMP, general-purpose process scheduling, a persistent filesystem, and Unix compatibility remain absent. The documented syscall ABI and process-root primitives are exercised only by an opt-in diagnostic process. Kernel-origin exceptions remain fatal; the opt-in user path terminates CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE and `just fault-smoke` separately verifies those four exceptions halt at CPL0. This is not a general recovery policy or physical-hardware validation. On 2026-10-21, `just verify` passed after adding CR3 decoding and the pure MTRR resolver, including host tests, target check, release build, ISO creation, and QEMU prompt smoke. On 2026-10-22, `just verify` passed after adding bounded read-only MTRR register capture and validated PAT/MTRR policy resolution. On 2026-10-24, the final `just verify`, `just frame-smoke`, and `just fault-smoke` runs passed after review. QEMU verified the 256 KiB stack request, cloned-root CR3 transition, kernel HHDM alias hardening, heap alignment/reuse/exhaustion probe, and shell prompt; the current emulator reports CR4.PGE clear, so it exercised CR3 invalidation with PGE disabled, while the PGE-toggle path was statically reviewed but not exercised. Milestone 2's local exit criteria are met. Hosted CI passed on the published `dev` commit, but it does not cover today's uncommitted work or establish physical-hardware behavior, a clean-room mapping policy, or exhaustive alias coverage. On 2026-11-07, `just verify` passed with 127 host tests and BIOS/OVMF QEMU coverage for APIC/PIT delivery, active mapping/TLB invalidation, cooperative scheduling, and UART/PS/2 input wakeups. On 2026-11-13, `just verify` passed with 130 host tests and extended OVMF coverage for IRQ-save lock IF restoration, non-yielding timer preemption, x87/SSE context preservation, and input wakeups. Milestone 3's single-vCPU exit criteria are met. Milestone 4 is in progress: the process/EFAULT/ready-child-wait/teardown and CPL3/CPL0 exception-matrix smokes pass locally, while blocking userspace `wait`, general process scheduling, per-process kernel stacks, virtual memory, and a reusable userspace runtime remain pending. SMP and physical-hardware validation remain pending.

## Documentation conventions

- **Implemented** means present in the repository and checked by current code or tests.
- **Planned** means an architectural direction, not a stable ABI or delivered capability.
- Any future ABI proposal must state versioning, error behavior, memory ownership, and compatibility expectations before it is treated as stable.

    16	## Initial syscall ABI v1 contract (specified; register decoding implemented)
    17	
    18	ABI version `1.0` is identified by `abi_version()`, syscall number `0`, returning `0x0001_0000` in `RAX`. In v1, `RAX` returns a signed 64-bit result: nonnegative values are success (including byte counts and PIDs); errors are negative stable error numbers. ABI versioning is append-only: existing syscall numbers, argument meanings, layouts, and error values never change or get reused. There is no POSIX compatibility claim. `src/syscall.rs` implements the stable number/error constants, host-tested request decoding and write service, and the assembly-matched syscall context layout. `interrupts.rs` installs the DPL-3 gate and dedicated entry stub. The opt-in diagnostic process runtime dispatches ABI-version, bounded write, exit, and wait for already-exited children; a wait on a running child returns `ENOTSUP` because blocking user-process scheduling is not integrated. The QEMU init uses a kernel-seeded exited-child fixture to test wait status copyout and verifies an invalid status pointer returns `EFAULT` without reaping the child. This fixture tests syscall copyout/reap mechanics, not concurrent child execution or scheduler integration. A separate kernel-side test harness waits for the synchronous process after its exit trampoline returns.
    19	
    20	| Number | Call | Register arguments | Result / behavior |
    21	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
    22	| 0 | `abi_version` | none | `0x0001_0000` (major 1, minor 0). |
    23	| 1 | `exit` | `RDI`: signed 32-bit status in the low 32 bits (upper bits ignored) | Does not return; status is retained exactly by the parent wait record. |
    24	| 2 | `write` | `RDI`: fd, `RSI`: user buffer, `RDX`: byte length | Returns bytes accepted; a short positive result is valid. Initial descriptors 1 and 2 are stdout/stderr console streams; other descriptors return `-EBADF`. Maximum request is 4096 bytes; zero length returns 0 without validating the pointer. |
    25	| 3 | `wait` | `RDI`: child PID (0 means any child), `RSI`: optional user pointer to signed 32-bit exit status | ABI contract: blocks until a matching child exits and returns its PID. A non-null status output must be writable before the child is reaped; no matching child returns `-ECHILD`. Current diagnostic support is nonblocking: it reaps an already-exited child, returns `-ENOTSUP` for a running child, and returns `-EFAULT` without reaping if status copyout fails. |
    26	
    27	All other numbers are unassigned and return `-ENOSYS`; assigning a number later is an additive extension, never a reinterpretation. Descriptor 0 is reserved for input but v1 has no `read`, `open`, `close`, or `dup` call. Standard descriptors exist for the process lifetime; inheritance and general file-object semantics are not yet exposed. The initial process is created by the kernel loader, not a syscall.
    28	
    29	Stable v1 error numbers (returned negated in `RAX`) are: `1 EINVAL`, `2 EBADF`, `3 EFAULT`, `4 ENOMEM`, `5 ECHILD`, `6 EINTR`, `7 EIO`, `8 ENOSYS`, `9 E2BIG`, `10 EOVERFLOW`, and `11 ENOTSUP`. Unknown syscall numbers return `-ENOSYS`. Pointer-plus-length ranges use checked arithmetic and must lie wholly in a mapped lower-half user range. `write` preflights the whole input range before output; a later endpoint failure may return a short count, and an error before progress returns `-EIO`. A copy fault after progress returns the completed prefix. An unmapped diagnostic `write` buffer returns `-EFAULT` before the syscall returns to userspace. For `wait`, the optional status is copied before the matching exited child is reaped; failed copyout returns `-EFAULT` and leaves the child waitable. The current diagnostic dispatcher implements that ready-child case only and returns `-ENOTSUP` for a running child; blocking and interruption behavior remain future work. V1 has no signals, asynchronous interruption, or automatic syscall restart.
    30	
    31	All ABI integers are fixed-width little-endian x86_64 values. The wait status is one signed 32-bit integer with no implicit padding or extra fields. No other user-visible structs exist in v1.

# Unix-like process and syscall direction

**Status: Milestone 4 is in progress. The opt-in single-vCPU QEMU diagnostic path creates a lower-half process root sharing the validated supervisor kernel half, loads and runs a bundled static ELF in Ring 3, serves ABI-version/write/ready-child-wait/exit syscalls, terminates CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE with status `128 + vector`, and restores/reaps the root. The normal kernel does not launch userspace. The diagnostic `wait` path reaps already-exited children and preserves a zombie when status copyout fails; blocking for a running child, general process scheduling/kernel stacks, virtual-memory allocation, and a userspace runtime remain unimplemented.**

Rustix aims to expose a small, versioned syscall surface that can support Unix-like processes and tools. The kernel must own this interface rather than inherit an ABI accidentally from a bootloader or emulator.

## Proposed compatibility principles

- Processes have independent virtual address spaces and explicit lifecycle states.
- File descriptors are per-process integer handles to kernel-managed objects; descriptor inheritance, close-on-exec, duplication, and sharing semantics must be specified together.
- Syscalls use one documented error convention and stable numeric identifiers. New operations must not silently repurpose old numbers.
- Arguments crossing privilege boundaries are copied or validated using narrowly scoped helpers. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::copy_from_user` and `copy_to_user` preflight the complete lower-half mapped range, check writable metadata for kernel-to-user copies, and operate only on owned frame tokens through `UserFrameMemory`; they never form a Rust reference from a user virtual address. Backend copy faults report the completed prefix. The diagnostic user-exception path terminates a process on supported CPL3 faults; it does not make arbitrary kernel memory accesses recoverable.
- Blocking, interruption, cancellation, and restart behavior are explicit for each syscall class.
- A compatibility layer (for example, POSIX-shaped libc behavior) remains separate from internal kernel APIs.

## Initial syscall ABI v1 contract (specified; register decoding implemented)

ABI version `1.0` is identified by `abi_version()`, syscall number `0`, returning `0x0001_0000` in `RAX`. In v1, `RAX` returns a signed 64-bit result: nonnegative values are success (including byte counts and PIDs); errors are negative stable error numbers. ABI versioning is append-only: existing syscall numbers, argument meanings, layouts, and error values never change or get reused. There is no POSIX compatibility claim. `src/syscall.rs` implements the stable number/error constants, host-tested request decoding and write service, and the assembly-matched syscall context layout. `interrupts.rs` installs the DPL-3 gate and dedicated entry stub. The opt-in diagnostic process runtime dispatches ABI-version, bounded write, exit, and wait for already-exited children; a wait on a running child returns `ENOTSUP` because blocking user-process scheduling is not integrated. The QEMU init uses a kernel-seeded exited-child fixture to test wait status copyout and verifies an invalid status pointer returns `EFAULT` without reaping the child. This fixture tests syscall copyout/reap mechanics, not concurrent child execution or scheduler integration. A separate kernel-side test harness waits for the synchronous process after its exit trampoline returns.

| Number | Call | Register arguments | Result / behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `abi_version` | none | `0x0001_0000` (major 1, minor 0). |
| 1 | `exit` | `RDI`: signed 32-bit status in the low 32 bits (upper bits ignored) | Does not return; status is retained exactly by the parent wait record. |
| 2 | `write` | `RDI`: fd, `RSI`: user buffer, `RDX`: byte length | Returns bytes accepted; a short positive result is valid. Initial descriptors 1 and 2 are stdout/stderr console streams; other descriptors return `-EBADF`. Maximum request is 4096 bytes; zero length returns 0 without validating the pointer. |
| 3 | `wait` | `RDI`: child PID (0 means any child), `RSI`: optional user pointer to signed 32-bit exit status | ABI contract: blocks until a matching child exits and returns its PID. A non-null status output must be writable before the child is reaped; no matching child returns `-ECHILD`. Current diagnostic support is nonblocking: it reaps an already-exited child, returns `-ENOTSUP` for a running child, and returns `-EFAULT` without reaping if status copyout fails. |

All other numbers are unassigned and return `-ENOSYS`; assigning a number later is an additive extension, never a reinterpretation. Descriptor 0 is reserved for input but v1 has no `read`, `open`, `close`, or `dup` call. Standard descriptors exist for the process lifetime; inheritance and general file-object semantics are not yet exposed. The initial process is created by the kernel loader, not a syscall.

Stable v1 error numbers (returned negated in `RAX`) are: `1 EINVAL`, `2 EBADF`, `3 EFAULT`, `4 ENOMEM`, `5 ECHILD`, `6 EINTR`, `7 EIO`, `8 ENOSYS`, `9 E2BIG`, `10 EOVERFLOW`, and `11 ENOTSUP`. Unknown syscall numbers return `-ENOSYS`. Pointer-plus-length ranges use checked arithmetic and must lie wholly in a mapped lower-half user range. `write` preflights the whole input range before output; a later endpoint failure may return a short count, and an error before progress returns `-EIO`. A copy fault after progress returns the completed prefix. An unmapped diagnostic `write` buffer returns `-EFAULT` before the syscall returns to userspace. For `wait`, the optional status is copied before the matching exited child is reaped; failed copyout returns `-EFAULT` and leaves the child waitable. The current diagnostic dispatcher implements that ready-child case only and returns `-ENOTSUP` for a running child; blocking and interruption behavior remain future work. V1 has no signals, asynchronous interruption, or automatic syscall restart.

All ABI integers are fixed-width little-endian x86_64 values. The wait status is one signed 32-bit integer with no implicit padding or extra fields. No other user-visible structs exist in v1.

## Initial x86_64 entry design (Milestone 4; diagnostic path integrated)

The opt-in single-vCPU process probe enters Ring 3 with a validated five-word `IRETQ` frame and enters the kernel with `int $0x80` through a dedicated DPL-3 IDT gate. This intentionally avoids `SYSCALL`/`SYSRET`, `STAR`/`LSTAR`/`FMASK`, and `SWAPGS` state transitions in this first slice. The register and error contract below is the versioned v1 ABI, but the runtime and syscall surface are not general-purpose or enabled in the default boot path.

- **Vector ownership:** `0x80` lies inside the device-vector range (`0x20..=0xef`) and is reserved by `InterruptVectorAllocator`; generic IRQ allocation/release cannot claim it. The IDT installs a dedicated DPL-3 interrupt gate rather than the generic device-IRQ stub. Its assembly entry rejects CPL0 invocation, saves all GPRs and x87/SSE state, clears the direction flag, and calls a normalized Rust dispatcher with IF clear. The opt-in process probe implements ABI-version discovery, write, exit, and wait for an already-exited child; it does not block or create children.
- **Selectors:** the current GDT uses `0x08` for kernel code, `0x10` for kernel data, and `0x18` for the two-slot TSS descriptor. Ring-3 data and 64-bit code descriptors are appended at GDT indexes 5 and 6, with compile-time selector assertions for user data `0x2b` and user code `0x33` (RPL 3); the process probe uses these selectors in its validated entry frame.
- **Privilege stack:** a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt uses `TSS.RSP0`. The current synchronous QEMU probe uses the bootstrap static ring-0 stack, mapped in both the kernel and process roots; it does not allocate per-process kernel stacks or schedule among user processes. `interrupts::set_kernel_entry_stack` validates canonical upper-half address shape and alignment before updating `RSP0`, but no general process scheduler calls it. Callers must disable local interrupts and guarantee the stack is mapped writable in every address space that can run until the next update. A future SMP design needs per-CPU TSS and entry-stack state.
- **Entry frame and state:** the dedicated assembly stub saves all GPRs in the `SyscallContext` layout, passes the five-word privilege frame separately from the exception frame, and saves/restores x87/SSE state around the Rust dispatcher; AVX remains disabled under the current CPU-state policy. Kernel code runs with the direction flag clear. The process probe validates saved RIP/RSP against the active process mappings and accesses user buffers only through owned frame tokens. It does not block or schedule in a syscall.
- **Initial register convention:** `RAX` carries the syscall number; arguments use `RDI`, `RSI`, `RDX`, `R10`, `R8`, and `R9`; `RAX` carries the result. This convention and its initial numbers/errors are versioned as ABI v1. Implemented operations remain a subset of the documented contract.
- **Return validation:** use `IRETQ`, not `SYSRET`. Initial entry uses a host-tested frame sanitizer that requires exact ring-3 selectors, a canonical lower-half instruction pointer, a lower-half stack range, 16-byte initial stack alignment, and safe flags. Syscall resume uses a separate sanitizer that keeps exact selectors, canonical lower-half address shape, and privileged-flag checks but does not impose 16-byte alignment on an in-function RSP; it replaces user flags with `0x2` (IF remains clear). Once a process is active, the dispatcher also validates the saved instruction pointer against an executable mapping and the saved stack pointer against a writable NX mapping. A malformed frame is converted into process exit rather than returned to CPL3.
- **NMI and interrupt policy:** no GS-base swap is needed on this entry path. NMI, double fault, and machine check remain fatal even when their saved CS indicates CPL3. Other user-origin exceptions terminate the process with status `128 + vector` in the diagnostic runtime; QEMU exercises CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE. Kernel-origin #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE are separately tested as fatal. Ordinary maskable IRQs stay disabled throughout the synchronous process run.

This path depends on each process root sharing supervisor-only upper-half mappings that cover syscall/exception code, the IDT, GDT, TSS, and active kernel stack. The bundled process root and syscall/exception transitions are exercised by opt-in QEMU smokes, but the shared Limine-derived kernel mapping is not a curated kernel map or a general isolation policy. Do not enable normal boot-time Ring 3 execution until process scheduling, per-process kernel stacks, blocking wait semantics, and the remaining Milestone 4 fault/teardown criteria are implemented and validated.

### Process address spaces (design; root construction partially implemented)

Use a separate four- or five-level root per process. The initial source is the retained active clone of Limine's hierarchy, not a curated clean-room root. Each process root owns its root page, all lower-half intermediate tables, and every user leaf frame. Keep the kernel-root owner alive for the lifetime of every process root. Copy only upper-half top-level entries from that owner into each process root; these entries are non-owning references to shared kernel subtrees, not deep copies, and must never be released by a process teardown. Do not copy lower-half entries from the kernel root.

Before publishing a shared kernel subtree, validate its page-table structure and physical bounds and reject any effectively user-accessible leaf. U/S permission is the conjunction of every entry on a path, so a U/S bit on one non-leaf alone does not grant user access. When copying upper-half root entries, clear their U/S bit as defense in depth; a user leaf then cannot become accessible if a lower entry changes. `paging::validate_supervisor_kernel_half` implements the bounded, read-only structural/effective-permission preflight, but it does not install roots or prove physical backing is readable; the supplied reader must provide that access guarantee. Sharing the active clone means every accepted upper-half supervisor mapping and alias is present in every process CR3. This is not a curated kernel map or kernel-page-table isolation, and it provides no transient-execution protection. User mappings remain private to one process, are confined to the lower canonical half, preserve W^X, and are non-global in the first implementation.

The kernel address-space owner is the only authority allowed to modify shared upper-half tables. Mutations must be serialized with local interrupts disabled on the current single-vCPU system and invalidate the affected local translation before the mapping change is relied on. A process root may not edit or reclaim shared tables. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::destroy` releases only private user leaves, intermediate tables, and the root; the caller must first switch CR3 to a different live root and invalidate this root's local non-global translations. Keep the shared kernel owner alive. PCID-aware invalidation and SMP shootdown remain unsupported and need a separate design.

The current `CandidatePageTables` deep-clones the inherited hierarchy, tracks all cloned tables as owned, and holds an exclusive mutable borrow of one memory backend; it is not itself the process-address-space abstraction. `SharedKernelHalf` validates and snapshots the sanitized upper root entries while borrowing the kernel owner. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` uses one exclusive backend borrow for multiple private roots, maps allocator-owned user 4 KiB leaves only in inactive lower halves, retains writable/executable permission metadata, validates the initial executable entry and writable NX stack, provides range-preflighted copy-in/copy-out through a separate `UserFrameMemory` backend, and destroys private leaf/table/root frames without freeing shared subtrees. Host tests cover four-/five-level sharing, U/S sanitization, independent mappings, permission checks, cross-page copies, unmap ownership, active-root release rejection, and rollback. The opt-in `probe-user-process` target additionally constructs and activates one root, loads the bundled ELF, serves write and ready-child wait-status copyout/exit calls using token-based copies, and restores CR3 before kernel wait/reap and teardown. The bootstrap static kernel-entry stack and Limine-derived shared kernel subtree are used; this is not a general multi-process or curated kernel-map policy. Keep the kernel owner alive and immutable for the shared view's lifetime; callers must use a distinct page-table backend for process-owned tables.

### Static ELF64 image validation and page initialization (partial)

`src/elf.rs` parses little-endian x86_64 `ET_EXEC` images without allocation. It bounds the program-header count, load-segment count, and total mapped pages; checks file and virtual arithmetic, page alignment and `p_align` congruence, lower-half canonical ranges, non-overlapping page spans, readable segment flags, W^X, and that the entry point lies in a non-writable executable `PT_LOAD`. It rejects dynamic/interpreter and TLS segments and executable-stack requests. This initial format intentionally requires page-aligned load offsets/addresses and supports at most 64 program headers, 16 load segments, and 64 load pages. `populate_segment_page` copies one load page into an allocator-owned frame through `UserFrameMemory`, zero-filling bytes beyond the file payload. `load_into_process_root` allocates, populates, cache-selects, and maps every load page into an inactive process root. The diagnostic build reproducibly compiles `crates/rustix-init` as a static ELF64 payload; `just process-smoke` loads and runs the normal image, and `just user-fault-smoke` builds a `ud2` entry variant and validates process termination/reaping/teardown.

## ABI decisions still pending beyond v1

The initial v1 versioning, error encoding, syscall numbers, register-level request decoding, and assembly-matched syscall context layout are implemented in `src/syscall.rs`. The diagnostic `int 0x80` path sanitizes return frames and serves ABI-version, bounded write, wait-for-exited-child, and exit calls; invalid unmapped write/status buffers return `EFAULT` without corrupting the process or consuming a waitable child. `src/process.rs` provides fixed-capacity identity/exit-state policy, and the diagnostic kernel harness performs a nonblocking kernel-side wait/reap after the user-entry trampoline returns. The userspace `wait` call can reap an already-exited child; it returns `ENOTSUP` for a running child because blocking user-process scheduling is not integrated. Status copyout is frame-token-based and happens before reaping, while child creation, scheduler integration, and descriptor tables are not implemented. User faults are process-terminating only while the opt-in callback is installed; QEMU covers CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE and kernel-fatal coverage for the same four vectors. This does not make arbitrary kernel accesses recoverable. Still to be specified before broader process operations are process-creation/exec and file-action semantics, general descriptor sharing/duplication/inheritance, read/open/close behavior, signal-like asynchronous delivery, clocks, and any additional structure layouts.

## Suggested first user-visible slice

The first controlled `no_std` init process now runs only in the opt-in QEMU probe and exercises ABI-version discovery, write, EFAULT, ready-child wait/status-copyout, exit, kernel-side wait/reap, and teardown. Its wait fixture is kernel-seeded; it does not establish child execution or scheduling. The next work is to make process execution reusable, implement blocking userspace wait and a real child lifecycle, define per-process kernel stacks and scheduler interaction, and expand user-fault/VM tests before considering a normal-boot userspace service. Read/write/open/close and descriptor-lifetime semantics need their own complete implementation and adversarial tests before any Unix-compatibility claim.

    pub fn peek_wait(
        &self,
        parent: ProcessId,
        child_pid: u64,
    ) -> Result<WaitResult, ProcessTableError> {
        if parent != KERNEL_PROCESS_ID {
            let parent_record = self
                .record(parent)
                .ok_or(ProcessTableError::InvalidParent)?;
            if parent_record.state != ProcessState::Running {
                return Err(ProcessTableError::ParentExited);
            }
        }

        let mut found_child = false;
        let mut running: Option<ProcessId> = None;
        let mut exited: Option<(ProcessId, i32)> = None;
        for record in self.records.iter().flatten().filter(|record| {
            record.parent == parent && (child_pid == 0 || record.pid.get() == child_pid)
        }) {
            found_child = true;
            match record.state {
                ProcessState::Running => {
                    if running.is_none_or(|pid| record.pid < pid) {
                        running = Some(record.pid);
                    }
                }
                ProcessState::Exited(status) => {
                    if exited.is_none_or(|(pid, _)| record.pid < pid) {
                        exited = Some((record.pid, status));
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        if let Some((pid, status)) = exited {
            return Ok(WaitResult::Exited { pid, status });
        }
        if let Some(pid) = running {
            return Ok(WaitResult::Running { pid });
        }
        if found_child {
            unreachable!("a matching child must be running or exited");
        }
        Err(ProcessTableError::NoChild)
    }

struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

// SAFETY: `prepare_table` accepts only an allocator-issued frame and validates
// its complete usable span and HHDM address. Handles are only used while the
// candidate retains the frame token and this unique backend borrow.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory for LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_> {
    type PreparedTable = u64;
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn prepare_table(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
    ) -> Result<Self::PreparedTable, Self::Error> {
        frame.hhdm_address(
            self.memory_map,
            self.hhdm_offset,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    unsafe fn read_entry(
        &self,
        table: Self::PreparedTable,
        index: u16,
    ) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let entry_address = table
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The unsafe trait contract requires `table` to be the prepared
        // HHDM address of a complete writable frame; the index is in [0, 512).
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }

    unsafe fn clear_table(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable) {
        let entries = table as *mut u64;
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a handle prepared by this backend for a
        // complete writable frame retained by its candidate.
        unsafe {
            for index in 0..512 {
                entries.add(index).write_volatile(0);
            }
        }
    }

    unsafe fn write_entry(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable, index: u16, value: u64) {
        if index >= 512 {
            return;
        }
        let entry = (table as *mut u64).wrapping_add(usize::from(index));
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a prepared complete frame and an index in
        // range; this writes one entry without creating a Rust reference.
        unsafe { entry.write_volatile(value) };
    }

    unsafe fn invalidate_page(&mut self, virtual_address: u64) {
        // SAFETY: Active mapping callers provide the current virtual page and run
        // at CPL 0 with exclusive local page-table ownership.
        unsafe {
            core::arch::asm!(
                "invlpg [{}]",
                in(reg) virtual_address,
                options(nostack, preserves_flags)
            );
        }
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
impl LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'_> {
    fn frame_slice_address(
        &self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        length: usize,
    ) -> Result<*mut u8, LimineUserFrameMemoryError> {
        if offset
            .checked_add(length)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE as usize)
        {
            return Err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::OutOfBounds);
        }
        if length == 0 {
            return Ok(core::ptr::null_mut());
        }

        let base = frame
            .hhdm_address(
                self.memory_map,
                self.hhdm_offset,
                self.physical_address_bits,
                self.virtual_address_bits,
            )
            .map_err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address)?;
        let address =
            base.checked_add(offset as u64)
                .ok_or(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address(
                    rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow,
                ))?;
        Ok(address as *mut u8)
    }
}

// SAFETY: The non-copyable Frame token and checked HHDM conversion authorize a

// faults from a broken mapping remain fatal and are not recoverable here.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::UserFrameMemory for LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'_> {
    type Error = LimineUserFrameMemoryError;

    fn copy_from_frame(

        offset: usize,

            unsafe { core::ptr::copy(source, destination.as_mut_ptr(), destination.len()) };

    }

    fn copy_to_frame(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,

        let destination = self.frame_slice_address(frame, offset, source.len())?;
        if !source.is_empty() {
            // SAFETY: The frame subrange was checked and the HHDM address was
            // validated for the full allocator-owned frame. `copy` permits overlap.
            unsafe { core::ptr::copy(source.as_ptr(), destination, source.len()) };
        }
        Ok(())
    }

            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        for (mapped, page) in (first_page..first_page + page_count).enumerate() {
            let virtual_address = KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE
                .checked_add((page as u64).checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE)?)?;
            let frame = match allocator.allocate() {
                Some(frame) => frame,
                None => {
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
                virtual_address,
                frame.address(),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                Some(physical_width),
                cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
            ) {
                Ok(mapping) => mapping,
                Err(_) => {
                    deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            let attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
                CachePolicy::WriteBack,
                pat,
                &mtrrs,
                cpu_info.normal_caching,
            ) {
                Ok(attributes) if attributes.effective_type() == EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack => {
                    attributes
                }
                _ => {
                    deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            // SAFETY: IF is clear, the current candidate owns the active root,
            // and the allocator-issued frame is mapped RW/NX with local TLB
            // invalidation before its token becomes page-table-owned.
            if let Err(failure) =
                unsafe { candidate.map_owned_page_active(allocator, frame, mapping, attributes) }
            {
                deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, failure.frame);
                rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                return None;
            }
        }
        Some(())
    })()
    .is_some();
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        // SAFETY: The mapping transaction is complete or fully rolled back.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("sti") };
    }
    result
}

fn rollback_kernel_heap_pages(
    candidate: &mut rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<
        'static,
        LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'static>,
    >,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    first_page: usize,
    mapped_pages: usize,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;

    for page in (first_page..first_page + mapped_pages).rev() {
        let Some(virtual_address) = (page as u64)
            .checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE)
            .and_then(|offset| KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE.checked_add(offset))
        else {
            halt_forever();
        };
        // SAFETY: The pages belong to this transaction in the current active
        // root; unmapping invalidates their TLB entries before token return.
        let frame = unsafe { candidate.unmap_owned_page_active(virtual_address) }
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_forever());
        deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
    }
}

fn deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if allocator.deallocate(frame).is_err() {
        halt_forever();
    }
}

// Error payloads provide boot diagnostics through the derived `Debug` output.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[derive(Debug)]
enum AcpiMappingError {
    InvalidAcpiSpan {
        physical_start: u64,
        length: usize,
        error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError,
    },
    InvalidMapping(rustix_kernel::paging::MappingError),
    CandidateMap(
        rustix_kernel::paging::CandidateMapErrorKind<rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError>,
    ),
    CandidateWalk,
    UnexpectedCurrentCr3,
}

struct CandidateAcpiReader<'candidate, 'memory, 'map> {
    candidate: &'candidate mut rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<
        'memory,
        LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'map>,
    >,
    allocator: &'candidate mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &'map rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    cache_layout: rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    normal_caching: bool,
    candidate_cr3: u64,
    previous_cr3: u64,
    virtual_address: u64,
}

impl CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    fn remove_temporary_mapping(&mut self) {
        if let Err(error) = self.candidate.unmap_acpi_page(self.virtual_address) {
            crate::kprintln!("temporary ACPI mapping could not be removed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    }
}

// The legacy-reserved authorization is accepted only for RSDP reads; all
// root and child tables require ACPI-reclaimable/NVS memory-map coverage.
impl CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    fn read_mapped(
        &mut self,
        physical_start: u64,
        output: &mut [u8],
        allow_legacy_rsdp: bool,
    ) -> Result<(), AcpiMappingError> {
        use rustix_kernel::paging::{
            validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
        };

        if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
            return Err(AcpiMappingError::UnexpectedCurrentCr3);
        }
        if output.is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let length =
            u64::try_from(output.len()).map_err(|_| AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
                physical_start,
                length: output.len(),
                error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow,
            })?;
        let span = if allow_legacy_rsdp {
            self.memory_map.validate_rsdp_span(
                physical_start,
                length,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            )
        } else {
            self.memory_map.validate_acpi_span(
                physical_start,
                length,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            )
        }
        .map_err(|error| AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
            physical_start,
            length: output.len(),
            error,
        })?;
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: false,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        let mut copied = 0usize;
        while copied < output.len() {
            let current_physical = physical_start.checked_add(copied as u64).ok_or(
                AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
                    physical_start,
                    length: output.len(),
                    error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow,
                },
            )?;
            let physical_page = current_physical & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
            let page_offset = current_physical - physical_page;
            let page_length = (PAGE_SIZE - page_offset).min((output.len() - copied) as u64);
            let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
                self.virtual_address,
                physical_page,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
                self.virtual_address_bits,
            )
            .map_err(AcpiMappingError::InvalidMapping)?;
            let cache_attributes = mapping
                .select_cache_attributes(
                    CachePolicy::Uncacheable,
                    self.pat,
                    &self.cache_layout,
                    self.normal_caching,
                )
                .map_err(AcpiMappingError::InvalidMapping)?;
            self.candidate
                .map_acpi_page(self.allocator, span, mapping, cache_attributes)
                .map_err(|failure| AcpiMappingError::CandidateMap(failure.cause))?;

            let candidate_mapping_is_valid = matches!(
                self.candidate.walk(self.virtual_address),
                Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
                    if translation.physical_address == physical_page
                        && translation.permissions == permissions
            );
            if !candidate_mapping_is_valid {
                self.remove_temporary_mapping();
                return Err(AcpiMappingError::CandidateWalk);
            }
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                halt_forever();
            }

            // SAFETY: The candidate is a complete clone of the current inherited
            // hierarchy with all critical paths verified; this temporary page is
            // supervisor R/NX and the candidate remains owned by this stack.
            unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.candidate_cr3) };
            // SAFETY: The CR3 write above installed the candidate root and maskable
            // interrupts remain disabled during this single-core bootstrap read.
            unsafe { self.candidate.mark_active() };
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.candidate_cr3 {
                // SAFETY: Restoring the previous validated root preserves all code,
                // stack, data, and exception mappings needed by this path.
                unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.previous_cr3) };
                if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                    halt_forever();
                }
                // SAFETY: The verified CR3 is no longer the candidate root.
                unsafe { self.candidate.mark_inactive() };
                self.remove_temporary_mapping();
                return Err(AcpiMappingError::UnexpectedCurrentCr3);
            }

            let source = (self.virtual_address + page_offset) as *const u8;
            for offset in 0..page_length as usize {
                // SAFETY: The exact physical page is temporarily mapped R/NX in
                // the active candidate and this byte lies within its 4 KiB leaf.
                output[copied + offset] = unsafe { source.add(offset).read_volatile() };
            }

            // SAFETY: The prior root remains allocated and its critical mappings
            // were verified before this temporary switch.
            unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.previous_cr3) };
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                halt_forever();
            }
            // SAFETY: The previous root was restored and verified above.
            unsafe { self.candidate.mark_inactive() };
            self.remove_temporary_mapping();
            copied += page_length as usize;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

// SAFETY: `read_mapped` authorizes ordinary table reads only through validated
// ACPI map regions; its separate RSDP entry point permits only the bounded legacy
// reserved window recognized by `MemoryMap::validate_rsdp_span`.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::acpi::AcpiPhysicalReader for CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    type Error = AcpiMappingError;

    fn read(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        self.read_mapped(physical_start, output, false)
    }

    fn read_rsdp(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        self.read_mapped(physical_start, output, true)
    }
}

// Capture Limine's entry RSP before a Rust prologue changes it. The synthetic
// return slot is part of the SysV entry stack; realign before calling Rust.
core::arch::global_asm!(
    ".section .text",
    ".code64",
    ".global _start",
    ".type _start, @function",
    "_start:",
    "mov rdi, rsp",
    "and rsp, -16",
    "call rustix_start",
    "ud2",
    ".size _start, . - _start",
);

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_start(entry_rsp: u64) -> ! {
    // Keep interrupts masked until FPU state and the IRQ save destination are ready.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    if let Err(error) = arch::x86_64::cpu::initialize_fpu_state() {
        kprintln!("required x87/SSE state unavailable: {:?}", error);
        halt_forever();
    }
    kernel_threads::initialize_fpu_context();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    kprintln!("x87/SSE context state enabled with FXSAVE/FXRSTOR; AVX disabled");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    let mut boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information(entry_rsp) {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if let Err(error) = arch::x86_64::interrupts::configure_user_address_width(
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        kprintln!("user syscall address-width setup failed: {:?}", error);
        halt_forever();
    }
    #[cfg(target_os = "none")]
    let init_image = match rustix_kernel::elf::Elf64Image::parse(
        INIT_ELF_IMAGE,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(image) => image,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("bundled init ELF rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    #[cfg(target_os = "none")]
    kprintln!(
        "bundled init ELF validated: entry={:#x}, load pages={}",
        init_image.entry_point(),
        init_image.load_page_count()
    );
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
    probe_hhdm_frame(&mut boot_info);

    #[cfg(any(
        feature = "inject-page-fault",
        feature = "inject-invalid-opcode",
        feature = "inject-general-protection",
        feature = "inject-divide-error"
    ))]
    run_fault_injection();

    activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(&mut boot_info)
}

fn activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) -> ! {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        encode_cr3_value, CandidatePageTables, PageWalkConfig, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let inherited_root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: inherited CR3: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: NXE is not enabled");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let config = PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "page-table transition failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    if let Err(error) =
        candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &reader, inherited_root)
    {
        kprintln!(
            "page-table transition failed to clone inherited root: {:?}",
            error
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    let spans = [
        (
            "kernel text",
            segments.text.virtual_start,
            segments.text.physical_start,
            segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel rodata",
            segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            segments.rodata.physical_start,
            segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel data",
            segments.data.virtual_start,
            segments.data.physical_start,
            segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "active boot stack",
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        ),
    ];
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            &reader,
            inherited_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: {} was not preserved",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    }
    if !harden_kernel_hhdm_aliases(
        &mut candidate,
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        KernelAliasHardeningContext {
            memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
            hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            physical_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
            virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
            segments: boot_info.kernel_image_segments,
            reader: &reader,
            inherited_root,
            config,
        },
    ) {
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    kprintln!("kernel HHDM aliases validated: text/rodata R/NX, data RW/NX, PAT preserved");
    let candidate_root = candidate
        .root_physical_address()
        .expect("a live candidate retains its root frame");
    let root_hhdm_address = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        candidate_root,
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let root_alias = match candidate.walk(root_hhdm_address) {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
            if translation.physical_address == candidate_root =>
        {
            translation
        }
        result => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM alias: {:?}",
                result
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    if !root_alias.permissions.writable || root_alias.permissions.user_accessible {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: candidate root alias permissions are unsafe");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let new_cr3 = match encode_cr3_value(
        candidate_root,
        inherited_root.low_bits(),
        physical_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: new CR3: {:?}", error);
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let inherited_cr3 = boot_info.inherited_cr3_raw;
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != inherited_cr3 {
        kprintln!("page-table transition aborted: active CR3 changed before switch");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    if let Some(rsdp_physical_address) = boot_info.rsdp_physical_address {
        match load_acpi_madt(
            &mut candidate,
            &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
            &boot_info.memory_map,
            &boot_info.cpu_info,
            rsdp_physical_address,
            new_cr3,
            inherited_cr3,
        ) {
            Ok(madt) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "ACPI MADT copied: LAPIC={:#x}, {} local APICs, {} I/O APICs, {} overrides",
                    madt.local_apic_address,
                    madt.local_apics().count(),
                    madt.io_apics().count(),
                    madt.interrupt_overrides().count()
                );
                boot_info.acpi_madt = Some(madt);
            }
            Err(error) => kprintln!("ACPI MADT unavailable: {:?}", error),
        }
    }
    let apic_virtual_addresses = match boot_info.acpi_madt.as_ref() {
        Some(madt) => match map_bootstrap_apic_pages(
            &mut candidate,
            &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
            &boot_info.cpu_info,
            madt,
            &boot_info.memory_map,
            (
                boot_info.kernel_physical_base,
                boot_info.kernel_physical_end,
            ),
        ) {
            Ok(addresses) => Some(addresses),
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("APIC MMIO mappings unavailable: {}", error);
                None
            }
        },
        None => None,
    };
    match candidate.validate_supervisor_kernel_half() {
        Ok(table_count) => kprintln!(
            "kernel upper-half preflight passed: {} shared supervisor tables",
            table_count
        ),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: unsafe kernel upper half: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: The candidate is a complete clone of every present inherited
    // hierarchy entry, with all referenced intermediate tables owned and the
    // critical code/data/stack paths compared before this point. The inherited
    // root's paging mode, address widths, PAT/MTRR state, and low CR3 mode are
    // preserved; interrupts remain disabled through this transition and are enabled
    // later only after the selected APIC routes and handlers are ready.
    let global_tlb_flushed = unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(new_cr3) };
    if global_tlb_flushed {
        kprintln!("page-table transition: global TLB flushed via CR4.PGE toggle");
    } else {
        kprintln!("page-table transition: CR4.PGE clear; CR3 reload flushed active translations");
    }
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != new_cr3
        || !spans
            .iter()
            .all(|(_, virtual_start, physical_start, length)| {
                candidate_span_matches_source(
                    &candidate,
                    &reader,
                    inherited_root,
                    config,
                    *virtual_start,
                    *physical_start,
                    *length,
                )
            })
    {
        // SAFETY: The inherited root and its backing memory remain untouched and
        // mapped by the candidate, so restoring its validated CR3 value is safe.
        unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(inherited_cr3) };
        if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != inherited_cr3 {
            kprintln!("page-table transition failed to restore inherited CR3; candidate retained");
            halt_forever();
        }
        kprintln!("page-table transition failed post-switch verification; restored inherited CR3");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    // SAFETY: CR3 matches `new_cr3` and post-switch translation checks passed;
    // interrupts are disabled and the candidate root must remain allocated.
    unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
    kprintln!(
        "page-table transition passed: active CR3={:#x}, cloned root={:#x}, {} owned tables",
        new_cr3,
        candidate_root,
        candidate.table_count()
    );

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-active-mapping")]
    {
        if let Err(error) = probe_active_mapping(
            &mut candidate,
            &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
            &boot_info.cpu_info,
        ) {
            kprintln!("active mapping probe failed: {}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
        kprintln!("active mapping probe passed: mapped, accessed, unmapped, reclaimed frame");
    }

    let mut vector_allocator = rustix_kernel::irq::InterruptVectorAllocator::new();
    let mut timer_vector = None;
    let mut timer_verified = false;
    if let (Some(madt), Some((local_apic_virtual, io_apic_virtual))) =
        (boot_info.acpi_madt.as_ref(), apic_virtual_addresses)
    {
        if let Some(vector) = vector_allocator.allocate() {
            let vector_number = vector.number();
            timer_vector = Some(vector);
            // SAFETY: Boot is single-core with IF=0. The cloned root is active,
            // and these virtual addresses were validated supervisor RW/NX/UC
            // mappings of the exact MADT-described APIC pages.
            match unsafe {
                arch::x86_64::apic::initialize(
                    madt,
                    local_apic_virtual,
                    io_apic_virtual,
                    arch::x86_64::cpu::bootstrap_apic_id(),
                )
            } {
                Err(error) => kprintln!(
                    "APIC initialization failed; IRQs remain disabled: {:?}",
                    error
                ),
                Ok(()) => {
                    // SAFETY: APIC initialization masked every route, including
                    // PIT IRQ0; the handler is ready before the route is armed.
                    match unsafe {
                        arch::x86_64::interrupts::register_irq_handler(
                            vector_number,
                            bootstrap_timer_irq,
                        )
                    } {
                        Err(error) => {
                            kprintln!("timer IRQ handler registration failed: {:?}", error)
                        }
                        Ok(()) => match PitRate::for_frequency(100) {
                            Err(error) => kprintln!("PIT rate selection failed: {:?}", error),
                            Ok(rate) => {
                                // SAFETY: The source remains masked through
                                // configuration and the ISR is already registered.
                                let configured = unsafe {
                                    arch::x86_64::apic::configure_pit_timer(
                                        vector_number,
                                        rate.divisor(),
                                    )
                                };
                                match configured {
                                    Err(error) => {
                                        kprintln!("PIT configuration failed: {:?}", error)
                                    }
                                    Ok(()) => {
                                        // SAFETY: Only the validated IRQ0 route is
                                        // unmasked after its handler is installed.
                                        match unsafe { arch::x86_64::apic::unmask_pit_timer() } {
                                            Err(error) => {
                                                kprintln!("PIT route unmask failed: {:?}", error)
                                            }
                                            Ok(()) => {
                                                // SAFETY: IDT/APIC/EOI/handler are
                                                // ready, every other route is masked,
                                                // and this ISR neither allocates nor
                                                // touches non-atomic shared state.
                                                unsafe {
                                                    core::arch::asm!(
                                                        "sti",
                                                        options(nomem, nostack)
                                                    );
                                                }
                                                let target =
                                                    BOOTSTRAP_TIMER_TICKS.ticks().saturating_add(3);
                                                let mut observed = false;
                                                for _ in 0..100_000_000 {
                                                    if BOOTSTRAP_TIMER_TICKS.ticks() >= target {
                                                        observed = true;
                                                        break;
                                                    }
                                                    spin_loop();
                                                }
                                                if observed {
                                                    timer_verified = true;
                                                    kprintln!("timer IRQ path passed: 3 ticks, EOI acknowledged");
                                                } else {
                                                    // SAFETY: Stop the sole unmasked
                                                    // source before continuing without
                                                    // a verified runtime clock.
                                                    unsafe {
                                                        core::arch::asm!(
                                                            "cli",
                                                            options(nomem, nostack)
                                                        );
                                                        let _ =
                                                            arch::x86_64::apic::mask_pit_timer();
                                                    }
                                                    kprintln!("timer IRQ validation timed out; interrupts disabled");
                                                }
                                            }
                                        }
                                    }
                                }
                            }
                        },
                    }
                }
            }
        } else {
            kprintln!("no device IRQ vector available; interrupts remain disabled");
        }
    } else {
        kprintln!("validated MADT/APIC mappings unavailable; polling mode retained");
    }
    let input_irq_flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: Route setup and callback registration require IF=0.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", "cli", out(reg) input_irq_flags) };
    let input_setup = if timer_verified {
        boot_info
            .acpi_madt
            .as_ref()
            .map(|madt| configure_input_irqs(madt, &mut vector_allocator))
            .unwrap_or_default()
    } else {
        InputIrqSetup::default()
    };
    if input_irq_flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        // SAFETY: Device handlers and masked-first routes are initialized.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("sti") };
    }
    let _keep_vector_allocator_and_token_live = (
        vector_allocator,
        timer_vector,
        input_setup.uart_vector,
        input_setup.keyboard_vector,
    );
    let mut heap_mapping_context = KernelHeapMappingContext {
        candidate: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(candidate).cast(),
        allocator: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(boot_info.frame_allocator),
        cpu_info: core::ptr::addr_of!(boot_info.cpu_info),
    };
    for page in 0..KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_MAX_PAGES {
        let address = KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE + page as u64 * PAGE_SIZE;
        if !matches!(
            candidate.walk(address),
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. })
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "frame-backed heap virtual range is already mapped at {:#x}",
                address
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: The full virtual range is confirmed unmapped and exclusively
    // reserved. Candidate, allocator, CPU snapshot, and context remain live on
    // this non-returning boot path; the callback is transactional and nonallocating.
    if let Err(error) = unsafe {
        KERNEL_HEAP.initialize_frame_backed_region(
            KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE as usize,
            KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_MAX_PAGES,
            core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(heap_mapping_context).cast(),
            map_kernel_heap_pages,
        )
    } {
        kprintln!("frame-backed heap setup failed: {:?}", error);
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "frame-backed heap configured: {} KiB maximum, demand-mapped",
        KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_MAX_PAGES * PAGE_SIZE as usize / 1024
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
    if timer_verified {
        if let Err(error) = kernel_threads::smoke(
            &mut candidate,
            &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
            &boot_info.cpu_info,
            &BOOTSTRAP_TIMER_TICKS,
        ) {
            kprintln!("cooperative thread probe failed: {}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    }
    probe_kernel_heap();

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
    {
        let probe_flags: u64;
        // SAFETY: This is the single-vCPU bootstrap path; retain IF for restoration.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", "cli", out(reg) probe_flags) };
        KERNEL_HEAP.seal_frame_backed_growth();

        let probe_result = probe_user_process_root(
            &candidate,
            &boot_info.memory_map,
            &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
            &boot_info.cpu_info,
            boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            config,
        );
        // SAFETY: The process root set and its shared borrow are dropped before
        // returning from the probe. The candidate and callback context remain live.
        if let Err(error) = unsafe {
            KERNEL_HEAP.initialize_frame_backed_region(
                KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE as usize,
                KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_MAX_PAGES,
                core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(heap_mapping_context).cast(),
                map_kernel_heap_pages,
            )
        } {
            kprintln!(
                "process-root probe could not restore heap growth: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        if probe_flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
            // SAFETY: The process root is destroyed and heap growth is restored.
            unsafe { core::arch::asm!("sti", options(nomem, nostack)) };
        }
        if let Err(error) = probe_result {
            kprintln!("process-root probe failed: {}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
        #[cfg(not(any(
            feature = "probe-user-fault",
            feature = "probe-user-page-fault",
            feature = "probe-user-general-protection",
            feature = "probe-user-divide-error"
        )))]
        kprintln!("Ring 3 init passed: write/EFAULT/wait/exit syscalls, kernel wait, and process-root teardown");
        #[cfg(any(
            feature = "probe-user-fault",
            feature = "probe-user-page-fault",
            feature = "probe-user-general-protection",
            feature = "probe-user-divide-error"
        ))]
        kprintln!(
            "Ring 3 user fault passed: process exited, was waited on, and its root was torn down"
        );
    }

    // Keep the candidate and its frame tokens alive for as long as this root is
    // active. The shell runs forever and does not return to this stack frame.
    // SAFETY: The bootstrap remains single-core. If enabled, the timer handler
    // touches only its atomic counter and APIC EOI; the shell owns the filesystem.
    let filesystem = unsafe { &mut *core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RAM_FILESYSTEM) };
    match filesystem.seed_defaults() {
        Ok(home) if input_setup.uart_ready && timer_verified => {
            let mut shell_context = ShellThreadContext {
                filesystem: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(*filesystem),
                cwd: home,
                memory_map: core::ptr::addr_of!(boot_info.memory_map),
                frame_allocator: core::ptr::addr_of!(boot_info.frame_allocator),
            };
            // SAFETY: The active root, candidate tokens, allocator, BootInfo,
            // filesystem, and callback context remain live on this non-returning
            // single-vCPU path. The allocator pointer stays raw between calls.
            kernel_threads::run_shell(
                &mut candidate,
                core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(boot_info.frame_allocator),
                &boot_info.cpu_info,
                &BOOTSTRAP_TIMER_TICKS,
                shell_thread_entry,
                core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(shell_context) as usize,
            )
        }
        Ok(home) => shell::run(
            filesystem,
            home,
            &boot_info.memory_map,
            core::ptr::addr_of!(boot_info.frame_allocator),
            core::ptr::null_mut(),
        ),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("RAM filesystem initialization failed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever()
        }
    }
}

extern "C" fn bootstrap_timer_irq() {
    BOOTSTRAP_TIMER_TICKS.tick();
    // Acknowledge before a scheduling switch so the APIC does not retain an
    // in-service timer vector while another context runs.
    arch::x86_64::apic::end_of_interrupt();
    kernel_threads::timer_interrupt();
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct InputIrqSetup {
    uart_vector: Option<rustix_kernel::irq::InterruptVector>,
    keyboard_vector: Option<rustix_kernel::irq::InterruptVector>,
    uart_ready: bool,
    keyboard_ready: bool,
}

fn configure_input_irqs(
    madt: &rustix_kernel::acpi::Madt,
    vectors: &mut rustix_kernel::irq::InterruptVectorAllocator,
) -> InputIrqSetup {
    let mut setup = InputIrqSetup::default();
    if let Some((vector, route_ready)) =
        configure_one_input_irq(madt, vectors, 4, arch::x86_64::serial::irq_handler)
    {
        let vector_number = vector.number();
        setup.uart_vector = Some(vector);
        if route_ready && arch::x86_64::serial::enable_receive_interrupts() {
            // SAFETY: The UART handler is installed, COM1 is initialized, and
            // only its previously masked MADT route is being unmasked.
            setup.uart_ready =
                unsafe { arch::x86_64::apic::unmask_isa_irq(4, vector_number).is_ok() };
            if !setup.uart_ready {
                arch::x86_64::serial::disable_receive_interrupts();
            }
        }
    }

    if let Some((vector, route_ready)) =
        configure_one_input_irq(madt, vectors, 1, arch::x86_64::keyboard::irq_handler)
    {
        let vector_number = vector.number();
        setup.keyboard_vector = Some(vector);
        if route_ready && arch::x86_64::keyboard::initialize_interrupts() {
            // SAFETY: The bounded PS/2 controller setup succeeded and its
            // registered IRQ handler is ready before unmasking the route.
            setup.keyboard_ready =
                unsafe { arch::x86_64::apic::unmask_isa_irq(1, vector_number).is_ok() };
        }
    }
    kprintln!(
        "interrupt-driven input: UART RX {}, PS/2 raw scancodes {}",
        if setup.uart_ready {
            "ready"
        } else {
            "unavailable"
        },
        if setup.keyboard_ready {
            "ready"
        } else {
            "unavailable"
        }
    );
    setup
}

fn configure_one_input_irq(
    madt: &rustix_kernel::acpi::Madt,
    vectors: &mut rustix_kernel::irq::InterruptVectorAllocator,
    isa_irq: u8,
    handler: arch::x86_64::interrupts::IrqHandler,
) -> Option<(rustix_kernel::irq::InterruptVector, bool)> {
    let vector = vectors.allocate()?;
    let vector_number = vector.number();
